types.name: BlobLink
types.description:
BlobLink is one shareable URL, keyed by the HASH of its token (R7).

 THE RAW TOKEN APPEARS NOWHERE PERSISTENT. It is returned once, by the call
 that minted it, and this row holds only `sha256(token)`; ListLinks returns no
 tokens, and the gateway redacts `/b/*` and `/upload/*` paths from its logs.
 So a reader of the record store — or of a log, or of a backup — cannot
 resolve any link.

 REVOCATION IS IMMEDIATE, which is v3's improvement over the v2 signed-URL
 design: we serve the bytes, so `revoked_ms` is checked on every resolve
 rather than waiting for a cloud URL to expire. It is kept rather than deleted
 so an audit can still say a link existed.

fields.name: token_hash
fields.description:
token_hash is the record key: the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw token.
 A resolve hashes what arrived in the path and looks up THAT, so the lookup
 key is not a secret even though the path is.

fields.name: blob_id
fields.description: blob_id is the Blob this link resolves to.

fields.name: filename
fields.description:
filename is what `Content-Disposition` offers, and the ONLY source of it
 (R8) — never a client-supplied header, never a query parameter. Validated
 at mint: a basename, no CR/LF, quote, backslash, semicolon, control
 character or path separator.

enum_values.name: LINK_POLICY_BEARER
enum_values.description:
BEARER: whoever holds the token. The only policy today (R7); SAME_TENANT
 and FLEET_ONLY are additive later and need a caller identity on the `/b/`
 path, which BEARER deliberately does not have.

fields.name: expires_ms
fields.description:
expires_ms is 0 for a durable shared link and non-zero for the short-lived
 one the owner mints for its own use. Checked on resolve alongside
 revoked_ms; the two are indistinguishable to the caller, who gets a 404
 either way.

fields.name: revoked_ms
fields.description:
revoked_ms is when the owner revoked the link, 0 while live. The row is
 KEPT — see the type comment.

types.name: BlobLinkStats
types.description:
BlobLinkStats is the coarse rollup of one link's resolutions (R10).

 The counters live IN MEMORY on the pod that served the request and are
 flushed here at most once a minute per token. That is the whole design: a
 `/b/` resolve must not cost a record write, and nobody needs a resolution
 count to be exact.

 `bytes_served` is honest here in a way it could not be in the v2 cloud
 design: we serve the bytes ourselves, so we count them rather than inferring
 them from a signed URL that may or may not have been followed.

 TWO PODS, TWO COUNTERS. Each pod flushes what it served, and a flush is a
 read-modify-write of this row — so the row is the SUM only as of the last
 flush either pod made. Exactness was never on offer for an in-memory counter;
 what matters is that a flush never loses another pod's contribution, which is
 why it reads before it adds.

fields.name: token_hash
fields.description:
token_hash is the key, and the same key BlobLink carries — the two rows are
 one link's two halves, split because the stats half is rewritten on a
 minute cadence and the link half is written once.

types.name: BlobstoreConfigState
types.description:
BlobstoreConfigState is the state boundary for blobstore service configuration.
 Auto-injected by tacplus from (spec.grpc_config) annotation.

message.name: Config
message.description: Config is delivered by kernel at startup and on every change.

fields.name: volume_groups
fields.description:
volume_groups is every group declared anywhere in the fleet, rendered by
 the operator. See VolumeGroup: empty means no upload is possible, which is
 correct and not a misconfiguration to paper over.

message.name: VolumeGroup
message.description:
VolumeGroup is one group's rules, as this service receives them.

 IT IS NOT DECLARED HERE. A group is declared at BUILD TIME by the consuming
 service — DocManager declares `documents`, a later feature declares `photos`
 — through the `(spec.volume_group)` service-level annotation tacplus surfaces
 in registry.json, and the operator renders every declared group into this
 config (R4, and the doc's Work split: the annotation is tacplus's slice, the
 rendering is the operator's). This message is the RECEIVING end of that
 pipeline and nothing more.

 So the list below being EMPTY is the correct state of a cluster whose
 services have declared no groups: every upload is then refused, which is what
 "no group, no upload" means. It is not a reason to invent a default group.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
name is the group's identity, and the first path segment of every file it
 holds (`<group>/<ns>/<sha256>`). Unique across the fleet — tacplus refuses
 a duplicate at generation, so this service does not have to arbitrate.

fields.name: max_blob_bytes
fields.description:
max_blob_bytes is the largest single blob the group accepts. Enforced ON
 THE WIRE, not from the declared size: an upload is aborted the moment the
 stream passes it (R9 step 2), because a client that lied about `size_bytes`
 must not be able to fill the disk before the check.

fields.name: content_types
fields.description:
content_types is the exhaustive allow-list. A type not listed is refused at
 CreateUpload, and the bytes are sniffed again at finish (R4) — a renamed
 `.exe` declaring `application/pdf` fails on its magic bytes even though it
 passed this list.

fields.name: tenant_quota_bytes
fields.description:
tenant_quota_bytes is the ceiling on the SUM of promoted blob sizes for one
 tenant in this group. Quotas hang off the group and there is no separate
 global tenant quota (R4).

fields.name: http_listener
fields.description:
http_listener is the bind address for the BYTE PATHS — `PUT /upload/<t>`
 and `GET|HEAD /b/<t>`, and nothing else.

 IN-CLUSTER ONLY, exactly like letsencrypt's ACME responder: the gateway
 owns the edge and proxies these two prefixes here, so this listener needs
 no externally-exposed Service of its own. It is plaintext because the hop
 is in-cluster and the token in the path is the whole authorization; the
 gateway is what terminates TLS for the client.

message.name: Host
message.description:
Host identifies a network endpoint by hostname/IP and port.
 The host field accepts either an FQDN or an IP address (v4/v6).

fields.name: host
fields.description: Hostname or IP address (e.g. "api.example.com" or "10.0.0.1").
constraints: must be a valid hostname or IP address

fields.name: port
fields.description: Port number (1-65535).
constraints: must be a valid network port (1-65535)

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: Transport protocol. Default TCP (zero value).

fields.name: peer_listener
fields.description:
peer_listener is the bind address for the MIRROR AND ANTI-ENTROPY paths,
 and it is a second listener rather than three more prefixes on the first
 for one reason: the anti-entropy path ENUMERATES the hashes this pod holds.
 The gateway proxies only the two prefixes above, so nothing outside the
 cluster can reach this port at all.

fields.name: peers
fields.description:
peers is the `host:port` peer_listener address of EVERY replica, including
 this pod's own, from the StatefulSet's stable per-pod DNS
 (`blobstore-0.blobstore:8081,blobstore-1.blobstore:8081`). The pod finds
 itself by matching its hostname against the first DNS label and treats the
 rest as peers.

 Delivered by the operator as BLOBSTORE_PEERS, the same env shape as
 stratum's STRATUM_SEED_MEMBERS — peer wiring is deployment topology the
 operator already knows, and inventing a second typed path for it would
 only let the two disagree.

fields.name: data_dir
fields.description:
data_dir is the PVC mount holding `<group>/<ns>/<sha256>` and the `tmp`
 directory partial uploads are written into.

 The default is UNDER /app/data because that is where the operator's chart
 mounts a service's volumeClaimTemplate (`- name: data / mountPath:
 /app/data`). A default anywhere else would put the blobs on the pod's
 ephemeral filesystem and lose them on every restart, which is the kind of
 mistake nothing would report — the writes would all succeed.

fields.name: upload_token_ttl_seconds
fields.description:
upload_token_ttl_seconds is how long a CreateUpload token is good for —
 the doc's ceiling is 15 minutes (R9 step 1) and that is the default. It
 bounds how long a reservation can sit unused, not how long an upload may
 take: the TTL is checked when the PUT arrives, not while it streams.

fields.name: stats_flush_interval_seconds
fields.description:
stats_flush_interval_seconds is the metrics rollup cadence: per-token
 counters live in memory and reach BlobLinkStats at most once a minute per
 token (R10). Held in config rather than as a constant for the same reason
 mailbox's sweep interval is — changing it must not need a rebuild.

fields.name: session_sweep_interval_seconds
fields.description:
session_sweep_interval_seconds is how often expired UploadSession rows have
 their reservations released (R9 step 4). The same sweep deletes leftover
 `tmp` files, which is also done once unconditionally at start-up: a crash
 mid-upload leaves temp files and nothing else cleans them.

types.name: CancelUploadRequest
CancelUploadResponse

fields.name: cancelled
fields.description:
cancelled is false when the session had already settled — committed,
 aborted, or expired and swept. Not an error; see CancelUpload.

 mid-upload leaves temp files and nothing else cleans them.

fields.name: token

fields.name: group
fields.description:

 does not name is refused — "no group, no upload" (R4).

fields.name: content_hash
fields.description:

fields.name: size_bytes

fields.name: content_type

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:

types.name: CreateUploadResponse

fields.name: upload_id
fields.description: upload_id is the UploadSession key, and what CancelUpload names.

fields.name: upload_token
fields.description:

 `/upload/<upload_token>` through the gateway. Returned once and stored
 nowhere.

fields.name: upload_path
fields.description:

 here so a caller does not hard-code the prefix.

fields.name: expires_ms
fields.description: expires_ms is when the token stops being accepted.

fields.name: already_present
fields.description:

types.name: EventBusRecordMeta
GetLinkStatsRequest
ListLinksRequest

fields.name: page_size
fields.description:
page_size and page_token are the PAGE envelope tacplus validates. page_size
 0 means "use default_page_size"; page_token is opaque to the caller and is
 the last token_hash of the previous page — the keyset cursor over the
 declared order_by, so a page is stable under concurrent CreateLink.

types.name: ListLinksResponse

fields.name: links
fields.description:
links carries the record type rather than a hand-rolled summary row,
 because (spec.store_principal) and (spec.store_namespace) filter repeated
 fields OF THAT RECORD TYPE on the way out — a bespoke row would be a read
 path with the generated backstop switched off.

 NO TOKENS ARE IN HERE, and none can be: BlobLink holds only the hash.

message.name: BlobLink
message.description:
BlobLink is one shareable URL, keyed by the HASH of its token (R7).

 THE RAW TOKEN APPEARS NOWHERE PERSISTENT. It is returned once, by the call
 that minted it, and this row holds only `sha256(token)`; ListLinks returns no
 tokens, and the gateway redacts `/b/*` and `/upload/*` paths from its logs.
 So a reader of the record store — or of a log, or of a backup — cannot
 resolve any link.

 REVOCATION IS IMMEDIATE, which is v3's improvement over the v2 signed-URL
 design: we serve the bytes, so `revoked_ms` is checked on every resolve
 rather than waiting for a cloud URL to expire. It is kept rather than deleted
 so an audit can still say a link existed.

fields.name: token_hash
fields.description:
token_hash is the record key: the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw token.
 A resolve hashes what arrived in the path and looks up THAT, so the lookup
 key is not a secret even though the path is.

fields.name: blob_id
fields.description: blob_id is the Blob this link resolves to.

fields.name: filename
fields.description:
filename is what `Content-Disposition` offers, and the ONLY source of it
 (R8) — never a client-supplied header, never a query parameter. Validated
 at mint: a basename, no CR/LF, quote, backslash, semicolon, control
 character or path separator.

enum_values.name: LINK_POLICY_BEARER
enum_values.description:
BEARER: whoever holds the token. The only policy today (R7); SAME_TENANT
 and FLEET_ONLY are additive later and need a caller identity on the `/b/`
 path, which BEARER deliberately does not have.

fields.name: expires_ms
fields.description:
expires_ms is 0 for a durable shared link and non-zero for the short-lived
 one the owner mints for its own use. Checked on resolve alongside
 revoked_ms; the two are indistinguishable to the caller, who gets a 404
 either way.

fields.name: revoked_ms
fields.description:
revoked_ms is when the owner revoked the link, 0 while live. The row is
 KEPT — see the type comment.

fields.name: next_page_token
fields.description:
next_page_token is empty on the last page. It is the PAGE envelope's other
 half; see ListLinksRequest.page_token.

fields.name: token_hash

fields.name: revoked

types.name: UploadSession
types.description:
UploadSession is one upload's durable reservation and audit trail (R9).

 IT IS THE AUTHORIZATION FOR THE PUT. The upload token carries nothing: it is
 raw randomness, and this row — keyed by its sha256 — is where the upload's
 terms live. A pod receiving a PUT hashes the token, reads this row, and takes
 the group, namespace, declared hash, size and content type from it. Exactly
 the shape BlobLink gives a `/b/` token (R3, R7); there is no signing key and
 nothing to rotate.

 THE COST, STATED: a record reaches stratum on an eventbus publish, which is
 enqueue-and-retry, so a PUT arriving milliseconds after CreateUpload returned
 can find this row missing and be refused. BlobLink has had exactly that race
 since it was written and it is accepted there for the same reason — a caller
 that just asked for the token retries.

 This row is ALSO the quota reservation, the expiry sweep that releases it, the
 single-use ledger (state leaves PENDING once), and the answer to "what was
 uploaded, by whom, when".

fields.name: upload_id
fields.description:
upload_id is the record key: the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw upload
 token, exactly as BlobLink.token_hash is for a `/b/` token. A PUT hashes
 what arrived in the path and looks up THAT, so the key is not a secret even
 though the path is. It is derived from the token and not from the content
 hash: two tenants uploading the same bytes at the same time are two
 sessions.

fields.name: group
fields.description:
group, content_hash, size_bytes and content_type are what the upload
 DECLARED. The Blob row carries what actually arrived; the two are compared
 at end of stream and a mismatch fails the upload (R9 step 3).

fields.name: reserved_bytes
fields.description:
reserved_bytes is what this session holds against the tenant's group quota
 while it is PENDING. It is the DECLARED size — the only number available
 before the bytes arrive — which is why `max_blob_bytes` is also enforced on
 the wire: the reservation is a promise the stream still has to keep.

fields.name: state
fields.description: state is the session's terminal answer. See UploadState.

enum_values.name: UPLOAD_STATE_PENDING
enum_values.description:
PENDING: quota is reserved and the token is live. No bytes have been
 promoted.

enum_values.name: UPLOAD_STATE_COMMITTED
enum_values.description:
COMMITTED: the bytes are fsynced and renamed on both pods and the Blob row
 is published. The reservation became real usage.

enum_values.name: UPLOAD_STATE_ABORTED
enum_values.description:
ABORTED: CancelUpload, an expiry sweep, or a failed PUT. Temps are gone
 from both pods and the reservation is released.

fields.name: created_ms
fields.description:
created_ms and expires_ms bound the token. expires_ms is checked when the
 PUT ARRIVES, not while it streams: a 50 MiB upload on a slow link must not
 fail at minute 16 having transferred everything.

fields.name: owner_principal
fields.description:
owner_principal and namespace are the owning service and owning tenant, as
 on Blob. The reservation is against exactly this pair's group quota.

types.name: VolumeGroup
types.description:
VolumeGroup is one group's rules, as this service receives them.

 IT IS NOT DECLARED HERE. A group is declared at BUILD TIME by the consuming
 service — DocManager declares `documents`, a later feature declares `photos`
 — through the `(spec.volume_group)` service-level annotation tacplus surfaces
 in registry.json, and the operator renders every declared group into this
 config (R4, and the doc's Work split: the annotation is tacplus's slice, the
 rendering is the operator's). This message is the RECEIVING end of that
 pipeline and nothing more.

 So the list below being EMPTY is the correct state of a cluster whose
 services have declared no groups: every upload is then refused, which is what
 "no group, no upload" means. It is not a reason to invent a default group.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
name is the group's identity, and the first path segment of every file it
 holds (`<group>/<ns>/<sha256>`). Unique across the fleet — tacplus refuses
 a duplicate at generation, so this service does not have to arbitrate.

fields.name: max_blob_bytes
fields.description:
max_blob_bytes is the largest single blob the group accepts. Enforced ON
 THE WIRE, not from the declared size: an upload is aborted the moment the
 stream passes it (R9 step 2), because a client that lied about `size_bytes`
 must not be able to fill the disk before the check.

fields.name: content_types
fields.description:
content_types is the exhaustive allow-list. A type not listed is refused at
 CreateUpload, and the bytes are sniffed again at finish (R4) — a renamed
 `.exe` declaring `application/pdf` fails on its magic bytes even though it
 passed this list.

fields.name: tenant_quota_bytes
fields.description:
tenant_quota_bytes is the ceiling on the SUM of promoted blob sizes for one
 tenant in this group. Quotas hang off the group and there is no separate
 global tenant quota (R4).

rpcs.description:
CreateUpload checks the group's rules and the tenant's quota, reserves the
 quota, writes an UploadSession row, and returns the single-use upload token
 (R9 step 1). It does not touch a byte.
rpcs.verb_definition: Bring a new resource into existence.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Mint; creates durable resource state.

rpcs.description:
CancelUpload releases the reservation and settles the session ABORTED.
 IDEMPOTENT: cancelling a session that has already settled is a no-op, not
 an error, because a client that times out and retries must not fail on it.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Delete; terminates active work without deleting the target resource.

rpcs.description:
CreateLink mints a shareable bearer link for a blob the caller owns and
 returns the raw token EXACTLY ONCE (R7). The token is never stored and
 cannot be recovered; a caller that loses it mints another.
rpcs.verb_definition: Bring a new resource into existence.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Mint; creates durable resource state.

rpcs.description:
CreateBlobUrl mints a SHORT-LIVED link for the owner's own use — the
 doc's GetBlobUrl, renamed per the service comment. Same row type, same
 path; only `expires_ms` differs, and it is required here.
rpcs.verb_definition: Bring a new resource into existence.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Mint; creates durable resource state.

rpcs.description:
RevokeLink stops a link resolving, immediately. The row is kept with
 `revoked_ms` set, for audit. IDEMPOTENT.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Delete; invalidates credential/session/grant semantics without deleting a resource.

rpcs.description:
ListLinks returns the caller's links for one blob, WITHOUT tokens (R7).

 PAGED rather than a single snapshot. This was originally forced by a tacplus
 Go-emitter bug (a unary COLLECTION_MODE_SNAPSHOT method compiled to a
 server-streaming wrapper against a unary descriptor) — tacplus@7c483bab fixed
 that (see tacplus/looper/workers/blobstore-gaps-result.md), so SNAPSHOT would
 work now too. Left as PAGE anyway: it's the standard envelope tacplus
 validates, not a bespoke one, and reworking already-tested/committed
 request/response shapes back to a bare snapshot buys nothing a bounded
 hundred-row page doesn't already give.
rpcs.verb_definition: Finite/paginated set, ordered by order_by; filters are fields.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get-plural/Search/Query; collection reads must declare method_collection.

rpcs.description:
DeleteBlob unlinks the bytes from both pods and flags the Blob row deleted.
 Owner-only, like every RPC here.

 It is NOT garbage collection: the store cannot know when a blob is
 unreferenced, because the pointers live in consumers (R12). This is the
 owner saying "I am done with this one".
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Revoke; removes resource state rather than invalidating a credential or grant.

services.name: BlobStore
services.description:
BlobStore is the owning service's control surface. Every RPC is s2s: the
 owner of a blob is a SERVICE identity (R6), and there is no user-facing RPC
 here at all — a person reaches a blob through the `/b/` path with a token
 their service minted for them.

 VERB NAMES DIFFER FROM THE DECISION DOC'S SKETCH, which wrote BeginUpload,
 AbortUpload and GetBlobUrl. The RPC verb registry is CLOSED
 (tacplus/pkg/internal/common/verbs/registry.json) and is enforced on s2s
 services as well as c2s (parser.serviceEnforcesVerbs), so `Begin` and `Abort`
 do not generate at all. The registered verbs whose definitions are these
 operations are used instead:

   BeginUpload  -> CreateUpload   ("bring a new resource into existence" — the
                                   UploadSession row is that resource)
   AbortUpload  -> CancelUpload   ("stop in-flight work", which is the session)
   GetBlobUrl   -> CreateBlobUrl  (Get's boundary is "must not mutate state",
                                   and minting a self-use link writes a
                                   BlobLink row)

 Nothing about the semantics the doc settled changes.

types.name: Config
types.description: Config is delivered by kernel at startup and on every change.

fields.name: max_open_ingests
fields.description:
max_open_ingests bounds how many ingest pipelines may be in flight at
 once. A resource limit on the service (same category as
 scotty.Config.max_open_tickets), not a business rule.

types.name: CreateDocFileLinkRequest

fields.name: file_id
fields.description:
file_id is the only field, and namespace is deliberately NOT one — matching
 GetDocFileMetadataRequest and UpdateDocFileLocationRequest, the other two
 single-row rpcs keyed on the record key. Those derive the tenant from the
 caller's token claim inside the handler rather than from a request field,
 and a THIRD shape for the same lookup would be the only thing a
 (spec.namespace) field here would add: the wrapper's (spec.namespace) bind
 refuses a namespace that does not equal the caller's claim, so it cannot
 authorize anything the handler's own fail-closed check does not already
 refuse. The namespace blobstore.CreateLink is called with comes off the
 fetched row, after that check.

types.name: CreateDocFileLinkResponse

fields.name: link_path
fields.description:
link_path is `/b/<token>` — the path the holder GETs, straight from
 blobstore. It embeds the raw token, which is why this response is the ONE
 place it appears: see token_hash below.

fields.name: token_hash
fields.description:
token_hash names the link for a later RevokeLink and is safe to hand back
 or log: it cannot be turned back into the token.

 THE RAW TOKEN IS NOT A FIELD HERE, and that is non-negotiable rather than an
 omission. blobstore's CreateLink doc-comment is explicit that it "returns
 the raw token EXACTLY ONCE (R7)" and that the token is never stored; a
 `token` field on this response would be DocManager re-emitting a credential
 blobstore handed it in confidence, and a persisted copy anywhere on this
 side would break the once-only property outright. The token reaches the
 direct caller inside link_path and nowhere else, and DocManager writes no
 record of this call at all.

fields.name: created_ms
fields.description:
created_ms is blobstore's own creation timestamp for the link, passed
 through rather than re-derived from this service's clock, so it agrees with
 what ListLinks/GetLinkStats report for the same link.

types.name: CreateIngestRequest

fields.name: content_hash
fields.description:
content_hash is the caller's DECLARED lowercase hex SHA-256 of the bytes it
 is about to PUT. It is what makes this ingest content-addressed: blobstore
 binds it into the upload token, so the token authorizes exactly these bytes,
 and it is the key of the DocHashIndex row this ingest writes. Same 64-hex
 bound blobstore.CreateUploadRequest.content_hash asserts — a hash that does
 not match the bytes fails at the gateway-verified PUT, not here.

fields.name: content_type
fields.description:
content_type must be in the `documents` volume group's allow-list (declared
 on the service above). Refused at CreateUpload if it is not, and sniffed
 against the bytes' magic numbers at finish.

types.name: CreateIngestResponse

fields.name: blob_id
fields.description:
blob_id is `documents/<namespace>/<content_hash>`, straight from
 blobstore.CreateUpload. Final already — there is no later id to wait for.

fields.name: upload_path
fields.description:
upload_path is `/upload/<token>`: where the CALLER PUTs the bytes, through
 the gateway. Carrying it back is what makes this response actionable —
 without it a caller knows a document exists but has nowhere to send it.
 Populated even when already_present is true (the PUT still works and
 dedups); it is the caller's choice to skip it.

fields.name: already_present
fields.description:
already_present: these exact bytes are already stored for this tenant in
 the `documents` group, so the PUT can be skipped. This is the dedup
 short-circuit the declared content_hash buys.

types.name: DocFileMetadata
types.description:
DocFileMetadata is the customer-facing view: owner, namespace, and the
 folder/path structure the customer sees — independent of how the bytes
 are actually stored. Fast lookup by owner/namespace/path.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
store_namespace: MANDATORY. Exact-match isolation — a caller only ever
 sees rows in their own namespace. Also (spec.query_field) = {op:
 QUERY_OP_EQ}: the s2s record_read plane (unlike c2s reads) does not
 auto-scope by namespace, so this is what lets a record_read caller
 actually filter by it — see
 decisions/record-read-mechanism-not-yet-built-2026-09-01.md point 1.
 Without this, DocFileMetadataFilter would carry only the record key
 (file_id), and a namespace-scoped list against the reader would have to
 filter every row in the fleet client-side instead of at the query.

fields.name: owner_principal
fields.description:
owner_principal: who owns this file. (spec.store_principal), NOT
 (spec.principal) — the latter is for a REQUEST field the wrapper stamps
 from the caller's subject on the way IN; this is a RECORD field naming
 the row's owning principal for egress filtering (every c2s read of this
 record type is filtered down to rows the caller owns). Found the
 distinction by hitting stratum's real generation error: "RecordQuery
 ...GetDocFileMetadataSample cannot be generated for a c2s surface
 because its response field 'items' carries (spec.record) rows declaring
 no owner the wrapper can filter on" — (spec.principal) doesn't count as
 that, only (spec.store_principal) does. CreateIngestRequest.owner_principal
 below is a genuine request field, so it correctly keeps (spec.principal).

fields.name: customer_path
fields.description:
customer_path is the folder/file path as the customer sees it (the
 Box Drive tree, once that milestone lands) — independent of
 content_hash, which only identifies the bytes.

fields.name: content_hash
fields.description:
content_hash joins to DocHashIndex.content_hash. Not declared as a
 foreign-key type here — tacplus's record plane has no cross-record FK
 annotation as of this writing; the join is application-level.

fields.name: stage
fields.description: Ingest pipeline stage this row has reached. See IngestStage below.

fields.name: blob_id
fields.description:
blob_id is the platform blob store's id for this document's bytes,
 `documents/<namespace>/<content_hash>` — the same value DocHashIndex.blob_id
 carries for this row's content_hash. It is what makes a document a CONSUMER
 POINTER at a blob rather than a thing that owns bytes (blob store v3 R5: "a
 consumer's record points at a hash and moves its own pointer"), and it is
 the one field CreateDocFileLink below needs in order to call
 blobstore.CreateLink.

 It comes STRAIGHT FROM blobstore's CreateUploadResponse.blob_id, copied onto
 this row by the same CreateIngest handler that writes the DocHashIndex row
 from the same response (services/docmanager/src/service.rs, write_ingest) —
 NOT read back off the DocHashIndex row at this content_hash. That
 distinction is not a style choice: DocHashIndex has no `s2s_read` grant, so
 tacplus generates no reader over it, and a file_id -> blob_id join through
 it is therefore not expressible today. Copying the value at ingest is the
 only path that exists, and it is safe to copy because a blob_id is derived
 entirely from (group, namespace, content_hash) and blobs are immutable, so
 the two copies cannot drift.

 DocHashIndex stays the per-tenant content_hash -> blob_id index for dedup
 lookups; this field is the per-document pointer. Same 1024 bound
 DocHashIndex.blob_id uses, for the same value.
 See decisions/documents-volume-group-2026-09-26.md.

types.name: DocHashIndex
types.description:
DocHashIndex is the content-addressing index: a hash resolves to where the
 actual bytes live in the external object store. Near-infrastructure — this
 is NOT the customer-facing view of a document, which is DocFileMetadata
 below. One row per distinct content hash: identical bytes uploaded twice
 produce one row, which is the dedup the design doc calls out.

fields.name: content_hash
namespace
fields.description:
store_namespace: MANDATORY per the namespace-isolation decision. A hash
 index row is still per-tenant — two tenants uploading byte-identical
 files must not collide across the isolation boundary, even though the
 content hash alone would be identical. Dedup therefore happens WITHIN a
 namespace, not globally across tenants.

fields.name: blob_id
fields.description:
blob_id is the platform blob store's id for these bytes:
 `documents/<namespace>/<content_hash>`, the `documents` volume group
 declared on the service below. It is NOT assembled here — blobstore
 returns it from CreateUpload (blobstore.proto's CreateUploadResponse.blob_id,
 known before a byte moves because the key IS the declared content hash),
 and DocManager stores what it was given.

 This field was `object_store_location`, an opaque caller-supplied
 placeholder, until 2026-09-26. Same field number: the placeholder was
 renamed to the real value it always stood for, which is why the record
 shape did not have to change when the store was wired in.
 See decisions/documents-volume-group-2026-09-26.md.

fields.name: indexed_at_ms
fields.description:
indexed_at_ms is when this hash was first indexed. It was the retention
 clock until retention was removed (see the record option above); nothing
 measures from it today.

fields.name: ref_count
fields.description:
ref_count is a hint for reclamation (delete the object once no
 DocFileMetadata row references this hash any more), maintained by
 DocManager's own write path, not derived by generation.

fields.name: owning_service
fields.description:
owning_service names DocManager's own service identity, NOT a customer.
 A hash-index row has no single natural owner — dedup means several
 customers' DocFileMetadata rows can reference the same content_hash
 within a namespace — so there is no per-user principal to declare
 honestly here. This record type still needs SOME (spec.store_principal)
 field: stratum hosts a generic RecordQuery/RecordMap c2s surface over
 EVERY (spec.record) in the fleet regardless of that record's own
 s2s/c2s declaration (confirmed by reading tacplus's
 recordprincipal_gen.go — javaRecordPrincipalUnenforceable fails
 generation for any (spec.record) with no resolvable owner, fleet-wide,
 not just for records that opt into the query trait themselves), so this
 field exists purely to satisfy that platform-wide constraint. Declaring
 the SERVICE as owner (same pattern spec.proto documents for
 service-emitted accounting rows) is also the semantically-honest answer
 AND fails closed: no human caller's token subject will ever equal a
 service identity, so DocHashIndex's (otherwise unused — see
 decisions/docmanageragent-read-path-open-2026-09-01.md, Reveille
 reads DocFileMetadata directly via its own stratum grant, not this
 trait) c2s query surface can never actually return rows to anyone.

Kept equal to the method_collection max_items above — the two describe
 one cap and must not drift (see scotty.proto's ListHumansResponse for
 the same pairing).

message.name: DocFileMetadata
message.description:
DocFileMetadata is the customer-facing view: owner, namespace, and the
 folder/path structure the customer sees — independent of how the bytes
 are actually stored. Fast lookup by owner/namespace/path.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
store_namespace: MANDATORY. Exact-match isolation — a caller only ever
 sees rows in their own namespace. Also (spec.query_field) = {op:
 QUERY_OP_EQ}: the s2s record_read plane (unlike c2s reads) does not
 auto-scope by namespace, so this is what lets a record_read caller
 actually filter by it — see
 decisions/record-read-mechanism-not-yet-built-2026-09-01.md point 1.
 Without this, DocFileMetadataFilter would carry only the record key
 (file_id), and a namespace-scoped list against the reader would have to
 filter every row in the fleet client-side instead of at the query.

fields.name: owner_principal
fields.description:
owner_principal: who owns this file. (spec.store_principal), NOT
 (spec.principal) — the latter is for a REQUEST field the wrapper stamps
 from the caller's subject on the way IN; this is a RECORD field naming
 the row's owning principal for egress filtering (every c2s read of this
 record type is filtered down to rows the caller owns). Found the
 distinction by hitting stratum's real generation error: "RecordQuery
 ...GetDocFileMetadataSample cannot be generated for a c2s surface
 because its response field 'items' carries (spec.record) rows declaring
 no owner the wrapper can filter on" — (spec.principal) doesn't count as
 that, only (spec.store_principal) does. CreateIngestRequest.owner_principal
 below is a genuine request field, so it correctly keeps (spec.principal).

fields.name: customer_path
fields.description:
customer_path is the folder/file path as the customer sees it (the
 Box Drive tree, once that milestone lands) — independent of
 content_hash, which only identifies the bytes.

fields.name: content_hash
fields.description:
content_hash joins to DocHashIndex.content_hash. Not declared as a
 foreign-key type here — tacplus's record plane has no cross-record FK
 annotation as of this writing; the join is application-level.

fields.name: stage
fields.description: Ingest pipeline stage this row has reached. See IngestStage below.

fields.name: blob_id
fields.description:
blob_id is the platform blob store's id for this document's bytes,
 `documents/<namespace>/<content_hash>` — the same value DocHashIndex.blob_id
 carries for this row's content_hash. It is what makes a document a CONSUMER
 POINTER at a blob rather than a thing that owns bytes (blob store v3 R5: "a
 consumer's record points at a hash and moves its own pointer"), and it is
 the one field CreateDocFileLink below needs in order to call
 blobstore.CreateLink.

 It comes STRAIGHT FROM blobstore's CreateUploadResponse.blob_id, copied onto
 this row by the same CreateIngest handler that writes the DocHashIndex row
 from the same response (services/docmanager/src/service.rs, write_ingest) —
 NOT read back off the DocHashIndex row at this content_hash. That
 distinction is not a style choice: DocHashIndex has no `s2s_read` grant, so
 tacplus generates no reader over it, and a file_id -> blob_id join through
 it is therefore not expressible today. Copying the value at ingest is the
 only path that exists, and it is safe to copy because a blob_id is derived
 entirely from (group, namespace, content_hash) and blobs are immutable, so
 the two copies cannot drift.

 DocHashIndex stays the per-tenant content_hash -> blob_id index for dedup
 lookups; this field is the per-document pointer. Same 1024 bound
 DocHashIndex.blob_id uses, for the same value.
 See decisions/documents-volume-group-2026-09-26.md.

rpcs.description:
CreateIngest starts the async pipeline for a document, and reserves the
 document's place in the blob store BEFORE any bytes move: the handler
 calls blobstore.CreateUpload with the caller's declared content_hash,
 size_bytes and content_type against the `documents` volume group declared
 above, and returns the resulting blob_id together with the upload_path the
 CALLER then PUTs the bytes to. DocManager never carries the bytes itself —
 a blob is up to max_blob_bytes and the fleet's unary ceiling is 10MB, so
 the byte path is HTTP through the gateway (blobstore.proto's header).
 There is no second RPC after the PUT: CreateUpload already returns the
 final blob_id, and blobstore promotes the row on the hash-verified PUT.
 When already_present is true the bytes are already stored for this tenant
 and group and the caller can skip the PUT entirely.

 The RPC no longer accepts a caller-supplied object_store_location — the
 blob store assigns the id (decisions/documents-volume-group-2026-09-26.md).
 Returns immediately; the pipeline runs event-driven.

 This RPC IS the `Put` of the service/agent split
 (decisions/service-agent-rpc-split-and-identity-2026-09-07.md): the
 user-facing "land a file" call. `Put` is that decision's NAME for this
 surface, not a second RPC — see
 decisions/put-is-create-ingest-and-agent-move-rpc-2026-09-07.md for why
 no rename happened. What DID change to satisfy it: the request no longer
 carries customer_path, so a caller cannot file directly into an
 organized location. Every ingest lands in the inbox
 (INBOX_CUSTOMER_PATH in services/docmanager/src/service.rs) and only
 UpdateDocFileLocation (Reveille, one field) moves it out.
rpcs.verb_definition: Bring a new resource into existence.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Mint; creates durable resource state.

rpcs.description:
Read one document's metadata by its file_id: who owns it, the customer-facing
 folder path it currently sits at, its display name, size, content hash and
 ingest stage. Returns not_found if no document with that file_id exists in
 the caller's namespace. Metadata only — this never returns file bytes.

 The doc comment is load-bearing, not decoration: this RPC is published as an
 MCP tool, and tacplus takes the leading comment as the tool description a
 model sees when deciding whether to call it.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.

rpcs.description:
List the documents in the caller's namespace, newest-first by file_id, as a
 single snapshot of up to 50 rows — owner, customer path, display name, size,
 content hash and ingest stage for each. Use it to see what documents exist
 and where they are filed; use GetDocFileMetadata for one known file_id.
 Metadata only, never file bytes. See max_items below: this is deliberately
 not a full-collection read.
rpcs.verb_definition: Finite/paginated set, ordered by order_by; filters are fields.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get-plural/Search/Query; collection reads must declare method_collection.

rpcs.description:
Create a shareable download link for one of your own documents, named by its
 file_id. Returns the link path anyone holding the link GETs, plus the link's
 hash and creation time. Owner-only: you can only share a document you own.
 The link's download filename is the document's own display_name — a caller
 does not choose it.

 The doc comment is load-bearing, not decoration: every user rpc of a
 service_c2s service is auto-published as an MCP tool, and tacplus takes the
 leading comment as the tool description a model sees when deciding whether
 to call it. Same reason GetDocFileMetadata's comment is written the way it
 is.

 NAMED `CreateDocFileLink`, NOT `ShareDocument`. The rpc verb registry is
 closed and `Share` is not in it — generation fails outright with `verb
 "Share" ... is not in the closed verb registry; add it (fold test →
 registry) or rename` (verified 2026-09-27). `Create` is the right registered
 verb for the same reason blobstore's own RPC is `CreateLink`: the BlobLink
 row this mints IS durable resource state, which is precisely `Create`'s
 boundary against `Mint` ("a self-contained credential", which a
 server-stored link is not). `DocFile` matches this file's existing naming
 (DocFileMetadata, UpdateDocFileLocation).

 WHAT IT DOES: reads the caller's DocFileMetadata row, refuses unless the
 caller both owns it and is in its namespace, then calls
 blobstore.BlobStore/CreateLink with that row's blob_id and display_name.
 DocManager stores NOTHING about the link — see CreateDocFileLinkResponse for
 why the raw token is neither returned nor persisted, and
 looper/workers/share-document-rpc-2026-09-27-result.md for why no revoke or
 list surface is declared here yet.

rpcs.description:
UpdateDocFileLocation changes ONLY a row's customer_path — the
 service-surface half of Reveille's update_doc_location MCP tool, per
 decisions/service-agent-rpc-split-and-identity-2026-09-07.md's rule that
 "everything the agent does to organize files must go through a
 corresponding `service` RPC". The agent calls this over S2S; it never
 writes DocFileMetadata itself (its stratum grant on that record is
 read-only anyway — see reveille.proto's header).

 It is the ONLY mutation on this service. UpdateDocFileMetadata and
 DeleteDocFileMetadata were removed 2026-09-17 (Jody): the store is
 write-once — display names and paths are what a filing clerk may
 correct by re-filing, content is never overwritten and nothing is ever
 deleted (decisions/no-update-no-delete-2026-09-17.md). RPC_PRINCIPAL_SERVICE
 so a user cannot call it directly and a prompt-injected agent's blast
 radius is "the file is in the wrong folder", nothing more. See
 decisions/put-is-create-ingest-and-agent-move-rpc-2026-09-07.md.

 handshake per tool call.

Config
types.description:
Config for the event-bus service. Stored in kernel via grpc_config.
 At boot, eventbus connects to kernel to fetch this config, then merges
 with env vars (env takes precedence via PROTO_CONFIG_* env var mappings).

fields.name: node_role
fields.description: node_role determines the embedded Kafka (KRaft) process role.

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_COMBINED
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_COMBINED: runs both broker and controller in one process.
 Simplest deployment for small clusters (3-5 nodes).

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_BROKER
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_BROKER: data-only node. Stores partitions, serves producers
 and consumers. Scales horizontally.

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_CONTROLLER
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_CONTROLLER: metadata quorum only. Runs the KRaft consensus
 protocol for leader election and partition assignment.
 Deploy an odd number (3 or 5) for quorum.

fields.name: data_dir
fields.description: data_dir is the Kafka log/data directory.
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_DIR)

fields.name: default_retention_hours
fields.description: default_retention_hours for new topics. Default: 168 (7 days).

fields.name: default_partitions
fields.description: default_partitions for new topics. Default: 6.

fields.name: default_replication_factor
fields.description: default_replication_factor for new topics. Default: 3.

fields.name: controller_count
fields.description: controller_count is the expected number of Controller nodes. Default: 3.

fields.name: broker_count
fields.description: broker_count is the expected number of Broker nodes. Default: 1.

fields.name: broker_port
fields.description: broker_port is the Kafka broker listener port.

fields.name: controller_port
fields.description: controller_port is the KRaft controller listener port.

fields.name: node_id
fields.description: node_id is the unique KRaft node identifier for this instance.

fields.name: cluster_seed
fields.description: cluster_seed is a stable string used to deterministically derive the KRaft cluster UUID.

fields.name: state_refresh_interval_seconds
fields.description: state_refresh_interval_seconds controls how often this node re-registers in EventbusState.

fields.name: state
fields.description: state: Kafka consumer group state (Stable, Empty, Dead, etc.)

types.name: ResetConsumerGroupOffsetsRequest
SortField
SubscribeRequest
types.description:
SubscribeRequest is sent on the bidi stream to control replay.
 The first message establishes the session; subsequent messages adjust
 position, speed, pause state, or backpressure without closing the stream.

 Every field is applied as-is — the server replaces its current state
 with the full contents of each new SubscribeRequest. To change only
 the speed, the client re-sends the same seek + the new speed.

fields.name: consumer_group
fields.description:
Consumer group for offset tracking. Only read from the first message;
 ignored on subsequent resubscribes (consumer group is immutable per session).

fields.name: speed_multiplier
fields.description:
speed_multiplier controls replay pacing relative to original event timestamps.
 0 = max throughput (catch-up mode, no delay between events).
 1.0 = real-time (events delivered at the same rate they were produced).
 10.0 = 10x fast-forward.
 Can be changed mid-stream without seeking.

fields.name: pause
fields.description:
pause stops delivery without closing the stream or releasing the consumer.
 The server holds its position. Send pause=false (or a new seek) to resume.

fields.name: backpressure
fields.description: backpressure tells the server what to do when the client is slow.

enum_values.name: BACKPRESSURE_BUFFER
enum_values.description:
BACKPRESSURE_BUFFER: server buffers events until the client catches up.
 Default gRPC behaviour. Safe but risks unbounded memory if the client
 falls behind permanently.

enum_values.name: BACKPRESSURE_DROP_OLD
enum_values.description:
BACKPRESSURE_DROP_OLD: server skips ahead to the latest available offset,
 discarding events the client couldn't consume in time. The client sees
 a gap but never falls behind.

enum_values.name: BACKPRESSURE_SAMPLE
enum_values.description:
BACKPRESSURE_SAMPLE: server delivers every Nth event (N = sample_interval),
 dropping the rest. Useful for dashboards that need shape, not completeness.

fields.name: sample_interval
fields.description:
sample_interval: when backpressure=BACKPRESSURE_SAMPLE, deliver every
 Nth event and drop the rest. Ignored for other policies.

fields.name: partitions
fields.description:
partitions restricts consumption to specific partition IDs.
 Empty = subscribe to all partitions (default, uses consumer-group rebalancing).
 When set, uses manual assignment (no rebalancing).

fields.name: external_tls_mode
fields.description: external_tls_mode controls how the public-facing TLS certificate is provisioned.

enum_values.name: EXTERNAL_TLS_MODE_CERT_CHAIN
enum_values.description: CERT_CHAIN: use the cert and key supplied in external_cert_pem / external_key_pem.

enum_values.name: EXTERNAL_TLS_MODE_LETSENCRYPT
enum_values.description:
LETSENCRYPT: obtain and renew the certificate automatically via LetsEncrypt.
 Gateway subscribes RO to LetsEncryptState for the current cert.

fields.name: external_hostnames
fields.description:
external_hostnames lists the domain names gateway serves externally.
 Used for SNI-based cert selection at runtime. In LETSENCRYPT mode,
 letsencrypt.Config.hostnames must match this list.

fields.name: external_cert_pem
fields.description:
external_cert_pem is the PEM-encoded certificate chain for CERT_CHAIN mode.
 Ignored in LETSENCRYPT mode. Supplied via secrets overlay — never committed to VCS.

fields.name: external_key_pem
fields.description:
external_key_pem is the PEM-encoded private key for CERT_CHAIN mode.
 Ignored in LETSENCRYPT mode. Supplied via secrets overlay — never committed to VCS.

fields.name: root_ca
fields.description:
root_ca holds the root CA certificate(s) that clients should trust when
 connecting to the gateway's external HTTPS endpoint. Served via PublicCa
 so clients (schematicctl, webapp) can configure TLS trust automatically.
 Required in CERT_CHAIN mode. Omit in LETSENCRYPT mode (publicly trusted).

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.name: http_listener
fields.description:
http_listener is the PLAINTEXT listener behind the edge's port 80. The
 gateway owns port 80 as well as 443: one LoadBalancer carries both, so
 there is no second externally-exposed Service to reach the ACME responder
 with.

 On this listener the gateway does exactly three things:
   - GET/HEAD /.well-known/acme-challenge/* is proxied to acme_backend
   - any other GET/HEAD gets a 301 to the same path on https://
   - any other method gets a 405

 Empty disables the listener — nothing binds. It has no declared default
 because the answer depends on external_tls_mode, which tacplus cannot
 express as a conditional default: the operator sets it (to 0.0.0.0:8080,
 the container-side port the LoadBalancer's port 80 targets) exactly when
 external_tls_mode = LETSENCRYPT, and leaves it empty otherwise.

fields.name: acme_backend
fields.description:
acme_backend is the IN-CLUSTER address of the letsencrypt service's
 HTTP-01 responder — its own http_listener, reachable on the letsencrypt
 ClusterIP Service. The gateway is the only thing that reaches it; the
 responder is no longer exposed outside the cluster.

 Empty while http_listener is set means challenge requests are answered
 503: the redirect and 405 halves still work, but no certificate can be
 issued. Set together with http_listener.

http_listener is the PLAINTEXT listener behind the edge's port 80. The
 gateway owns port 80 as well as 443: one LoadBalancer carries both, so
 there is no second externally-exposed Service to reach the ACME responder
 with.

 On this listener the gateway does exactly three things:
   - GET/HEAD /.well-known/acme-challenge/* is proxied to acme_backend
   - any other GET/HEAD gets a 301 to the same path on https://
   - any other method gets a 405

 Empty disables the listener — nothing binds. It has no declared default
 because the answer depends on external_tls_mode, which tacplus cannot
 express as a conditional default: the operator sets it (to 0.0.0.0:8080,
 the container-side port the LoadBalancer's port 80 targets) exactly when
 external_tls_mode = LETSENCRYPT, and leaves it empty otherwise.

fields.name: acme_backend
fields.description:
acme_backend is the IN-CLUSTER address of the letsencrypt service's
 HTTP-01 responder — its own http_listener, reachable on the letsencrypt
 ClusterIP Service. The gateway is the only thing that reaches it; the
 responder is no longer exposed outside the cluster.

 Empty while http_listener is set means challenge requests are answered
 503: the redirect and 405 halves still work, but no certificate can be
 issued. Set together with http_listener.

types.name: BrokerPendingApprovalRequest
types.description:
BrokerPendingApprovalRequest is the generated requires_device check's call:
 the approval it was handed, the live request it is about to serve, the user it
 is serving, and the device signature that has to cover all of it.

fields.name: rpc_method
fields.description:
rpc_method and request_hash are the LIVE values, computed by the check from
 the request in front of it — never echoed back out of the record. Both must
 equal what was approved, and both are inside the challenge the device
 signed, so a same-shaped-but-different request fails twice over.

fields.name: caller_namespace
fields.description:
caller_namespace and caller_subject are the `namespace` and `sub` claims of
 the USER the calling service is serving, out of the token it has already
 verified. Kernel resolves them to a person and requires that to be the
 person the approval names, so one person's approval can never be spent on
 another person's call.

fields.name: device_assertion
fields.description:
device_assertion is the tap: a WebAuthn assertion whose challenge is the one
 CreatePendingApprovalResponse returned. Kernel verifies it against the
 STORED credential — an approving device must already be registered and
 linked, so no key travels in this request at all.

message.name: WebauthnAssertion
message.description:
WebauthnAssertion is one WebAuthn (passkey) assertion, exactly as the
 authenticator produced it — the four fields of an
 AuthenticatorAssertionResponse, unaltered.

 NOTHING HERE IS PARSED BY A BROKER AND BELIEVED. Kernel recomputes the signed
 bytes itself (authenticator_data || SHA-256(client_data_json)), reads the
 challenge out of client_data_json itself, and verifies signature against the
 credential's own public key itself. A broker that rewrote any of these four
 fields produces a proof that fails, which is what keeps "compromising the
 broker forges no identity" (personalauth.proto's header) true of this path
 too.

 NO ATTESTATION OBJECT, DELIBERATELY. This is the desktop-passkey arm of the
 identity decision doc's §3 — the one whose device proof is explicitly the
 weaker one, because Windows/Linux have no App Attest / Play Integrity. The
 public key therefore arrives as an ordinary jwk.Jwk (the platform's key type
 everywhere else, including CreatePersonalPrincipal) and is trusted only as
 far as the nonce binding makes it trustworthy: the IdP's id_token carries
 that key's RFC 7638 thumbprint as its `nonce`, so a substituted key has no
 matching login. App Attest and Play Integrity are named as follow-ons, not
 stubbed: both need live verification against Apple's and Google's own
 services, and a mocked verifier would be a device proof nobody could trust.

fields.name: credential_id
fields.description:
credential_id is the authenticator's credential id, base64url without
 padding. It becomes PersonalCredential.credential_id.

fields.name: authenticator_data
fields.description: authenticator_data is the raw authenticatorData the authenticator signed.

fields.name: client_data_json
fields.description:
client_data_json is the raw clientDataJSON the authenticator signed over
 the SHA-256 of. Kernel parses it for `type` and `challenge`; both are
 checked, and the challenge is what binds this assertion to one IdP login.

fields.name: signature
fields.description:
signature is the authenticator's signature over
 authenticator_data || SHA-256(client_data_json), in the encoding the key's
 algorithm defines (DER for ECDSA, raw for Ed25519, PKCS#1 v1.5 for RSA).

types.name: Cluster
types.description:
============================================================================
 Cluster State (cluster diagnostics, health, and metrics)
 ============================================================================

 Cluster is a state root that exposes cluster diagnostics and
 operational metrics. A background publisher in each node periodically
 computes metrics from JVM/Hazelcast APIs and writes them to the maps.
 Tacplus auto-generates Get/Set/Watch RPCs for each boundary.

 PATTERNS TO ADDRESS LATER:

 1. Filtered queries: GetMapEntries needs key_prefix filter and limit.
    The auto-generated collection Get doesn't support ad-hoc filtering.
    Needs a hand-wrapped RPC or a new tacplus pattern for parameterized
    queries on collections.

 2. Transient point-in-time queries: ListLocks returns a snapshot of
    lock state that changes too rapidly to publish to maps. Needs a
    hand-wrapped RPC. Same applies to thread deadlock detection —
    better as on-demand than periodic.

 3. Publisher latency vs event-driven updates: Watch fires when maps
    update, but the publisher writes on a fixed interval. For membership
    changes, consider event-driven publishing (MembershipListener
    triggers immediate cluster_info/cluster_health write) alongside
    periodic publishing for metrics.

constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_ANY)

fields.name: disable_caller
fields.description:
DisableCaller disables automatic inclusion of caller information (file:line) in log entries
 Default: false (caller information is included)

fields.name: disable_stacktrace
fields.description:
DisableStacktrace disables automatic stacktraces for error-level and above log entries
 Default: false (stacktraces are included for errors)

fields.name: initial_fields
disk_dir
fields.description:
disk_dir is kernel's one on-disk directory. It holds exactly two artifacts:
 the identity snapshot (KernelDiskState) and the FencedLock Raft log under
 <disk_dir>/fencedlock. Kernel does no other durability and holds no user
 data; durable data is stratum's.
 Default: "data/kernel".

fields.name: hazelcast_listener
fields.description: hazelcast_listener is the bind address for Hazelcast cluster communication. Default port 5001.

fields.name: tls
fields.description:
tls is the node's X.509 certificate and private key, used for
 gRPC server TLS and Hazelcast mTLS.

message.name: X509CertChain
message.description:
X509CertChain contains a certificate chain and optional private key.
 chain[0] is the leaf (end-entity) cert, followed by intermediates, ordered toward root.
 When key is present, the chain is a full credential suitable for TLS.

fields.name: chain
fields.description: chain[0] is the leaf (end-entity) cert, followed by intermediates, ordered toward root.

message.name: X509Cert
message.description:
ProtoCert represents an X.509 certificate.
 The certificate is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block.
 Use NewProtoCert() in Go with DER-encoded certificate bytes to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the certificate

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM certificate block

fields.name: key
fields.description: optional private key for the leaf cert; present when chain is a full credential.

message.name: Key
message.description: Key represents a private cryptographic key (alias for ProtoKey).

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the key (corresponds to kid in JWK)

fields.name: base64
fields.description: Base64 contains the base64url-encoded PEM private key block

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created
 Valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is an optional stable key for chain collections.

fields.name: cluster_ca
fields.description:
cluster_ca holds the cluster root CA certificate(s) for populating
 Ca.ca_certs on startup and for Hazelcast mTLS trust.
 These are the trust anchors for all cert chain validation in the cluster.

fields.name: signing_ca
fields.description:
signing_ca is the node's intermediate CA chain issued by schematic,
 used by X509Mint to sign service certificates. The chain is:
   node intermediate (pathlen:0) → cluster intermediate → root CA.
 The private key is included (for signing) but never leaves the node.

fields.name: trusted_cas
fields.description: trusted_cas lists the trusted CA certificates for TLS verification.

fields.name: rate_limit
fields.description: rate_limit configures rate limiting for unary read RPCs to detect polling.

message.name: RateLimitConfig
message.description:
RateLimitConfig configures rate limiting for unary read RPCs to detect polling.
 Two categories are tracked independently:
 - polling_rate: unary RPCs that have streaming alternatives (Watch/Subscribe)
 - unary_rate: unary read RPCs without streaming alternatives

fields.name: polling_rate
fields.description: Max req/s per peer per method for unary RPCs that have streaming alternatives.

fields.name: unary_rate
fields.description: Max req/s per peer per method for unary read RPCs without streaming alternatives.

fields.name: configs
fields.description:
configs holds per-service configurations. On each config load,
 each entry is written to the corresponding service config state boundary.

fields.name: health_poll_interval_seconds
fields.description: How often to refresh health state (seconds). Default 5.

fields.name: enable_http
fields.description: Enable HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2 listener (TCP). Default true.

fields.name: enable_http3
fields.description: Enable HTTP/3 listener (QUIC/UDP). Default true.

fields.name: enable_grpc
fields.description: Enable gRPC listener (TCP). Default true.

fields.name: tcp_listener
fields.description: TCP listener for HTTP/1.1, HTTP/2, and gRPC. Default port 8443.

fields.name: quic_listener
fields.description: QUIC/UDP listener for HTTP/3. Default port 8443.

fields.name: external_tls_mode
fields.description: external_tls_mode controls how the public-facing TLS certificate is provisioned.

enum_values.name: EXTERNAL_TLS_MODE_CERT_CHAIN
enum_values.description: CERT_CHAIN: use the cert and key supplied in external_cert_pem / external_key_pem.

enum_values.name: EXTERNAL_TLS_MODE_LETSENCRYPT
enum_values.description:
LETSENCRYPT: obtain and renew the certificate automatically via LetsEncrypt.
 Gateway subscribes RO to LetsEncryptState for the current cert.

fields.name: external_hostnames
fields.description:
external_hostnames lists the domain names gateway serves externally.
 Used for SNI-based cert selection at runtime. In LETSENCRYPT mode,
 letsencrypt.Config.hostnames must match this list.

fields.name: external_cert_pem
fields.description:
external_cert_pem is the PEM-encoded certificate chain for CERT_CHAIN mode.
 Ignored in LETSENCRYPT mode. Supplied via secrets overlay — never committed to VCS.

fields.name: external_key_pem
fields.description:
external_key_pem is the PEM-encoded private key for CERT_CHAIN mode.
 Ignored in LETSENCRYPT mode. Supplied via secrets overlay — never committed to VCS.

fields.name: root_ca
fields.description:
root_ca holds the root CA certificate(s) that clients should trust when
 connecting to the gateway's external HTTPS endpoint. Served via PublicCa
 so clients (schematicctl, webapp) can configure TLS trust automatically.
 Required in CERT_CHAIN mode. Omit in LETSENCRYPT mode (publicly trusted).

fields.name: http_listener
fields.description:
http_listener is the PLAINTEXT listener behind the edge's port 80. The
 gateway owns port 80 as well as 443: one LoadBalancer carries both, so
 there is no second externally-exposed Service to reach the ACME responder
 with.

 On this listener the gateway does exactly three things:
   - GET/HEAD /.well-known/acme-challenge/* is proxied to acme_backend
   - any other GET/HEAD gets a 301 to the same path on https://
   - any other method gets a 405

 Empty disables the listener — nothing binds. It has no declared default
 because the answer depends on external_tls_mode, which tacplus cannot
 express as a conditional default: the operator sets it (to 0.0.0.0:8080,
 the container-side port the LoadBalancer's port 80 targets) exactly when
 external_tls_mode = LETSENCRYPT, and leaves it empty otherwise.

fields.name: acme_backend
fields.description:
acme_backend is the IN-CLUSTER address of the letsencrypt service's
 HTTP-01 responder — its own http_listener, reachable on the letsencrypt
 ClusterIP Service. The gateway is the only thing that reaches it; the
 responder is no longer exposed outside the cluster.

 Empty while http_listener is set means challenge requests are answered
 503: the redirect and 405 halves still work, but no certificate can be
 issued. Set together with http_listener.

fields.name: lets_encrypt_email
fields.description:
lets_encrypt_email is the email address for Let's Encrypt account
 registration and certificate expiration notifications.
 If empty, letsencrypt will use "admin@<fqdn>".
 NOTES: needs email assertion

fields.name: http_listener
fields.description:
http_listener is the bind address for the HTTP server used for ACME HTTP-01
 challenge responses. IN-CLUSTER ONLY: the gateway owns the edge's port 80
 and proxies /.well-known/acme-challenge/* here, so this listener needs no
 externally-exposed Service of its own — only a ClusterIP the gateway can
 reach. Default port 80.

fields.name: renewal_check_interval_seconds
fields.description:
renewal_check_interval_seconds is how often to check if the certificate
 needs renewal (seconds). Default: 3600 (1 hour).

fields.name: hostnames
fields.description:
hostnames is the list of domain names to include as SANs on the
 Let's Encrypt certificate (e.g. ["api.schematic.io", "console.schematic.io"]).
 All hostnames must resolve to the gateway's external address, which is what
 answers on port 80 for HTTP-01 challenge validation.

message.name: Config
message.description:
Config for the event-bus service. Stored in kernel via grpc_config.
 At boot, eventbus connects to kernel to fetch this config, then merges
 with env vars (env takes precedence via PROTO_CONFIG_* env var mappings).

fields.name: node_role
fields.description: node_role determines the embedded Kafka (KRaft) process role.

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_COMBINED
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_COMBINED: runs both broker and controller in one process.
 Simplest deployment for small clusters (3-5 nodes).

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_BROKER
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_BROKER: data-only node. Stores partitions, serves producers
 and consumers. Scales horizontally.

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_CONTROLLER
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_CONTROLLER: metadata quorum only. Runs the KRaft consensus
 protocol for leader election and partition assignment.
 Deploy an odd number (3 or 5) for quorum.

fields.name: data_dir
fields.description: data_dir is the Kafka log/data directory.
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_DIR)

fields.name: default_retention_hours
fields.description: default_retention_hours for new topics. Default: 168 (7 days).

fields.name: default_partitions
fields.description: default_partitions for new topics. Default: 6.

fields.name: default_replication_factor
fields.description: default_replication_factor for new topics. Default: 3.

fields.name: controller_count
fields.description: controller_count is the expected number of Controller nodes. Default: 3.

fields.name: broker_count
fields.description: broker_count is the expected number of Broker nodes. Default: 1.

fields.name: broker_port
fields.description: broker_port is the Kafka broker listener port.

fields.name: controller_port
fields.description: controller_port is the KRaft controller listener port.

fields.name: node_id
fields.description: node_id is the unique KRaft node identifier for this instance.

fields.name: cluster_seed
fields.description: cluster_seed is a stable string used to deterministically derive the KRaft cluster UUID.

fields.name: state_refresh_interval_seconds
fields.description: state_refresh_interval_seconds controls how often this node re-registers in EventbusState.

fields.name: session_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
session_timeout_seconds is how long an unauthenticated bidi session
 waits for token delivery before timing out.
 Minimum: 30 seconds. Maximum: 600 (10 minutes). Default: 300 (5 minutes).

fields.name: refresh_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
refresh_token_lifetime_seconds is the lifetime for long-lived refresh
 tokens issued to CLI clients. Longer than browser sessions because
 laptops may be offline for extended periods.
 Minimum: 3600 (1 hour). Maximum: 2592000 (30 days). Default: 604800 (7 days).

fields.name: auto_refresh_before_seconds
fields.description:
auto_refresh_before_seconds is how far before token expiry the service
 proactively refreshes tokens for connected daemon clients.
 Minimum: 60 (1 minute). Maximum: 86400 (1 day). Default: 3600 (1 hour).

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables OAuth2 authentication.

fields.name: scopes
fields.description:
scopes are the default OAuth2 scopes requested from all providers.
 If empty, defaults to ["openid", "profile", "email"].

fields.name: providers
fields.description: providers is the list of OAuth2 identity provider configurations.

message.name: ProviderConfig
message.description: ProviderConfig configures a single OAuth2 identity provider.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this provider.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is a human-friendly label (e.g. "Google", "Okta", "Microsoft").

fields.name: domains
fields.description:
domains maps email domains to this provider. When a user's email domain
 matches, they are routed to this IDP automatically. Each entry is a DNS
 hostname, bounded to 253 bytes by RFC 1035/1123.

fields.name: issuer
fields.description:
issuer is the OpenID Connect issuer URL.
 Used for .well-known/openid-configuration auto-discovery.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the OAuth2 client identifier.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the OAuth2 client secret.

fields.name: authorization_endpoint
fields.description: authorization_endpoint overrides the auto-discovered authorization URL.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: token_endpoint
fields.description: token_endpoint overrides the auto-discovered token URL.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: end_session_endpoint
fields.description: end_session_endpoint overrides the auto-discovered logout URL.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: scopes
fields.description: scopes overrides the default scopes for this provider.

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description:
ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate to trust for this provider.
 Used for providers with self-signed or private CA certificates (e.g. mock IDPs).
 If empty, the system default CA bundle is used.

fields.name: allowed_redirect_uri_prefixes
fields.description:
allowed_redirect_uri_prefixes is the operator-configured allowlist of
 callback URLs this provider may redirect a user back to. AuthorizeRequest
 .callback_url is caller-supplied and unauthenticated; without this list it
 would be handed to the IDP as redirect_uri verbatim, letting anyone start a
 login that delivers the authorization code to a host they control.

 Matching rule (deliberately strict, no wildcards, no URL parsing):
   - An entry that does NOT end in "/" matches only a byte-identical
     callback_url.
   - An entry that DOES end in "/" additionally matches any callback_url
     that begins with it. The trailing slash is what makes the prefix end on
     a path boundary, so "https://legit.example.com/app/" cannot be
     satisfied by "https://legit.example.com/app-evil/..." and
     "https://legit.example.com/app" cannot be satisfied by
     "https://legit.example.comX/".

 Comparison is exact and case-sensitive. There is no implicit default: a
 provider with an empty list authorizes nothing, so the service fails closed
 if the field is ever missing at runtime.

fields.name: nonce_expire_seconds
fields.description:
nonce_expire_seconds is how long OAuth2 nonces/state remain valid.
 Nonces prevent replay attacks in the authorization code flow.
 Minimum: 1 second. Maximum: 86400 (24 hours). Default: 300 (5 minutes).

fields.name: jwk_refetch_interval_seconds
fields.description:
jwk_refetch_interval_seconds is the minimum interval between JWKS fetches
 from the same external IDP. Prevents excessive outbound requests.
 Default: 300 (5 minutes).

fields.name: entitlements_policy
fields.description:
entitlements_policy is the OPA bundle for entitlement evaluation.
 Loaded from services/opa/ by schematic, delivered to opa via config push.

message.name: OpaPolicy
message.description:
OpaPolicy defines an OPA policy bundle for authorization evaluation.
 The bundle is a filesystem.Directory tree containing .rego policy files.

fields.name: entry_point
fields.description: entry_point specifies the main package/decision point for policy evaluation.

fields.name: bundle
fields.description: bundle is the directory tree containing .rego policy files.

message.name: Directory
message.description:
Directory represents a directory node in a filesystem tree.
 Directories are recursive — each may contain child directories and files.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the directory name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this directory

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: directories
fields.description: directories holds zero or more child directories

fields.name: files
fields.description: files holds zero or more files in this directory

message.name: File
message.description: File represents a single file with permissions and content.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the file name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this file

fields.name: content
fields.description: content is the raw file content (max 10 MB)

fields.name: created
fields.description: created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the policy was created.

fields.name: version
fields.description: version is an optional version string for this policy (e.g., "1.0.0").
constraints: must be a valid semantic version

fields.name: proxy_policy
fields.description:
proxy_policy is the OPA bundle for proxy request policy evaluation.
 The policy receives caller claims and opaque routing metadata, returns
 an allow/deny decision plus the resolved destination URL.

fields.name: tenant_entitlements_policies
fields.description:
tenant_entitlements_policies holds one entitlements policy per project
 namespace (full path, e.g. "/tenants/drpepper"). Kernel reconciles each
 tenant_config's OpaTenantConfig into this list; EvalEntitlement dispatches
 on the caller's namespace, falling back to entitlements_policy (cluster
 root) when absent. (repeated-entry, not map<> — map<> round-trips badly
 through tacplus codegen; matches the repeated-entry convention elsewhere.)

message.name: NamespaceEntitlementsPolicy
message.description:
NamespaceEntitlementsPolicy binds a project namespace to its entitlements
 policy bundle — a repeated (map-like) entry used in opa Config/OpaState.

fields.name: hazelcast_memory_mb
fields.description: hazelcast_memory_mb is the Hazelcast cluster memory limit in MB. Default: 2048.

fields.name: map_idle_ttl_seconds
fields.description: map_idle_ttl_seconds evicts idle working-set maps. Default: 7200 (2h).

fields.name: max_maps
fields.description: max_maps limits concurrent working-set maps. Default: 20.

fields.name: retention_days
fields.description: retention_days is the number of days to retain hot events. Default: 90.

fields.name: cleanup_interval_seconds
fields.description: cleanup_interval_seconds is how often the retention cleanup job runs. Default: 3600.

fields.name: active_session_idle_seconds
fields.description:
active_session_idle_seconds is the idle threshold for ListActiveSessions.
 A session is considered active if its last event was within this window.
 Default: 900 (15 min). Min: 30.

fields.name: warm_window_seconds
fields.description:
warm_window_seconds is the memory-residency window for warm-tiered records:
 rows younger than this are served from memory, rows older than it are served
 from the on-disk warm tier. It is the default applied to a record type that
 declares the warm residency preset without a window_seconds of its own.

 It must be SHORTER than retention_days or the disk tier is never reached:
 retention deletes a row before it is ever old enough to age out of memory,
 and the "still queryable, only slower" promise the disk tier exists to keep
 never applies to anything. Default: 604800 (7 days), which leaves rows aged
 7-90 days served from disk under the 90-day retention default. Min: 60.

message.name: Config
message.description:
OperatorConfig is the top-level operator configuration.

 Lifecycle:
   1. operator init ca                   — generate root CA → crypto.yaml
   2. operator init cluster --ca <path>  — generate cluster PKI + write operator.yaml
   3. operator                           — run (IN_CLUSTER) or generate charts (GENERATE_ONLY)

 When deployed to Kubernetes:
   operator.yaml  → ConfigMap  (schematic-operator-config)
   crypto.yaml    → Secret     (schematic-operator-crypto)
 Both are mounted and merged by the operator at startup.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: How the operator runs.

enum_values.name: IN_CLUSTER
enum_values.description:
IN_CLUSTER is the default: the operator runs inside Kubernetes and
 continuously reconciles the desired cluster state by managing Helm releases.
 gateway_nodes is automatically set to the number of schedulable nodes.

enum_values.name: GENERATE_ONLY
enum_values.description:
GENERATE_ONLY: one-shot CLI mode. Generates Helm charts, writes them to
 output_dir, and exits. Does not communicate with the Kubernetes API.

fields.name: fqdn
fields.description: Public FQDN for the cluster (e.g. "api.example.com").

fields.name: port
fields.description: HTTPS gateway port. Default 443 for production; 8443 for local testing.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description: Kubernetes namespace to deploy all schematic services into.

fields.name: topology
fields.description: Service replica topology.

message.name: Topology
message.description:
Topology declares the desired replica count for each service.

 gateway_nodes is special: when set to 0 and mode = IN_CLUSTER, the operator
 automatically sets it to the number of schedulable Kubernetes nodes at each
 reconciliation cycle (one gateway per node). When mode = GENERATE_ONLY,
 gateway_nodes must be set explicitly.

fields.name: gateway_nodes
fields.description:
Set to 0 to auto-derive from schedulable node count (IN_CLUSTER only).
 When enabled proxy services (anthropic, openai, gitlab, github) also
 scale to one replica per gateway node.

fields.name: oauth_nodes
