 reach. Default port 80.

fields.name: renewal_check_interval_seconds
fields.description:
renewal_check_interval_seconds is how often to check if the certificate
 needs renewal (seconds). Default: 3600 (1 hour).

fields.name: hostnames
fields.description:
hostnames is the list of domain names to include as SANs on the
 Let's Encrypt certificate (e.g. ["api.schematic.io", "console.schematic.io"]).
 All hostnames must resolve to the gateway's external address, which is what
 answers on port 80 for HTTP-01 challenge validation.

message.name: Config
message.description:
Config for the event-bus service. Stored in kernel via grpc_config.
 At boot, eventbus connects to kernel to fetch this config, then merges
 with env vars (env takes precedence via PROTO_CONFIG_* env var mappings).

fields.name: node_role
fields.description: node_role determines the embedded Kafka (KRaft) process role.

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_COMBINED
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_COMBINED: runs both broker and controller in one process.
 Simplest deployment for small clusters (3-5 nodes).

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_BROKER
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_BROKER: data-only node. Stores partitions, serves producers
 and consumers. Scales horizontally.

enum_values.name: KAFKA_ROLE_CONTROLLER
enum_values.description:
KAFKA_ROLE_CONTROLLER: metadata quorum only. Runs the KRaft consensus
 protocol for leader election and partition assignment.
 Deploy an odd number (3 or 5) for quorum.

fields.name: data_dir
fields.description: data_dir is the Kafka log/data directory.
constraints: must be a valid file path (type: PATH_DIR)

fields.name: default_retention_hours
fields.description: default_retention_hours for new topics. Default: 168 (7 days).

fields.name: default_partitions
fields.description: default_partitions for new topics. Default: 6.

fields.name: default_replication_factor
fields.description: default_replication_factor for new topics. Default: 3.

fields.name: controller_count
fields.description: controller_count is the expected number of Controller nodes. Default: 3.

fields.name: broker_count
fields.description: broker_count is the expected number of Broker nodes. Default: 1.

fields.name: broker_port
fields.description: broker_port is the Kafka broker listener port.

fields.name: controller_port
fields.description: controller_port is the KRaft controller listener port.

fields.name: node_id
fields.description: node_id is the unique KRaft node identifier for this instance.

fields.name: cluster_seed
fields.description: cluster_seed is a stable string used to deterministically derive the KRaft cluster UUID.

fields.name: state_refresh_interval_seconds
fields.description: state_refresh_interval_seconds controls how often this node re-registers in EventbusState.

fields.name: session_timeout_seconds
fields.description:
session_timeout_seconds is how long an unauthenticated bidi session
 waits for token delivery before timing out.
 Minimum: 30 seconds. Maximum: 600 (10 minutes). Default: 300 (5 minutes).

fields.name: refresh_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
refresh_token_lifetime_seconds is the lifetime for long-lived refresh
 tokens issued to CLI clients. Longer than browser sessions because
 laptops may be offline for extended periods.
 Minimum: 3600 (1 hour). Maximum: 2592000 (30 days). Default: 604800 (7 days).

fields.name: auto_refresh_before_seconds
fields.description:
auto_refresh_before_seconds is how far before token expiry the service
 proactively refreshes tokens for connected daemon clients.
 Minimum: 60 (1 minute). Maximum: 86400 (1 day). Default: 3600 (1 hour).

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables OAuth2 authentication.

fields.name: scopes
fields.description:
scopes are the default OAuth2 scopes requested from all providers.
 If empty, defaults to ["openid", "profile", "email"].

fields.name: providers
fields.description: providers is the list of OAuth2 identity provider configurations.

message.name: ProviderConfig
message.description: ProviderConfig configures a single OAuth2 identity provider.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this provider.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is a human-friendly label (e.g. "Google", "Okta", "Microsoft").

fields.name: domains
fields.description:
domains maps email domains to this provider. When a user's email domain
 matches, they are routed to this IDP automatically. Each entry is a DNS
 hostname, bounded to 253 bytes by RFC 1035/1123.

fields.name: issuer
fields.description:
issuer is the OpenID Connect issuer URL.
 Used for .well-known/openid-configuration auto-discovery.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the OAuth2 client identifier.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the OAuth2 client secret.

fields.name: authorization_endpoint
fields.description: authorization_endpoint overrides the auto-discovered authorization URL.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: token_endpoint
fields.description: token_endpoint overrides the auto-discovered token URL.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: end_session_endpoint
fields.description: end_session_endpoint overrides the auto-discovered logout URL.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: scopes
fields.description: scopes overrides the default scopes for this provider.

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description:
ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate to trust for this provider.
 Used for providers with self-signed or private CA certificates (e.g. mock IDPs).
 If empty, the system default CA bundle is used.

fields.name: allowed_redirect_uri_prefixes
fields.description:
allowed_redirect_uri_prefixes is the operator-configured allowlist of
 callback URLs this provider may redirect a user back to. AuthorizeRequest
 .callback_url is caller-supplied and unauthenticated; without this list it
 would be handed to the IDP as redirect_uri verbatim, letting anyone start a
 login that delivers the authorization code to a host they control.

 Matching rule (deliberately strict, no wildcards, no URL parsing):
   - An entry that does NOT end in "/" matches only a byte-identical
     callback_url.
   - An entry that DOES end in "/" additionally matches any callback_url
     that begins with it. The trailing slash is what makes the prefix end on
     a path boundary, so "https://legit.example.com/app/" cannot be
     satisfied by "https://legit.example.com/app-evil/..." and
     "https://legit.example.com/app" cannot be satisfied by
     "https://legit.example.comX/".

 Comparison is exact and case-sensitive. There is no implicit default: a
 provider with an empty list authorizes nothing, so the service fails closed
 if the field is ever missing at runtime.

fields.name: nonce_expire_seconds
fields.description:
nonce_expire_seconds is how long OAuth2 nonces/state remain valid.
 Nonces prevent replay attacks in the authorization code flow.
 Minimum: 1 second. Maximum: 86400 (24 hours). Default: 300 (5 minutes).

fields.name: jwk_refetch_interval_seconds
fields.description:
jwk_refetch_interval_seconds is the minimum interval between JWKS fetches
 from the same external IDP. Prevents excessive outbound requests.
 Default: 300 (5 minutes).

fields.name: entitlements_policy
fields.description:
entitlements_policy is the OPA bundle for entitlement evaluation.
 Loaded from services/opa/ by schematic, delivered to opa via config push.

message.name: OpaPolicy
message.description:
OpaPolicy defines an OPA policy bundle for authorization evaluation.
 The bundle is a filesystem.Directory tree containing .rego policy files.

fields.name: entry_point
fields.description: entry_point specifies the main package/decision point for policy evaluation.

fields.name: bundle
fields.description: bundle is the directory tree containing .rego policy files.

message.name: Directory
message.description:
Directory represents a directory node in a filesystem tree.
 Directories are recursive — each may contain child directories and files.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the directory name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this directory

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: directories
fields.description: directories holds zero or more child directories

fields.name: files
fields.description: files holds zero or more files in this directory

message.name: File
message.description: File represents a single file with permissions and content.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the file name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this file

fields.name: content
fields.description: content is the raw file content (max 10 MB)

fields.name: created
fields.description: created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the policy was created.

fields.name: version
fields.description: version is an optional version string for this policy (e.g., "1.0.0").
constraints: must be a valid semantic version

fields.name: proxy_policy
fields.description:
proxy_policy is the OPA bundle for proxy request policy evaluation.
 The policy receives caller claims and opaque routing metadata, returns
 an allow/deny decision plus the resolved destination URL.

fields.name: tenant_entitlements_policies
fields.description:
tenant_entitlements_policies holds one entitlements policy per project
 namespace (full path, e.g. "/tenants/drpepper"). Kernel reconciles each
 tenant_config's OpaTenantConfig into this list; EvalEntitlement dispatches
 on the caller's namespace, falling back to entitlements_policy (cluster
 root) when absent. (repeated-entry, not map<> — map<> round-trips badly
 through tacplus codegen; matches the repeated-entry convention elsewhere.)

message.name: NamespaceEntitlementsPolicy
message.description:
NamespaceEntitlementsPolicy binds a project namespace to its entitlements
 policy bundle — a repeated (map-like) entry used in opa Config/OpaState.

fields.name: hazelcast_memory_mb
fields.description: hazelcast_memory_mb is the Hazelcast cluster memory limit in MB. Default: 2048.

fields.name: map_idle_ttl_seconds
fields.description: map_idle_ttl_seconds evicts idle working-set maps. Default: 7200 (2h).

fields.name: max_maps
fields.description: max_maps limits concurrent working-set maps. Default: 20.

fields.name: retention_days
fields.description: retention_days is the number of days to retain hot events. Default: 90.

fields.name: cleanup_interval_seconds
fields.description: cleanup_interval_seconds is how often the retention cleanup job runs. Default: 3600.

fields.name: active_session_idle_seconds
fields.description:
active_session_idle_seconds is the idle threshold for ListActiveSessions.
 A session is considered active if its last event was within this window.
 Default: 900 (15 min). Min: 30.

fields.name: warm_window_seconds
fields.description:
warm_window_seconds is the memory-residency window for warm-tiered records:
 rows younger than this are served from memory, rows older than it are served
 from the on-disk warm tier. It is the default applied to a record type that
 declares the warm residency preset without a window_seconds of its own.

 It must be SHORTER than retention_days or the disk tier is never reached:
 retention deletes a row before it is ever old enough to age out of memory,
 and the "still queryable, only slower" promise the disk tier exists to keep
 never applies to anything. Default: 604800 (7 days), which leaves rows aged
 7-90 days served from disk under the 90-day retention default. Min: 60.

message.name: Config
message.description:
OperatorConfig is the top-level operator configuration.

 Lifecycle:
   1. operator init ca                   — generate root CA → crypto.yaml
   2. operator init cluster --ca <path>  — generate cluster PKI + write operator.yaml
   3. operator                           — run (IN_CLUSTER) or generate charts (GENERATE_ONLY)

 When deployed to Kubernetes:
   operator.yaml  → ConfigMap  (schematic-operator-config)
   crypto.yaml    → Secret     (schematic-operator-crypto)
 Both are mounted and merged by the operator at startup.

fields.name: mode
fields.description: How the operator runs.

enum_values.name: IN_CLUSTER
enum_values.description:
IN_CLUSTER is the default: the operator runs inside Kubernetes and
 continuously reconciles the desired cluster state by managing Helm releases.
 gateway_nodes is automatically set to the number of schedulable nodes.

enum_values.name: GENERATE_ONLY
enum_values.description:
GENERATE_ONLY: one-shot CLI mode. Generates Helm charts, writes them to
 output_dir, and exits. Does not communicate with the Kubernetes API.

fields.name: fqdn
fields.description: Public FQDN for the cluster (e.g. "api.example.com").

fields.name: port
fields.description: HTTPS gateway port. Default 443 for production; 8443 for local testing.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description: Kubernetes namespace to deploy all schematic services into.

fields.name: topology
fields.description: Service replica topology.

message.name: Topology
message.description:
Topology declares the desired replica count for each service.

 gateway_nodes is special: when set to 0 and mode = IN_CLUSTER, the operator
 automatically sets it to the number of schedulable Kubernetes nodes at each
 reconciliation cycle (one gateway per node). When mode = GENERATE_ONLY,
 gateway_nodes must be set explicitly.

fields.name: gateway_nodes
fields.description:
Set to 0 to auto-derive from schedulable node count (IN_CLUSTER only).
 When enabled proxy services (anthropic, openai, gitlab, github) also
 scale to one replica per gateway node.

fields.name: oauth_nodes
fields.description: oauth_nodes is used when optional_services.oauth = true (default).

fields.name: stratum_nodes
fields.description:
stratum_nodes is the number of WRITER members: the StatefulSet with volumes.
 A writer holds partitions like any member AND persists every write — its redo
 log, its record index, its share of the daily checkpoint — so this is the
 count that decides durability. It is counted for min_durable_copies and for
 the hot-restore barrier, and it is meant to be fairly static (2 or 3).

fields.name: stratum_search_nodes
fields.description:
stratum_search_nodes is the number of SEARCH members: a second, volume-less
 workload joining the same Hazelcast cluster with the member attribute
 stratum.role=search.

 A search member holds partitions (primaries and backups) and answers the
 parallel scatter-gather a predicate query is, and does nothing else: no
 volume, no redo log, no record index, no checkpoint. It is never a durable
 copy and never a restore contributor, so a search member that leaves loses
 nothing durable and scaling this number up or down changes query throughput
 and nothing about durability.

 Defaults to 0: query throughput is a thing a deployment asks for. Raising
 this is NOT a way to raise durability — min_durable_copies counts writers
 (stratum_nodes) only, and a cluster with fewer writers than the floor refuses
 writes however many search members are running.

fields.name: kmaker_nodes
fields.description:
kmaker_nodes is the number of bootstrap certificate authority replicas.
 Kernel instances contact kmaker with Kubernetes projected service account
 tokens to obtain kernel certificates before kernel itself is available.

fields.name: echo_nodes
fields.description:
echo_nodes is used when optional_services.echo = true.
 Defaults to 1 rather than 3: the sample service is stateless and exists to
 be poked at, so a second replica proves nothing and costs a pod.

fields.name: messaging_nodes
fields.description:
messaging_nodes is used when optional_services.messaging = true.
 Defaults to 1: the service is stateless mediation over eventbus, so a
 second replica buys availability, not throughput, and a cluster that wants
 it says so.

fields.name: mailbox_nodes
fields.description:
mailbox_nodes is used when optional_services.mailbox = true.
 Defaults to 1 for the same reason as messaging_nodes.

fields.name: personalauth_nodes
fields.description:
personalauth_nodes is used when optional_services.personalauth = true.
 Defaults to 3, not 1: this is the login path for PERSONAL principals, so a
 single replica makes every device registration and every device login
 unavailable for the length of a rollout. Same reasoning, and the same
 count, as oauth_nodes.

fields.name: blobstore_nodes
fields.description:
blobstore_nodes is used when optional_services.blobstore = true.

 DEFAULTS TO 2, AND 2 IS THE ONLY SUPPORTED VALUE. blobstore is a mirrored
 PAIR: an upload is acked only when both pods have the bytes fsynced, and each
 pod streams to exactly one peer (blob-store-2026-09-25.md R2). The service
 refuses to start if the peer list it is given does not reduce to one peer, so a
 1 or a 3 here is a cluster that will not come up rather than a cluster that
 quietly degrades. It is a field rather than a constant only so that the
 rendering path is uniform with every other service's.

fields.name: app_services
fields.description:
app_services declares replica counts for services that are NOT part of the
 platform: an application's own services, defined in the application's proto
 repo and merged into the build.

 Every field above is a PLATFORM service with a fixed field number. That is
 fine for the platform, whose service set is what "the platform" means — but
 it made the platform unable to host anything else. An application could not
 declare a service without editing this file, and proto3 gives no way to add
 a field to a message from another repo, so "schematic is reusable" was not
 true: echo, a sample service, had to take field 17 here to be deployable.

 Keyed by service name, so an app adds a service by naming it in its own
 config and this file never changes. Presence with a count > 0 IS the
 enablement — an app service needs no parallel optional_services flag.

fields.name: tls
fields.description:
TLS configuration — letsencrypt or custom CA.
 Validation: if tls.letsencrypt = false, tls.ca must be set.

message.name: TLSConfig
message.description:
TLSConfig controls how edge-facing TLS certificates are obtained.
 When letsencrypt = true, the operator deploys one letsencrypt service replica.

fields.name: letsencrypt
fields.description:
When true, Let's Encrypt is used for edge TLS and one letsencrypt service
 replica is deployed. The gateway must be reachable on port 443 from the
 public internet.
 When false, ca must be populated with a valid CA chain.

fields.name: ca
fields.description:
Custom CA chain for edge TLS certificates.
 Required when letsencrypt = false. Ignored when letsencrypt = true.

fields.name: email
fields.description:
email is the ACME account registration address, rendered into the
 letsencrypt service's config as lets_encrypt_email. Let's Encrypt sends
 certificate expiry notices there. Empty leaves the letsencrypt service on
 its own "admin@<fqdn>" default. Ignored when letsencrypt = false.

fields.name: pki
fields.description: PKI material. Loaded from crypto.yaml and merged at runtime.

message.name: PKI
message.description:
PKI holds all PKI material for the cluster.

 root_ca is generated once per organization via 'operator init ca'.
 All other fields are generated per-cluster via 'operator init cluster'.
 PKI material lives in crypto.yaml and is merged into OperatorConfig at
 load time. The crypto.yaml file must be kept secret.

fields.name: root_ca
fields.description: Shared root CA across all clusters (cert + private key).

fields.name: cluster_ca
fields.description: Cluster intermediate CA, signed by root_ca.

fields.name: node_tls
fields.description: Per-node TLS server certificates (one per kernel/sentinel replica).

fields.name: node_signing_ca
fields.description: Per-node signing CAs for token issuance (one per kernel replica).

fields.name: edge_tls
fields.description:
Edge TLS certificates for gateway and oauth.
 Not used when tls.letsencrypt = true.

fields.name: edge_signing_ca
fields.description: Edge signing CAs.

fields.name: kmaker_signing_ca
fields.description:
Kmaker signing CA, signed by cluster_ca and constrained to issue only
 kernel bootstrap leaf certificates.

fields.name: optional_services
fields.description: Optional add-on services.

message.name: OptionalServices
message.description: OptionalServices controls which optional services are enabled.

fields.name: oauth
fields.description:
OAuth2/OIDC broker — oauth_nodes replicas when enabled.
 Enabled by default.

fields.name: keycloak
fields.description:
Keycloak IDP — production identity provider.
 Replaces mockidp. Enabled by default.

fields.name: echo
fields.description:
Echo sample service — echo_nodes replicas when enabled.
 Disabled by default: it is a diagnostic/reference service, not something a
 production cluster should carry.

fields.name: messaging
fields.description:
Messaging — the platform's message primitive (messaging.proto).
 messaging_nodes replicas when enabled. Disabled by default: it is a
 primitive an application opts into, not something every cluster carries.

fields.name: mailbox
fields.description:
Mailbox — pull delivery and eviction eligibility over messaging's
 deliveries (mailbox.proto). mailbox_nodes replicas when enabled.
 Disabled by default; requires messaging.

fields.name: personalauth
fields.description:
personalauth — the login broker for PERSONAL principals (personalauth.proto).
 Today one arm: DEVICE, a device-held key registering and logging itself in.
 personalauth_nodes replicas when enabled. Disabled by default: a cluster
 whose people all arrive through a tenant IdP has no use for it.

fields.name: blobstore
fields.description:
blobstore — the platform's binary blob primitive (blobstore.proto): a
 two-pod mirror of content-addressed files, with its metadata in stratum
 records. blobstore_nodes replicas when enabled, which is 2.

 Disabled by default, and enabling it costs two PersistentVolumeClaims, so a
 cluster whose services declare no volume groups should leave it off — with no
 group declared it would accept no upload anyway ("no group, no upload").

fields.name: harness
fields.description:
harness — the runtime test harness (D27, clients/harness.proto). Not a
 service: a suspended CronJob template "harness" running the gate profile,
 which the pipeline starts with `kubectl create job --from=cronjob/harness`.
 Its ServiceAccount has no kernel delegate and its pod mounts no token, so
 it reaches the fleet only through public doors. Disabled by default.

fields.name: harness_destructive
fields.description:
harness_destructive adds the second template, "harness-destructive", which
 runs the destructive profile (pod kill, PVC wipe) under a Role that may
 delete only the named blobstore and kernel pods and blobstore PVCs. Dev
 only: never enable it on pilot. Has no effect unless harness is enabled.

fields.name: output_dir
fields.description:
Filesystem path where generated Helm charts are written.
 Only used in GENERATE_ONLY mode. Default: "charts".

fields.name: web_root
fields.description:
Filesystem path to the web UI build, mounted read-only into gateway.
 Leave empty to use the gateway's embedded webapp.

fields.name: patch
fields.description:
patch is the service image patch number to deploy.
 When 0 (default), the operator auto-tracks the latest patch and polls the
 registry for upgrades (every hour for stable, every 60s for dev builds).
 When set, the operator pins to that exact patch and does no polling.

fields.name: dev
fields.description:
dev selects dev builds when true, stable builds when false (default).
 Affects both the image tag suffix and the polling interval.

fields.name: gitlab_registry_token
fields.description:
gitlab_registry_token is an OAuth2 personal access token (read_registry scope)
 used to pull images from registry.gitlab.com. When set, the operator creates a
 "gitlab-registry" docker-registry Secret in the schematic namespace as part of
 the generated Helm chart. Keep this out of version control — store in crypto.yaml.

fields.name: spiffe_prefix
fields.description:
SPIFFE trust domain for identity URIs: the URI authority, so it must not
 contain '/'. Workload identities are formed as
 `spiffe://${spiffe_prefix}/system/services/${service_name}` — this powers
 token subject claims, mTLS URI SANs, and (post-B-end-state) SPIFFE-aware
 client cert verification. Operator propagates this value to kernel's
 bootstrap AND to every service configmap so all components agree on the
 trust domain at boot, without a runtime SCS round-trip. Must equal
 kernel.Config.spiffe_trust_domain.

fields.name: root_cred_pairs
fields.description:
root_cred_pairs are the bootstrap admin credentials, loaded from
 operator.yaml. The operator renders them into kernel's Helm-deployed config
 (kernel.Config.root_cred_pairs); kernel installs them into the root
 namespace's TenantConfig so they can provision tenants via TenantAdmin.
 Ordinary C2S CredPairs at the root namespace; only public halves are carried.

message.name: CredPair
message.description:
CredPair is a tenant-scoped credential. Public key stored in the tenant's
 KernelTenantConfig slice; private key never leaves the holder. Used to
 authenticate kernel.TenantAdmin RPCs and (downstream) any tenant-scoped
 RPC across the cluster.

 A request authenticated by CredPair carries the SPIFFE URI
 `spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/<tenant_name>/users/cred-pair:<id>`.

 `entitlements` must always be a subset of the tenant's ceiling
 (kernel.Constraints.entitlements_ceiling). Enforcement is in
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig.

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is a unique identifier for this cred_pair within its owning tenant.

fields.name: tenant_name
fields.description:
tenant_name names the owning tenant — the namespace that `namespaces` are
 relative to. The cluster cred_pair's owner is the root "/".

fields.name: public_key
fields.description:
public_key is the cred_pair's public key, as a JWK. Mint verifies a
 cred_pair-signed proof against it to issue a token.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: entitlements
fields.description:
entitlements this cred_pair holds (⊆ the owning tenant's ceiling), as the
 SAME TokenEntitlements the C2S authorizer checks: the minted cred_pair token
 sets service_entitlements = this directly (uniform with IDP-user tokens).

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: principal_scope
fields.description:
principal_scope is how wide the caller's authority over PRINCIPALS is, as a
 spec.PrincipalScope enum VALUE NAME (e.g. "PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_ANY"). It is the
 claim the generated (spec.owner_default) guard reads to tell an owner acting
 on its own row from a principal whose authority is wider than itself.
 Absent, empty, PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED and PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_SELF_ONLY all
 mean self-scoped: the guard fails closed, so a policy that stamps nothing
 leaves every caller exactly as narrow as it is today.
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity
 property, never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: namespaces
fields.description:
namespaces are the authorized namespaces, RELATIVE to the owning tenant
 (e.g. "default", "prod", or "*" for all of the tenant's projects). The
 cred_pair can only act at-or-below these and literally cannot name another
 tenant. The cluster cred_pair is relative to "/", so it can span tenants.

fields.name: description
fields.description: description is a human-readable label.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: created_at is when this credential was created.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.description: expires_at is the optional expiry. Zero value means no expiry.

fields.name: cluster_oauth
fields.description:
cluster_oauth holds shared (cluster-level) IDP providers — Google, GitHub, etc.
 Configured once by a cluster admin. Delivered to the oauth service for
 initial token validation; tenant routing happens via ClaimMatcher entries
 in each tenant's OAuthTenantConfig.

message.name: ClusterOAuthConfig
message.description:
ClusterOAuthConfig holds cluster-level shared IDP configuration.
 Configured once by a cluster admin; shared across all tenants.
 Delivered to the oauth service alongside per-tenant OAuthTenantConfig slices.

message.name: ClusterOAuthProvider
message.description:
ClusterOAuthProvider describes a shared IDP (e.g. Google, GitHub) available
 to all tenants. Tenants route users from these IDPs via ClaimMatcher entries.

fields.name: issuer_url
fields.description: issuer_url is the OpenID Connect issuer (e.g. "https://accounts.google.com").
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the shared OAuth app client identifier.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the sensitive OAuth app secret; supplied by cluster admin.

fields.name: allowed_scopes
fields.description: allowed_scopes are the OAuth2 scopes requested from this IDP.

fields.name: jwks_uri
fields.description: jwks_uri overrides the auto-discovered JWKS endpoint.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description: ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate for self-signed IDPs.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this cluster IDP.

fields.name: kmaker
fields.description:
kmaker owns cluster bootstrap certificate signing for kernel. Operator
 renders this into kmaker's mounted runtime config and owns the Secret that
 carries kmaker.Config.signing_ca.

message.name: Config
message.description: Config is rendered by operator and mounted into kmaker at startup.

fields.name: cluster_name
fields.description: cluster_name is the logical Schematic cluster this kmaker signs for.

fields.name: listener
fields.description: listener is the gRPC bind address for kmaker.

fields.name: logger
fields.description: logger configures kmaker process logging.

fields.name: cluster_ca
fields.description: cluster_ca holds trust anchors that kernel nodes should trust.

fields.name: signing_ca
fields.description:
signing_ca is the cluster signing CA used to issue kernel certificates.
 The private key is present in the mounted kmaker config and must be backed
 by a Kubernetes Secret owned by operator.

fields.name: spiffe_prefix
fields.description:
spiffe_prefix is the SPIFFE trust domain for kernel SPIFFE URI SANs: the
 URI authority, so it must not contain '/'. Certificates minted here
 receive spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/kernel. Operator supplies this from
 operator.Config.spiffe_prefix.

fields.name: token_audience
fields.description: token_audience is the required Kubernetes TokenReview audience.

fields.name: kernel_service_accounts
fields.description:
kernel_service_accounts are Kubernetes service accounts allowed to request
 kernel certificates. Empty means namespace=schematic, name=kernel.

fields.name: kernel_cert_lifetime_seconds
fields.description: kernel_cert_lifetime_seconds caps issued kernel certificate lifetimes.

fields.name: tls
fields.description:
tls is the optional serving certificate for kmaker's own gRPC listener.
 When unset, kmaker starts without transport TLS for local/dev only.

fields.name: health_probe_port
fields.description:
health_probe_port is the plaintext gRPC port for k8s health probes.
 Kmaker's hand-written bootstrap bypasses the generated ServiceManager,
 so this field must be on Kmaker.Config (not only on Grpcconfig.Config).
 Default matches the platform-wide health probe port.

fields.name: llm_credential
fields.description:
llm_credential is a shared secret (e.g. an Anthropic API key) fanned out
 into the generated bootstrap config of every app service named in
 llm_credential_services, under the YAML key "llm_credential" — so it is
 configured once here rather than duplicated per app service. The
 receiving app service's own Config must declare a matching field. Keep
 this out of version control — store in crypto.yaml.

fields.name: llm_credential_services
fields.description:
llm_credential_services names the app services (by AppServiceNames key)
 that should receive llm_credential in their generated bootstrap config.

fields.name: tenants
fields.description:
tenants names the tenants this cluster hosts, e.g. ["acme", "beta"]. Each
 entry is a bare tenant name; the canonical authorization namespace is
 "/tenants/<name>" (see kernel.Delegate.tenant_namespace).

 The operator is the single source of truth for the tenant list, the same
 way it is for app_services: nothing queries kernel to discover tenants and
 no second config file lists them. For every service that registry.json
 marks (spec.service).tenant_owned, the operator deploys one Deployment +
 ServiceAccount named "<svc>-<tenant>" per entry here, and writes one kernel
 delegate named <svc> with tenant_namespace "/tenants/<name>" for each.
 Services NOT marked tenant_owned ignore this field entirely and keep their
 single shared instance.

 This does NOT tell a service its own tenant. Tenant identity is derived
 only from the SPIFFE ID in the caller's token at runtime, never from
 config a service can read.

fields.name: external_ip
fields.description:
external_ip pins the cluster's external LoadBalancer Service to a
 pre-reserved static external address (e.g. a GCP regional compute
 address). It is rendered as spec.loadBalancerIP on the gateway's
 "<gateway>-lb" Service — the ONE externally-exposed Service there is,
 carrying TCP/443 and TCP/80 together.

 Both ports are on the one Service on purpose: fqdn's public A record
 resolves to this address, and ACME HTTP-01 validation connects to port 80
 on that same name. The gateway answers on 80 and proxies challenge
 requests to the letsencrypt service in-cluster, so letsencrypt needs no
 external address of its own.

 Leave empty to let the provider assign an ephemeral address per Service —
 fine for local and dev clusters, but then the address changes on every
 re-render and any DNS record pointing at it goes stale.

fields.name: extra_hostnames
fields.description:
extra_hostnames are public names served IN ADDITION to fqdn (e.g. a second
 domain during a cutover). The operator renders fqdn followed by these into
 the gateway's external_hostnames and letsencrypt's hostnames. fqdn stays
 the primary name: the OIDC issuer and every other single-name use of fqdn
 ignore this field.

 Not usable until N-cert/SNI (option b) exists: certmagic issues one
 single-name certificate per name (not one multi-SAN cert), letsencrypt
 publishes only fqdn's, and the gateway has no SNI selection — an extra name
 is served fqdn's certificate and fails TLS name checks. Leave empty.

fields.name: image_digests
fields.description:
image_digests pins service images by digest. Key is the image name (the
 registry project, equal to the service name for every platform service);
 value is a manifest digest "sha256:<hex>". A pinned image renders as
 <repository>@<digest> in place of <repository>:<tag>; an image with no
 entry keeps its tag. Loaded from images.yaml (written by
 scripts/promote.sh), not operator.yaml.

message.name: Config
message.description: Config is delivered by kernel at startup and on every change.

fields.name: max_recipients
fields.description:
max_recipients bounds the recipient fan-out of ONE submission, and it is a
 resource limit on the service, not a business rule: N recipients means N
 publishes, so an unbounded list is an unbounded amount of work bought with
 one RPC. Held in config rather than as a constant for the same reason
 tasks.Config.max_open_tasks is — changing it in kernel must change
 behaviour with no redeploy.

 It must not exceed SendMessageRequest.recipients' assert_max_size (256):
 the two describe the same cap and the generated request validation is the
 hard edge, so a config above it could never take effect.

message.name: Config
message.description: Config is delivered by kernel at startup and on every change.

fields.name: lock_acquire_attempts
fields.description:
lock_acquire_attempts bounds how many times a cycle retries a contended
 per-user lock before giving the record back to the queue.

 kernel.FencedLock.Acquire is NON-BLOCKING — a key held by a different
 holder returns granted=false rather than parking the call — so a contended
 acquire is a poll, and something has to bound the polling. Giving up is not
 a failure: the record has not been ACKed, so it is redelivered, and by then
 the instance that held the lock has finished the cycle that would have
 absorbed it anyway.

 Config rather than a constant for the same reason messaging's
 max_recipients is: contention is a property of the deployment, and changing
 it must not need a redeploy.

fields.name: lock_acquire_backoff_ms
fields.description: lock_acquire_backoff_ms is the wait between those attempts.

fields.name: max_events_per_cycle
fields.description:
max_events_per_cycle bounds the AGGREGATION. Multiple events landing for
 one user while a cycle is running are drained into that cycle rather than
 starting a cycle each — "they are aggregated and processed together rather
 than firing one loop per event", per the design record. This is the ceiling
 on one cycle's drain, so a burst cannot buy unbounded work with one lock
 hold; the remainder is picked up by the next cycle.

 It must not exceed AgentCycle.woke_for's assert_max_size (256), which is
 the hard edge on how many wake events one cycle row can record.

message.name: Config
message.description: Config is delivered by kernel at startup and on every change.

fields.name: sweep_interval_seconds
fields.description:
sweep_interval_seconds is INERT as of 2026-09-27 and is read by nothing.

 It was the cadence of the STATE-ROOT sweep: `MailboxState.entries` was this
 service's own root in kernel, nothing else pruned it, and an unbounded one
 eventually reached its declared 1,000,000 bound and started refusing
 writes. There is no such root any more — the rows live in stratum, whose
 bound is disk and whose memory clock is `residency.idle_seconds` below, a
 per-type clock this service can neither observe nor set. A sweep from here
 would have nothing to sweep.

 WHAT WENT WITH IT: the 90-day `held_since_ms` floor. That age was the STATE
 ROOT's bound, not the record's, and no record-side clock replaces it —
 `residency.deleted_max_age_seconds` measures a purge from a
 `(spec.deleted_flag)` this record does not declare. So a mailbox entry is
 now kept for as long as stratum keeps it. See held_since_ms's comment and
 workers/mailbox-llmsettings-stratum-result.md; deliberately NOT closed here
 by inventing a delete path this migration was not asked for.

 (Until 2026-09-20 the sweep had a second half, reconciling the retired
 `ejectionable` marker. That half went first; this is the rest.)

 DECLARED, not deleted, for the same reason retrieved_grace_seconds below is:
 kernel holds mailbox's config, and removing a field kernel sets is a
 config-compatibility question this migration has no answer for. Both should
 be deleted and fields 1 and 2 reserved in a follow-up once nothing in kernel
 sets either.

fields.name: retrieved_grace_seconds
fields.description:
retrieved_grace_seconds is INERT as of 2026-09-20 and is read by nothing.

 It had exactly one job: to defer the moment the sweep flipped a retrieved
 row's `ejectionable` from NEVER to WINDOW, so that a client which acks and
 then immediately re-reads still found the row resident. Both ends of that
 sentence are gone. The marker went with `spec.Ejectionable`, and residency
 is now a per-TYPE idle clock on the row's last touch — a grace period
 cannot shift it, because the retrieval write IS the touch.

 DECLARED, not deleted, on purpose: kernel holds mailbox's config, and
 removing the field is a config-compatibility question this migration has no
 answer for. It should be deleted and field 2 reserved in a follow-up once
 nothing in kernel sets it — see
 looper/schematic/workers/mailbox-ejectionable-migration-questions.md. The
 same now applies to sweep_interval_seconds above.

message.name: Config
message.description: Config is delivered by kernel at startup and on every change.

fields.name: api_key_hint_chars
fields.description:
api_key_hint_chars is how many trailing characters of a stored key the read
 surface may echo back, so a person can tell WHICH key is saved without the
 key being retrievable. Config rather than a constant because it is a
 privacy/usability trade a deployment makes, and moving it must not need a
 redeploy. 0 disables the hint entirely.

 Capped at 8: a hint long enough to be searched for is not a hint.

message.name: Config
message.description: Config is delivered by kernel at startup and on every change.

fields.name: link_ttl_seconds
fields.description:
link_ttl_seconds is how long an emailed login link stays redeemable. It is
 INERT today — nothing in this file reads it — and is declared now because
 Config exists from day one and the EMAIL_LINK arm will need exactly this
 knob. The bounds are the useful range for a single-use login link: under a
 minute is unusable on a phone that has to leave the app to read mail, over
 an hour is a credential sitting in an inbox.

message.name: Config
message.description: Config is delivered by kernel at startup and on every change.

fields.name: volume_groups
fields.description:
volume_groups is every group declared anywhere in the fleet, rendered by
 the operator. See VolumeGroup: empty means no upload is possible, which is
 correct and not a misconfiguration to paper over.

message.name: VolumeGroup
message.description:
VolumeGroup is one group's rules, as this service receives them.

 IT IS NOT DECLARED HERE. A group is declared at BUILD TIME by the consuming
 service — DocManager declares `documents`, a later feature declares `photos`
 — through the `(spec.volume_group)` service-level annotation tacplus surfaces
 in registry.json, and the operator renders every declared group into this
 config (R4, and the doc's Work split: the annotation is tacplus's slice, the
 rendering is the operator's). This message is the RECEIVING end of that
 pipeline and nothing more.

 So the list below being EMPTY is the correct state of a cluster whose
 services have declared no groups: every upload is then refused, which is what
 "no group, no upload" means. It is not a reason to invent a default group.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
name is the group's identity, and the first path segment of every file it
 holds (`<group>/<ns>/<sha256>`). Unique across the fleet — tacplus refuses
 a duplicate at generation, so this service does not have to arbitrate.

fields.name: max_blob_bytes
fields.description:
max_blob_bytes is the largest single blob the group accepts. Enforced ON
 THE WIRE, not from the declared size: an upload is aborted the moment the
 stream passes it (R9 step 2), because a client that lied about `size_bytes`
 must not be able to fill the disk before the check.

fields.name: content_types
fields.description:
content_types is the exhaustive allow-list. A type not listed is refused at
 CreateUpload, and the bytes are sniffed again at finish (R4) — a renamed
 `.exe` declaring `application/pdf` fails on its magic bytes even though it
 passed this list.

fields.name: tenant_quota_bytes
fields.description:
tenant_quota_bytes is the ceiling on the SUM of promoted blob sizes for one
 tenant in this group. Quotas hang off the group and there is no separate
 global tenant quota (R4).

fields.name: http_listener
fields.description:
http_listener is the bind address for the BYTE PATHS — `PUT /upload/<t>`
 and `GET|HEAD /b/<t>`, and nothing else.

 IN-CLUSTER ONLY, exactly like letsencrypt's ACME responder: the gateway
 owns the edge and proxies these two prefixes here, so this listener needs
 no externally-exposed Service of its own. It is plaintext because the hop
 is in-cluster and the token in the path is the whole authorization; the
 gateway is what terminates TLS for the client.

fields.name: peer_listener
fields.description:
peer_listener is the bind address for the MIRROR AND ANTI-ENTROPY paths,
 and it is a second listener rather than three more prefixes on the first
 for one reason: the anti-entropy path ENUMERATES the hashes this pod holds.
 The gateway proxies only the two prefixes above, so nothing outside the
 cluster can reach this port at all.

fields.name: peers
fields.description:
peers is the `host:port` peer_listener address of EVERY replica, including
 this pod's own, from the StatefulSet's stable per-pod DNS
 (`blobstore-0.blobstore:8081,blobstore-1.blobstore:8081`). The pod finds
 itself by matching its hostname against the first DNS label and treats the
 rest as peers.

 Delivered by the operator as BLOBSTORE_PEERS, the same env shape as
 stratum's STRATUM_SEED_MEMBERS — peer wiring is deployment topology the
 operator already knows, and inventing a second typed path for it would
 only let the two disagree.

fields.name: data_dir
fields.description:
data_dir is the PVC mount holding `<group>/<ns>/<sha256>` and the `tmp`
 directory partial uploads are written into.

 The default is UNDER /app/data because that is where the operator's chart
 mounts a service's volumeClaimTemplate (`- name: data / mountPath:
 /app/data`). A default anywhere else would put the blobs on the pod's
 ephemeral filesystem and lose them on every restart, which is the kind of
 mistake nothing would report — the writes would all succeed.

fields.name: upload_token_ttl_seconds
fields.description:
upload_token_ttl_seconds is how long a CreateUpload token is good for —
 the doc's ceiling is 15 minutes (R9 step 1) and that is the default. It
 bounds how long a reservation can sit unused, not how long an upload may
 take: the TTL is checked when the PUT arrives, not while it streams.

fields.name: stats_flush_interval_seconds
fields.description:
stats_flush_interval_seconds is the metrics rollup cadence: per-token
 counters live in memory and reach BlobLinkStats at most once a minute per
 token (R10). Held in config rather than as a constant for the same reason
 mailbox's sweep interval is — changing it must not need a rebuild.

fields.name: session_sweep_interval_seconds
fields.description:
session_sweep_interval_seconds is how often expired UploadSession rows have
 their reservations released (R9 step 4). The same sweep deletes leftover
 `tmp` files, which is also done once unconditionally at start-up: a crash
 mid-upload leaves temp files and nothing else cleans them.

message.name: Config
message.description: Config is delivered by kernel at startup and on every change.

fields.name: max_open_tickets
fields.description:
max_open_tickets bounds how many tickets may be open at once, and exists
 for the same reason tasks.Config.max_open_tasks does: to give the service a
 rule that comes from CONFIG rather than from code, so changing it in kernel
 changes behaviour with no redeploy.

 NOT a written policy. §2 is explicit that "an entitlement makes an action
 impossible, a written policy makes it inadvisable" — a config bound that
 hard-fails a create is neither, it is a resource limit on the service. No
 business rule may be expressed here.

fields.name: max_chain_hops
fields.description:
max_chain_hops is the CIRCUIT BREAKER on AI-mediated negotiation, and it is
 a HOP COUNT, not a duration. A chain's hop count is the number of turns
 taken in it — every Ticket, TicketAdvice and TicketComment sharing a
 chain_id — and when it reaches this bound Scotty stops adding its own
 judgement to that chain. Jody, 2026-08-30: "it escalates to the human at
 the same level. It just keeps LLMs from getting stuck in a loop."

 Config for the same reason max_open_tickets is: it is a resource-shaped
 bound on the service, changeable in kernel with no redeploy, and it is NOT
 a written policy — nothing here decides anything about a request.

 A wall-clock TTL was proposed for this and explicitly discarded; see
 loopers/schematic/decisions/ticket-ttl-hop-count-circuit-breaker-2026-08-30.md.

message.name: Config
message.description:
Config is delivered by kernel at startup and on every change.

 The four knobs are the 2026-09-07 sketch's ConfigAdditions, retagged from 1
 because this is a new service's Config rather than an addition to `scotty`'s.
 Nothing else moved: they are resource-shaped bounds on the session runtime,
 changeable in kernel with no redeploy, and none of them decides anything
 about a request. No business rule may be expressed here — the same rule
 scotty.Config.max_open_tickets states.

 NO llm_credential FIELD YET. The persona runtime does call a model, and
 `scotty.Config.llm_credential` is the pattern for holding that key — but the
 fan-out is driven by operator's own `llm_credential_services` list, so adding
 the field here without adding "scottypersonal" there produces a service that
 starts and cannot talk to a model. Both halves are one change and belong to
 whoever builds the runtime.

fields.name: session_idle_seconds
fields.description:
session_idle_seconds is how long an ACTIVE session (in-process LLM
 transcript + cached state) survives without a turn before it is dropped.
 Dropping loses nothing: session state is in kernel and history is in
 kernel, so the next turn rehydrates. Config so it changes with no redeploy.

fields.name: max_active_sessions
fields.description:
max_active_sessions bounds the in-process cache (LRU). A resource limit,
 not a business rule.

fields.name: rehydrate_history_events
fields.description:
rehydrate_history_events is how many trailing ChatEvent rows a rehydrated
 session reads into its transcript. Older history is not lost, it is a tool
 call away.

fields.name: max_turn_hops
fields.description:
max_turn_hops caps model<->tool round-trips in ONE turn. Same shape and
 reason as scotty.Config.max_chain_hops: a hop count, not a TTL, and it
 exists to keep an LLM from looping rather than to express a policy.

message.name: Config
message.description: Config is delivered by kernel at startup and on every change.

fields.name: max_open_jobs
fields.description:
Resource bounds, not business rules — the same rule scotty.Config states.
 An entitlement makes an action impossible and a written policy makes it
 inadvisable; a config bound that hard-fails a create is neither, it is a
 resource limit on the service.

fields.name: permit_warning_days
fields.description:
permit_warning_days is how far ahead a lapsing permit is surfaced. It is a
 DEFAULT the runtime uses when no written policy says otherwise — Jody's
 "Warn me three days before any 811 ticket expires" is a rule in scotty, and
 it wins. Config so the default changes with no redeploy.

fields.name: observation_poll_seconds
fields.description:
Poll cadence. Jody said "probably hourly"; Config so it changes without a
 redeploy, and because NWS's own update rhythms differ per product
 (observations roughly hourly, gridpoint forecasts a few times a day,
 alerts whenever the office issues one).

fields.name: max_places
fields.description:
max_places bounds how many points the fleet may ask this service to track.
 A resource bound, not a business rule (same reasoning as scotty.Config).

fields.name: nws_user_agent
fields.description:
nws_user_agent is the contact string api.weather.gov requires of every
 caller. Config because it is deployment identity, not code.

message.name: Config
message.description: Config is delivered by kernel at startup and on every change.

fields.name: llm_credential
fields.description:
llm_credential is the ONE real Anthropic API key on the whole fleet, fanned out
 by operator into ONLY this service's generated bootstrap config (operator's
 llm_credential_services must name "llmproxy" and nothing else — see
 platform/proto/services/operator.proto's Config.llm_credential and
 .llm_credential_services). Field name and type must match what operator's
 bootstrap.go writes, or the service fails to unmarshal its own generated config.

 ConfigHasKeyMaterial must be true for this service in operator's helm generator
 (pkg/helm/generator.go), the same treatment kernel/kmaker/gateway already get, so
 this renders as a Kubernetes Secret, never a ConfigMap.

fields.name: default_provider_base_url
fields.description:
default_provider_base_url lets the Anthropic API host move (a proxy, a private
 endpoint) without a redeploy. Empty means the real api.anthropic.com.

fields.name: tool_call_timeout_ms
fields.description:
tool_call_timeout_ms bounds one tools/call frame on a caller's stream. On
 expiry the model gets a descriptive is_error tool_result (A25) and the dog's
 late answer is dropped and logged.

fields.name: max_tool_rounds_ceiling
fields.description:
max_tool_rounds_ceiling is the hard upper bound on
 SessionTurnRequest.max_tool_rounds; a larger request value is clamped to it.

fields.name: callback_reopen_grace_ms
fields.description:
callback_reopen_grace_ms is how long a turn waits for a dropped callback
 stream to be re-opened before it ends with STOP_REASON_CALLBACK_LOST.

fields.name: blocked_callers
fields.description:
blocked_callers is the per-identity kill switch (BQ7): a caller whose SPIFFE
 ID starts with any entry gets PERMISSION_DENIED on every rpc, and its open
 callback stream is closed when this config is delivered.

fields.name: oauth_token_path
fields.description: oauth_token_path is the token endpoint's path on default_provider_base_url.

fields.name: default_day_job_micro_usd
fields.description:
--- Budgets (crew runtime §10, A11, A24, D18), integer micro-USD per day ---

 RESOURCE LIMITS in config, same doctrine as before. A company dog's two
 buckets and the tenant reserve are tenant policy on crew.CompanyStructure
 (dog_budgets, reserve_micro_usd); these are the D18 defaults used where that
 record has no entry. Scotty's per-person budget is SeaBeam's (A24), not
 tenant policy, so it is only here.

message.name: Config
message.description:
Config is delivered by kernel at startup and on every change.

 Resource bounds, not business rules — the same rule scotty.Config and
 work.Config both state. An entitlement makes an action impossible and a
 written policy makes it inadvisable; a config bound that hard-fails a create
 is neither, it is a resource limit on the service.

fields.name: max_rules_per_user
fields.description:
max_rules_per_user bounds one person's whole tree — groups and rules
 together, deleted ones included, since a deleted node is still a row.

fields.name: activity_coalesce_seconds
fields.description:
activity_coalesce_seconds is the window the in-process activity bump
 coalesces into: at most one hit republish per user per window. NO RPC
 PERFORMS THIS — the user RPCs below bump hit_count/last_hit_ms on the
 caller's own row from inside their own handlers (Jody, 2026-09-20; see
 UserProfile.hit_count). The ruling fixes the behaviour ("at most one per
 user per hour") and puts the number here so it changes with no redeploy.

message.name: Config
message.description: Config is delivered by kernel at startup and on every change.

fields.name: max_open_ingests
fields.description:
max_open_ingests bounds how many ingest pipelines may be in flight at
 once. A resource limit on the service (same category as
 scotty.Config.max_open_tickets), not a business rule.

fields.name: llm_credential
fields.description:
Fanned out by operator's Config.llm_credential/llm_credential_services
 (schematic platform/proto@77b4733, platform/services/operator@6a1fd9c,
 both local-only per ALLOW_PUSH=0) into this service's generated
 bootstrap YAML under the key "llm_credential" — field name/type must
 match for the YAML to unmarshal. Populated by adding "reveille"
 to bootstrap/operator.yaml's llm_credential_services and setting
 llm_credential to the real Anthropic key (kept out of version control,
 same as the rest of bootstrap/). See llm.rs's LlmClient::from_env() for
 the current stub the agentic-loop scaffold reads instead — this field
 is the not-yet-wired real credential path.

fields.name: delegates
fields.description:
delegates hold credentials for services that can request tokens.
 Each delegate identifies a service and its authorized target services.

message.name: Delegate
message.description:
Delegate holds bootstrap matchers for a service or machine client that can request tokens.
 Each delegate carries a name, which becomes the service path segment in the
 issued token's SPIFFE URI, and the namespace that URI is rooted at:
 spiffe://<trust-domain>/system/<location>/services/<delegate_name> for a
 shared platform service, spiffe://<trust-domain>/tenants/<tenant>/services/<delegate_name>
 for a tenant-owned instance (see tenant_namespace).
 Authenticates via a projected Kubernetes service-account token or cloud identity.

 Two authorization models:
   - S2S (identity-only): tokens carry only the SPIFFE URI as sub.
     Receiving services enforce access via auth_services RE2 patterns
     that match against the caller's service path.
   - C2S (entitlement-based): OPA returns TokenEntitlements directly.
     Kernel embeds expanded per-service RPC lists in the user token.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
name is the delegate's service path — becomes the final service path segment
 in the SPIFFE URI. For workload children: parent/<child>.

 NOT unique on its own: a tenant-owned service has one delegate per tenant,
 all carrying the same name (the service path that auth_services patterns
 match on), distinguished only by tenant_namespace. The delegate's key is
 the (name, tenant_namespace) pair.

fields.name: tenant_namespace
fields.description:
tenant_namespace is the authorization namespace this delegate's minted
 identity is rooted at. Empty — the default, and what every shared platform
 service uses — means the /system root, so the minted subject is
 spiffe://<td>/system/services/<name>. A tenant-owned service instance sets
 the canonical tenant namespace /tenants/<tenant>, and the minted subject
 becomes spiffe://<td>/tenants/<tenant>/services/<name>, from which every
 token minted for it takes its namespace claim.

 This is the ONLY place a service's tenant is configured. Nothing a service
 sends can influence it: the tenant reaches the rest of the fleet solely as
 part of the SPIFFE subject kernel stamps here.

 Distinct from KubernetesServiceAccountMatcher.kubernetes_namespace, which
 is the K8s namespace the pod runs in, not an authorization namespace.

message.name: CloudIdentityMatcher
message.description:
CloudIdentityMatcher configures which cloud identities a delegate accepts.
 The delegate proves identity using a CloudIdentityProof; this config
 tells kernel what to expect.

fields.name: vendor
fields.description: vendor identifies the cloud provider.

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_AWS
enum_values.description: Amazon Web Services (AWS)

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_AZURE
enum_values.description: Microsoft Azure

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_GCP
enum_values.description: Google Cloud Platform (GCP)

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_ORACLE
enum_values.description: Oracle Cloud

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_ALIBABA
enum_values.description: Alibaba Cloud

enum_values.name: CLOUD_VENDOR_IBM
enum_values.description: IBM Cloud

fields.name: expected_identity
fields.description:
expected_identity is the cloud identity to match against.
 AWS: IAM role ARN. GCP: service account email. Azure: managed identity client ID.

fields.name: kubernetes_service_accounts
fields.description:
kubernetes_service_accounts lists the Kubernetes (namespace, service
 account) pairs that authenticate as this delegate via a projected SA
 token.

message.name: KubernetesServiceAccountMatcher
message.description:
KubernetesServiceAccountMatcher configures which Kubernetes service accounts
 a delegate accepts. The workload proves identity with a projected
 service-account token; this config tells kernel which (namespace, service
 account) pairs map to this delegate. Repeated on Delegate so multiple SAs
 (multi-namespace / migration) can map to one delegate.

fields.name: kubernetes_namespace
fields.description:
kubernetes_namespace is the Kubernetes namespace of the service account.
 Named explicitly to avoid collision with the Schematic tenant namespace
 concept — this is the K8s namespace, not an authorization namespace.

fields.name: kubernetes_service_account
fields.description: kubernetes_service_account is the Kubernetes ServiceAccount name.

fields.name: authorized_services
fields.description:
authorized_services lists services this delegate can request tokens for.
 Values are generated ServiceName enum entries matching service declarations.
 The delegate can always request a token for itself (sub=name).
 Use SERVICE_NAME_ANY to allow all services.

fields.name: custom_claims
fields.description:
custom_claims are static key-value pairs added to every access token
 minted for this delegate. Useful for identity claims (e.g. email).
 Standard JWT claims (sub, iss, aud, exp, iat, azp, nbf, jti, typ,
 parent_sub) are reserved and will be skipped.

fields.name: auth_broker_kinds
fields.description:
auth_broker_kinds declares which classes of user-authentication proof this
 delegate is trusted to broker into Mint.MintUserToken. EMPTY — the default,
 and every delegate in the fleet today — means this delegate is NOT an auth
 broker and MintUserToken refuses it. This replaces the former hardcoded
 auth_services broker allowlist on that RPC: who may attest a
 human login is per-delegate runtime config, not a compile-time literal in
 this file.

enum_values.name: AUTH_BROKER_KIND_IDP
enum_values.description:
An IdP assertion the broker has already validated (oauth). Kernel
 trusts the broker's attestation — today's behaviour, unchanged.

enum_values.name: AUTH_BROKER_KIND_DEVICE
enum_values.description:
Possession of a personal principal's device key. Kernel verifies the
 proof itself; may mint only a /people/<pid> personal token.

enum_values.name: AUTH_BROKER_KIND_EMAIL_LINK
enum_values.description: Control of an email address a tenant authorized.

enum_values.name: AUTH_BROKER_KIND_PERSONAL_LINK
enum_values.description: An admin-issued link accepted on the member's own device.

fields.name: fqdn
fields.description:
fqdn is the fully qualified domain name for this cluster
 (e.g. "api.example.com"). Published to Identity state for
 services like letsencrypt. No default — must be set for production.
constraints: must be a fully qualified domain name

fields.name: issuer
fields.description:
issuer is the full issuer URL for tokens minted by this cluster.
 For local development, computed as https://<fqdn>:<port> (port omitted if 443).
 For production behind a load balancer, set explicitly (e.g. "https://api.example.com").

fields.name: key_rotation_interval_seconds
fields.description:
key_rotation_interval_seconds is how often the exchanger rotates
 its own signing keys. Default: 24 hours.

fields.name: default_token_expiry_seconds
fields.description:
default_token_expiry_seconds is the default lifetime for issued
 access tokens when the request does not specify an expiry. Default: 1 hour.

fields.name: ca_cert_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
ca_cert_lifetime_seconds is the lifetime for node CA certificates.
 Default: 31536000 (1 year). Node CA certs are regenerated on restart.

fields.name: access_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
access_token_lifetime_seconds is the default lifetime for user access tokens
 minted via MintToken. Default: 900 (15 minutes).

fields.name: refresh_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
refresh_token_lifetime_seconds is the default lifetime for user refresh tokens
 minted via MintToken. Default: 86400 (24 hours).

fields.name: tls_cert_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
tls_cert_lifetime_seconds is the lifetime for auto-TLS service certificates.
 Kernel sends a renewal request at half-life. Default: 86400 (24 hours).

fields.name: max_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
max_token_lifetime_seconds is the maximum lifetime kernel will allow for
 any minted token. Requests with exp beyond now + this value are rejected.
 Delegates control their own exp policy within this ceiling.
 Default: 2592000 (30 days).

fields.name: offline_token_lifetime_seconds
fields.description:
offline_token_lifetime_seconds is the default lifetime for Offline Tokens
 (OT) — the long-lived, identity-only tokens persisted on disk by the
 schematic daemon and renewed before half-life. Months, not hours.
 Default: 7776000 (90 days). Exempt from max_token_lifetime_seconds, which
 caps short-lived access/service tokens.

fields.name: root_cred_pairs
fields.description:
root_cred_pairs are the bootstrap admin credentials, rendered into this
 config by the operator from operator.yaml. Each is an ordinary C2S CredPair
 owned by the root namespace; kernel installs them into the root namespace's
 TenantConfig at boot (granting full entitlements) so a holder can sign a
 proof, exchange it via MintClientToken, and provision tenants/projects via
 TenantAdmin. Only the public half is carried here.

fields.name: spiffe_trust_domain
fields.description:
spiffe_trust_domain is the SPIFFE URI authority: a globally unique instance
 name for this autonomous-system instance (need not be a DNS domain). It must
 not contain '/', a scheme, query, or fragment, and carries no path. Service
 identity is built by the generated sys/spiffe helper as:
   spiffe://<spiffe_trust_domain>/system/<location_path...>/services/<service_label>
 If empty, SPIFFE IDs are not set on issued tokens or X509 URI SANs. Kernel
 copies this (with location_path) into the runtime grpcconfig.Config it seeds
 into ServiceConfigState, so every service shares one trust domain.

fields.name: location_path
fields.description:
location_path is this deployment's topology path under /system — opaque,
 tag-delimited, slash-separated segments, arity not fixed (e.g.
 "aws/123456789012/us-east-1a/cluster-7/team-a"). Segments follow the SPIFFE
 segment grammar and must not be reserved tags. Supplied by the operator from
 runtime config (where the cluster runs); it is not a token claim. May be
 empty (no topology tiers).

fields.name: health_probe_port
fields.description:
health_probe_port is the plaintext gRPC port for k8s health probes.
 Kernel's hand-written bootstrap bypasses the generated ServiceManager,
 so this field must be on Kernel.Config (not only on Grpcconfig.Config).
 Default matches the platform-wide health probe port.

fields.name: grants
fields.description:
grants seeds the standing delegation Grant catalog at boot, loaded into
 the live grants store the same way delegates (above) are — there is no
 runtime grant-creation RPC yet, so this is the only way a Grant exists
 today.

message.name: Grant
message.description:
Grant is a standing delegation: a user authorizes a delegate (an intermediary
 service, e.g. an agent acting on a schedule) to act on their behalf later,
 asynchronously. Kernel
 stores the GRANT, never a minted token — the delegate holds only `id`.

 On use the delegate presents its own S2S identity plus `id`; kernel replays
 `claims` into OPA fresh (the same EntitlementEvalInput shape
 `IdentityServiceImpl.buildClaimsStruct` already builds from a token payload),
 intersects the result with `authorized_scope`, and mints a short-lived token
 (sub=subject, act=delegate_name, azp=kernel — kernel mints Grant tokens
 directly, so azp is always the closed-enum `kernel` value; the delegate name
 goes on the `act` claim instead). Fresh OPA gives "cannot exceed the user's
 current authority"; the recorded scope gives "the user downscoped it". Nothing
 is snapshotted that can go stale except the claims themselves — which catches
 policy changes, never IDP changes.

 This message is carried in KernelDiskState and mutated at runtime by
 Mint.RevokeGrant (revoked_at_ms) only; there is no create/list RPC yet — the
 catalog is still seeded from Config.grants at boot.

 PROVISIONAL: this field set is a prerequisite storage layer built ahead of,
 not instead of, the design conversation with the maintainer. What is settled:
 id, delegate_name, subject, authorized_scope, claims, created_at_ms,
 expires_at_ms, revoked_at_ms. NOT settled: how the system learns a user's IDP
 claims changed or the user was deleted — claim-provenance and epoch are still
 open and may add fields here.

fields.name: id
fields.description:
id is the opaque grant identifier the delegate holds and presents. Unique
 across the cluster.

fields.name: delegate_name
fields.description:
delegate_name is the Delegate.name of the intermediary holding this grant.
 It becomes the minted token's act claim (azp on a Grant mint is always
 kernel — see the message comment above). Paired with delegate_namespace:
 the name alone does not identify a delegate (see Delegate.name).

fields.name: subject
fields.description:
subject is the user this grant acts for — the sub of the token that will be
 minted, and the identity whose claims were recorded below.

fields.name: authorized_scope
fields.description:
authorized_scope is the per-service scope the user recorded at consent time.
 Every mint intersects the fresh OPA result with this, so the grant can only
 ever narrow the user's live authority, never widen it.

fields.name: claims
fields.description:
claims are the user's IDP claims as captured at consent time, in the same
 google.protobuf.Struct shape that userentitlements.EntitlementEvalInput.claims
 takes, so they can be replayed into OPA verbatim.

fields.name: created_at_ms
fields.description: created_at_ms is the consent time, epoch milliseconds.

fields.name: expires_at_ms
fields.description:
expires_at_ms is when the grant itself stops being usable, epoch
 milliseconds. 0 means no expiry (revocation only).

fields.name: revoked_at_ms
fields.description:
revoked_at_ms is when the grant was revoked via Mint.RevokeGrant, epoch
 milliseconds. 0 means not revoked. A revoked grant is MARKED, never
 deleted, so the record remains as an audit trail of the delegation that
 existed and when it was withdrawn. Every mint from the grant and every
 later exchange of a token minted from it is denied once this is set
 (IdentityServiceImpl.assertGrantStillActive), so revocation kills
 already-minted derived tokens within one request.

fields.name: delegate_namespace
fields.description:
delegate_namespace is the Delegate.tenant_namespace of the intermediary
 holding this grant, completing the (name, namespace) key delegate_name
 alone cannot supply. Empty means the /system delegate of that name — the
 shared-service case, and every grant written before tenant-owned services
 existed. A grant held by tenant acme's docmanager carries /tenants/acme
 here, so tenant beta's docmanager — same delegate_name — cannot mint from
 it or revoke it.

fields.name: ratis_listener
fields.description:
ratis_listener is the bind address for the embedded Apache Ratis peer
 group that backs the FencedLock service. Kernel is the only service in the
 fleet that runs Ratis. Peers are derived from `members` above (same hosts,
 this port) so lock membership tracks cluster membership and there is no
 second topology to keep in sync. Default port 5002 — the next one after
 hazelcast_listener's 5001.

fields.name: people_idp_credentials
fields.description:
people_idp_credentials are the OAuth client credentials for the RESERVED
 `people` tenant's two fixed identity providers (Sign in with Apple, Google
 Sign-In). Kernel seeds them into /tenants/people's TenantConfig.oauth at
 every boot, exactly as root_cred_pairs are seeded into the root namespace.

 Only the client credentials are configurable: each entry names a provider
 from the closed PeopleIdpProvider enum and kernel supplies the issuer URL
 from its own fixed table. "The `people` tenant's IdP set is fixed" is
 therefore a property of this type, not of an operator's discipline — there
 is no field a deployment could point at a third issuer.

message.name: PeopleIdpCredential
message.description:
PeopleIdpCredential is one provider's OAuth client credentials, the only part
 of the `people` tenant's IdP configuration a deployment supplies. Kernel adds
 the issuer URL from its fixed table and writes the pair into
 /tenants/people's oauth.OAuthTenantConfig, so oauth reads the `people`

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the OAuth2 client identifier registered with the provider.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the OAuth2 client secret; comes from the secrets overlay.

types.name: ConfigState
types.description:

 Kernel writes it and persists it; other services watch their per-tenant/
 per-project config slice via the export: true wire.

fields.name: tenants
fields.description: tenants is the list of all tenant records, keyed by tenant.name.

message.name: Tenant
message.description:

   spiffe://<trust-domain>/tenants/<name>/...

fields.name: constraints
fields.description:
constraints is the ancestor-set limits (entitlements ceiling now; domain
 later). Set at creation; mutable only by an ancestor.

message.name: Constraints
message.description:

 Tenant record (set at CreateTenant), are mutable only by an ancestor, and are
 immutable to the tenant itself — so the tenant genuinely cannot raise its own
 limits. Validated on CreateTenant and SetTenantConfig.

 invariant enforced in the SetTenantConfig validation path, satisfiable by
 create-and-discard. It is not an ancestor toggle.)

fields.name: entitlements_ceiling
fields.description:

 tenant may ever hold. Every cred_pair's entitlements ⊆ this; a sub-tenant's
 ceiling ⊆ this. Replaces the former standalone Tenant.entitlements field.

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:

 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).

 never a request parameter.

fields.name: principal_scope

 spec.PrincipalScope enum VALUE NAME (e.g. "PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_ANY"). It is the
 claim the generated (spec.owner_default) guard reads to tell an owner acting
 on its own row from a principal whose authority is wider than itself.

 mean self-scoped: the guard fails closed, so a policy that stamps nothing
 leaves every caller exactly as narrow as it is today.
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity
 property, never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: tenant_configs
fields.description: tenant_configs stores each tenant's TenantConfig, keyed by tenant_name.

message.name: TenantConfigEntry
message.description:

 config slices: kernel cred_pairs, oauth IDP, opa policy). TenantAdmin RPCs
 write these.

message.name: TenantConfig
message.description:
TenantConfig aggregates per-service tenant configuration slices.
 Field names match service names; field numbers are stable via registry.yaml.

message.name: KernelTenantConfig
message.description:
KernelTenantConfig is the per-tenant kernel configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the kernel field.

fields.name: cred_pairs
fields.description:
