fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:

 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.description:

fields.name: people
fields.description:
people is the `people` tenant's user rows, keyed by Person.user_id. It
 lives in THIS boundary rather than one of its own because it is the same
 registry: kernel's record of which humans exist, kernel-only and unexported
 for the same reason personal_principals is. PersonalPrincipal is the
 superseded /people/<pid> shape and goes away with the device slice; Person
 is what remains.

message.name: Person
message.description:
Person is one human: a user row in the reserved `people` tenant, created the
 first time an IdP token for its (provider, provider_subject) pair is seen and
 found on every login after that, from any device or browser.

 One provider identity is one person. A human who signs in with both Apple and
 Google is two Person rows until an explicit, both-sides-proven merge exists —
 guessing they are the same human is how accounts get hijacked.

fields.name: user_id
fields.description:
user_id is the <u> in /tenants/people/users/<u>. It is DERIVED, not minted:
 "<provider>.<provider_subject>", with the provider drawn from the closed
 enum above (neither `apple` nor `google` contains a '.', so the first dot is
 an unambiguous delimiter). The provider's subject is already stable and
 unique within that provider, so there is no hash of our own to keep
 consistent, and the same human lands on the same row without a lookup
 table.

fields.name: provider
fields.description: provider is which IdP proved this person.

enum_values.name: PEOPLE_IDP_PROVIDER_APPLE
enum_values.description: Sign in with Apple (issuer https://appleid.apple.com).

enum_values.name: PEOPLE_IDP_PROVIDER_GOOGLE
enum_values.description: Google Sign-In (issuer https://accounts.google.com).

fields.name: provider_subject
fields.description:
provider_subject is the IdP's own `sub` claim, verbatim. Never an email:
 an email is reassignable, and comparing them is how one human's rows become
 another's.

fields.name: disabled_at_ms
fields.description:
disabled_at_ms marks, never deletes — the same audit rule
 PersonalPrincipal.disabled_at_ms states.

fields.name: tenant_user_links
fields.description:
tenant_user_links is the link registry, keyed by TenantUserLinks.user_path.
 It lives in THIS boundary for the same reason people does: a link is
 identity, not user data, so it belongs in kernel's own registry of who
 exists — kernel-only and unexported.

message.name: TenantUserLinks
message.description:
TenantUserLinks is ONE tenant user's links.

 Keyed per user, and written on BOTH sides of every link, deliberately: this
 is read on every user mint, so it must be one O(1) keyed lookup and not a
 scan of every row for one that mentions the caller.

fields.name: user_key
fields.description:
user_key identifies the linked user as "<namespace>|<sub>" — the exact
 namespace and sub claims kernel mints for them. Deliberately the minted
 pair rather than a derived path: an ordinary tenant's `sub` is whatever its
 IdP broker supplies (an email, today) and is not required to be a SPIFFE
 id, so there is no path to derive. The namespace half is what keeps two
 tenants' identically-named users apart.

message.name: TenantUserLink
message.description:
TenantUserLink is one edge out of a linked tenant user: which identity in
 another tenant is the same human. Linking is GENERIC — any two tenants, not
 `people` and one other. The first use is drpepper's `jody` linked to that
 human's `people` row, but a contractor in two companies and a tenant
 migrating IdPs are the same record.

 peer_namespace, not a peer user path, is what the token's `linked` claim
 carries. The generated namespace backstop compares that claim against
 (spec.store_namespace), which holds a NAMESPACE, so a user path would never
 compare equal and a linked caller's read would never be accepted.

fields.name: peer_namespace
fields.description: peer_namespace is the canonical /tenants/<t> the linked identity lives in.

fields.name: peer_subject
fields.description:
peer_subject is the linked identity's `sub` as kernel mints it. Kernel
 keeps it because peer_namespace alone does not identify a human, and
 because a re-key has to find and rewrite the edge that names one user.

fields.name: revoked_at_ms
fields.description:
revoked_at_ms is the unlink mark. Marks, never deletes — the same audit rule
 Grant.revoked_at_ms and PersonalCredential.revoked_at_ms state, and for the
 stronger reason here that a link is proved once by live credentials and
 nothing kernel holds can re-derive it: a deleted edge is indistinguishable
 from one that was never proved.

 A revoked edge contributes no `linked` claim at mint. Re-proving the same
 link clears the mark rather than adding a second edge, because the same two
 credentials presented again are the same fact.

fields.name: pending_approvals
fields.description:
pending_approvals is the device-only-approval registry, keyed by
 PendingApproval.approval_id. It is in THIS boundary because an approval is
 identity — which human, holding which device, consented to which call — and
 because the verification path is kernel's own: a read from another service
 would put the platform's approval check behind a second service's
 availability.

 Deliberately WITHOUT (spec.persistence), and absent from KernelDiskState.
 It is the one collection here that is ephemeral on purpose; see the
 message's own comment for why losing one is harmless and losing a link is
 not.

message.name: PendingApproval
message.description:
PendingApproval is the platform's one approval primitive: who, which RPC, a
 hash of the exact request, and an expiry.

 It exists because "the token is the user" is not enough for an RPC that is an
 APPROVAL. A browser IdP session or a delegated agent token can BE the user
 without a human touching hardware, so an approval needs a proof no session
 and no delegate can produce: a signature by a key linked to that person's
 devices. The record is what that signature is verified AGAINST, which is what
 lets the generated (spec.rpc).requires_device check say WHAT was approved and
 not merely that somebody tapped something.

 It lives in kernel, beside Person and TenantUserLink, because it is identity:
 the proof that one human, holding one device, consented to one call. It is
 generated against and never reimplemented per product.

 NOT SNAPSHOTTED TO DISK, and no (spec.persistence) — the one collection in
 PrincipalState that is deliberately ephemeral. KernelDiskState's own rule is
 that only state which must survive a restart is persisted; an approval lives
 for minutes, and losing one fails CLOSED (the id is simply not found) with
 the person proposing again at the cost of one more tap. TenantUserLink is
 snapshotted precisely because losing IT fails silently instead.

fields.name: approval_id
fields.description:
approval_id is kernel-minted and opaque. Never derived from the request: two
 people proposing the same call must not collide, and a derivable id would
 let anyone name somebody else's pending approval.

fields.name: person_user_key
fields.description:
person_user_key is WHO, in the form the link registry keys them by:
 "/tenants/people|<the person's SPIFFE sub>" (TenantUserLinks.user_key). The
 registry key rather than a bare user path because it is compared against the
 approving device's own link edges, and that is the form those hold.

fields.name: rpc_method
fields.description:
rpc_method is WHICH RPC, as "pkg.Service/Method" — the qualified method key
 the platform already identifies an RPC by (the generated authorizer's
 _qualified_method_key; kernel's own rate limiter's per-method bucket), i.e.
 gRPC's full method name without its leading slash. Deliberately not a new
 naming scheme and not an entitlement grant name: the generated check has the
 gRPC method in hand and nothing else.

fields.name: request_hash
fields.description:
request_hash is a SHA-256 over the EXACT request being approved. Kernel
 treats it as 32 opaque bytes and compares them for equality; WHAT is hashed,
 and how it is canonicalised, is the generator's contract — the same rule has
 to be applied by the proposer and by the generated check, in whatever
 languages each is written in. Kernel never re-derives it, so kernel can
 never silently disagree with either.

fields.name: expires_at_ms
fields.description:
expires_at_ms is kernel's, from a capped TTL, never the caller's number. An
 approval is consent to one call happening NOW; a long-lived one is a
 standing permission, which is the thing §5 exists to refuse.

fields.name: consumed_at_ms
fields.description:
consumed_at_ms burns the approval single-use. Marked rather than deleted so
 a replay inside the window is refused as ALREADY USED rather than as an
 unknown id; the expiry sweep deletes it afterwards. Single-use because a
 guarded RPC need not be idempotent — a captured signature must not be able
 to make the same approved transfer twice.

types.name: ServiceHealth
types.description:
ServiceHealth is a state root for service instance health.
 All microservices have RW access. The server enforces per-instance write
 isolation via the token's instance_id claim (instance_keyed annotation).

fields.name: instances
fields.description:
instances holds health data for each running service instance.
 Keyed by "service_id@instance_id" (composed by server from token claims).
 Entries TTL-expire in 30s if not refreshed, ensuring stale instances
 are removed when a process dies.

message.name: ServiceInstanceHealth
message.description:
ServiceInstanceHealth captures the health, load, and reachability of a
 single running instance of a microservice. The composite key
 "service_id@instance_id" is set by the server from the caller's token claims.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Composite key: "service:fleetwood@uuid" — set by server from token claims

fields.name: grpc_endpoint
fields.description: Reachability

message.name: Host
message.description:
Host identifies a network endpoint by hostname/IP and port.
 The host field accepts either an FQDN or an IP address (v4/v6).

fields.name: host
fields.description: Hostname or IP address (e.g. "api.example.com" or "10.0.0.1").
constraints: must be a valid hostname or IP address

fields.name: port
fields.description: Port number (1-65535).
constraints: must be a valid network port (1-65535)

fields.name: protocol
fields.description: Transport protocol. Default TCP (zero value).

fields.name: status
fields.description: Health

fields.name: cpu_usage
fields.description: Load (auto-collected from runtime)

fields.name: active_requests
fields.description: Load (from grpcserver metrics)

fields.name: p50_latency_us
fields.description: Performance (from grpcserver metrics)

fields.name: version
fields.description: Routing metadata

fields.name: started_at_ms
fields.description: Timestamps

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
SPIFFE identity
 spiffe_id is the full SPIFFE URI for this instance, built by the owning
 service manager via the generated sys/spiffe helper (service_spiffe_id) —
 never hand-formatted. It is one of the durable materialization points of
 the computed identity (health identity, X509 URI SAN, workload keys).
 Format: spiffe://<trust_domain>/system/<location...>/services/<service>[/workloads/<child>...]
 Service:  spiffe://example.com/system/aws/us-east-1a/cluster-7/services/identity
 Workload: spiffe://example.com/system/aws/us-east-1a/cluster-7/services/mud-controller/workloads/agent-42
 Consumers needing the location-agnostic service identity parse it with
 service_path_from_spiffe (the bare label, plus any /workloads suffix).

types.name: SetProjectConfigRequest

message.name: ProjectConfig
message.description:
ProjectConfig is a project's configuration. EMPTY for now — its presence
 records the project's existence. Per-project settings will be added later.
 (IDP/OPA live at the tenant, not here.)

types.name: SetTenantConfigRequest

message.name: TenantConfig
message.description:
TenantConfig aggregates per-service tenant configuration slices.
 Field names match service names; field numbers are stable via registry.yaml.

message.name: KernelTenantConfig
message.description:
KernelTenantConfig is the per-tenant kernel configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the kernel field.

fields.name: cred_pairs
fields.description:
cred_pairs are the tenant's cred_pairs (JWK + entitlements + tenant-relative
 namespaces). They authenticate management RPCs as ordinary C2S identities
 (no P2S). Public keys only — private keys never enter the cluster. The
 creating root registers the tenant's first cred_pair public key via
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig (bootstrap); nothing is minted or
 delivered server-side. Holders generate their own keypairs off-cluster.

message.name: CredPair
message.description:
CredPair is a tenant-scoped credential. Public key stored in the tenant's
 KernelTenantConfig slice; private key never leaves the holder. Used to
 authenticate kernel.TenantAdmin RPCs and (downstream) any tenant-scoped
 RPC across the cluster.

 A request authenticated by CredPair carries the SPIFFE URI
 `spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/<tenant_name>/users/cred-pair:<id>`.

 `entitlements` must always be a subset of the tenant's ceiling
 (kernel.Constraints.entitlements_ceiling). Enforcement is in
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig.

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is a unique identifier for this cred_pair within its owning tenant.

fields.name: tenant_name
fields.description:
tenant_name names the owning tenant — the namespace that `namespaces` are
 relative to. The cluster cred_pair's owner is the root "/".

fields.name: public_key
fields.description:
public_key is the cred_pair's public key, as a JWK. Mint verifies a
 cred_pair-signed proof against it to issue a token.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: entitlements
fields.description:
entitlements this cred_pair holds (⊆ the owning tenant's ceiling), as the
 SAME TokenEntitlements the C2S authorizer checks: the minted cred_pair token
 sets service_entitlements = this directly (uniform with IDP-user tokens).

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: principal_scope
fields.description:
principal_scope is how wide the caller's authority over PRINCIPALS is, as a
 spec.PrincipalScope enum VALUE NAME (e.g. "PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_ANY"). It is the
 claim the generated (spec.owner_default) guard reads to tell an owner acting
 on its own row from a principal whose authority is wider than itself.
 Absent, empty, PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED and PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_SELF_ONLY all
 mean self-scoped: the guard fails closed, so a policy that stamps nothing
 leaves every caller exactly as narrow as it is today.
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity
 property, never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: namespaces
fields.description:
namespaces are the authorized namespaces, RELATIVE to the owning tenant
 (e.g. "default", "prod", or "*" for all of the tenant's projects). The
 cred_pair can only act at-or-below these and literally cannot name another
 tenant. The cluster cred_pair is relative to "/", so it can span tenants.

fields.name: description
fields.description: description is a human-readable label.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: created_at is when this credential was created.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.description: expires_at is the optional expiry. Zero value means no expiry.

message.name: OpaTenantConfig
message.description:
OpaTenantConfig is the per-tenant OPA policy configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the opa field.
 (OPA lives at the TENANT level — one policy per tenant, evaluated at login;
 it converts IDP claims (groups) into per-project entitlements + authorized
 projects + default project.)

fields.name: entitlements_policy
fields.description: entitlements_policy is the OPA bundle for entitlement evaluation.

message.name: OpaPolicy
message.description:
OpaPolicy defines an OPA policy bundle for authorization evaluation.
 The bundle is a filesystem.Directory tree containing .rego policy files.

fields.name: entry_point
fields.description: entry_point specifies the main package/decision point for policy evaluation.

fields.name: bundle
fields.description: bundle is the directory tree containing .rego policy files.

message.name: Directory
message.description:
Directory represents a directory node in a filesystem tree.
 Directories are recursive — each may contain child directories and files.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the directory name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this directory

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: directories
fields.description: directories holds zero or more child directories

fields.name: files
fields.description: files holds zero or more files in this directory

message.name: File
message.description: File represents a single file with permissions and content.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the file name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this file

fields.name: content
fields.description: content is the raw file content (max 10 MB)

fields.name: created
fields.description: created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the policy was created.

fields.name: version
fields.description: version is an optional version string for this policy (e.g., "1.0.0").
constraints: must be a valid semantic version

fields.name: proxy_policy
fields.description: proxy_policy is the OPA bundle for proxy request policy evaluation.

message.name: OAuthTenantConfig
message.description:
OAuthTenantConfig is the per-tenant OAuth configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the oauth field.
 (IDP lives at the TENANT level — humans log into their tenant's IDP; the
 tenant's OPA policy then derives their per-project entitlements.)

fields.name: providers
fields.description: providers are the tenant's IDPs (e.g. a corporate Okta instance).

message.name: OAuthProvider
message.description:
OAuthProvider describes a tenant-owned IDP. The (issuer_url, client_id) pair
 uniquely identifies this tenant — no claim matching needed.

fields.name: issuer_url
fields.description: issuer_url is the OpenID Connect issuer. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the OAuth2 client identifier. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the OAuth2 client secret; comes from secrets overlay layer.

fields.name: allowed_scopes
fields.description: allowed_scopes are the OAuth2 scopes requested from this IDP.

fields.name: jwks_uri
fields.description: jwks_uri overrides the auto-discovered JWKS endpoint.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description: ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate for self-signed IDPs.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this provider.

fields.name: claim_matchers
fields.description: claim_matchers route users from cluster-level shared IDPs to this tenant.

message.name: ClaimMatcher
message.description:
ClaimMatcher routes users arriving via a cluster-level shared IDP to this tenant.
 The token has already been validated against the cluster IDP before matching.

fields.name: provider_issuer_url
fields.description: provider_issuer_url identifies which cluster IDP this rule applies to.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: claim_key
fields.description: claim_key is the JWT claim name (e.g. "hd", "email").

fields.name: claim_value
fields.description: claim_value is the expected value (e.g. "mycompany.com").

Tenant
types.description:

 `name` is unique, immutable, and becomes the tenant's SPIFFE segment:

fields.name: constraints
fields.description:

message.name: Constraints
message.description:

 create-and-discard. It is not an ancestor toggle.)

message.name: TenantConfigEntry
message.description:
TenantConfigEntry maps a tenant_name to its full TenantConfig (the tacplus
 config slices: kernel cred_pairs, oauth IDP, opa policy). TenantAdmin RPCs
 write these.

message.name: TenantConfig
message.description:
TenantConfig aggregates per-service tenant configuration slices.
 Field names match service names; field numbers are stable via registry.yaml.

message.name: KernelTenantConfig
message.description:
KernelTenantConfig is the per-tenant kernel configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the kernel field.

fields.name: cred_pairs
fields.description:
cred_pairs are the tenant's cred_pairs (JWK + entitlements + tenant-relative
 namespaces). They authenticate management RPCs as ordinary C2S identities
 (no P2S). Public keys only — private keys never enter the cluster. The
 creating root registers the tenant's first cred_pair public key via
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig (bootstrap); nothing is minted or
 delivered server-side. Holders generate their own keypairs off-cluster.

message.name: CredPair
message.description:
CredPair is a tenant-scoped credential. Public key stored in the tenant's
 KernelTenantConfig slice; private key never leaves the holder. Used to
 authenticate kernel.TenantAdmin RPCs and (downstream) any tenant-scoped
 RPC across the cluster.

 A request authenticated by CredPair carries the SPIFFE URI
 `spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/<tenant_name>/users/cred-pair:<id>`.

 `entitlements` must always be a subset of the tenant's ceiling
 (kernel.Constraints.entitlements_ceiling). Enforcement is in
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig.

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is a unique identifier for this cred_pair within its owning tenant.

fields.name: tenant_name
fields.description:
tenant_name names the owning tenant — the namespace that `namespaces` are
 relative to. The cluster cred_pair's owner is the root "/".

fields.name: public_key
fields.description:
public_key is the cred_pair's public key, as a JWK. Mint verifies a
 cred_pair-signed proof against it to issue a token.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: entitlements
fields.description:
entitlements this cred_pair holds (⊆ the owning tenant's ceiling), as the
 SAME TokenEntitlements the C2S authorizer checks: the minted cred_pair token
 sets service_entitlements = this directly (uniform with IDP-user tokens).

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: principal_scope
fields.description:
principal_scope is how wide the caller's authority over PRINCIPALS is, as a
 spec.PrincipalScope enum VALUE NAME (e.g. "PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_ANY"). It is the
 claim the generated (spec.owner_default) guard reads to tell an owner acting
 on its own row from a principal whose authority is wider than itself.
 Absent, empty, PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED and PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_SELF_ONLY all
 mean self-scoped: the guard fails closed, so a policy that stamps nothing
 leaves every caller exactly as narrow as it is today.
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity
 property, never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: namespaces
fields.description:
namespaces are the authorized namespaces, RELATIVE to the owning tenant
 (e.g. "default", "prod", or "*" for all of the tenant's projects). The
 cred_pair can only act at-or-below these and literally cannot name another
 tenant. The cluster cred_pair is relative to "/", so it can span tenants.

fields.name: description
fields.description: description is a human-readable label.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: created_at is when this credential was created.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.description: expires_at is the optional expiry. Zero value means no expiry.

message.name: OpaTenantConfig
message.description:
OpaTenantConfig is the per-tenant OPA policy configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the opa field.
 (OPA lives at the TENANT level — one policy per tenant, evaluated at login;
 it converts IDP claims (groups) into per-project entitlements + authorized
 projects + default project.)

fields.name: entitlements_policy
fields.description: entitlements_policy is the OPA bundle for entitlement evaluation.

message.name: OpaPolicy
message.description:
OpaPolicy defines an OPA policy bundle for authorization evaluation.
 The bundle is a filesystem.Directory tree containing .rego policy files.

fields.name: entry_point
fields.description: entry_point specifies the main package/decision point for policy evaluation.

fields.name: bundle
fields.description: bundle is the directory tree containing .rego policy files.

message.name: Directory
message.description:
Directory represents a directory node in a filesystem tree.
 Directories are recursive — each may contain child directories and files.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the directory name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this directory

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: directories
fields.description: directories holds zero or more child directories

fields.name: files
fields.description: files holds zero or more files in this directory

message.name: File
message.description: File represents a single file with permissions and content.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the file name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this file

fields.name: content
fields.description: content is the raw file content (max 10 MB)

fields.name: created
fields.description: created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the policy was created.

fields.name: version
fields.description: version is an optional version string for this policy (e.g., "1.0.0").
constraints: must be a valid semantic version

fields.name: proxy_policy
fields.description: proxy_policy is the OPA bundle for proxy request policy evaluation.

message.name: OAuthTenantConfig
message.description:
OAuthTenantConfig is the per-tenant OAuth configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the oauth field.
 (IDP lives at the TENANT level — humans log into their tenant's IDP; the
 tenant's OPA policy then derives their per-project entitlements.)

fields.name: providers
fields.description: providers are the tenant's IDPs (e.g. a corporate Okta instance).

message.name: OAuthProvider
message.description:
OAuthProvider describes a tenant-owned IDP. The (issuer_url, client_id) pair
 uniquely identifies this tenant — no claim matching needed.

fields.name: issuer_url
fields.description: issuer_url is the OpenID Connect issuer. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the OAuth2 client identifier. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the OAuth2 client secret; comes from secrets overlay layer.

fields.name: allowed_scopes
fields.description: allowed_scopes are the OAuth2 scopes requested from this IDP.

fields.name: jwks_uri
fields.description: jwks_uri overrides the auto-discovered JWKS endpoint.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description: ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate for self-signed IDPs.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this provider.

fields.name: claim_matchers
fields.description: claim_matchers route users from cluster-level shared IDPs to this tenant.

message.name: ClaimMatcher
message.description:
ClaimMatcher routes users arriving via a cluster-level shared IDP to this tenant.
 The token has already been validated against the cluster IDP before matching.

fields.name: provider_issuer_url
fields.description: provider_issuer_url identifies which cluster IDP this rule applies to.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: claim_key
fields.description: claim_key is the JWT claim name (e.g. "hd", "email").

fields.name: claim_value
fields.description: claim_value is the expected value (e.g. "mycompany.com").

message.name: TenantConfigEntry
message.description:
TenantConfigEntry maps a tenant_name to its full TenantConfig (the tacplus
 config slices: kernel cred_pairs, oauth IDP, opa policy). TenantAdmin RPCs
 write these.

message.name: TenantConfig
message.description:
TenantConfig aggregates per-service tenant configuration slices.
 Field names match service names; field numbers are stable via registry.yaml.

message.name: KernelTenantConfig
message.description:
KernelTenantConfig is the per-tenant kernel configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the kernel field.

fields.name: cred_pairs
fields.description:
cred_pairs are the tenant's cred_pairs (JWK + entitlements + tenant-relative
 namespaces). They authenticate management RPCs as ordinary C2S identities
 (no P2S). Public keys only — private keys never enter the cluster. The
 creating root registers the tenant's first cred_pair public key via
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig (bootstrap); nothing is minted or
 delivered server-side. Holders generate their own keypairs off-cluster.

message.name: CredPair
message.description:
CredPair is a tenant-scoped credential. Public key stored in the tenant's
 KernelTenantConfig slice; private key never leaves the holder. Used to
 authenticate kernel.TenantAdmin RPCs and (downstream) any tenant-scoped
 RPC across the cluster.

 A request authenticated by CredPair carries the SPIFFE URI
 `spiffe://<spiffe_prefix>/<tenant_name>/users/cred-pair:<id>`.

 `entitlements` must always be a subset of the tenant's ceiling
 (kernel.Constraints.entitlements_ceiling). Enforcement is in
 kernel.TenantAdmin.SetTenantConfig.

fields.name: id
fields.description: id is a unique identifier for this cred_pair within its owning tenant.

fields.name: tenant_name
fields.description:
tenant_name names the owning tenant — the namespace that `namespaces` are
 relative to. The cluster cred_pair's owner is the root "/".

fields.name: public_key
fields.description:
public_key is the cred_pair's public key, as a JWK. Mint verifies a
 cred_pair-signed proof against it to issue a token.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: entitlements
fields.description:
entitlements this cred_pair holds (⊆ the owning tenant's ceiling), as the
 SAME TokenEntitlements the C2S authorizer checks: the minted cred_pair token
 sets service_entitlements = this directly (uniform with IDP-user tokens).

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: principal_scope
fields.description:
principal_scope is how wide the caller's authority over PRINCIPALS is, as a
 spec.PrincipalScope enum VALUE NAME (e.g. "PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_ANY"). It is the
 claim the generated (spec.owner_default) guard reads to tell an owner acting
 on its own row from a principal whose authority is wider than itself.
 Absent, empty, PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED and PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_SELF_ONLY all
 mean self-scoped: the guard fails closed, so a policy that stamps nothing
 leaves every caller exactly as narrow as it is today.
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity
 property, never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: namespaces
fields.description:
namespaces are the authorized namespaces, RELATIVE to the owning tenant
 (e.g. "default", "prod", or "*" for all of the tenant's projects). The
 cred_pair can only act at-or-below these and literally cannot name another
 tenant. The cluster cred_pair is relative to "/", so it can span tenants.

fields.name: description
fields.description: description is a human-readable label.

fields.name: created_at
fields.description: created_at is when this credential was created.

fields.name: expires_at
fields.description: expires_at is the optional expiry. Zero value means no expiry.

message.name: OpaTenantConfig
message.description:
OpaTenantConfig is the per-tenant OPA policy configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the opa field.
 (OPA lives at the TENANT level — one policy per tenant, evaluated at login;
 it converts IDP claims (groups) into per-project entitlements + authorized
 projects + default project.)

fields.name: entitlements_policy
fields.description: entitlements_policy is the OPA bundle for entitlement evaluation.

message.name: OpaPolicy
message.description:
OpaPolicy defines an OPA policy bundle for authorization evaluation.
 The bundle is a filesystem.Directory tree containing .rego policy files.

fields.name: entry_point
fields.description: entry_point specifies the main package/decision point for policy evaluation.

fields.name: bundle
fields.description: bundle is the directory tree containing .rego policy files.

message.name: Directory
message.description:
Directory represents a directory node in a filesystem tree.
 Directories are recursive — each may contain child directories and files.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the directory name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this directory

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: directories
fields.description: directories holds zero or more child directories

fields.name: files
fields.description: files holds zero or more files in this directory

message.name: File
message.description: File represents a single file with permissions and content.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is the file name (not a path)

fields.name: permission
fields.description: permission is the Unix-style permission for this file

fields.name: content
fields.description: content is the raw file content (max 10 MB)

fields.name: created
fields.description: created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the policy was created.

fields.name: version
fields.description: version is an optional version string for this policy (e.g., "1.0.0").
constraints: must be a valid semantic version

fields.name: proxy_policy
fields.description: proxy_policy is the OPA bundle for proxy request policy evaluation.

message.name: OAuthTenantConfig
message.description:
OAuthTenantConfig is the per-tenant OAuth configuration slice.
 Tacplus auto-generates TenantConfig with this as the oauth field.
 (IDP lives at the TENANT level — humans log into their tenant's IDP; the
 tenant's OPA policy then derives their per-project entitlements.)

fields.name: providers
fields.description: providers are the tenant's IDPs (e.g. a corporate Okta instance).

message.name: OAuthProvider
message.description:
OAuthProvider describes a tenant-owned IDP. The (issuer_url, client_id) pair
 uniquely identifies this tenant — no claim matching needed.

fields.name: issuer_url
fields.description: issuer_url is the OpenID Connect issuer. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: client_id
fields.description: client_id is the OAuth2 client identifier. Part of the (iss, aud) lookup key.

fields.name: client_secret
fields.description: client_secret is the OAuth2 client secret; comes from secrets overlay layer.

fields.name: allowed_scopes
fields.description: allowed_scopes are the OAuth2 scopes requested from this IDP.

fields.name: jwks_uri
fields.description: jwks_uri overrides the auto-discovered JWKS endpoint.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: ca_pem
fields.description: ca_pem is an optional PEM-encoded CA certificate for self-signed IDPs.

fields.name: enable
fields.description: enable enables or disables this provider.

fields.name: claim_matchers
fields.description: claim_matchers route users from cluster-level shared IDPs to this tenant.

message.name: ClaimMatcher
message.description:
ClaimMatcher routes users arriving via a cluster-level shared IDP to this tenant.
 The token has already been validated against the cluster IDP before matching.

fields.name: provider_issuer_url
fields.description: provider_issuer_url identifies which cluster IDP this rule applies to.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: claim_key
fields.description: claim_key is the JWT claim name (e.g. "hd", "email").

fields.name: claim_value
fields.description: claim_value is the expected value (e.g. "mycompany.com").

types.name: TenantMembership
types.description:
TenantMembership is one person's membership of one tenant. It is the record
 that authorizes minting a /tenants/<t> token for this principal (see
 Mint.MintToken's tenant_namespace): no live membership, no token.

fields.name: tenant_namespace
fields.description: tenant_namespace is the canonical /tenants/<name> form, never a bare name.

enum_values.name: MEMBERSHIP_PROOF_KIND_TENANT_IDP
enum_values.description: The tenant's own IdP (Entra, Google Workspace, Keycloak, ...).

enum_values.name: MEMBERSHIP_PROOF_KIND_EMAIL_LINK
enum_values.description: A link emailed to an address the tenant's admin authorized (§6 item 5).

enum_values.name: MEMBERSHIP_PROOF_KIND_LINKED_PERSONAL_IDENTITY
enum_values.description:
The admin linked this personal principal directly; the device login alone
 suffices thereafter (login doc §2b proof 3).

fields.name: customer
fields.description:
customer designates this membership as customer-facing: the person deals
 with the tenant as an outside party, not as a worker inside it. It is a
 DESIGNATION ON THIS MEMBERSHIP, deliberately not a principal kind — the same
 person is a customer of one tenant and a member of another, and may be both
 of the same tenant over time. Mint intersects the requested service_auds
 with the tenant's customer-facing service list when this is set.

fields.name: proof_reference
fields.description:
proof_reference is the opaque handle to what was proved (the tenant IdP
 subject, the redeemed link id). Opaque to kernel, never an email string —
 login doc §2 rules out comparing email strings, and nothing here does.

fields.name: revoked_at_ms
fields.description:
revoked_at_ms marks, never deletes: a departure is a withdrawal that must
 remain visible in the audit trail (login doc §7 bullet 3).

types.name: TenantUserLink
types.description:
TenantUserLink is one edge out of a linked tenant user: which identity in
 another tenant is the same human. Linking is GENERIC — any two tenants, not
 `people` and one other. The first use is drpepper's `jody` linked to that
 human's `people` row, but a contractor in two companies and a tenant
 migrating IdPs are the same record.

 peer_namespace, not a peer user path, is what the token's `linked` claim
 carries. The generated namespace backstop compares that claim against
 (spec.store_namespace), which holds a NAMESPACE, so a user path would never
 compare equal and a linked caller's read would never be accepted.

fields.name: peer_namespace
fields.description: peer_namespace is the canonical /tenants/<t> the linked identity lives in.

fields.name: peer_subject
fields.description:
peer_subject is the linked identity's `sub` as kernel mints it. Kernel
 keeps it because peer_namespace alone does not identify a human, and
 because a re-key has to find and rewrite the edge that names one user.

fields.name: revoked_at_ms
fields.description:
revoked_at_ms is the unlink mark. Marks, never deletes — the same audit rule
 Grant.revoked_at_ms and PersonalCredential.revoked_at_ms state, and for the
 stronger reason here that a link is proved once by live credentials and
 nothing kernel holds can re-derive it: a deleted edge is indistinguishable
 from one that was never proved.

 A revoked edge contributes no `linked` claim at mint. Re-proving the same
 link clears the mark rather than adding a second edge, because the same two
 credentials presented again are the same fact.

types.name: TenantUserLinkSide
types.description:
TenantUserLinkSide is one half of a link: either one IdP login the calling
 broker has just verified, or one device that has just signed a WebAuthn
 assertion. Exactly one of the two shapes is set.

fields.name: claims
fields.description:
claims are the verified IdP claims, the same shape MintUserToken carries —
 the IdP's own iss/sub/nonce under origin_*, copied verbatim out of the
 id_token the broker verified. origin_iss, origin_sub and origin_nonce are
 all required ON AN IdP SIDE: a side with no nonce cannot be bound to the
 other side. Absent on a device side, which carries no login at all.

 NOT assert_required, because a device side has no claims to carry. The
 handler requires exactly one of (claims, device_assertion) per side and
 refuses a side that sets both or neither — a check a field-level assertion
 cannot express.

fields.name: subject
fields.description:
subject is the SPIFFE user id this login resolves to, as
 MintUserTokenRequest.subject carries it. Required for an ordinary tenant
 side, where it is what names the user; IGNORED on a `people` side, which
 derives its user id from the verified claims and takes nothing from the
 request, and IGNORED on a device side, which derives its principal from the
 credential the assertion is signed by.

fields.name: device_assertion
fields.description:
device_assertion is a WebAuthn assertion signed by the device's passkey.
 Setting it makes this a DEVICE side: the peer side must then be a `people`
 side, and the two are bound by the pair of checks the §3 design names —
 the peer's id_token `nonce` is this key's RFC 7638 thumbprint, and this
 assertion's challenge names that exact login. Neither half alone is
 accepted and nothing can be replayed onto a different device.

message.name: WebauthnAssertion
message.description:
WebauthnAssertion is one WebAuthn (passkey) assertion, exactly as the
 authenticator produced it — the four fields of an
 AuthenticatorAssertionResponse, unaltered.

 NOTHING HERE IS PARSED BY A BROKER AND BELIEVED. Kernel recomputes the signed
 bytes itself (authenticator_data || SHA-256(client_data_json)), reads the
 challenge out of client_data_json itself, and verifies signature against the
 credential's own public key itself. A broker that rewrote any of these four
 fields produces a proof that fails, which is what keeps "compromising the
 broker forges no identity" (personalauth.proto's header) true of this path
 too.

 NO ATTESTATION OBJECT, DELIBERATELY. This is the desktop-passkey arm of the
 identity decision doc's §3 — the one whose device proof is explicitly the
 weaker one, because Windows/Linux have no App Attest / Play Integrity. The
 public key therefore arrives as an ordinary jwk.Jwk (the platform's key type
 everywhere else, including CreatePersonalPrincipal) and is trusted only as
 far as the nonce binding makes it trustworthy: the IdP's id_token carries
 that key's RFC 7638 thumbprint as its `nonce`, so a substituted key has no
 matching login. App Attest and Play Integrity are named as follow-ons, not
 stubbed: both need live verification against Apple's and Google's own
 services, and a mocked verifier would be a device proof nobody could trust.

fields.name: credential_id
fields.description:
credential_id is the authenticator's credential id, base64url without
 padding. It becomes PersonalCredential.credential_id.

fields.name: authenticator_data
fields.description: authenticator_data is the raw authenticatorData the authenticator signed.

fields.name: client_data_json
fields.description:
client_data_json is the raw clientDataJSON the authenticator signed over
 the SHA-256 of. Kernel parses it for `type` and `challenge`; both are
 checked, and the challenge is what binds this assertion to one IdP login.

fields.name: signature
fields.description:
signature is the authenticator's signature over
 authenticator_data || SHA-256(client_data_json), in the encoding the key's
 algorithm defines (DER for ECDSA, raw for Ed25519, PKCS#1 v1.5 for RSA).

fields.name: device_public_key
fields.description:
device_public_key is the public half of the passkey, as a jwk.Jwk. Kernel
 verifies device_assertion against THIS key on a first link — the same
 bootstrap CreatePersonalPrincipal has, where the key must come out of the
 request because no stored credential exists yet — and against the STORED
 key on every link after that. The request's copy is never consulted again
 once the credential row exists.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP

fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: x

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: device_label
fields.description: device_label is human-facing ("Jody's ThinkPad"), stored on the credential.

fields.name: device_platform_synced
fields.description:
device_platform_synced records whether the passkey lives in a synced
 credential store (iCloud Keychain / Google passkey) or on this device only,
 exactly as CreatePersonalPrincipalRequest.platform_synced does.

types.name: TenantUserLinks
types.description:
TenantUserLinks is ONE tenant user's links.

 Keyed per user, and written on BOTH sides of every link, deliberately: this
 is read on every user mint, so it must be one O(1) keyed lookup and not a
 scan of every row for one that mentions the caller.

fields.name: user_key
fields.description:
user_key identifies the linked user as "<namespace>|<sub>" — the exact
 namespace and sub claims kernel mints for them. Deliberately the minted
 pair rather than a derived path: an ordinary tenant's `sub` is whatever its
 IdP broker supplies (an email, today) and is not required to be a SPIFFE
 id, so there is no path to derive. The namespace half is what keeps two
 tenants' identically-named users apart.

TenantUserLink is one edge out of a linked tenant user: which identity in
 another tenant is the same human. Linking is GENERIC — any two tenants, not

 human's `people` row, but a contractor in two companies and a tenant
 migrating IdPs are the same record.

 peer_namespace, not a peer user path, is what the token's `linked` claim
 carries. The generated namespace backstop compares that claim against
 (spec.store_namespace), which holds a NAMESPACE, so a user path would never
 compare equal and a linked caller's read would never be accepted.

fields.name: peer_namespace
fields.description: peer_namespace is the canonical /tenants/<t> the linked identity lives in.

fields.name: peer_subject
fields.description:
peer_subject is the linked identity's `sub` as kernel mints it. Kernel
 keeps it because peer_namespace alone does not identify a human, and
 because a re-key has to find and rewrite the edge that names one user.

fields.name: revoked_at_ms
fields.description:
revoked_at_ms is the unlink mark. Marks, never deletes — the same audit rule
 Grant.revoked_at_ms and PersonalCredential.revoked_at_ms state, and for the
 stronger reason here that a link is proved once by live credentials and

 from one that was never proved.

 link clears the mark rather than adding a second edge, because the same two

fields.name: peer_subject
fields.description:
peer_subject is the linked identity's `sub` as kernel mints it. Kernel
 keeps it because peer_namespace alone does not identify a human, and
 because a re-key has to find and rewrite the edge that names one user.

fields.name: revoked_at_ms
fields.description:
revoked_at_ms is the unlink mark. Marks, never deletes — the same audit rule
 Grant.revoked_at_ms and PersonalCredential.revoked_at_ms state, and for the
 stronger reason here that a link is proved once by live credentials and
 nothing kernel holds can re-derive it: a deleted edge is indistinguishable
 from one that was never proved.

 A revoked edge contributes no `linked` claim at mint. Re-proving the same
 link clears the mark rather than adding a second edge, because the same two
 credentials presented again are the same fact.

types.name: TenantUserLinksQueryRequest
TenantUserLinksQueryResponse

message.name: TenantUserLinks
message.description:
TenantUserLinks is ONE tenant user's links.

 Keyed per user, and written on BOTH sides of every link, deliberately: this
 is read on every user mint, so it must be one O(1) keyed lookup and not a
 scan of every row for one that mentions the caller.

fields.name: user_key
fields.description:
user_key identifies the linked user as "<namespace>|<sub>" — the exact
 namespace and sub claims kernel mints for them. Deliberately the minted
 pair rather than a derived path: an ordinary tenant's `sub` is whatever its
 IdP broker supplies (an email, today) and is not required to be a SPIFFE
 id, so there is no path to derive. The namespace half is what keeps two
 tenants' identically-named users apart.

message.name: TenantUserLink
message.description:
TenantUserLink is one edge out of a linked tenant user: which identity in
 another tenant is the same human. Linking is GENERIC — any two tenants, not
 `people` and one other. The first use is drpepper's `jody` linked to that
 human's `people` row, but a contractor in two companies and a tenant
 migrating IdPs are the same record.

 peer_namespace, not a peer user path, is what the token's `linked` claim
 carries. The generated namespace backstop compares that claim against
 (spec.store_namespace), which holds a NAMESPACE, so a user path would never
 compare equal and a linked caller's read would never be accepted.

fields.name: peer_namespace
fields.description: peer_namespace is the canonical /tenants/<t> the linked identity lives in.

fields.name: peer_subject
fields.description:
peer_subject is the linked identity's `sub` as kernel mints it. Kernel
 keeps it because peer_namespace alone does not identify a human, and
 because a re-key has to find and rewrite the edge that names one user.

message.name: Tenant
message.description:
Tenant is the core identity record for a tenant in the cluster.
 `name` is unique, immutable, and becomes the tenant's SPIFFE segment:
   spiffe://<trust-domain>/tenants/<name>/...

fields.name: constraints
fields.description:
constraints is the ancestor-set limits (entitlements ceiling now; domain
 later). Set at creation; mutable only by an ancestor.

message.name: Constraints
message.description:
Constraints are the limits an ancestor places on a tenant. They live on the
 Tenant record (set at CreateTenant), are mutable only by an ancestor, and are
 immutable to the tenant itself — so the tenant genuinely cannot raise its own
 limits. Validated on CreateTenant and SetTenantConfig.

 (The "min-admin-credential" rule — config must always contain >=1 cred_pair
 entitled to administer the tenant — is NOT a field here: it is an always-on
 invariant enforced in the SetTenantConfig validation path, satisfiable by
 create-and-discard. It is not an ancestor toggle.)

fields.name: entitlements_ceiling
fields.description:
entitlements_ceiling is the maximum set of entitlements anyone inside this
 tenant may ever hold. Every cred_pair's entitlements ⊆ this; a sub-tenant's
 ceiling ⊆ this. Replaces the former standalone Tenant.entitlements field.

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: principal_scope
fields.description:
principal_scope is how wide the caller's authority over PRINCIPALS is, as a
 spec.PrincipalScope enum VALUE NAME (e.g. "PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_ANY"). It is the
 claim the generated (spec.owner_default) guard reads to tell an owner acting
 on its own row from a principal whose authority is wider than itself.
 Absent, empty, PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED and PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_SELF_ONLY all
 mean self-scoped: the guard fails closed, so a policy that stamps nothing
 leaves every caller exactly as narrow as it is today.
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity
 property, never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)
