 EQ-queryable since 2026-09-25, and that is half the annotation rather than
 decoration: the c2s record-read plane REFUSES C2S_SCOPE_PRINCIPAL when no
 principal criterion resolves (rather than degrading it to a tenant-wide
 read), and the handler pins this same field into the predicate before the
 store is asked, which is what keeps `total` this person's own count instead
 of the fleet's.

fields.name: archived
fields.description:
archived hides the chat from the live list. It is NOT terminal —
 UpdateChatMembership clears it. Purging a chat would be a Delete, and there
 is none: a chat is never gone.

fields.name: muted
fields.description:
muted: Scotty surfaces nothing from this chat unless notify_policy_text
 says otherwise.

fields.name: notify_policy_text
fields.description:
notify_policy_text is this person's standing instruction to THEIR OWN
 Scotty about this chat ("only tell me if there is something I should
 know"). Read by that runtime and nothing else; prose by nature, and no
 other member's runtime may read it — the principal pin above is what makes
 that true rather than promised.

fields.name: last_read_seq
fields.description:
last_read_seq is this owner's ChatEvent.seq high-water mark, which is what
 "unread" is computed from.

 IT INHERITS ChatEvent.seq's UNSOLVED ASSIGNMENT. Read that field's comment
 before treating this number as a reliable watermark: until per-owner seq
 assignment has an answer, so does unread.

fields.name: last_event_at_ms
fields.description:
last_event_at_ms orders the chat list. Maintained by the handler when it
 appends this owner's copy of an event.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace: see ChatSession.namespace. EQ-queryable because tacplus refuses
 (spec.record).c2s_read on a record whose (spec.store_namespace) field is
 not: the client-facing plane pins the field to the caller's verified claim
 before the store is asked, and a pin needs a criterion to be pinned into.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record's declared `owner` and the PUBLISHER — this
 SERVICE, never the person. `principal` above is where the person is. See
 Chat.spiffe_id for why the name is load-bearing and why it is never a read
 filter.

types.name: GetChatRequest
GetChatResponse

message.name: Chat
message.description:
Chat is who is in a conversation. It is the one row in this service that
 belongs to SEVERAL people at once, and that is the whole difficulty with it.

 NO (spec.store_principal), AND THAT IS NOT AN OMISSION. The annotation pins a
 row to exactly one subject — tacplus refuses a second field carrying it
 (`principal_validate.go`, recorded in decisions/work-service-2026-09-09.md
 VERIFY answer 4) — and a chat with four participants has no one owner to pin
 to. `created_by` would pin reads to the creator and hide the chat from
 everyone else in it. So this collection gets NO generated egress filter, and
 "only a member may read a chat" is a hand-written check in the handler,
 enforced against the caller's own ChatMembership row.

 That is the same unbuilt entitlement gap `scotty.Human` records (see
 schematic/looper/schematic/decisions/scotty-read-authorization-not-wired.md)
 and it is NOT solved here. What IS structural is the membership row: every
 list of chats goes through ChatMembership, which is principal-pinned, so the
 only way to learn a chat_id you are not in is to be told one.

 A stratum record since 2026-09-25, and the ONE of this file's four with no
 owning principal — which is exactly what decides its record shape. Read the
 (spec.record_read) block at the top of this file for why it gets no c2s half.

fields.name: chat_id
fields.description:
chat_id is DERIVED for the singletons and minted otherwise:
   DIRECT: "direct/<min(a,b)>/<max(a,b)>"  — 1:1, one per pair by
           construction, so CreateChat on an existing pair returns it
           instead of making a second one.
   SELF default: "self/<principal>/default" — the catch-all a message with
           no chat lands in.
   SELF other, GROUP, JOB: minted timestamp-first.

 (spec.indexed) WAS HERE AND IS GONE WITH THE STATE COLLECTION: it is the
 statedb field-index marker, and there is no state map left to index. The
 key is an EQ criterion on ChatFilter without any annotation, because
 declaring s2s_read above folds a record's key into its filter
 (record_map.go's keyFilterCriterion) — which is what the point read behind
 GetChat is.

enum_values.name: CHAT_KIND_SELF_CHAT
enum_values.description:
SELF: the user and their own Scotty. Goes nowhere. Many per user.

 NAMED _SELF_CHAT AND NOT _SELF, and that is a tacplus defect worked around
 rather than a shade of meaning. `CHAT_KIND_SELF` renders as the Rust variant
 `Self`, which is a reserved word: prost's own emitter sanitizes it to
 `Self_`, but tacplus's `toProstEnumVariant`
 (pkg/internal/rust/types/enums.go:229) PascalCases without consulting its
 own `rustKeywords` set, so the serde and helper files it generates alongside
 say `ChatKind::Self` and the model crate does not compile:
   error[E0433]: `Self` in paths can only be used in start position
     types/services/scottypersonal/helpers.rs:25  "chat-kind-self" => Ok(ChatKind::Self)
     types/services/scottypersonal/scottypersonal.serde.rs:2364  Self::Self => "CHAT_KIND_SELF"
 (verified 2026-09-11 against tacplus c33d7d56 by building services/work,
 the first Rust service generated since this enum landed). The upstream fix
 is for toProstEnumVariant to mirror prost's trailing-underscore rule; until
 it does, no proto in this fleet may end an enum value in _SELF. Rename this
 back the day that lands — nothing has ever been stored under either name.

enum_values.name: CHAT_KIND_DIRECT
enum_values.description: DIRECT: two people (and their Scottys). One per pair.

enum_values.name: CHAT_KIND_GROUP
enum_values.description: GROUP: people who join and leave.

enum_values.name: CHAT_KIND_JOB
enum_values.description:
JOB: a GROUP whose closure is company-wide. Reserved from the 2026-09-07
 sketch: the job type does not exist yet and nothing here invents it.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
participants are HUMAN principals and AGENT identities. The caller's own
 Scotty is implicit in every chat and is not listed; a participant of kind
 AGENT is a NAMED one (a DocManager, a JobManager, a customer's agent).

 A PARTICIPANT IS A PERSONAL PRINCIPAL, not a per-tenant identity, for the
 same reason ChatSession.principal is: the chat spans every tenant its
 members belong to. A member of this chat is not thereby a member of any
 tenant — where work gets FILED is the routing map's business, and
 GetMyRoutingMap answers it separately for each person.

fields.name: principal
fields.description: principal is a token subject for HUMAN, an agent identity for AGENT.

fields.name: joined_at_ms
fields.description: joined_at_ms is stamped by the handler, never by the caller.

fields.name: title
fields.description:
title is set by the creator or by Scotty (through UpdateChat). Prose;
 nothing derives from it.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace: see ChatSession.namespace. Same field, same open question about
 what claim a personal principal carries, same reason for keeping it.

 EQ-queryable since 2026-09-25, because it is now the ONLY pin this record
 has: with no owning principal, the caller's verified namespace is the whole
 of what `require_chat` pins into the store predicate before it asks (the
 same value it compared in-process when these rows came from kernel).

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record's declared `owner` and the PUBLISHER — eventbus
 stamps this service's own identity onto it. The field NAME is load-bearing
 (eventbus's topic discovery matches the literal string "spiffe_id" of
 string type when it decides which topics get publisher-identity stamping),
 which is why it carries (spec.identity_spiffe_subject) exactly as
 work.WorkActivity.spiffe_id does.

 IT IS THE SERVICE, NOT A PERSON, and so it is never a read filter. Every
 row of this type in the fleet carries the same value; narrowing a read by
 it would show a reader every chat in the fleet while looking like it
 narrowed something.

types.name: GetChatSessionPageRequest
GetChatSessionPageResponse

message.name: ChatSession
message.description:
ChatSession is what one person's Scotty is currently holding in mind about
 one chat. It is knowledge, re-derivable from ChatEvent; it is not an
 artifact, which is why this service's state root carries no
 requires_artifact_on_write. What Scotty DOES from a chat leaves its artifact
 where the doing happens — a ticket in the tenant that owns it.

 A stratum record since 2026-09-25, principal-owned and NOT `private` — see
 the (spec.record_read) block at the top of this file. THIS is the one type in
 this file that `private` would fit on its own terms (it is never read across
 owners); it stays non-private with its siblings because the reader it would
 need does not exist, and because one private row among three ordinary ones
 buys a second plane client and no guarantee the store_principal pin does not
 already give.

fields.name: session_id
fields.description:
session_id is the record key: "<chat_id>/<principal>". Derived rather than
 minted, so one person has exactly one session per chat by construction and
 a second one cannot be created by racing.

 (spec.indexed) is gone with the state collection — see Chat.chat_id.

fields.name: principal
fields.description:
principal is the OWNING principal, and it is the whole egress mechanism for
 this collection: (spec.store_principal) generates the read-side filter that
 pins every surface returning this row to the caller's own subject.

 It is the PERSONAL principal (login doc §2b: the device's synced keychain
 key), never a per-tenant identity. That is the split: this row is one
 person's, across every tenant they belong to, and there is no tenant-scoped
 reader of it at all.

 EQ-queryable since 2026-09-25 — see ChatMembership.principal for why that
 is half the annotation and not decoration.

fields.name: state_text
fields.description:
state_text is the ONE generic text field Jody asked for: the LLM gets it,
 modifies it, puts it back whole. Nothing parses it, nothing derives
 authority from it, and NO FACT MAY LIVE ONLY HERE — see the 2026-09-07
 decision doc §2. In particular the routing map is not remembered here: it
 is read from kernel every time (login doc §4, and GetMyRoutingMap below).

fields.name: state_version
fields.description:
state_version increments on every replace and must be presented on the
 next replace. A stale replace is FAILED_PRECONDITION. Cheap insurance
 against a dormant session that woke twice.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning namespace, held to the reader's claim by
 exact equality by the generated egress filter.

 WHAT VALUE A PERSONAL PRINCIPAL'S ROWS CARRY IS NOT SETTLED, and this is
 the one place the service split reaches down to a field. Device principals
 do not exist yet (login doc §6 item 1) and nothing has decided what
 namespace claim one holds. What IS settled is that it must not be a
 TENANT's: a personal chat spans every tenant the person belongs to, so
 pinning the row to one tenant would contradict §3's "the personal runtime
 sees everything the user sees".

 The field is kept — with the marker — rather than dropped, because
 (spec.store_namespace) is only mandatory on a (spec.record) and a state row
 may legally omit it, which would mean silently generating NO egress
 backstop at all. Whoever settles the device-principal claim settles this
 field's value; the annotation is not the thing to remove if it turns out
 the claim is empty.

 MANDATORY NOW, not merely kept: tacplus's ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations
 fails generation for a (spec.record) declaring no such field, "on the
 reasoning that the record nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one
 that leaks". The paragraph above anticipated this ("(spec.store_namespace)
 is only mandatory on a (spec.record)") — the move to stratum is what made
 it so. EQ-queryable because c2s_read requires it.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record's declared `owner` and the PUBLISHER — this
 SERVICE, never the person. See Chat.spiffe_id.

GetChatSessionResponse

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record's declared `owner` and the PUBLISHER — this
 SERVICE, never the person. See Chat.spiffe_id.

types.name: GetMyRoutingMapRequest
types.description:
GetMyRoutingMapRequest carries NO caller identity a caller may set.

 `principal` is the ordinary (spec.principal) marker: the generated MCP
 dispatch computes it from the verified caller, OMITS it from the published
 tool schema and REFUSES a tool call that names it. "My memberships" is
 therefore not a filter the model is trusted to pass — it is a value the model
 cannot express, which is what makes "it never invents a destination"
 structural rather than a prompt instruction that can drift.

 NO (spec.namespace) FIELD, for the reason the other two MCP reads in this
 fleet carry none: the request-side marker's job is to bind a value the
 handler then STAMPS ONTO A ROW, and this rpc writes nothing. It would be
 actively wrong here besides — a namespace on this request would be the caller
 asking about ONE tenant, and the whole point of the map is that it spans
 every tenant the person belongs to.

types.name: GetMyRoutingMapResponse
types.description:
GetMyRoutingMapResponse is the complete map, not a page of it. A person's
 memberships are counted in ones and tens — login doc §1's "anybody can access
 multiple accounts", not thousands — so a paging surface would be machinery
 for a case that does not occur, and a partial routing map is worse than
 useless: it is a map that omits a legitimate home and makes Scotty file into
 the wrong one.

fields.name: memberships
fields.description:
memberships are the homes. Empty is a complete and meaningful answer: a
 brand-new personal principal with no tenant yet has nowhere business can
 go, and everything stays personal.

message.name: TenantMembership
message.description:
TenantMembership is one home this person is entitled to file things in.

 IT IS NOT THIS SERVICE'S ROW. Memberships are kernel state on the personal
 principal (login doc §6 item 3), so nothing below appears in
 ScottypersonalState and no RPC here creates, updates or deletes one — this is
 the shape of an ANSWER, not of a store. That placement is the point of §4
 rule 2: "the routing map is not something Scotty learns; the kernel tells
 him." A membership Scotty remembered instead of read is a home the kernel may
 already have revoked.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the tenant, in the canonical vocabulary DECISIONS.md item 5
 fixes: "/tenants/<name>". It is the value a per-tenant delegated token is
 minted for and the value that names the home in a readback.

fields.name: display_name
fields.description:
display_name is the tenant's human-readable name, empty when kernel has
 none. It exists because login doc §4's disambiguation is a SPOKEN one —
 "Jimerson reminder: call Mike Faraday Friday" — and a readback that says
 "/tenants/jimerson" has not confirmed anything to a person.

fields.name: customer
fields.description:
customer marks a membership that is scoped to the tenant's customer-facing
 service and nothing else. Jody: "think of customer as just a service inside
 a tenant" (login doc §1). Routing-relevant, not merely descriptive: it is
 the difference between a home a person can file work into and one where
 they can only deal with that tenant as an outsider.

fields.name: trace_id
fields.description:
NO PROOF TYPE FIELD. A membership carries how it was proven — tenant IdP,
 emailed link, linked personal Scotty (login doc §1, §6 item 3) — and that
 fact belongs to LOGIN, not to routing. The runtime reading this map is
 choosing among homes that already exist; how each was established changes
 none of them. Add it when something actually reads it.

fields.name: links
fields.description:
links are the tenant-to-tenant relationships where from_namespace is one of
 the memberships above. Not every link in the fleet — only the ones this
 person's own memberships put them on one end of.

message.name: TenantLink
message.description:
TenantLink is a relationship between two tenants that is relevant to this
 person because one end of it is one of their memberships.

 A LINK IS CONTEXT, NOT A DESTINATION. Joe files his work in Jimerson;
 knowing Jimerson is a customer of Acme is what lets Scotty understand a
 request about Acme without concluding that Acme is a home Joe may write to.
 The homes are the memberships above and only those.

enum_values.name: TENANT_LINK_KIND_CUSTOMER_OF
enum_values.description:
from_namespace is a CUSTOMER OF to_namespace. Login doc §4's own example:
 "Joe works for Jimerson. Jimerson is a customer of Acme" — from=jimerson,
 to=acme.

fields.name: to_display_name
fields.description:
display_name of to_namespace, for the same readback reason
 TenantMembership.display_name exists. from_namespace's name is already
 carried by the membership it matches.

types.name: ListChatEventsRequest

fields.name: chat_id
fields.description: chat_id empty is every chat the caller is in — the unified timeline.

types.name: ListChatEventsResponse

message.name: ChatEvent
message.description:
ChatEvent is the append-only record of what was said and what Scotty did. One
 row per OWNER copy, which is what makes history entitleable per person with
 no hand-written check: `owner` carries (spec.store_principal) and the
 generated filter does the rest.

 A stratum record since 2026-09-25, principal-owned and NOT `private` — see
 the (spec.record_read) block at the top of this file, whose second reason is
 about THIS type: one logical event is one row per member, and appending it
 reads every other member's high-water seq. A pin that admits only the
 caller's own rows cannot do that.

fields.name: event_key
fields.description:
event_key is the record key: "<event_id>/<owner>". event_id for a sent
 message is "<chat_id>/<sender>/<client_message_id>", which is what makes a
 retried send rewrite the same rows instead of appending duplicates.
 Service-originated events mint event_id timestamp-first.

 (spec.indexed) is gone with the state collection — see Chat.chat_id.

fields.name: chat_id
fields.description:
chat_id is the ONE predicate this file pushes down past the two pins, and
 it is the exception that proves work's rule (its D4: "there is no predicate
 pushdown here beyond the tenant"). Two things make it different. It is a
 DECLARED PARAMETER of both reads that use it — ListChatEvents(chat_id) and
 ListMyChatHistory(chat_id) — rather than a predicate the handler invents;
 and this collection is the largest in the file by two orders of magnitude
 (its state bound was 10,000,000 against Chat's 100,000), so "every event
 this person owns, then filter" is the one read here where the difference
 is a number rather than a preference. An empty chat_id is still the
 unified timeline: the criterion is simply not sent.

fields.name: owner
fields.description:
owner is whose COPY this is — the personal principal, as on ChatSession.
 EQ-queryable since 2026-09-25 — see ChatMembership.principal.

fields.name: seq
fields.description:
seq is monotonic PER OWNER across all their chats: it is the WATCH revision
 and the PAGE keyset in one.

 HOW IT IS ASSIGNED IS OPEN, and the split is what opened it. The 2026-09-07
 sketch assigns it under the owner's kernel.FencedLock, copying scottyagent
 — but that needs (spec.grpc_s2s_client) = {service: "kernel.FencedLock"},
 which is service-identity S2S reach and is exactly what DECISIONS.md item
 9c denies this class of service. A delegated user token cannot stand in: a
 per-owner sequence is the SERVICE's bookkeeping, not an action taken on the
 user's behalf, and it must hold across owners who are mid-turn in different
 tenants. Nothing here decides the answer — the field's meaning is unchanged
 whichever way it is assigned. Written up rather than improvised.

fields.name: author
fields.description:
author is the principal whose message or action this is; author_actor is
 the delegate that produced it (the author's Scotty), empty when the human
 did it directly. Same split as scotty.TicketDecision.decided_by /
 decided_by_actor and messaging.Message.spiffe_actor: "attribution must be
 tracked state, not inferred per-turn" (design record §9).

fields.name: text
fields.description: MESSAGE, and the message half of MOVED_OUT.

fields.name: ticket_id
fields.description:
TICKET_*: which ticket, and (TICKET_OPENED) the other side's chat if known.

 A TICKET ID HERE NAMES A ROW IN A TENANT'S `scotty`, NOT IN THIS SERVICE.
 That is the split working as intended and not a dangling reference: the
 artifact has exactly one home (login doc §4 rule 1) and this row is the
 personal-side KNOWLEDGE that it happened. There is deliberately no field
 recording which tenant, because the chat's own routing already fixed it and
 a second copy could disagree with the first.

fields.name: tool_name
fields.description:
TOOL_CALLED: which generated tool, and whether Config.max_turn_hops halted
 the turn.

fields.name: moved_to_chat_id
fields.description: MOVED_OUT: where Scotty filed it; on the target copy, where it came from.

fields.name: member_principal
fields.description: MEMBER_JOINED / MEMBER_LEFT.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace: see ChatSession.namespace. Same field, same open question, same
 reason for keeping it. EQ-queryable because c2s_read requires it.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record's declared `owner` and the PUBLISHER — this
 SERVICE, never the person. `owner` above is where the person is; filtering
 a person's reads on THIS field would show them every row in the fleet while
 looking like it showed them their own. See Chat.spiffe_id.

fields.name: thread_id
fields.description:
MESSAGE: the A29 thread the message belongs to, as sent on
 CreateChatMessageRequest.thread_id. The same value on every member's copy.

types.name: ListChatMembershipsRequest

fields.name: include_archived
fields.description:
include_archived false is the live list; true is everything, for the
 archived section of a client.

fields.name: page_size
fields.description:
The PAGE envelope. Both field names are tacplus's convention, not this
 file's choice, and a PAGE rpc whose request lacks either fails generation.

types.name: ListChatMembershipsResponse

fields.name: memberships
fields.description:
memberships is the ONE repeated field a PAGE response may carry.

 THE CLIENT STILL NEEDS EACH CHAT'S TITLE, AND THIS RESPONSE DOES NOT CARRY
 IT. The 2026-09-07 sketch paired a `repeated Chat chats` alongside so the
 list cost one round trip; validatePageEnvelope refuses a second repeated
 field outright ("the collection item is ambiguous"). Two ways out, and this
 file picks NEITHER rather than guessing: a GetChat per row (N+1 reads on
 the most-opened screen there is), or denormalising title and kind onto
 ChatMembership (a second copy of a fact that UpdateChat can change, which
 the design record §2 rule against facts living in two places is aimed at).
 Whoever builds the client surface decides; nothing here is shaped to make
 either harder.

message.name: ChatMembership
message.description:
ChatMembership is what ONE person has decided about one chat: archived,
 muted, what they told their Scotty to do about it, how far they have read.
 None of it is anyone else's business and none of it is shared, which is why
 this row can carry the pin `Chat` cannot.

 It is also the chat list. Every read of "my chats" goes through here, so the
 generated per-principal filter is the list's authorization, not a check.

 A stratum record since 2026-09-25, principal-owned and NOT `private` — read
 the (spec.record_read) block at the top of this file for why `private` is the
 right description of this row and the wrong annotation for it today.

fields.name: membership_id
fields.description:
membership_id is the record key: "<chat_id>/<principal>". Derived rather
 than minted, exactly as ChatSession.session_id is and for the same reason:
 one row per (chat, person) by construction.

 (spec.indexed) is gone with the state collection — see Chat.chat_id.

fields.name: principal
fields.description:
principal is the OWNING principal — the personal principal, as on
 ChatSession. (spec.store_principal) generates the read-side filter that
 pins every surface returning this row to the caller's own subject, which is
 what makes archive and mute per person with no hand-written check.

 EQ-queryable since 2026-09-25, and that is half the annotation rather than
 decoration: the c2s record-read plane REFUSES C2S_SCOPE_PRINCIPAL when no
 principal criterion resolves (rather than degrading it to a tenant-wide
 read), and the handler pins this same field into the predicate before the
 store is asked, which is what keeps `total` this person's own count instead
 of the fleet's.

fields.name: archived
fields.description:
archived hides the chat from the live list. It is NOT terminal —
 UpdateChatMembership clears it. Purging a chat would be a Delete, and there
 is none: a chat is never gone.

fields.name: muted
fields.description:
muted: Scotty surfaces nothing from this chat unless notify_policy_text
 says otherwise.

fields.name: notify_policy_text
fields.description:
notify_policy_text is this person's standing instruction to THEIR OWN
 Scotty about this chat ("only tell me if there is something I should
 know"). Read by that runtime and nothing else; prose by nature, and no
 other member's runtime may read it — the principal pin above is what makes
 that true rather than promised.

fields.name: last_read_seq
fields.description:
last_read_seq is this owner's ChatEvent.seq high-water mark, which is what
 "unread" is computed from.

 IT INHERITS ChatEvent.seq's UNSOLVED ASSIGNMENT. Read that field's comment
 before treating this number as a reliable watermark: until per-owner seq
 assignment has an answer, so does unread.

fields.name: last_event_at_ms
fields.description:
last_event_at_ms orders the chat list. Maintained by the handler when it
 appends this owner's copy of an event.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace: see ChatSession.namespace. EQ-queryable because tacplus refuses
 (spec.record).c2s_read on a record whose (spec.store_namespace) field is
 not: the client-facing plane pins the field to the caller's verified claim
 before the store is asked, and a pin needs a criterion to be pinned into.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record's declared `owner` and the PUBLISHER — this
 SERVICE, never the person. `principal` above is where the person is. See
 Chat.spiffe_id for why the name is load-bearing and why it is never a read
 filter.

types.name: ListMyChatHistoryRequest
types.description:
NO PAGE ENVELOPE, because this rpc is SNAPSHOT — see its declaration for why
 an MCP tool may not be PAGE in a Rust host. The page_size/page_token pair and
 the next_page_token/total_count pair that used to be here are gone rather
 than left unused: a field a tool publishes in its JSON schema is a field the
 model will fill in, and a cursor it invents is worse than no cursor at all.

types.name: ListMyChatHistoryResponse

fields.name: events
fields.description: Equal to the method's default_page_size; the two describe one cap.

message.name: ChatEvent
message.description:
ChatEvent is the append-only record of what was said and what Scotty did. One
 row per OWNER copy, which is what makes history entitleable per person with
 no hand-written check: `owner` carries (spec.store_principal) and the
 generated filter does the rest.

 A stratum record since 2026-09-25, principal-owned and NOT `private` — see
 the (spec.record_read) block at the top of this file, whose second reason is
 about THIS type: one logical event is one row per member, and appending it
 reads every other member's high-water seq. A pin that admits only the
 caller's own rows cannot do that.

fields.name: event_key
fields.description:
event_key is the record key: "<event_id>/<owner>". event_id for a sent
 message is "<chat_id>/<sender>/<client_message_id>", which is what makes a
 retried send rewrite the same rows instead of appending duplicates.
 Service-originated events mint event_id timestamp-first.

 (spec.indexed) is gone with the state collection — see Chat.chat_id.

fields.name: chat_id
fields.description:
chat_id is the ONE predicate this file pushes down past the two pins, and
 it is the exception that proves work's rule (its D4: "there is no predicate
 pushdown here beyond the tenant"). Two things make it different. It is a
 DECLARED PARAMETER of both reads that use it — ListChatEvents(chat_id) and
 ListMyChatHistory(chat_id) — rather than a predicate the handler invents;
 and this collection is the largest in the file by two orders of magnitude
 (its state bound was 10,000,000 against Chat's 100,000), so "every event
 this person owns, then filter" is the one read here where the difference
 is a number rather than a preference. An empty chat_id is still the
 unified timeline: the criterion is simply not sent.

fields.name: owner
fields.description:
owner is whose COPY this is — the personal principal, as on ChatSession.
 EQ-queryable since 2026-09-25 — see ChatMembership.principal.

fields.name: seq
fields.description:
seq is monotonic PER OWNER across all their chats: it is the WATCH revision
 and the PAGE keyset in one.

 HOW IT IS ASSIGNED IS OPEN, and the split is what opened it. The 2026-09-07
 sketch assigns it under the owner's kernel.FencedLock, copying scottyagent
 — but that needs (spec.grpc_s2s_client) = {service: "kernel.FencedLock"},
 which is service-identity S2S reach and is exactly what DECISIONS.md item
 9c denies this class of service. A delegated user token cannot stand in: a
 per-owner sequence is the SERVICE's bookkeeping, not an action taken on the
 user's behalf, and it must hold across owners who are mid-turn in different
 tenants. Nothing here decides the answer — the field's meaning is unchanged
 whichever way it is assigned. Written up rather than improvised.

fields.name: author
fields.description:
author is the principal whose message or action this is; author_actor is
 the delegate that produced it (the author's Scotty), empty when the human
 did it directly. Same split as scotty.TicketDecision.decided_by /
 decided_by_actor and messaging.Message.spiffe_actor: "attribution must be
 tracked state, not inferred per-turn" (design record §9).

fields.name: text
fields.description: MESSAGE, and the message half of MOVED_OUT.

fields.name: ticket_id
fields.description:
TICKET_*: which ticket, and (TICKET_OPENED) the other side's chat if known.

 A TICKET ID HERE NAMES A ROW IN A TENANT'S `scotty`, NOT IN THIS SERVICE.
 That is the split working as intended and not a dangling reference: the
 artifact has exactly one home (login doc §4 rule 1) and this row is the
 personal-side KNOWLEDGE that it happened. There is deliberately no field
 recording which tenant, because the chat's own routing already fixed it and
 a second copy could disagree with the first.

fields.name: tool_name
fields.description:
TOOL_CALLED: which generated tool, and whether Config.max_turn_hops halted
 the turn.

fields.name: moved_to_chat_id
fields.description: MOVED_OUT: where Scotty filed it; on the target copy, where it came from.

fields.name: member_principal
fields.description: MEMBER_JOINED / MEMBER_LEFT.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace: see ChatSession.namespace. Same field, same open question, same
 reason for keeping it. EQ-queryable because c2s_read requires it.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record's declared `owner` and the PUBLISHER — this
 SERVICE, never the person. `owner` above is where the person is; filtering
 a person's reads on THIS field would show them every row in the fleet while
 looking like it showed them their own. See Chat.spiffe_id.

fields.name: thread_id
fields.description:
MESSAGE: the A29 thread the message belongs to, as sent on
 CreateChatMessageRequest.thread_id. The same value on every member's copy.

fields.name: next_page_token
fields.description: Empty means this was the last page.

types.name: ListMySessionStateRequest
ListMySessionStateResponse

fields.name: sessions
fields.description:
sessions is 0 or 1 rows: none before the first turn in this chat, one
 after. Empty is a complete answer and needs no companion bool. Repeated
 because the (spec.store_principal) egress backstop is generated only for
 repeated message fields — a singular `ChatSession session` would carry the
 annotation and generate no backstop at all, silently
 (scottyagent.proto's ListMyAgentStateResponse).

message.name: ChatSession
message.description:
ChatSession is what one person's Scotty is currently holding in mind about
 one chat. It is knowledge, re-derivable from ChatEvent; it is not an
 artifact, which is why this service's state root carries no
 requires_artifact_on_write. What Scotty DOES from a chat leaves its artifact
 where the doing happens — a ticket in the tenant that owns it.

 A stratum record since 2026-09-25, principal-owned and NOT `private` — see
 the (spec.record_read) block at the top of this file. THIS is the one type in
 this file that `private` would fit on its own terms (it is never read across
 owners); it stays non-private with its siblings because the reader it would
 need does not exist, and because one private row among three ordinary ones
 buys a second plane client and no guarantee the store_principal pin does not
 already give.

fields.name: session_id
fields.description:
session_id is the record key: "<chat_id>/<principal>". Derived rather than
 minted, so one person has exactly one session per chat by construction and
 a second one cannot be created by racing.

 (spec.indexed) is gone with the state collection — see Chat.chat_id.

fields.name: principal
fields.description:
principal is the OWNING principal, and it is the whole egress mechanism for
 this collection: (spec.store_principal) generates the read-side filter that
 pins every surface returning this row to the caller's own subject.

 It is the PERSONAL principal (login doc §2b: the device's synced keychain
 key), never a per-tenant identity. That is the split: this row is one
 person's, across every tenant they belong to, and there is no tenant-scoped
 reader of it at all.

 EQ-queryable since 2026-09-25 — see ChatMembership.principal for why that
 is half the annotation and not decoration.

fields.name: state_text
fields.description:
state_text is the ONE generic text field Jody asked for: the LLM gets it,
 modifies it, puts it back whole. Nothing parses it, nothing derives
 authority from it, and NO FACT MAY LIVE ONLY HERE — see the 2026-09-07
 decision doc §2. In particular the routing map is not remembered here: it
 is read from kernel every time (login doc §4, and GetMyRoutingMap below).

fields.name: state_version
fields.description:
state_version increments on every replace and must be presented on the
 next replace. A stale replace is FAILED_PRECONDITION. Cheap insurance
 against a dormant session that woke twice.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning namespace, held to the reader's claim by
 exact equality by the generated egress filter.

 WHAT VALUE A PERSONAL PRINCIPAL'S ROWS CARRY IS NOT SETTLED, and this is
 the one place the service split reaches down to a field. Device principals
 do not exist yet (login doc §6 item 1) and nothing has decided what
 namespace claim one holds. What IS settled is that it must not be a
 TENANT's: a personal chat spans every tenant the person belongs to, so
 pinning the row to one tenant would contradict §3's "the personal runtime
 sees everything the user sees".

 The field is kept — with the marker — rather than dropped, because
 (spec.store_namespace) is only mandatory on a (spec.record) and a state row
 may legally omit it, which would mean silently generating NO egress
 backstop at all. Whoever settles the device-principal claim settles this
 field's value; the annotation is not the thing to remove if it turns out
 the claim is empty.

 MANDATORY NOW, not merely kept: tacplus's ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations
 fails generation for a (spec.record) declaring no such field, "on the
 reasoning that the record nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one
 that leaks". The paragraph above anticipated this ("(spec.store_namespace)
 is only mandatory on a (spec.record)") — the move to stratum is what made
 it so. EQ-queryable because c2s_read requires it.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record's declared `owner` and the PUBLISHER — this
 SERVICE, never the person. See Chat.spiffe_id.

fields.name: next_page_token
fields.description: Always empty: there is never a second page of a one-row collection.

types.name: MapEmpty
ScottypersonalConfigState
types.description:
ScottypersonalConfigState is the state boundary for scottypersonal service configuration.
 Auto-injected by tacplus from (spec.grpc_config) annotation.

message.name: Config
message.description:
Config is delivered by kernel at startup and on every change.

 The four knobs are the 2026-09-07 sketch's ConfigAdditions, retagged from 1
 because this is a new service's Config rather than an addition to `scotty`'s.
 Nothing else moved: they are resource-shaped bounds on the session runtime,
 changeable in kernel with no redeploy, and none of them decides anything
 about a request. No business rule may be expressed here — the same rule
 scotty.Config.max_open_tickets states.

 NO llm_credential FIELD YET. The persona runtime does call a model, and
 `scotty.Config.llm_credential` is the pattern for holding that key — but the
 fan-out is driven by operator's own `llm_credential_services` list, so adding
 the field here without adding "scottypersonal" there produces a service that
 starts and cannot talk to a model. Both halves are one change and belong to
 whoever builds the runtime.

fields.name: session_idle_seconds
fields.description:
session_idle_seconds is how long an ACTIVE session (in-process LLM
 transcript + cached state) survives without a turn before it is dropped.
 Dropping loses nothing: session state is in kernel and history is in
 kernel, so the next turn rehydrates. Config so it changes with no redeploy.

fields.name: max_active_sessions
fields.description:
max_active_sessions bounds the in-process cache (LRU). A resource limit,
 not a business rule.

fields.name: rehydrate_history_events
fields.description:
rehydrate_history_events is how many trailing ChatEvent rows a rehydrated
 session reads into its transcript. Older history is not lost, it is a tool
 call away.

fields.name: max_turn_hops
fields.description:
max_turn_hops caps model<->tool round-trips in ONE turn. Same shape and
 reason as scotty.Config.max_chain_hops: a hop count, not a TTL, and it
 exists to keep an LLM from looping rather than to express a policy.

types.name: ScottypersonalState
types.description:
ScottypersonalState is EMPTY, and that is the whole point of it.

 It exists because servicemanager's generated wiring requires every service in
 the build to host a state root (the same reason profile.ProfileState and
 work.WorkState are empty), not because this service keeps anything in kernel.
 The ruling is explicit — kernel is in-memory coordination only, and
 "something went very wrong if we are holding user data like tasks in kernel
 state" (decisions/kernel-no-durability-user-data-to-stratum-2026-09-25.md
 item 3). Every person's chat history is exactly that kind of data, and more
 of it: this is what they said to their own Scotty.

 WHAT WAS HERE, until 2026-09-25: `chat_sessions`, `chat_events`, `chats` and
 `chat_memberships`, four `repeated` fields carrying (spec.persistence) = true,
 which the same ruling's item 2 makes a generation error ("durable data belongs
 in stratum records"). All four are (spec.record)s above, and the day a field
 is added back here is the day this service changed storage planes.

 NO requires_artifact_on_write, unlike scotty.ScottyState, and its absence is
 unchanged rather than relaxed: the design record's §1 rule — "nothing reaches
 knowledge without leaving an artifact" — is satisfied elsewhere for
 everything here. ChatEvent rows ARE the immutable append-only record of the
 chat, and ChatSession is knowledge re-derivable from them. What Scotty does
 from a chat leaves its artifact in the tenant where it was done. See the
 2026-09-07 decision doc §2.

 The rows' entitlement model is unchanged by the move and is now stated on the
 records themselves: three of the four are PERSONAL-PRINCIPAL-owned and carry
 (spec.store_principal); Chat has several owners and is gated by hand. There is
 no tenant chroot on this service — it is /system (DECISIONS.md item 9c) — so
 the store's per-principal filter is the boundary, not the kernel path rewrite
 that protects a tenant-owned service. That was true of the kernel collections
 and it is true of the records.

types.name: TenantLink
types.description:
TenantLink is a relationship between two tenants that is relevant to this
 person because one end of it is one of their memberships.

 A LINK IS CONTEXT, NOT A DESTINATION. Joe files his work in Jimerson;
 knowing Jimerson is a customer of Acme is what lets Scotty understand a
 request about Acme without concluding that Acme is a home Joe may write to.
 The homes are the memberships above and only those.

enum_values.name: TENANT_LINK_KIND_CUSTOMER_OF
enum_values.description:
from_namespace is a CUSTOMER OF to_namespace. Login doc §4's own example:
 "Joe works for Jimerson. Jimerson is a customer of Acme" — from=jimerson,
 to=acme.

fields.name: to_display_name
fields.description:
display_name of to_namespace, for the same readback reason
 TenantMembership.display_name exists. from_namespace's name is already
 carried by the membership it matches.

types.name: TenantMembership
types.description:
TenantMembership is one home this person is entitled to file things in.

 IT IS NOT THIS SERVICE'S ROW. Memberships are kernel state on the personal
 principal (login doc §6 item 3), so nothing below appears in
 ScottypersonalState and no RPC here creates, updates or deletes one — this is
 the shape of an ANSWER, not of a store. That placement is the point of §4
 rule 2: "the routing map is not something Scotty learns; the kernel tells
 him." A membership Scotty remembered instead of read is a home the kernel may
 already have revoked.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the tenant, in the canonical vocabulary DECISIONS.md item 5
 fixes: "/tenants/<name>". It is the value a per-tenant delegated token is
 minted for and the value that names the home in a readback.

fields.name: display_name
fields.description:
display_name is the tenant's human-readable name, empty when kernel has
 none. It exists because login doc §4's disambiguation is a SPOKEN one —
 "Jimerson reminder: call Mike Faraday Friday" — and a readback that says
 "/tenants/jimerson" has not confirmed anything to a person.

fields.name: customer
fields.description:
customer marks a membership that is scoped to the tenant's customer-facing
 service and nothing else. Jody: "think of customer as just a service inside
 a tenant" (login doc §1). Routing-relevant, not merely descriptive: it is
 the difference between a home a person can file work into and one where
 they can only deal with that tenant as an outsider.

fields.name: trace_id
fields.description:
NO PROOF TYPE FIELD. A membership carries how it was proven — tenant IdP,
 emailed link, linked personal Scotty (login doc §1, §6 item 3) — and that
 fact belongs to LOGIN, not to routing. The runtime reading this map is
 choosing among homes that already exist; how each was established changes
 none of them. Add it when something actually reads it.

types.name: UpdateChatMembershipRequest

fields.name: archived
fields.description:
Each `optional`: unset leaves the field alone. Without presence, "false"
 and "not sent" are the same wire bytes, and unmuting would be
 indistinguishable from not mentioning mute.

types.name: UpdateChatMembershipResponse

message.name: ChatMembership
message.description:
ChatMembership is what ONE person has decided about one chat: archived,
 muted, what they told their Scotty to do about it, how far they have read.
 None of it is anyone else's business and none of it is shared, which is why
 this row can carry the pin `Chat` cannot.

 It is also the chat list. Every read of "my chats" goes through here, so the
 generated per-principal filter is the list's authorization, not a check.

 A stratum record since 2026-09-25, principal-owned and NOT `private` — read
 the (spec.record_read) block at the top of this file for why `private` is the
 right description of this row and the wrong annotation for it today.

fields.name: membership_id
fields.description:
membership_id is the record key: "<chat_id>/<principal>". Derived rather
 than minted, exactly as ChatSession.session_id is and for the same reason:
 one row per (chat, person) by construction.

 (spec.indexed) is gone with the state collection — see Chat.chat_id.

fields.name: principal
fields.description:
principal is the OWNING principal — the personal principal, as on
 ChatSession. (spec.store_principal) generates the read-side filter that
 pins every surface returning this row to the caller's own subject, which is
 what makes archive and mute per person with no hand-written check.

 EQ-queryable since 2026-09-25, and that is half the annotation rather than
 decoration: the c2s record-read plane REFUSES C2S_SCOPE_PRINCIPAL when no
 principal criterion resolves (rather than degrading it to a tenant-wide
 read), and the handler pins this same field into the predicate before the
 store is asked, which is what keeps `total` this person's own count instead
 of the fleet's.

fields.name: archived
fields.description:
archived hides the chat from the live list. It is NOT terminal —
 UpdateChatMembership clears it. Purging a chat would be a Delete, and there
 is none: a chat is never gone.

fields.name: muted
fields.description:
muted: Scotty surfaces nothing from this chat unless notify_policy_text
 says otherwise.

fields.name: notify_policy_text
fields.description:
notify_policy_text is this person's standing instruction to THEIR OWN
 Scotty about this chat ("only tell me if there is something I should
 know"). Read by that runtime and nothing else; prose by nature, and no
 other member's runtime may read it — the principal pin above is what makes
 that true rather than promised.

fields.name: last_read_seq
fields.description:
last_read_seq is this owner's ChatEvent.seq high-water mark, which is what
 "unread" is computed from.

 IT INHERITS ChatEvent.seq's UNSOLVED ASSIGNMENT. Read that field's comment
 before treating this number as a reliable watermark: until per-owner seq
 assignment has an answer, so does unread.

fields.name: last_event_at_ms
fields.description:
last_event_at_ms orders the chat list. Maintained by the handler when it
 appends this owner's copy of an event.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace: see ChatSession.namespace. EQ-queryable because tacplus refuses
 (spec.record).c2s_read on a record whose (spec.store_namespace) field is
 not: the client-facing plane pins the field to the caller's verified claim
 before the store is asked, and a pin needs a criterion to be pinned into.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record's declared `owner` and the PUBLISHER — this
 SERVICE, never the person. `principal` above is where the person is. See
 Chat.spiffe_id for why the name is load-bearing and why it is never a read
 filter.

types.name: UpdateChatRequest

fields.name: add_participants
fields.description:
add_participants and remove_principals are the join and leave halves. Both
 may be empty; a request with both empty and no title is a no-op rather than
 an error. Leaving a chat yourself is remove_principals = [you].

fields.name: principal
fields.description: principal is a token subject for HUMAN, an agent identity for AGENT.

fields.name: joined_at_ms
fields.description: joined_at_ms is stamped by the handler, never by the caller.

fields.name: title
fields.description:
title is `optional` so "not sent" and "sent empty" are different requests:
 unset leaves the title alone, empty clears it. proto3 explicit presence,
 the docmanager pattern confirmed in decisions/work-service-2026-09-09.md
 VERIFY answer 3.

types.name: UpdateChatResponse

message.name: Chat
message.description:
Chat is who is in a conversation. It is the one row in this service that
 belongs to SEVERAL people at once, and that is the whole difficulty with it.

 NO (spec.store_principal), AND THAT IS NOT AN OMISSION. The annotation pins a
 row to exactly one subject — tacplus refuses a second field carrying it
 (`principal_validate.go`, recorded in decisions/work-service-2026-09-09.md
 VERIFY answer 4) — and a chat with four participants has no one owner to pin
 to. `created_by` would pin reads to the creator and hide the chat from
 everyone else in it. So this collection gets NO generated egress filter, and
 "only a member may read a chat" is a hand-written check in the handler,
 enforced against the caller's own ChatMembership row.

 That is the same unbuilt entitlement gap `scotty.Human` records (see
 schematic/looper/schematic/decisions/scotty-read-authorization-not-wired.md)
 and it is NOT solved here. What IS structural is the membership row: every
 list of chats goes through ChatMembership, which is principal-pinned, so the
 only way to learn a chat_id you are not in is to be told one.

 A stratum record since 2026-09-25, and the ONE of this file's four with no
 owning principal — which is exactly what decides its record shape. Read the
 (spec.record_read) block at the top of this file for why it gets no c2s half.

fields.name: chat_id
fields.description:
chat_id is DERIVED for the singletons and minted otherwise:
   DIRECT: "direct/<min(a,b)>/<max(a,b)>"  — 1:1, one per pair by
           construction, so CreateChat on an existing pair returns it
           instead of making a second one.
   SELF default: "self/<principal>/default" — the catch-all a message with
           no chat lands in.
   SELF other, GROUP, JOB: minted timestamp-first.

 (spec.indexed) WAS HERE AND IS GONE WITH THE STATE COLLECTION: it is the
 statedb field-index marker, and there is no state map left to index. The
 key is an EQ criterion on ChatFilter without any annotation, because
 declaring s2s_read above folds a record's key into its filter
 (record_map.go's keyFilterCriterion) — which is what the point read behind
 GetChat is.

enum_values.name: CHAT_KIND_SELF_CHAT
enum_values.description:
SELF: the user and their own Scotty. Goes nowhere. Many per user.

 NAMED _SELF_CHAT AND NOT _SELF, and that is a tacplus defect worked around
 rather than a shade of meaning. `CHAT_KIND_SELF` renders as the Rust variant
 `Self`, which is a reserved word: prost's own emitter sanitizes it to

enum_values.name: CHAT_KIND_DIRECT
enum_values.description: DIRECT: two people (and their Scottys). One per pair.

enum_values.name: CHAT_KIND_GROUP
enum_values.description: GROUP: people who join and leave.

enum_values.name: CHAT_KIND_JOB
enum_values.description:
JOB: a GROUP whose closure is company-wide. Reserved from the 2026-09-07
 sketch: the job type does not exist yet and nothing here invents it.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
participants are HUMAN principals and AGENT identities. The caller's own
 Scotty is implicit in every chat and is not listed; a participant of kind
 AGENT is a NAMED one (a DocManager, a JobManager, a customer's agent).

 A PARTICIPANT IS A PERSONAL PRINCIPAL, not a per-tenant identity, for the
 same reason ChatSession.principal is: the chat spans every tenant its
 members belong to. A member of this chat is not thereby a member of any
 tenant — where work gets FILED is the routing map's business, and
 GetMyRoutingMap answers it separately for each person.

fields.name: principal
fields.description: principal is a token subject for HUMAN, an agent identity for AGENT.

fields.name: joined_at_ms
fields.description: joined_at_ms is stamped by the handler, never by the caller.

fields.name: title
fields.description:
title is set by the creator or by Scotty (through UpdateChat). Prose;
 nothing derives from it.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace: see ChatSession.namespace. Same field, same open question about
 what claim a personal principal carries, same reason for keeping it.

 EQ-queryable since 2026-09-25, because it is now the ONLY pin this record
 has: with no owning principal, the caller's verified namespace is the whole
 of what `require_chat` pins into the store predicate before it asks (the
 same value it compared in-process when these rows came from kernel).

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record's declared `owner` and the PUBLISHER — eventbus
 stamps this service's own identity onto it. The field NAME is load-bearing
 (eventbus's topic discovery matches the literal string "spiffe_id" of
 string type when it decides which topics get publisher-identity stamping),
 which is why it carries (spec.identity_spiffe_subject) exactly as
 work.WorkActivity.spiffe_id does.

 IT IS THE SERVICE, NOT A PERSON, and so it is never a read filter. Every
 row of this type in the fleet carries the same value; narrowing a read by
 it would show a reader every chat in the fleet while looking like it
 narrowed something.

types.name: UpdateMyChatMembershipRequest
UpdateMyChatMembershipResponse

fields.name: archived
fields.description:
The resulting state of the three settable fields, so the model can say back
 to the person what it actually did — "muted, and I'll only tell you if the
 pour date moves" — rather than reporting what it asked for. Not the row,
 for the reason UpdateMySessionStateResponse gives.

types.name: UpdateMySessionStateRequest

fields.name: expected_version
fields.description:
expected_version is the state_version you read. A stale one is
 FAILED_PRECONDITION and you must read again.

types.name: UpdateMySessionStateResponse

fields.name: state_version
fields.description:
The row is NOT returned, only its new version — which is the one thing the
 caller does not already have and needs for its next write. A returned row
 would have to be `repeated`-of-one for the egress backstop, and a unary
 response whose only meaningful field is a single repeated field is a
 collection read as far as tacplus is concerned: it demands a
 method_collection, which demands the verb List, which a write is not. The
 rows come back through ListMySessionState.

types.name: WatchChatEventsEnvelope
types.description:
WatchChatEventsEnvelope is the WATCH contract's envelope, and every name in
 it is fixed by tacplus: the three fields must be called snapshot_item,
 snapshot_done and delta, must sit in ONE oneof, and snapshot_done must be
 int64. The oneof's own name is free.

fields.name: snapshot_item
fields.description:
snapshot_item is one row of the catch-up snapshot; the item type is what
 the rpc's order_by resolves against.

message.name: ChatEvent
message.description:
ChatEvent is the append-only record of what was said and what Scotty did. One
 row per OWNER copy, which is what makes history entitleable per person with
 no hand-written check: `owner` carries (spec.store_principal) and the
 generated filter does the rest.

 A stratum record since 2026-09-25, principal-owned and NOT `private` — see
 the (spec.record_read) block at the top of this file, whose second reason is
 about THIS type: one logical event is one row per member, and appending it
 reads every other member's high-water seq. A pin that admits only the
 caller's own rows cannot do that.

fields.name: event_key
fields.description:
event_key is the record key: "<event_id>/<owner>". event_id for a sent
 message is "<chat_id>/<sender>/<client_message_id>", which is what makes a
 retried send rewrite the same rows instead of appending duplicates.
 Service-originated events mint event_id timestamp-first.

 (spec.indexed) is gone with the state collection — see Chat.chat_id.

fields.name: chat_id
fields.description:
chat_id is the ONE predicate this file pushes down past the two pins, and
 it is the exception that proves work's rule (its D4: "there is no predicate
 pushdown here beyond the tenant"). Two things make it different. It is a
 DECLARED PARAMETER of both reads that use it — ListChatEvents(chat_id) and
 ListMyChatHistory(chat_id) — rather than a predicate the handler invents;
 and this collection is the largest in the file by two orders of magnitude
 (its state bound was 10,000,000 against Chat's 100,000), so "every event
 this person owns, then filter" is the one read here where the difference
 is a number rather than a preference. An empty chat_id is still the
 unified timeline: the criterion is simply not sent.

fields.name: owner
fields.description:
owner is whose COPY this is — the personal principal, as on ChatSession.
 EQ-queryable since 2026-09-25 — see ChatMembership.principal.

fields.name: seq
fields.description:
seq is monotonic PER OWNER across all their chats: it is the WATCH revision
 and the PAGE keyset in one.

 HOW IT IS ASSIGNED IS OPEN, and the split is what opened it. The 2026-09-07
 sketch assigns it under the owner's kernel.FencedLock, copying scottyagent
 — but that needs (spec.grpc_s2s_client) = {service: "kernel.FencedLock"},
 which is service-identity S2S reach and is exactly what DECISIONS.md item
 9c denies this class of service. A delegated user token cannot stand in: a
 per-owner sequence is the SERVICE's bookkeeping, not an action taken on the
 user's behalf, and it must hold across owners who are mid-turn in different
 tenants. Nothing here decides the answer — the field's meaning is unchanged
 whichever way it is assigned. Written up rather than improvised.

fields.name: author
fields.description:
author is the principal whose message or action this is; author_actor is
 the delegate that produced it (the author's Scotty), empty when the human
 did it directly. Same split as scotty.TicketDecision.decided_by /
 decided_by_actor and messaging.Message.spiffe_actor: "attribution must be
 tracked state, not inferred per-turn" (design record §9).

fields.name: text
fields.description: MESSAGE, and the message half of MOVED_OUT.

fields.name: ticket_id
fields.description:
TICKET_*: which ticket, and (TICKET_OPENED) the other side's chat if known.

 A TICKET ID HERE NAMES A ROW IN A TENANT'S `scotty`, NOT IN THIS SERVICE.
 That is the split working as intended and not a dangling reference: the
 artifact has exactly one home (login doc §4 rule 1) and this row is the
 personal-side KNOWLEDGE that it happened. There is deliberately no field
 recording which tenant, because the chat's own routing already fixed it and
 a second copy could disagree with the first.

fields.name: tool_name
fields.description:
TOOL_CALLED: which generated tool, and whether Config.max_turn_hops halted
 the turn.

fields.name: moved_to_chat_id
fields.description: MOVED_OUT: where Scotty filed it; on the target copy, where it came from.

fields.name: member_principal
fields.description: MEMBER_JOINED / MEMBER_LEFT.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace: see ChatSession.namespace. Same field, same open question, same
 reason for keeping it. EQ-queryable because c2s_read requires it.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record's declared `owner` and the PUBLISHER — this
 SERVICE, never the person. `owner` above is where the person is; filtering
 a person's reads on THIS field would show them every row in the fleet while
 looking like it showed them their own. See Chat.spiffe_id.

fields.name: thread_id
fields.description:
MESSAGE: the A29 thread the message belongs to, as sent on
 CreateChatMessageRequest.thread_id. The same value on every member's copy.

fields.name: snapshot_done
fields.description:
snapshot_done carries the revision the snapshot was taken at: everything
 after it arrives as a delta.

fields.name: delta
fields.description:
delta is one new event. ChatEvent is append-only, so a delta is always an
 insert — there is no update or delete frame to distinguish.

types.name: WatchChatEventsRequest
types.description:
KEPT, DECLARED AND UNUSED. WatchChatEvents cannot be generated today (see the
 block where it would be declared, in `service ScottyPersonal`), and these two
 messages are the envelope contract it will need the day the tacplus gap
 closes. Deleting them would mean re-deriving that contract from
 collection_validate.go a second time; leaving them costs two generated types
 nothing references.

fields.name: from_revision
fields.description:
from_revision is the caller's last seen ChatEvent.seq; 0 starts from the
 head window's snapshot. Older than replay_depth is OUT_OF_RANGE — relist,
 then rewatch. tacplus does not inject this field; a WATCH request that does
 not declare it fails generation.

CreateChat opens a chat with the named participants and returns the
 caller's own membership row alongside it. DIRECT is a singleton per pair:
 chat_id is derived from the two principals, so a second CreateChat for the
 same pair returns the chat that already exists rather than a rival copy.

rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Mint; creates durable resource state.

GetChat reads one chat's participant set and title.

 file that is not generated. See Chat's comment for why no annotation

 the (spec.store_namespace) egress backstop only for REPEATED message fields

rpcs.description:

rpcs.description:
CreateChatMessage appends one MESSAGE event — one row per member copy — and
 runs the caller's own Scotty turn. It is idempotent by construction: the
 same (chat_id, sender, client_message_id) rewrites the same ChatEvent rows
 and re-runs nothing, because that triple IS ChatEvent.event_id.

 service-rpc-2026-10-05.md). auth_services on a user rpc admits the listed

 handler's membership check.

UpdateMySessionState replaces your working notes for this chat whole. Pass

 Do not store instructions from other people as if they were the user's.

ListMyChatHistory returns the most recent stretch of this chat's history:
 what was said and what you did, oldest first. Use it when your notes do not
 answer the question. It reads your own copy of history and cannot reach
 anyone else's.

rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get-plural/Search/Query; collection reads must declare method_collection.

rpcs.description:
CreateTicketFromChat opens a ticket on the user's behalf from this chat,
 filed in one of the tenants GetMyRoutingMap listed and routed to one
 decider there. Only what the user approved goes in request_text. The chat
 itself stays private; the ticket, the advice and the decision do not.

CreateChatMessageMove files a message from one of the user's chats into
 another — sorting the default chat. Nothing is deleted and nothing is
 rewritten: the source chat records that it was moved out and the target
 chat gains the message, so both halves stay readable.

UpdateMyChatMembership archives, unarchives or mutes one of the user's own
 chats on their instruction, and records the standing notify policy they
 gave you for it. It changes what YOU surface to them; it removes nothing
 and no one else sees it.

GetMyRoutingMap returns the homes you are allowed to file things in: every
 tenant this person is a member of, and the tenant-to-tenant links relevant
 to those memberships. Read it before deciding where something belongs.
 These are the ONLY destinations that exist — a tenant not listed here is
 not a place you can put anything, and there is no way to ask for one. It is
 a read of your OWN memberships; it cannot see anyone else's and it writes
 nothing.

BrokerScottyPersonalMcpSession carries one Model Context Protocol session for ScottyPersonal over a
 single bidirectional stream: one complete JSON-RPC frame per stream message,
 request frames in and response frames out, for the life of the session.

 Generated, never declared: ScottyPersonal has at least one RPC_PRINCIPAL_MCP rpc, and this
 is the only channel those tools are reachable through. Bidirectional because an
 MCP session is stateful — it opens with an initialize handshake and holds the
 negotiated protocol version after it — so a unary call would repeat that
 handshake per tool call.

services.name: ScottyPersonal
services.description:
ScottyPersonal's caller-facing surface is the chat plane a person's client
 talks to, plus the MCP tools their own persona runtime calls in-process as
 them.

 THE VERB REGISTRY IS CLOSED (tacplus/pkg/internal/common/verbs/registry.json)
 and it is why three rpcs here are not spelled the way the 2026-09-07 sketch
 spelled them. `Replace` and `Move` are not registered verbs and not folded
 synonyms of any, and a collection read may not be spelled `Get` — the
 classifier refuses all three outright. The domain word survives in the noun,
 exactly as `scotty.proto`'s "open/advise/decide/seal" survive inside its
 Create verbs. There is no Delete anywhere in this service: a chat is never
 gone, an event is never unsaid, and a membership is archived rather than
 removed.

 CATEGORY B, not category A. decisions/mcp-generation-and-service-owned-
 data-2026-08-31.md §4 splits the two on who the session belongs to: in (A)
 the SERVICE is the MCP client and a model acts with the service's own
 authority; in (B) the service is the MCP SERVER, a REAL caller's session is
 bound to a real principal at handshake, and every tool call is authorized
 against that principal exactly as a gRPC call would be. This is (B), the same
 as `scotty` and `scottyagent`.

 It is also how the in-process persona runtime reaches the tool: tacplus
 generates `<Service>McpSurface::call(name, arguments)`, a session-free entry
 point the runtime's dispatch step calls directly (tacplus 2cfbd932; see
 decisions/persona-runtime-dispatch-helper-needed-2026-09-02.md). So one
 declaration serves both the model in-process and an external MCP client
 reading as the same person — there is no second surface to keep in step.

 Everything below the declaration is generated and nothing is hand-written:
 the tool name (snake_case of the rpc name), the description (the rpc's whole
 leading doc comment, verbatim), the JSON schema from the request message with
 server-computed fields omitted AND refused as arguments, and the
 session-carrying transport rpc, which exists the moment a service has >= 1
 MCP rpc and is never declared.

 itself stays private; the ticket, the advice and the decision do not.

CreateChatMessageMove files a message from one of the user's chats into
 another — sorting the default chat. Nothing is deleted and nothing is
 rewritten: the source chat records that it was moved out and the target
 chat gains the message, so both halves stay readable.

UpdateMyChatMembership archives, unarchives or mutes one of the user's own
 chats on their instruction, and records the standing notify policy they
 gave you for it. It changes what YOU surface to them; it removes nothing
 and no one else sees it.

GetMyRoutingMap returns the homes you are allowed to file things in: every
 tenant this person is a member of, and the tenant-to-tenant links relevant
 to those memberships. Read it before deciding where something belongs.
 These are the ONLY destinations that exist — a tenant not listed here is
 not a place you can put anything, and there is no way to ask for one. It is
 a read of your OWN memberships; it cannot see anyone else's and it writes
 nothing.

fields.name: hazelcast_memory_mb
fields.description: hazelcast_memory_mb is the Hazelcast cluster memory limit in MB. Default: 2048.

fields.name: map_idle_ttl_seconds
fields.description: map_idle_ttl_seconds evicts idle working-set maps. Default: 7200 (2h).

fields.name: max_maps
fields.description: max_maps limits concurrent working-set maps. Default: 20.

fields.name: retention_days
fields.description: retention_days is the number of days to retain hot events. Default: 90.

fields.name: cleanup_interval_seconds
fields.description: cleanup_interval_seconds is how often the retention cleanup job runs. Default: 3600.

fields.name: active_session_idle_seconds
fields.description:
active_session_idle_seconds is the idle threshold for ListActiveSessions.
 A session is considered active if its last event was within this window.
 Default: 900 (15 min). Min: 30.

fields.name: warm_window_seconds
fields.description:
warm_window_seconds is the memory-residency window for warm-tiered records:
 rows younger than this are served from memory, rows older than it are served
 from the on-disk warm tier. It is the default applied to a record type that
 declares the warm residency preset without a window_seconds of its own.

 It must be SHORTER than retention_days or the disk tier is never reached:
 retention deletes a row before it is ever old enough to age out of memory,
 and the "still queryable, only slower" promise the disk tier exists to keep
 never applies to anything. Default: 604800 (7 days), which leaves rows aged
 7-90 days served from disk under the 90-day retention default. Min: 60.

types.name: Alert
types.description:
NWS issues alerts against zones, and a zone covers many places. Storing an
 Alert per place would store the same hurricane watch once per job site in
 Harris County. So the row is keyed by NWS's own alert id and carries the zones
 it names; "alerts for this place" is a read that resolves the place's zones
 first (ListAlerts takes either form). Choice E.

 Write-once like the rest: an alert NWS UPDATEs or CANCELs arrives as a NEW
 alert row whose references name the one it supersedes. Nothing is edited in
 place, which is also why there is no "active" boolean — active is a function
 of (effective, expires, superseded) AT THE MOMENT YOU ASK, not a stored flag
 some poller has to remember to clear.

fields.name: zone_ids
fields.description:
zone_ids are the NWS zones this alert names — forecast zones, county zones,
 or both. Order is NWS's.

 A NOTE ON THE REPEATED-STRING BOUND, the same one work.Job carries:
 (spec.assert_max_size) does DOUBLE DUTY on a repeated string field — tacplus
 reads it as the element byte cap AND as the element count, and there is no
 second annotation that separates them. 256 here therefore means "at most 256
 zone ids, each at most 256 bytes". A zone id is 6 bytes; 256 zones is a wide
 hurricane watch but not an unheard-of one, and this is the number to revisit
 first if a real alert is ever truncated.

fields.name: event
fields.description:
event is NWS's event name, verbatim: "Hurricane Watch", "Flash Flood
 Warning", "Heat Advisory". NOT an enum: NWS's list is long, changes, and is
 authoritative elsewhere. A rule in Reveille matches on this string, and
 matching on the bureau's own word is more honest than matching on our lossy
 re-encoding of it. Choice F.

fields.name: severity
fields.description:
ALL FOUR CARRY (spec.assert_enum_defined), AND THAT ANNOTATION REFUSES THE
 *_UNSPECIFIED ZERO VALUE. It is worth saying at the point of use because the
 consequence is a long way from the declaration: a row stored with one of
 these left at zero is written happily by the state client and then fails
 RESPONSE validation inside the generated wrapper on every read of it,
 including every WATCH frame. That is why the ingest in services/weather/
 src/nws.rs falls back to a DECLARED value for each — UNKNOWN for the first
 three, and ALERT for message_type, which is also CAP's own default for the
 field — rather than leaving an absent value at zero.

fields.name: sent_at_ms
fields.description:
sent_at_ms is a RANGE (spec.query_field), emitting sent_at_ms_from /
 sent_at_ms_to — ListAlerts's declared window and this type's ONLY store-side
 criterion beyond the key. The other four stamps are not criteria: they are
 what `active_at_ms` is COMPUTED from, and that computation needs the
 supersession set over every alert, so narrowing on one of them in the store
 would change the answer rather than speed it up.

fields.name: sender_name
fields.description: sender_name is the issuing office ("NWS Houston/Galveston TX").

fields.name: references
fields.description:
references are the alert ids this one updates, corrects or cancels. The
 superseded rows STAY. Same rule as a renewed permit in `work` and a
 corrected document in the Doc Manager: the correction is a new row that
 points at the old one. Bounded at 256 for the same double-duty reason as
 zone_ids — an alert id is up to 256 bytes, so the count cannot be lower.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace: mandatory, `/system` on every row, no criterion. See message Place,
 including the WATCH-egress hazard note on its copy of this field.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description: spiffe_id: the publisher's identity, stamped by eventbus. See message Place.
