 no change when empty.

 THE SKETCH'S `bool set_crew` / `bool set_subs` MARKER IS NOT USED, and it is
 not a small omission: a fleet-wide grep found no `set_*`/`clear_*`/
 `replace_*` repeated-field marker anywhere, tacplus has no FieldMask support
 and no (spec.*) annotation for repeated-field replace semantics, so the pair
 would have been this platform's first — invented by one service for itself,
 which is the trap docmanager's update-is-partial-not-full-replace record was
 written to avoid. The cost of leaving it out is exactly one thing: a job's
 crew cannot be emptied by this rpc. That is a real gap, written down rather
 than papered over with a local convention, and the answer is a platform-wide
 one whenever somebody needs to clear a list.

types.name: UpdateJobResponse

message.name: Job
message.description:
One customer, any number of subs (Jody, 2026-09-09). A real place. The crew
 on it. Permits and papers hang off it by id. The job's chat is a Chat of
 kind JOB in the chat plane, referenced here, never duplicated.

 A NOTE ON THE REPEATED-STRING BOUNDS BELOW. (spec.assert_max_size) bounds
 the element COUNT; (spec.assert_element_max_size) bounds each element's
 BYTE LENGTH. Each of the three repeated id lists here is bounded at 64 ids
 of at most 64 bytes each, which is exactly the width of every *_id key in
 this file. That is also what keeps one Job inside the Tier-1 inline budget
 the MCP job list needs; see ListMyJobs.
 THE SIX KNOWLEDGE RECORDS ARE TENANT-OWNED, NOT `private`, AND THIS IS THE
 ONE PLACE THAT DISTINCTION IS WRITTEN DOWN. Job is the first of them, so the
 reasoning lives here and the other five point at it.

 Every record in this fleet before 2026-09-25 was one of two shapes, and these
 six are the third:

   - WorkActivity / ScottyActivity / AgentCycle: rows with an OWNING PERSON.
     Each carries (spec.store_principal) on the field naming that person, and
     the c2s read plane pins a caller to their own rows at C2S_SCOPE_PRINCIPAL.
   - profile.UserProfile / profile.RuleNode: the same, plus (spec.record).
     private — "a user's data and nobody else's, ever"
     (decisions/identity-people-tenant-devices-private-2026-09-21.md §4).
   - THESE: rows with no owning person at all. A job belongs to the COMPANY.
     So does a customer, a permit, the C88, a bid. The design record's own
     first line says it — "these rows belong to the company, not to a person,
     and exist whether or not anyone talks to Scotty" — and
     decisions/profile-service-proto-design-2026-09-20.md draws the same line
     from the other side when it puts a person's preferences in a PERSONAL
     service precisely because work's rows are not personal.

 So NO (spec.store_principal) ON ANY OF THE SIX, and that is not the omission
 it looks like. The annotation declares "the one principal whose rows these
 are", and naming one here would be a false statement with a real consequence:
 the generated egress row filter would drop every job not created by the
 reader, so a foreman would stop seeing the jobs the office opened. `created_by`
 is provenance, not ownership, and it is left as a plain string for that reason.
 (The same argument Task.assigned_to already makes for a different reason — two
 principals rather than none — and it is why the task participant gate is in the
 handler.)

 NOT `private` EITHER, for the reverse of profile's reason:
 ValidateRecordPrivateAnnotations requires a private record to carry
 (spec.store_principal), which these have nothing truthful to put in, and it
 refuses s2s_subscribe on one, which would leave these rows with no declared
 ingest path into stratum at all (the unresolved gap
 decisions/profile-people-tenant-single-instance-2026-09-21.md §Gap 2 records,
 and the reason profile cannot read its own rows today —
 decisions/profile-private-record-read-gap-2026-09-23.md). A tenant-scoped
 record has no such gap: it subscribes, it is read over the plane's S2S half,
 and its boundary is the tenant.

 WHAT KEEPS TENANTS APART IS `namespace`, AND IT IS BOTH HALVES OF THAT JOB.
 (spec.store_namespace) is mandatory on a record (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations)
 and drives the generated wrapper's egress filter; the EQ (spec.query_field)
 added to it here is what lets a criterion be PINNED into the predicate before
 the store is asked. Both are needed, and the query_field is the half that is
 easy to forget: the store evaluates only the criteria a record annotates, so
 an unannotated namespace field yields a filter that is "present, generated,
 and inert" (record_read_validate.go), leaving the crashing egress backstop as
 the only boundary. It matters more on the S2S half than it did in kernel:
 (spec.record).s2s_read's own cross-tenant doctrine is that "an authorized peer
 service reads FLEET-WIDE, across every tenant's rows", where the kernel state
 this replaced was chrooted per tenant. So the pin is not belt-and-braces here,
 it IS the tenant boundary, and services/work/src/service.rs applies it on every
 read path from the caller's verified claim.

 NO OTHER (spec.query_field) ON THESE SIX, deliberately. Every filter the
 Get/List rpcs offer — a status, a customer, membership of a repeated sub or
 crew list, a lapsing horizon, the two-principal task gate — is applied by the
 handler over the tenant's rows, which is exactly what it did when those rows
 came from kernel's fetch_all. Declaring criteria for the subset that happens
 to be expressible would push half of one read into the store and leave the
 other half in the handler, for no behaviour change; when a collection gets
 big enough that the tenant scan is the problem, the pushdown is a measured
 change with a number behind it, not a guess made here.

fields.name: job_id
fields.description:
job_id is the record key.

 (spec.indexed) WAS HERE AND IS GONE WITH THE STATE COLLECTION: it is the
 statedb field-index marker, and there is no state map left to index. The key
 is an EQ criterion on JobFilter without any annotation, because declaring
 s2s_read above folds a record's key into its filter (record_map.go's
 keyFilterCriterion) — which is what GetJob's point read is.

fields.name: customer_id
fields.description: customer_id is a Partner of kind CUSTOMER. Exactly one; required.

fields.name: sub_ids
fields.description: sub_ids are Partners of kind SUB. Order is not meaningful.

location is embedded, not a collection: a job has one place and the place
 has no life outside the job. If a yard or a customer site later needs to be
 a shared thing, it becomes a Location collection and this becomes an id.
 Choice D.

fields.name: note

note is prose for a person: "stage on the church lot, gate code 4471".
 Nothing parses it (design record §5).

fields.name: crew_human_ids
fields.description: crew is human_ids (scotty.Human), not names.

document_ids point INTO the Doc Manager. Kind, title, who filed it, when,

chat_id of the job's Chat (kind JOB) in the chat plane. Set when the job is
 created; the room is created alongside.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT, and on a record it is the tenant
 boundary rather than a second opinion about it — see the block above this
 message for why, and for why the EQ criterion is half the annotation.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record's declared `owner` and the PUBLISHER — eventbus
 stamps work's own service identity onto it. The field NAME is load-bearing
 (eventbus's topic discovery matches the literal string "spiffe_id" of
 string type when it decides which topics get publisher-identity stamping),

 narrowed something. The value the reads narrow by is `namespace` above.

WorkConfigState is the state boundary for work service configuration.
 Auto-injected by tacplus from (spec.grpc_config) annotation.

message.description: Config is delivered by kernel at startup and on every change.

fields.name: max_open_jobs
fields.description:
Resource bounds, not business rules — the same rule scotty.Config states.
 An entitlement makes an action impossible and a written policy makes it
 inadvisable; a config bound that hard-fails a create is neither, it is a
 resource limit on the service.

fields.name: permit_warning_days
fields.description:
permit_warning_days is how far ahead a lapsing permit is surfaced. It is a
 DEFAULT the runtime uses when no written policy says otherwise — Jody's
 "Warn me three days before any 811 ticket expires" is a rule in scotty, and
 it wins. Config so the default changes with no redeploy.

types.name: WorkState
types.description:
WorkState IS EMPTY, and that is the whole point of it — the same statement
 profile.ProfileState makes, in the same words, for the same reason.

 It exists because servicemanager's generated wiring requires every service in
 the build to host one state root (the same reason llmproxy.LlmProxyState is
 empty), not because this service keeps anything in kernel. Jody's 2026-09-25
 ruling is explicit — "kernel is in-memory coordination only", "something went
 very wrong if we are holding user data like tasks in kernel state" — so a
 field added here later is a CHANGE OF STORAGE PLANE, not a new field.

 WHAT WAS HERE, and where it went. Six `repeated` collections — jobs, tasks,
 partners, permits, equipment, rfps — each carrying (spec.persistence) = true,
 which the same ruling's item 2 turns into a generation error ("durable data
 belongs in stratum records"). Every one is now a (spec.record) below, read
 and written through stratum. The dev rows that were in kernel are lost on the
 next full kernel restart and that is accepted (ruling item 5).

 requires_artifact_on_write WENT WITH THEM, and the discipline it named did
 not. That option makes kernel refuse a STATE write with no accompanying
 artifact type; with no state fields left there is no state write for it to
 govern. Every write in services/work/src/service.rs still leaves a
 WorkActivity (design record §1: "nothing reaches knowledge without leaving an
 artifact") — it is now the handler's invariant, asserted in
 service_tests.rs, rather than kernel's.

rpcs.description:
CreateJob opens a new job: real work at a real place, for one customer,
 with the crew and the subs on it. Use it when work has been won or
 scheduled and needs somewhere for its tasks, permits and papers to live.
rpcs.verb_definition: Bring a new resource into existence.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Mint; creates durable resource state.

rpcs.description:
GetJob returns the job and the permits that hang off it — the job page's
 one read. The papers themselves are Doc Manager ids on the job.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.

rpcs.description:
ListJobs lists the company's jobs, optionally narrowed to one status, one
 customer, one sub or one crew member. Use it to answer what work is open,
 what somebody is on, or to find a job's id before reading or changing it.
 It writes nothing.
rpcs.verb_definition: Finite/paginated set, ordered by order_by; filters are fields.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get-plural/Search/Query; collection reads must declare method_collection.

rpcs.description:
UpdateJob: status, crew, subs, dates, location note. Name and customer are
 not updatable — a job for a different customer is a different job.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Merge; changes one existing resource rather than combining resources.

rpcs.description:
CreateTask raises something a person has to do — approve a timesheet, call
 a supplier back, be somewhere at a time — for whoever it is for, with a due
 date. Use it when something has come up that needs to land on a named
 person's list rather than be remembered.
rpcs.verb_definition: Bring a new resource into existence.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Mint; creates durable resource state.

rpcs.description:
ListTasks lists tasks with the soonest due first, optionally only one
 person's, only one job's, or only the ones still outstanding. Use it to
 answer what somebody still owes and what is due next. It writes nothing.
rpcs.verb_definition: Finite/paginated set, ordered by order_by; filters are fields.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get-plural/Search/Query; collection reads must declare method_collection.

rpcs.description: UpdateTask ticks a task off. `done` is the only mutable fact on one.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Merge; changes one existing resource rather than combining resources.

rpcs.description:
CreatePartner puts another company on the books — a customer, a
 subcontractor or a vendor — with its trade and who to call there. Use it
 when a company has to exist by name before a job, permit or bid can be
 opened against it.
rpcs.verb_definition: Bring a new resource into existence.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Mint; creates durable resource state.

rpcs.description:
GetPartner looks one customer, sub or vendor up by its id and returns who
 they are, what they do and how to reach them. Use it when a job or a bid
 names a partner and you need to know which company that is. It writes
 nothing.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.

rpcs.description:
ListPartners lists the companies this company works with, optionally only
 the customers, only the subs or only the vendors. Use it to find a company
 by name or to get its id before opening a job or a bid against it. It
 writes nothing.
rpcs.verb_definition: Finite/paginated set, ordered by order_by; filters are fields.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get-plural/Search/Query; collection reads must declare method_collection.

rpcs.description:
UpdatePartner changes what is on file for a customer, sub or vendor: their
 trade and who to call there. Use it when a company has changed its contact,
 its number or the work it does; a field left unset is left alone.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Merge; changes one existing resource rather than combining resources.

rpcs.description:
CreatePermit files a paper that can run out against a job — an 811 locate,
 a right-of-way, a stormwater notice — with the number it was issued under
 and the date it lapses. Use it when a job has been granted one; to renew
 one, file a new permit naming the old one rather than editing it.
rpcs.verb_definition: Bring a new resource into existence.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Mint; creates durable resource state.

rpcs.description:
ListPermits lists permits with the soonest to lapse first, optionally only
 the ones on one job. Use it to answer what is about to run out and what
 still covers a job. It writes nothing.
rpcs.verb_definition: Finite/paginated set, ordered by order_by; filters are fields.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get-plural/Search/Query; collection reads must declare method_collection.

rpcs.description: UpdatePermit: status only. A renewal is CreatePermit with renews_permit_id.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Merge; changes one existing resource rather than combining resources.

rpcs.description:

 truck 12 — with its unit number, its make and model, and the beacon a phone
 can recognize it by. Use it when a new piece of kit has to be tracked,
 serviced and put on jobs.
rpcs.verb_definition: Bring a new resource into existence.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Mint; creates durable resource state.

rpcs.description:
GetEquipment answers by equipment_id OR by beacon_id — the beacon form is
 what the phone asks when somebody sits on the machine.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.

rpcs.description:
ListEquipment lists the company's machines and vehicles — hours, oil life,
 when each was last serviced and when it is next due — optionally only the
 ones on one job. Use it to see what is out where and what is coming due for
 service. It writes nothing.
rpcs.verb_definition: Finite/paginated set, ordered by order_by; filters are fields.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get-plural/Search/Query; collection reads must declare method_collection.

rpcs.description: UpdateEquipment: readings and job assignment.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Merge; changes one existing resource rather than combining resources.

rpcs.description:
CreateRfp records work a customer has put out to bid, with what it is and
 the date the bid is due. Use it when a prospect comes in that is not a job
 yet — it becomes one only if the bid is won.
rpcs.verb_definition: Bring a new resource into existence.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Mint; creates durable resource state.

rpcs.description:
ListRfps lists the bids in flight with the soonest due first, optionally
 only one customer's or only the ones at one stage. Use it to answer what is
 out for bid and what is due next. It writes nothing.
rpcs.verb_definition: Finite/paginated set, ordered by order_by; filters are fields.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get-plural/Search/Query; collection reads must declare method_collection.

rpcs.description:
UpdateRfp moves a bid along — submitted, won, lost, withdrawn — and, once
 it is won, names the job it turned into. Use it when the standing of an
 outstanding bid has changed.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Merge; changes one existing resource rather than combining resources.

rpcs.description:
CreateMyTask raises a new task. Use it when something came up that a person
 has to do — approve a timesheet, call a supplier back, be somewhere. Say
 who it is for in assigned_to (leave it empty for the person you are talking
 to), what it is in title, and when it is due. It cannot create a task for
 someone outside this tenant.

UpdateMyTask ticks a task off as done. It is the only change that can be
 made to a task: a task that was raised in error is not deleted, it is
 completed and the artifact records who completed it and when.

GetMyJob looks one job up by its id and returns it with every permit that
 hangs off it — what is on that job and what is about to run out on it. It
 writes nothing.

ListMyJobs lists the company's jobs, newest status first, optionally
 narrowed to one customer, one sub or one crew member. Ask it "what jobs am
 I on" by passing your own human id as crew_human_id. It writes nothing.
rpcs.verb_definition: Finite/paginated set, ordered by order_by; filters are fields.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get-plural/Search/Query; collection reads must declare method_collection.

rpcs.description:
ListMyLapsingPermits lists the permits that run out soonest — 811 locates,
 right-of-way, stormwater — optionally only the ones on one job, and
 optionally only the ones lapsing within N days. This is the read behind
 "what is about to run out". It writes nothing.
rpcs.verb_definition: Finite/paginated set, ordered by order_by; filters are fields.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get-plural/Search/Query; collection reads must declare method_collection.

rpcs.description:
UpdateMyJob changes a job that is already open: its status, its crew, its
 subs, its dates, the note on its location. A field left unset is left
 alone. The job's name and its customer cannot be changed — a job for a
 different customer is a different job.

CreateMyPermit files a permit against a job: an 811 locate, a right-of-way,
 a stormwater notice. To RENEW one, file a new permit and name the old one
 in renews_permit_id — the old permit is never edited.

GetMyEquipment looks a machine up by its id or by the beacon id the phone
 just matched, and returns what is known about it: hours, oil life, when it
 was last serviced and when it is next due, and which job it is on today. It
 writes nothing.

BrokerWorkMcpSession carries one Model Context Protocol session for Work over a
 single bidirectional stream: one complete JSON-RPC frame per stream message,
 request frames in and response frames out, for the life of the session.

 Generated, never declared: Work has at least one RPC_PRINCIPAL_MCP rpc, and this
 is the only channel those tools are reachable through. Bidirectional because an
 MCP session is stateful — it opens with an initialize handshake and holds the
 negotiated protocol version after it — so a unary call would repeat that
 handshake per tool call.

services.name: Work
services.description:
The verb registry is CLOSED (tacplus/pkg/internal/common/verbs/registry.json)
 and this service uses five of it: Create / Get / List / Update / Watch. There
 is NO Delete anywhere, and that is choice F made structural rather than
 guarded — a wrong task is done with a note on the artifact, a lapsed permit
 is renewed by a new permit with renews_permit_id, a job is CLOSED.

 Every List is COLLECTION_MODE_PAGE: these are the app's own tiles and they
 grow without bound, so the client drives a resumable window with an opaque
 page_token rather than asking for a snapshot whose cap would eventually bite.
 The wrapper owns the token codec and the page_size bound; the handler is a
 keyset producer.

 can recognize it by. Use it when a new piece of kit has to be tracked,
 serviced and put on jobs.
rpcs.verb_definition: Bring a new resource into existence.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Mint; creates durable resource state.

rpcs.description:
GetEquipment answers by equipment_id OR by beacon_id — the beacon form is
 what the phone asks when somebody sits on the machine.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT List/Watch; returns one resource or not-found and must not mutate state.

rpcs.description:
ListEquipment lists the company's machines and vehicles — hours, oil life,
 when each was last serviced and when it is next due — optionally only the
 ones on one job. Use it to see what is out where and what is coming due for
 service. It writes nothing.
rpcs.verb_definition: Finite/paginated set, ordered by order_by; filters are fields.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get-plural/Search/Query; collection reads must declare method_collection.

rpcs.description: UpdateEquipment: readings and job assignment.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Merge; changes one existing resource rather than combining resources.

rpcs.description:
CreateRfp records work a customer has put out to bid, with what it is and
 the date the bid is due. Use it when a prospect comes in that is not a job
 yet — it becomes one only if the bid is won.
rpcs.verb_definition: Bring a new resource into existence.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Mint; creates durable resource state.

rpcs.description:
ListRfps lists the bids in flight with the soonest due first, optionally
 only one customer's or only the ones at one stage. Use it to answer what is
 out for bid and what is due next. It writes nothing.
rpcs.verb_definition: Finite/paginated set, ordered by order_by; filters are fields.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get-plural/Search/Query; collection reads must declare method_collection.

rpcs.description:
UpdateRfp moves a bid along — submitted, won, lost, withdrawn — and, once
 it is won, names the job it turned into. Use it when the standing of an
 outstanding bid has changed.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Merge; changes one existing resource rather than combining resources.

rpcs.description:
CreateMyTask raises a new task. Use it when something came up that a person
 has to do — approve a timesheet, call a supplier back, be somewhere. Say
 who it is for in assigned_to (leave it empty for the person you are talking
 to), what it is in title, and when it is due. It cannot create a task for
 someone outside this tenant.

UpdateMyTask ticks a task off as done. It is the only change that can be
 made to a task: a task that was raised in error is not deleted, it is
 completed and the artifact records who completed it and when.

GetMyJob looks one job up by its id and returns it with every permit that
 hangs off it — what is on that job and what is about to run out on it. It
 writes nothing.

ListMyJobs lists the company's jobs, newest status first, optionally
 narrowed to one customer, one sub or one crew member. Ask it "what jobs am
 I on" by passing your own human id as crew_human_id. It writes nothing.
rpcs.verb_definition: Finite/paginated set, ordered by order_by; filters are fields.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get-plural/Search/Query; collection reads must declare method_collection.

rpcs.description:
ListMyLapsingPermits lists the permits that run out soonest — 811 locates,
 right-of-way, stormwater — optionally only the ones on one job, and
 optionally only the ones lapsing within N days. This is the read behind
 "what is about to run out". It writes nothing.
rpcs.verb_definition: Finite/paginated set, ordered by order_by; filters are fields.
rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Get-plural/Search/Query; collection reads must declare method_collection.

rpcs.description:
UpdateMyJob changes a job that is already open: its status, its crew, its
 subs, its dates, the note on its location. A field left unset is left
 alone. The job's name and its customer cannot be changed — a job for a
 different customer is a different job.

CreateMyPermit files a permit against a job: an 811 locate, a right-of-way,
 a stormwater notice. To RENEW one, file a new permit and name the old one
 in renews_permit_id — the old permit is never edited.

GetMyEquipment looks a machine up by its id or by the beacon id the phone
 just matched, and returns what is known about it: hours, oil life, when it
 was last serviced and when it is next due, and which job it is on today. It
 writes nothing.

BrokerWorkMcpSession carries one Model Context Protocol session for Work over a
 single bidirectional stream: one complete JSON-RPC frame per stream message,
 request frames in and response frames out, for the life of the session.

 Generated, never declared: Work has at least one RPC_PRINCIPAL_MCP rpc, and this
 is the only channel those tools are reachable through. Bidirectional because an
 MCP session is stateful — it opens with an initialize handshake and holds the
 negotiated protocol version after it — so a unary call would repeat that
 handshake per tool call.

rpcs.verb_boundary: NOT Proxy; owns matching, relay, or completion semantics rather than transparently forwarding one backend call.

fields.name: can

fields.name: ask_instead

types.name: CompanyStructure
types.description:
CompanyStructure — ONE row per tenant (A17), keyed by tenant id. Written
 only from the web console by the owner role (D6); for the first tenant,
 seeded once by the import service (Q27). Deterministic rules are structured
 fields here, checked by the service path, not by a model.

 NOT HERE, on purpose (Jody, 2026-09-29):
   - Quiet hours / holds. Whether a PERSON is interrupted is their own
     Scotty's call against their own rules; no company dog decides a hold.
     TODO(CP3): A17 listed quiet hours as a company rule; that entry is
     superseded by "holds are Scotty's" and no field is declared.
   - Language. A per-person user setting, not a company one.
   - Birthdays / anniversaries and muting a persona. Scotty rules on the
     person's profile, not company features.
   - Break-glass. Tenant two.

 RETENTION: OPERATIONAL.

fields.name: reports_to
fields.description:
reports_to orders the org chart; it also sets Scotty budget precedence
 among members (A11).

fields.name: room_ids
fields.description:
room_ids: for a guest role, the ONLY rooms they see and may @ a dog in
 (A21).

fields.name: time_zone
fields.description:
time_zone is IANA; the scheduler and the budget day are tenant-local and
 DST-safe (A18).

fields.name: muster_minute
fields.description: muster_minute: tenant-local minute of the daily muster (Sarge's routine).

fields.name: escalation_chain
fields.description:
escalation_chain: roles in order, first to last. The top is who decides
 when nobody else will (DQ35); the ack window before the next is tried is
 runtime Config (DQ14: 30 min in work hours).

fields.name: offboarding_role
fields.description: offboarding_role handles a member leaving.

fields.name: dog_budgets
fields.description:
Tenant policy (A16). One DogBudget per company dog; a dog with no entry
 gets the D18 defaults.

message.name: DogBudget
message.description:
DogBudget is one company dog's two daily buckets, in integer micro-USD
 (A11). Defaults (D18): $1 day job, $1 above-and-beyond; revisable after the
 pilot. Scotty's $0.50/person/day is SeaBeam's (A24) and not tenant policy,
 so it is not here.

fields.name: reserve_micro_usd
fields.description:
reserve_micro_usd is the tenant's daily priority lane for approvals and
 Barry's safety events (A11; D18 default $2).

fields.name: all_dogs_room_id
fields.description: all_dogs_room_id is the tenant's all-dogs channel (Q12: CHAT_KIND_CREW).

fields.name: office_room_id
fields.description:
office_room_id is where unroutable inbound mail lands for a person
 (crew-email decision: no match is never a guess).

types.name: ConversationMove
types.description:
ConversationMove is the typed "moving this to …" (A6). Rendered as that
 line; the chat's CHAT_EVENT_KIND_MOVED_OUT event still records the move.

types.name: CrewCommand
types.description:
CrewCommand is a typed request from one dog to the dog that owns a record
 type (A4): "change your record this way". Sent in the open room; the owner
 fulfils or declines on its own record. No field-level rights machinery.

fields.name: record_type
fields.description: record_type + record_key: the target, e.g. "beagle.JobPermits" + job id.

fields.name: read_version
fields.description: read_version is the version the sender read (A4 optimistic versions).

fields.name: verb
fields.description: verb is one of the owning dog's command verbs ("add_permit").

fields.name: args_json
fields.description:
args_json: JSON because the verbs are per owner and a oneof over every
 dog's verbs would make this file import the crew (Q6's reasoning).

types.name: CrewCommandReply
types.description: CrewCommandReply is the owner's answer, in the same thread.

fields.name: new_version
fields.description: new_version of the owner's record after a fulfilment.

types.name: CrewCursor
types.description:
CrewCursor is one row per logical instance: scottyagent.AgentCursor
 generalized. Queued = done_through_seq < seq < next_seq.
 RETENTION: follows CHAT (runtime bookkeeping).

fields.name: instance_key
fields.description:
instance_key is the KEY and the only criterion (scottyagent-record-shapes
 D2: a second criterion loses the point read).

fields.name: next_seq
fields.description: next_seq is the seq the next enqueued event will take.

fields.name: done_through_seq
fields.description:
done_through_seq is the highest seq acknowledged by `done`. It is written
 AFTER the step checkpoints, never with them (A1). Under A29 acks are per
 thread (ThreadMapEntry.done_through_seq) and this is their LOW-WATER MARK
 over live threads (lowest un-acked seq minus one), used only by restart
 recovery.

fields.name: parked_until_ms
fields.description:
parked_until_ms is set when the budget parks the queue (A11): events keep
 queueing, nothing is re-delivered, no run starts before this time
 (tenant-local midnight), and catch-up is one compacted run.

fields.name: fence_epoch
fields.description:
fence_epoch / fence_counter: the last run lease's token (A2). Stratum is
 the guard (high-water mark per lock name, ask S7); this copy is for
 recovery and inspection.

types.name: CrewEvent
types.description:
CrewEvent is ONE queued event for ONE logical dog instance. The runtime
 writes it before it acks the source, so an event is durable here or still
 on the source topic, never only in process memory (§2.3, A1). A redelivered
 source is recognised by source_key and not given a second seq.

 RETENTION: CHAT (90 days working set, archived 1 year) — it carries text.

fields.name: instance_key
fields.description:
instance_key is the logical instance: "<dog>" for a TENANT persona (the
 tenant is `namespace`), "<dog>/<person>" for Scotty.

fields.name: seq
fields.description:
seq is strictly increasing per instance_key, no gaps once assigned. The
 single writer is the dog's pod under its run lease (A2).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_ROOM_MESSAGE
enum_values.description:
A room message or DM addressed to this dog (a messaging delivery whose
 recipient is the dog's principal; Q8).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_RECORD_CHANGE
enum_values.description: A row of a subscribed record type was written.

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_SCHEDULE_TICK
enum_values.description: A Scheduler wake-up fired (§5; ask S1).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_CREW_COMMAND
enum_values.description: A CrewCommand from another dog, or the reply to one of this dog's (A4).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_PROPOSAL_DECISION
enum_values.description: A decision on a scotty.Ticket this dog filed (A10).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_EMAIL
enum_values.description:
Inbound mail routed to this dog by the tenant's mailbox (D4, D16;
 decisions/crew-email-2026-09-29.md).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_WAIT_DEADLINE
enum_values.description: A Wait's deadline passed with no match (A3).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_PIGEON
enum_values.description:
A FROM_PIGEON / FROM_COOP message on coop.PigeonMessage for a run this
 instance started (A30).

fields.name: source_key
fields.description:
source_key identifies the source event: a delivery_id, "<record type>/
 <key>/<store_epoch>", a scheduler fire id, a decision id, a mail id.

fields.name: actor
fields.description: actor is the principal that caused the event. Empty for a schedule tick.

fields.name: actor_is_member
fields.description:
actor_is_member is resolved at enqueue against the tenant's memberships.
 A fact for the disclosure policy (A32); it does not gate the queue.

fields.name: refs
fields.description: refs are the job / room / record the event references.

fields.name: record_type
fields.description: record_type is the proto full name for REF_KIND_RECORD, e.g. "work.Permit".

fields.name: text
fields.description:
text is UNTRUSTED (A9).
 TODO(CP4): for a person<->Scotty conversation this stays EMPTY — those
 conversations are never logged (Jody, 2026-09-29); Scotty reads the text
 from the person's own private chat rows at run time.

fields.name: is_direct
fields.description: is_direct: a DM rather than a room message.

fields.name: addressed
fields.description:
addressed: the dog was @-mentioned or DM'd, so the message earns a reply.
 False = woken by a wake word: act silently and log (A5, A8).

message.name: RecordChange
message.description: RecordChange carries a written row as record_type + key + proto3 JSON (Q6).

fields.name: wakeup_id
fields.description: wakeup_id is the Scheduler's id for the registration that fired.

fields.name: tag
fields.description:
tag is the registration's name, keyed (dog, tenant, name) (A18): "muster",
 "wait:<wait_id>", "proposal-expiry:<ticket_id>", "permit-expiry:<id>".

message.name: ProposalDecided
message.description: ProposalDecided points at the scotty.Ticket and its decision (A10).

message.name: EmailMessage
message.description:
EmailMessage is one inbound mail the tenant's mailbox routed to this dog
 (decisions/crew-email-2026-09-29.md). UNTRUSTED (A9). The company has ONE

 classifier, never by a per-dog address.

 names a dog's own address.

fields.name: mail_thread_token

mail_thread_token is the +t.<thread> token the reply came back on; empty
 for genuinely new mail.

fields.name: auto_submitted
fields.description:
auto_submitted: the mail declared itself automated (Auto-Submitted other
 than "no", Precedence bulk/junk/list, or our own agent header). The
 runtime never replies to such a mail (loop protection).

fields.name: question
fields.description: question: the pigeon needs a choice the request did not make.

message.name: Question
message.description:
Question: the page offers a choice the request does not decide (e.g. two
 county matches). The pigeon never guesses a field the request names. Script
 mode asks too (PG7).

fields.name: field
fields.description: field is the request field it concerns.

fields.name: prompt
fields.description: prompt is scrubbed (§1.5).

fields.name: snapshot
fields.description: snapshot is the page as the pigeon saw it.

message.name: EvidenceRef
message.description:
EvidenceRef points at one blob the pigeon captured (blobstore, tenant
 namespace). Declared here and imported by crew, beagle and tally.

fields.name: source_url
fields.description: source_url is scrubbed of query secrets (§1.5 S5).

fields.name: answer_by_ms
fields.description:
answer_by_ms: after this the run ends RESULT_STATUS_NEEDS_ANSWER (PG7:
 5 min after asking by default).

fields.name: result
fields.description: result is terminal; the pigeon then waits for discard or deadline.

enum_values.name: RUN_MODE_MIXED
enum_values.description: MIXED: script with model takeover at one or more steps (§1.7 drift).

enum_values.name: RESULT_STATUS_NEEDS_ANSWER
enum_values.description: NEEDS_ANSWER: a Question went unanswered by answer_by_ms.

fields.name: draft_id
fields.description:
draft_id is the portal's suspended-ticket id: the prepared ticket lives in
 Sonar's state account as a draft until a person submits it.

fields.name: entered
fields.description:
entered: field -> value as the portal shows it after entry (read back
 from the review page), for the §1.6 compare.

fields.name: review_page
fields.description: review_page: screenshot + HTML of the final review step.

fields.name: status
fields.description: status is the portal's word, verbatim.

fields.name: fields
fields.description: fields as filed, for the compare.

fields.name: evidence
fields.description:
evidence: every page/screenshot/download the result relies on (blobstore,
 tenant namespace). The dog copies refs onto its own record; never the bytes.

fields.name: failure
fields.description: failure is set iff status != OK.

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_UNRECOGNIZED_PAGE
enum_values.description: UNRECOGNIZED_PAGE: script mode, and model mode is not allowed for the kind.

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_LEASE_UNAVAILABLE
enum_values.description: LEASE_UNAVAILABLE: coop FAILED_PRECONDITION until the lease store exists.

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_DOMAIN_BLOCKED
enum_values.description: DOMAIN_BLOCKED: pigeonproxy refused a CONNECT.

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_PORTAL_REJECTED
enum_values.description: PORTAL_REJECTED: the portal's validation message, quoted in detail.

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_COMMIT_CONTROL_BLOCKED
enum_values.description: COMMIT_CONTROL_BLOCKED: the path required actuating a commit control.

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_READBACK_MISMATCH
enum_values.description: READBACK_MISMATCH: the §1.6 compare failed.

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_SCRUB_FAILED
enum_values.description: SCRUB_FAILED: a snapshot could not be scrubbed and was withheld (§1.5 S7).

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_INVALID_TASK
enum_values.description: INVALID_TASK: the body failed the kind's schema.

fields.name: detail
fields.description: detail is scrubbed (§1.5).

fields.name: trace
fields.description: trace: scrubbed step snapshots.

fields.name: recorded_path
fields.description:
recorded_path: set when any step ran in model mode and the run succeeded
 (§1.7). A blob of RecordedStep rows; the promotion input.

fields.name: error_code
fields.description:
error_code / error_detail are set for FROM_COOP, e.g. "PIGEON_GONE" /
 "discarded".

fields.name: thread_id
fields.description: thread_id of the message this event carries or was caused by (A6).

fields.name: causation_id
fields.description:
causation_id + hop_count (A7): copied from the message that caused this
 one with the hop incremented; a human message starts a new chain at 0.
 The model is warned past the soft threshold and the chain is parked at the
 hard ceiling (runtime Config; Jody: soft 10, hard 50).

fields.name: wait_id
fields.description: wait_id is set when this event closes a Wait (A3).

fields.name: actor_name
fields.description:
The A32 envelope. 25 is the pigeon payload arm.
 actor_name is the actor's crew or person name, rendered "name@tenant".

fields.name: actor_tenant
fields.description: actor_tenant is from the actor's SPIFFE tenant, never the body.

fields.name: orgs_present
fields.description: orgs_present are the tenants in the room, plus the addressed org.

types.name: CrewEventBus
types.description: tacplus:generated EventBus topic wrapper for CrewEvent.

message.name: CrewEvent
message.description:
CrewEvent is ONE queued event for ONE logical dog instance. The runtime
 writes it before it acks the source, so an event is durable here or still
 on the source topic, never only in process memory (§2.3, A1). A redelivered
 source is recognised by source_key and not given a second seq.

 RETENTION: CHAT (90 days working set, archived 1 year) — it carries text.

fields.name: instance_key
fields.description:
instance_key is the logical instance: "<dog>" for a TENANT persona (the
 tenant is `namespace`), "<dog>/<person>" for Scotty.

fields.name: seq
fields.description:
seq is strictly increasing per instance_key, no gaps once assigned. The
 single writer is the dog's pod under its run lease (A2).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_ROOM_MESSAGE
enum_values.description:
A room message or DM addressed to this dog (a messaging delivery whose
 recipient is the dog's principal; Q8).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_RECORD_CHANGE
enum_values.description: A row of a subscribed record type was written.

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_SCHEDULE_TICK
enum_values.description: A Scheduler wake-up fired (§5; ask S1).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_CREW_COMMAND
enum_values.description: A CrewCommand from another dog, or the reply to one of this dog's (A4).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_PROPOSAL_DECISION
enum_values.description: A decision on a scotty.Ticket this dog filed (A10).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_EMAIL
enum_values.description:
Inbound mail routed to this dog by the tenant's mailbox (D4, D16;
 decisions/crew-email-2026-09-29.md).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_WAIT_DEADLINE
enum_values.description: A Wait's deadline passed with no match (A3).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_PIGEON
enum_values.description:
A FROM_PIGEON / FROM_COOP message on coop.PigeonMessage for a run this
 instance started (A30).

fields.name: source_key
fields.description:
source_key identifies the source event: a delivery_id, "<record type>/
 <key>/<store_epoch>", a scheduler fire id, a decision id, a mail id.

fields.name: actor
fields.description: actor is the principal that caused the event. Empty for a schedule tick.

fields.name: actor_is_member
fields.description:
actor_is_member is resolved at enqueue against the tenant's memberships.
 A fact for the disclosure policy (A32); it does not gate the queue.

fields.name: refs
fields.description: refs are the job / room / record the event references.

fields.name: record_type
fields.description: record_type is the proto full name for REF_KIND_RECORD, e.g. "work.Permit".

fields.name: text
fields.description:
text is UNTRUSTED (A9).
 TODO(CP4): for a person<->Scotty conversation this stays EMPTY — those
 conversations are never logged (Jody, 2026-09-29); Scotty reads the text
 from the person's own private chat rows at run time.

fields.name: is_direct
fields.description: is_direct: a DM rather than a room message.

fields.name: addressed
fields.description:
addressed: the dog was @-mentioned or DM'd, so the message earns a reply.
 False = woken by a wake word: act silently and log (A5, A8).

message.name: RecordChange
message.description: RecordChange carries a written row as record_type + key + proto3 JSON (Q6).

fields.name: wakeup_id
fields.description: wakeup_id is the Scheduler's id for the registration that fired.

fields.name: tag
fields.description:
tag is the registration's name, keyed (dog, tenant, name) (A18): "muster",
 "wait:<wait_id>", "proposal-expiry:<ticket_id>", "permit-expiry:<id>".

message.name: ProposalDecided
message.description: ProposalDecided points at the scotty.Ticket and its decision (A10).

message.name: EmailMessage
message.description:
EmailMessage is one inbound mail the tenant's mailbox routed to this dog
 (decisions/crew-email-2026-09-29.md). UNTRUSTED (A9). The company has ONE
 address; the dog was chosen by the thread token, a plus-address hint or the
 classifier, never by a per-dog address.
 TODO(FD-8): per-dog email is open (the crew-email decision); nothing here
 names a dog's own address.

fields.name: mail_thread_token
fields.description:
mail_thread_token is the +t.<thread> token the reply came back on; empty
 for genuinely new mail.

fields.name: auto_submitted
fields.description:
auto_submitted: the mail declared itself automated (Auto-Submitted other
 than "no", Precedence bulk/junk/list, or our own agent header). The
 runtime never replies to such a mail (loop protection).

message.name: CrewCommand
message.description:
CrewCommand is a typed request from one dog to the dog that owns a record
 type (A4): "change your record this way". Sent in the open room; the owner
 fulfils or declines on its own record. No field-level rights machinery.

fields.name: record_type
fields.description: record_type + record_key: the target, e.g. "beagle.JobPermits" + job id.

fields.name: read_version
fields.description: read_version is the version the sender read (A4 optimistic versions).

fields.name: verb
fields.description: verb is one of the owning dog's command verbs ("add_permit").

fields.name: args_json
fields.description:
args_json: JSON because the verbs are per owner and a oneof over every
 dog's verbs would make this file import the crew (Q6's reasoning).

message.name: CrewCommandReply
message.description: CrewCommandReply is the owner's answer, in the same thread.

fields.name: new_version
fields.description: new_version of the owner's record after a fulfilment.

message.name: ConversationMove
message.description:
ConversationMove is the typed "moving this to …" (A6). Rendered as that
 line; the chat's CHAT_EVENT_KIND_MOVED_OUT event still records the move.

message.name: PigeonEvent
message.description:
PigeonEvent is one coop.PigeonMessage for a run this instance started
 (A30). The thread is CrewEvent.thread_id: the pigeon thread, an ordinary
 ThreadMapEntry. body is DATA (A9). A FROM_COOP PIGEON_GONE or ENDED closes
 any wait_for on the thread.

fields.name: body
fields.description: body is set for FROM_PIGEON.

message.name: FromPigeon
message.description: FromPigeon is the body of a FROM_PIGEON message (pigeon -> dog).

fields.name: actor_name
fields.description:
The A32 envelope. 25 is the pigeon payload arm.
 actor_name is the actor's crew or person name, rendered "name@tenant".

fields.name: actor_tenant
fields.description: actor_tenant is from the actor's SPIFFE tenant, never the body.

fields.name: orgs_present
fields.description: orgs_present are the tenants in the room, plus the addressed org.

types.name: DogBudget
types.description:
DogBudget is one company dog's two daily buckets, in integer micro-USD
 (A11). Defaults (D18): $1 day job, $1 above-and-beyond; revisable after the
 pilot. Scotty's $0.50/person/day is SeaBeam's (A24) and not tenant policy,
 so it is not here.

types.name: EmailMessage
types.description:
EmailMessage is one inbound mail the tenant's mailbox routed to this dog
 (decisions/crew-email-2026-09-29.md). UNTRUSTED (A9). The company has ONE
 address; the dog was chosen by the thread token, a plus-address hint or the
 classifier, never by a per-dog address.
 TODO(FD-8): per-dog email is open (the crew-email decision); nothing here
 names a dog's own address.

fields.name: mail_thread_token
fields.description:
mail_thread_token is the +t.<thread> token the reply came back on; empty
 for genuinely new mail.

fields.name: auto_submitted
fields.description:
auto_submitted: the mail declared itself automated (Auto-Submitted other
 than "no", Precedence bulk/junk/list, or our own agent header). The
 runtime never replies to such a mail (loop protection).

types.name: EventBusRecordMeta
GetRoomDigestRequest
types.description:
GetRoomDigestRequest is get_room_digest's arguments. PAGE-shaped: the token
 comes back in the structured result and the model passes it back (§2.6).

fields.name: record_type
fields.description: record_type is the proto full name for REF_KIND_RECORD, e.g. "work.Permit".

types.name: GetRoomDigestResponse

message.name: RoomDigestThread
message.description:
RoomDigestThread is one thread of a room, deterministically derived (BQ11).
 NEVER a message body: subject is at most the thread's first line.

fields.name: open_proposal_ids
fields.description: open_proposal_ids / open_wait_ids: what is still pending in the thread.

fields.name: subject
fields.description: subject is at most 80 characters; the bound is bytes, so 4 per character.

types.name: Grant
types.description:
Grant — a right delegated from one person to another through the
 delegator's Scotty (A15): time-boxed, in force automatically inside its
 window, revocable, and dead the moment the delegator no longer holds the
 right. Checked by the service path wherever the right is checked. Written
 only on the delegator's explicit instruction (DQ28).
 RETENTION: OPERATIONAL.

fields.name: scope
fields.description:
scope narrows the grant (e.g. one job); empty = wherever the delegator
 holds the right.

fields.name: record_type
fields.description: record_type is the proto full name for REF_KIND_RECORD, e.g. "work.Permit".

fields.name: revoked_at_ms
fields.description: revoked_at_ms: 0 = not revoked.

types.description:

 mutating tool call, written by the runtime, never by the model. It carries
 ids and a one-line summary, never message text, so a person<->Scotty
 conversation never lands here (Jody, 2026-09-29).
 TODO(design §6): PersonalLogbookEntry (Scotty's private copy, P8/S3) and
 Reveille's actor-stripped projection (A19) are not declared yet.
 RETENTION: LOG (2 years).

fields.name: reports_to
fields.description:
reports_to orders the org chart; it also sets Scotty budget precedence
 among members (A11).

fields.name: room_ids
fields.description:
room_ids: for a guest role, the ONLY rooms they see and may @ a dog in
 (A21).

types.name: PersonaDefinition
types.description:
PersonaDefinition is one dog, fixed at build time. A change is a release; a
 dog is the same dog in every company. Tenant policy (budgets, rooms,
 escalation, rules) is CompanyStructure and CrewRule, never this.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
name is the dog's name as people say it ("Barry"). Unique fleet-wide.
 Proper names never translate (D20): Reveille is always Reveille.

fields.name: species
fields.description: species is presentation only. FIXED, and so is the art (A16).

fields.name: scope
fields.description:
scope is who one logical instance belongs to: TENANT for the eight company
 dogs, PERSON for Scotty (contract §1).

enum_values.name: PERSONA_SCOPE_TENANT
enum_values.description:
One logical instance per tenant; pod identity
 spiffe://<td>/tenants/<tenant>/services/<dog> ((spec.service).tenant_owned).

enum_values.name: PERSONA_SCOPE_PERSON
enum_values.description: One logical instance per person in the people tenant (Scotty, Q2).

fields.name: voice
fields.description:
voice is the style paragraph of the system prompt. 8192: Scotty's voice is
 its whole character prompt (services/scotty/src/persona.rs, ~4.5 KB).

fields.name: standing_orders
fields.description:
standing_orders are the ONLY instructions the dog ever receives (§10).
 Every persona carries the "functional-tools" order (A29; see StandingOrder).

message.name: StandingOrder
message.description:
StandingOrder. Every PersonaDefinition carries the A29 order with id
 "functional-tools", verbatim (backlog-scotty-slices §2.6):
   "Every tool call is a plain function call. Nothing is remembered for you
   between calls. When a tool returns a page token, query id, cursor, thread
   id or proposal id, you must pass it back yourself in your next call if you
   need it. If you leave it out, you start over."
 TODO(T1): the generate-time check that every (spec.persona) has it waits on
 T1; until then a crew-runtime unit test enforces it.

fields.name: id
fields.description:
id is cited as the authority of an act. Stable across releases; a changed
 meaning takes a new id.

fields.name: tools
tool
fields.description:
tool is "<package>.<Rpc>" of an MCP-exposed rpc, e.g. "work.CreateMyTask".
 At the fleet pin (tacplus 18e551be) a requires_device rpc is still
 auto-exposed to MCP; no persona may list one until the pin includes
 c50ca319 (ask T3).

fields.name: needs_thumb
fields.description:
needs_thumb: the model is NOT offered this tool; it can only file a
 Proposal whose payload is this call (§8, §10).

fields.name: triggers
fields.description:
triggers are what wake this dog; under T1 each becomes a generated
 (spec.subscribe).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_ROOM_MESSAGE
enum_values.description:
A room message or DM addressed to this dog (a messaging delivery whose
 recipient is the dog's principal; Q8).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_RECORD_CHANGE
enum_values.description: A row of a subscribed record type was written.

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_SCHEDULE_TICK
enum_values.description: A Scheduler wake-up fired (§5; ask S1).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_CREW_COMMAND
enum_values.description: A CrewCommand from another dog, or the reply to one of this dog's (A4).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_PROPOSAL_DECISION
enum_values.description: A decision on a scotty.Ticket this dog filed (A10).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_EMAIL
enum_values.description:
Inbound mail routed to this dog by the tenant's mailbox (D4, D16;
 decisions/crew-email-2026-09-29.md).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_WAIT_DEADLINE
enum_values.description: A Wait's deadline passed with no match (A3).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_PIGEON
enum_values.description:
A FROM_PIGEON / FROM_COOP message on coop.PigeonMessage for a run this
 instance started (A30).

fields.name: topic_ref
fields.description: topic_ref for EVENT_SOURCE_RECORD_CHANGE, e.g. "work.JobBus.stream".

fields.name: mention_only
fields.description:
mention_only for EVENT_SOURCE_ROOM_MESSAGE: wake only on an @mention, a DM
 or a wake word (A5), not on every line in a room the dog sits in (X2).

fields.name: bucket
fields.description: bucket pays for runs this trigger starts (A11, Q19).

fields.name: capability_manifest
fields.description:
capability_manifest is what the dog can do HERE TODAY and who to ask
 instead (A14). The runtime gates tools and routing on the same list.

fields.name: can
fields.description: can is one thing the dog does here today, in plain words.

fields.name: ask_instead
fields.description: ask_instead is a persona name, or empty for "a person".

fields.name: owned_record_types
fields.description:
owned_record_types / readable_record_types are proto full names (A4,
 A16), e.g. "beagle.JobPermits". Owned = the one writer by type.

fields.name: wake_words
fields.description:
wake_words wake this dog on an UNADDRESSED line (A5). At most two dogs
 wake per line, decided once at fan-out (Q17). A wake-word wake never
 replies (A8).

fields.name: proposal_kinds
fields.description:
proposal_kinds: the needs_thumb tools this dog may file as a Proposal
 (scotty.Ticket, extended; A10).

fields.name: wait_allowlist
fields.description: wait_allowlist is what wait_for may wait on (A3).

fields.name: scripted_routines
fields.description: scripted_routines run WITHOUT the model (A20).

message.name: ScriptedRoutine
message.description:
ScriptedRoutine is a fixed dialogue the runtime drives (A20): muster,
 Barry's checklists. The model only phrases a line or reads a free-text
 reply.

fields.name: templates
fields.description:
templates, one per language. Language is the PERSON's setting (Jody,
 2026-09-29): a person who chose Spanish hears every line in Spanish,
 scripted or model. A room-wide scripted post goes once per language
 present, English first (X4).

fields.name: lang
fields.description: lang is a BCP 47 tag: "en", "es".

fields.name: version_hash
fields.description:
version_hash is generated from this definition (T1) and carried by every
 ToolCallOutcome (A16, A26). Never written by hand.

fields.name: pigeon_allowance
fields.description:
pigeon_allowance is what this dog may ask the coop for (A30). Unset = no
 pigeons: request_pigeon is absent from the dog's tools (T2 intersection).
 Only Tally and Beagle carry one at MVP.

message.name: PigeonAllowance
message.description:
PigeonAllowance is the build-time CEILING on a dog's pigeon requests (A30;
 backlog-scotty-slices §3.1). A tenant rule may only narrow it (A16,
 fail-closed). The runtime pre-checks a request against it; the coop and its
 network policy are the enforcement.

fields.name: allowed_domains
fields.description: allowed_domains: a request's allowed_domains must be a subset.

fields.name: max_budget_micro_usd
fields.description: max_budget_micro_usd per request (default $0.50).

fields.name: max_deadline_ms
fields.description: max_deadline_ms per request (default 15 min).

fields.name: max_concurrent
fields.description: max_concurrent pigeons per dog per tenant.

fields.name: task_kinds
fields.description:
task_kinds the dog may request, as "<system>.<verb>" (pigeon.PigeonTask.kind),
 e.g. "texas811.prepare_ticket", "bidportal.fetch_packet".

types.name: PigeonEvent
types.description:
PigeonEvent is one coop.PigeonMessage for a run this instance started
 (A30). The thread is CrewEvent.thread_id: the pigeon thread, an ordinary
 ThreadMapEntry. body is DATA (A9). A FROM_COOP PIGEON_GONE or ENDED closes
 any wait_for on the thread.

fields.name: body
fields.description: body is set for FROM_PIGEON.

message.name: FromPigeon
message.description: FromPigeon is the body of a FROM_PIGEON message (pigeon -> dog).

enum_values.name: RUN_MODE_MIXED
enum_values.description: MIXED: script with model takeover at one or more steps (§1.7 drift).

fields.name: note
fields.description: note is one line for the logbook ("county list loaded", "draft saved").

fields.name: question
fields.description: question: the pigeon needs a choice the request did not make.

message.name: Question
message.description:
Question: the page offers a choice the request does not decide (e.g. two
 county matches). The pigeon never guesses a field the request names. Script
 mode asks too (PG7).

fields.name: field
fields.description: field is the request field it concerns.

fields.name: prompt
fields.description: prompt is scrubbed (§1.5).

fields.name: snapshot
fields.description: snapshot is the page as the pigeon saw it.

message.name: EvidenceRef
message.description:
EvidenceRef points at one blob the pigeon captured (blobstore, tenant
 namespace). Declared here and imported by crew, beagle and tally.

fields.name: source_url
fields.description: source_url is scrubbed of query secrets (§1.5 S5).

fields.name: answer_by_ms
fields.description:
answer_by_ms: after this the run ends RESULT_STATUS_NEEDS_ANSWER (PG7:
 5 min after asking by default).

fields.name: result
fields.description: result is terminal; the pigeon then waits for discard or deadline.

enum_values.name: RUN_MODE_MIXED
enum_values.description: MIXED: script with model takeover at one or more steps (§1.7 drift).

enum_values.name: RESULT_STATUS_NEEDS_ANSWER
enum_values.description: NEEDS_ANSWER: a Question went unanswered by answer_by_ms.

fields.name: draft_id
fields.description:
draft_id is the portal's suspended-ticket id: the prepared ticket lives in
 Sonar's state account as a draft until a person submits it.

fields.name: entered
fields.description:
entered: field -> value as the portal shows it after entry (read back
 from the review page), for the §1.6 compare.

fields.name: review_page
fields.description: review_page: screenshot + HTML of the final review step.

fields.name: status
fields.description: status is the portal's word, verbatim.

fields.name: fields
fields.description: fields as filed, for the compare.

fields.name: evidence
fields.description:
evidence: every page/screenshot/download the result relies on (blobstore,
 tenant namespace). The dog copies refs onto its own record; never the bytes.

fields.name: failure
fields.description: failure is set iff status != OK.

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_UNRECOGNIZED_PAGE
enum_values.description: UNRECOGNIZED_PAGE: script mode, and model mode is not allowed for the kind.

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_LEASE_UNAVAILABLE
enum_values.description: LEASE_UNAVAILABLE: coop FAILED_PRECONDITION until the lease store exists.

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_DOMAIN_BLOCKED
enum_values.description: DOMAIN_BLOCKED: pigeonproxy refused a CONNECT.

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_PORTAL_REJECTED
enum_values.description: PORTAL_REJECTED: the portal's validation message, quoted in detail.

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_COMMIT_CONTROL_BLOCKED
enum_values.description: COMMIT_CONTROL_BLOCKED: the path required actuating a commit control.

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_READBACK_MISMATCH
enum_values.description: READBACK_MISMATCH: the §1.6 compare failed.

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_SCRUB_FAILED
enum_values.description: SCRUB_FAILED: a snapshot could not be scrubbed and was withheld (§1.5 S7).

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_INVALID_TASK
enum_values.description: INVALID_TASK: the body failed the kind's schema.

fields.name: detail
fields.description: detail is scrubbed (§1.5).

fields.name: trace
fields.description: trace: scrubbed step snapshots.

fields.name: recorded_path
fields.description:
recorded_path: set when any step ran in model mode and the run succeeded
 (§1.7). A blob of RecordedStep rows; the promotion input.

fields.name: error_code
fields.description:
error_code / error_detail are set for FROM_COOP, e.g. "PIGEON_GONE" /
 "discarded".

types.name: PostRoomRequest
types.description:
PostRoomRequest is post_room's arguments. thread_id empty or the session's
 own thread = reply in it; any other EXISTING id is refused with a descriptive
 error (BQ9); a new thread (thread_id empty and room_ref set) gets a
 runtime-minted id, returned in the result. thread_id, causation_id and
 hop_count on the posted message are filled by the generated sender (T7).

fields.name: room_ref
fields.description: room_ref only for a new thread.

fields.name: record_type
fields.description: record_type is the proto full name for REF_KIND_RECORD, e.g. "work.Permit".

types.name: PostRoomResponse

fields.name: thread_id
fields.description:
thread_id the message was posted in. For a new thread the model must carry
 it itself ("functional-tools").

fields.name: event_id
fields.description: event_id of the posted scottypersonal.ChatEvent.

types.name: ProposalDecided
types.description: ProposalDecided points at the scotty.Ticket and its decision (A10).

types.name: RecordChange
types.description: RecordChange carries a written row as record_type + key + proto3 JSON (Q6).

types.name: Ref

fields.name: record_type
fields.description: record_type is the proto full name for REF_KIND_RECORD, e.g. "work.Permit".

types.name: Report
types.description:
Report — the dogs' formal, auditable channel to SeaBeam, and the ONLY one
 (A27). Lands on the company record; SeaBeam answers on the same record.

 one fleet-level ops service; neither the projection nor that service exists.

 private record instead; that private type is not declared here.
 RETENTION: LOG (2 years).

fields.name: words
fields.description: words is the dog's own account.

fields.name: answer
fields.description: answer is SeaBeam's reply, written back on the same record.

types.name: RunCheckpoint
types.description:
RunCheckpoint records one completed step, written after stratum acked the
 step's publish (A1, design §13.1). Its key IS the idempotency key
 (dog, tenant, event_seq, step): "<instance_key>/<event_seq>/<step>" in the
 row's namespace. A replay serves a matching call (same tool, same
 request_sha256) from here instead of calling again (Q20).
 RETENTION: follows CHAT.

ScriptedRoutine is a fixed dialogue the runtime drives (A20): muster,

 reply.

fields.description:
templates, one per language. Language is the PERSON's setting (Jody,
 2026-09-29): a person who chose Spanish hears every line in Spanish,
 scripted or model. A room-wide scripted post goes once per language
 present, English first (X4).

fields.name: lang
fields.description: lang is a BCP 47 tag: "en", "es".

types.name: StandingOrder
types.description:
StandingOrder. Every PersonaDefinition carries the A29 order with id
 "functional-tools", verbatim (backlog-scotty-slices §2.6):
   "Every tool call is a plain function call. Nothing is remembered for you
   between calls. When a tool returns a page token, query id, cursor, thread
   id or proposal id, you must pass it back yourself in your next call if you
   need it. If you leave it out, you start over."
 TODO(T1): the generate-time check that every (spec.persona) has it waits on
 T1; until then a crew-runtime unit test enforces it.

fields.name: id
fields.description:
id is cited as the authority of an act. Stable across releases; a changed
 meaning takes a new id.

types.name: ThreadMapEntry
types.description:
ThreadMapEntry is one thread of one logical instance (A29; backlog-scotty-
 slices §2.2). The dispatcher routes each CrewEvent by thread_id to that
 thread's session worker; this row is what survives the worker. A pigeon's
 private thread is an ordinary entry (room_ref = the pigeon thread, A30).
 Queued for thread T = events with thread_id T and seq > T.done_through_seq.
 RETENTION: OPERATIONAL (BQ10).

fields.name: instance_key
fields.description: instance_key as on CrewCursor.

fields.name: thread_id
fields.description: thread_id in the A29 format t_<created_ms base36>_<16 hex> (§2.3, BQ8).

fields.name: parent_thread_id
fields.description: parent_thread_id: set when this thread revived an aged-out one.

fields.name: successor_thread_id
fields.description:
successor_thread_id: set on the aged-out entry at revival, so a late reply
 to the old id is routed to the new one.

fields.name: room_ref
fields.description:
room_ref is the room the thread lives in (REF_KIND_ROOM), or the pigeon
 thread. move_conversation updates it (A6).

fields.name: record_type
fields.description: record_type is the proto full name for REF_KIND_RECORD, e.g. "work.Permit".

fields.name: last_used_ms
fields.description: last_used_ms drives age-out.

fields.name: use_counter
fields.description: use_counter is A29's "last-used counter": turns taken.

fields.name: done_through_seq
fields.description:
done_through_seq is the PER-THREAD ack (A29): the highest instance seq in
 this thread acked by `done`.

enum_values.description:

 thread_idle_ms, or evicted LRU past max_live_threads). A message to it
 revives it as a new thread with parent_thread_id = this one (§2.4).

types.name: Wait

 matching event (enqueued with wait_id) or the deadline (a Scheduler
 registration "wait:<wait_id>", EVENT_SOURCE_WAIT_DEADLINE) wakes the dog
 with `context` attached, and the unused wake-up is cancelled.
 RETENTION: follows CHAT.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: kind must be in the persona's wait_allowlist.

fields.name: context
fields.description: context is the dog's own note of why it waits; handed back on wake.

types.name: Diagnostic
types.description:
Diagnostic is the freeform escape hatch for cases where no typed event
 exists yet. [ERROR]

 Use this sparingly. When a Diagnostic pattern emerges (same context, same
 kind of message), promote it to a typed event. Diagnostics are a migration
 path, not a permanent solution.

message.name: ErrorContext
message.description:
ErrorContext captures the origin of an error or diagnostic event.
 "caller" and "function" are cheap (Go runtime.Caller, Rust std::panic::Location,
 Java StackWalker). "stack_trace" is only populated on actual errors.

fields.name: caller
fields.description: caller is the file and line where the event originated (e.g., "auth.go:142").

fields.name: function
fields.description: function is the fully qualified function name (e.g., "(*Authorizer).Authorize").

fields.name: stack_trace
fields.description: stack_trace is the full call stack, only populated on ERROR-level events.

types.name: EndpointHealthChanged
types.description:
EndpointHealthChanged records a change in endpoint health status. [WARN]
 Emitted by ServiceManager when an endpoint transitions healthy↔unhealthy.

fields.name: endpoint
fields.description: endpoint is the "host:port" of the affected endpoint.

fields.name: healthy
fields.description: healthy is the new health status.

fields.name: latency_ms
fields.description: latency_ms is the last measured latency (0 if unhealthy).

types.name: Event
types.description:
Event is the top-level envelope for all typed events. It carries common
 context (source, identity, request tracing) and a typed payload.

 This is what gets published to EventBus, spooled for guaranteed delivery,
 and indexed by consumers.

fields.name: timestamp_ms
fields.description: timestamp_ms is the event timestamp in milliseconds since epoch (UTC).

fields.name: source_id
fields.description:
source_id identifies the emitting process.
 Format: "{service_id}-{instance_id}" for services (e.g., "identity-a1b2c3")
 or "{tool}-{user}" for clients (e.g., "mycli-alice").

fields.name: request_id
fields.description:
request_id is the x-request-id that traces a request across gateway,
 backend services, and client tools. Set by gateway, forwarded as gRPC
 metadata, extracted by generated wrappers.

fields.name: identity
fields.description:
identity is the caller's identity — the claims from the verified token.
 Enables identity-scoped event access — users query only their own events.
 Keys are claim names (sub, aud, iss, etc.), values are claim values.

fields.name: level
fields.description:
level is the event level, derived from the event type.
 Included on the envelope for filtering without inspecting the payload.

fields.name: rpc_completed
fields.description: RPC lifecycle

message.name: RpcCompleted
message.description:
RpcCompleted records a successful RPC invocation. [INFO]
 This is the primary accounting event — one per completed request.

fields.name: method
fields.description: method is the RPC that was invoked (generated per-service type).

message.name: AccountingMethod
message.description:
AccountingMethod identifies which RPC an event relates to.
 Only one field will be set — the rest default to 0 (UNSPECIFIED)
 and are not encoded by proto3, so there is no overhead.

fields.name: duration_ms
fields.description: duration_ms is the server-side processing time in milliseconds.

message.name: RpcError
message.description:
RpcError records a failed RPC invocation. [ERROR]
 Only emitted for internal failures — our bugs, not user input errors.

fields.name: method
fields.description: method is the RPC that was invoked.

fields.name: code
fields.description: code is the gRPC status code (numeric).

fields.name: message
fields.description: message is the error description.

fields.name: duration_ms
fields.description: duration_ms is how long the request ran before failing.

fields.name: error_context
fields.description: error_context captures caller, function, and stack trace.

types.name: S2SCredPair
types.description:
S2SCredPair authenticates a service bootstrapping its identity (S2S). It
 confers the set of services the bootstrapped token may act as / call,
 formalizing service bootstrap delegate cred_pairs.

message.name: Jwk
message.description:
Jwk represents a JSON Web Key as defined in RFC 7517.
 It contains the public key parameters for RSA (e, n), EC (crv, x, y), or OKP (crv, x) keys.
 JWK is used for key distribution and verification in JSON-based protocols like JWT.

fields.name: kty
fields.description: Kty is the key type parameter (RSA, EC, or OKP)

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_RSA
enum_values.description: KeyTypeRsa represents an RSA key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_EC
enum_values.description: KeyTypeEc represents an Elliptic Curve key type

enum_values.name: KEY_TYPE_OKP
enum_values.description: KeyTypeOkp represents an Octet Key Pair (EdDSA) key type

fields.name: alg
fields.description: Alg is the algorithm intended for use with the key (e.g., "RS384", "ES256", "EdDSA")

fields.name: kid
fields.description: Kid is the key ID used to match keys with signatures

fields.name: use
fields.description: Use indicates the intended use of the key (sig for signatures, enc for encryption)

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_SIG
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeSig indicates the key is used for digital signatures

enum_values.name: JWK_USE_TYPE_ENC
enum_values.description: JwkUseTypeEnc indicates the key is used for encryption

fields.name: e
fields.description: E is the RSA public exponent (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: n
fields.description: N is the RSA modulus (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: crv
fields.description: Crv is the elliptic curve name (e.g., P-256, P-384, P-521, Ed25519)

fields.name: x
fields.description: X is the x coordinate for EC keys or the public key for OKP (base64url encoded without padding)

fields.name: y
fields.description: Y is the y coordinate for EC keys (base64url encoded without padding, not used for OKP)

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
Exp is the expiration in epoch seconds. This is not part of the JWK spec as the spec does
 not specify how to handle public key expiration.
 When stored in a collection with epoch_expiration, the state store computes TTL = exp - now
 and auto-evicts the entry on expiry.

fields.name: created
fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created (optional).
 If set, valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

types.name: DiskPersistenceConfig
types.description:
DiskPersistenceConfig configures the SM-managed persistence component that
 automates the redo-log lifecycle (UC2) for service_store-annotated types.
 It is embedded in the ServiceManager config.

fields.name: roll_interval_seconds
fields.description:
roll_interval_seconds is the compaction/roll period. Also bounds the
 per-node deterministic roll offset (hash(node-id) % roll_interval).

fields.name: archive_count
fields.description: archive_count is how many rolled archive files to retain.

fields.name: dir
fields.description:
dir is the base directory (on the service's own volume) for the
 active / building / temp / archive files.

fields.name: file_permission
fields.description: file_permission is the Unix permission for the data files (e.g. 0600).

message.name: Permission
message.description:
Permission represents Unix-style file permissions (e.g., 755).
 Each field is a 3-bit mask: read (4) + write (2) + execute (1).

fields.name: owner
fields.description: owner permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: group
fields.description: group permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: other
fields.description: other permission bits (0-7)

fields.name: compression
fields.description:
compression for rolled/archived files + snapshots; the live append tail
 stays uncompressed.

enums.name: Compression
enums.description:
Compression selects at-rest compression for rolled/archived files and
 snapshot baselines. The live redo-log append tail is always uncompressed so
 line appends stay cheap.

enums.name: EntitlementLevel
enums.description:
EntitlementLevel is the data-entitlement decision for one MAY_* field. The rule
 is FAIL-CLOSED: absent an explicit decision (UNSPECIFIED = 0, the proto3
 default), the field gets its MOST-PROTECTIVE level — MAY_REDACT defaults to
 REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE defaults to ANONYMIZE. A grant in the caller's token
 loosens a field toward RAW; it can never loosen below a hard floor
 (DROP/PSEUDONYMIZE fields are caller-independent and always applied).

values.name: ENTITLEMENT_LEVEL_UNSPECIFIED
values.description: No decision recorded — the field gets its most-protective default.

values.name: ENTITLEMENT_LEVEL_ANONYMIZE
values.description:
Replace with a keyed HMAC surrogate. Valid only on string/bytes fields; on any
 other field the generated transform clamps ANONYMIZE up to REDACT.

values.name: ENTITLEMENT_LEVEL_REDACT
values.description: Clear the field to its zero value (a message field clears the whole subtree).

values.name: ENTITLEMENT_LEVEL_RAW
values.description:
Egress the field raw — the explicit loosening grant ("this caller is
 permitted to see the value"). Only ever set from a matching token data grant.

types.name: Error
types.description:
Error represents a structured error with status information.
 This message is designed to work as a Go error type and follows the Google RPC error model.
 The generated code will have an Error() string method added to implement the error interface.
 See https://cloud.google.com/apis/design/errors for more information.

fields.name: code

 In Go, use google.golang.org/grpc/codes.Code for the status code.

fields.name: message

 Any user-facing error message should be localized and sent in the details field,
 or localized by the client.

fields.name: details
fields.description:

 There is a common set of message types for APIs to use.
