types.name: LlmProviderSettingsFilter
LlmProviderSettingsWatchChange

message.name: LlmProviderSettings
message.description:
LlmProviderSettings is ONE person's LLM API settings, MINUS the key. It is both
 the stored record and the read response's item type, deliberately:
 `(spec.store_principal)` and `(spec.store_namespace)` filter repeated fields OF
 THIS TYPE on the way out, so a bespoke response row would be a read path with
 the generated backstops switched off (mailbox.ListHeldMailResponse says the
 same thing).

 Returning the stored type is safe because the secret is NOT IN IT: the key is
 LlmProviderSecret's, and that type is the item of no rpc on this service. Until
 2026-09-27 the key was field 3 here, made safe by `(spec.redact)` =
 REDACT_MODE_DROP; see the file header for why that annotation and a stratum
 record cannot both hold a secret this service has to read back.

fields.name: owner
fields.description:
owner is the record key AND the row's owning principal.

 (spec.indexed) makes it the record's key, so there is exactly one row per
 person by construction rather than by a uniqueness check somebody has to
 remember to write. (spec.store_principal) is what holds a caller's reads to
 their own row: the generated wrapper filters every repeated
 LlmProviderSettings field in a response down to rows the caller owns, so the
 handler does not check and there is nothing left for it to get wrong.

 spiffe_id below is the record's declared owner but is the PUBLISHER —
 llmsettings' own service identity, stamped by eventbus — so it is the wrong
 field to filter a person's reads on, exactly as it is on mailbox.MailboxEntry.

fields.name: endpoint_url
fields.description:
endpoint_url is the LLM API base URL.

 HTTPS ONLY, and that is not tidiness: this field's companion is a bearer
 secret, and the service that eventually calls this endpoint would put that
 secret in an Authorization header. Permitting http:// here would let a
 person configure their own key's exfiltration. (spec.assert_url) is the
 generated check — nothing in the handler parses a URL.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTPS)

fields.name: api_key_set
fields.description:
api_key_set says whether a key is stored, and exists because the key is not
 in this message at all — a caller reading these rows cannot tell an unset
 key from an absent one without being told. Maintained by the handler on
 write, from the secret row it just published.

 It is what lets the form render "a key is saved — replace it?" rather than
 an empty box that silently means either thing.

fields.name: api_key_hint
fields.description:
api_key_hint is the last Config.api_key_hint_chars characters of the stored
 key, so a person with several keys can tell WHICH one is saved. Not
 redacted: it is a deliberate, bounded disclosure, and the bound is the
 config knob rather than this field's own max_size so that lowering the knob
 takes effect on the next write instead of needing a proto change.

 8 is the ceiling Config.api_key_hint_chars enforces; this bound restates it
 so an oversized value is rejected by generated validation even if a future
 handler computes it wrong.

fields.name: updated_at_ms
fields.description: updated_at_ms is when the row was last written. Server-assigned.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT, by exact string equality against the
 reader's namespace claim. MANDATORY on a record: tacplus fails generation for
 any (spec.record) declaring no such field, on the reasoning that the record
 nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.
 (spec.store_namespace) generates the read-side egress filter on every surface
 returning this row; the write half is UpdateLlmSettingsRequest.namespace's
 (spec.namespace).

 Not a query field: the field exists to BE the egress boundary, and a boundary
 a caller can predicate on is not one. The handler compares it itself on the
 record-plane read, because that plane leaves a `/system` peer's read
 deliberately unpinned — see ListMyLlmSettingsRequest.namespace.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner, and the name is LOAD-BEARING: eventbus's topic
 discovery matches the LITERAL field name "spiffe_id" of string type when it
 decides which topics get publisher-identity stamping, so renaming it silently
 turns the stamping off.

 It holds LLMSETTINGS' OWN service identity — this service is the publisher.
 `owner` above is where the person is.

types.name: Locate811TicketFilter
Locate811TicketWatchChange

message.name: Locate811Ticket
message.description:
Locate811Ticket — one Texas 811 locate ticket, from the prepared portal
 draft to the utilities' positive responses (D8; §1.6). Beagle's scripted
 routine (A20) writes it, never the model: PREPARED after the
 texas811.prepare_ticket pigeon saves a draft and the compare passes,
 PROPOSED once the submit_811_ticket proposal (A10) is filed, APPROVED on the
 company's thumb, FILED when the confirmation mail carries the ticket number,
 RESPONDED when texas811.read_ticket reports every utility in. A compare
 mismatch is PARKED with one crew.Report and never re-requested. No pigeon
 ever actuates Submit; a person submits the draft (PG2).
 JobPermits.locate_permit_id keeps pointing at the work.Permit once one
 exists. Updatable with the version guard (A4).
 RETENTION: OPERATIONAL (7 years after job close).

fields.name: job_id
fields.description: job_id: work.Job.job_id; a job's tickets are a query on it.

fields.name: draft_id
fields.description:
draft_id is the portal's suspended-ticket id
 (pigeon.Texas811PrepareTicketResult.draft_id).

fields.name: ticket_number
fields.description: ticket_number is empty until FILED.

fields.name: proposal_id
fields.description: proposal_id is the submit_811_ticket proposal; empty while PREPARED.

fields.name: prepare_run_id
fields.description: prepare_run_id / last_read_run_id: coop PigeonRun ids.

fields.name: responses
fields.description: responses as last read back from the portal.

fields.name: evidence
fields.description: evidence: the review page and each read-back.

message.name: EvidenceRef
message.description:
EvidenceRef points at one blob the pigeon captured (blobstore, tenant
 namespace). Declared here and imported by crew, beagle and tally.

fields.name: source_url
fields.description: source_url is scrubbed of query secrets (§1.5 S5).

fields.name: filed_by
fields.description:
filed_by is the person who submitted the draft, "name@tenant" (PG2: at
 MVP, Sonar's state-account holder).
 TODO(PG3): how the filer is named once a fleet-scoped texas811 lease
 holds the per-state account.

fields.name: version
fields.description: version is optimistic (A4).

types.name: MailboxEntryFilter
MailboxEntryWatchChange

message.name: MailboxEntry
message.description:
MailboxEntry is ONE DELIVERY'S mailbox state, keyed by the SAME delivery_id
 as the `messaging.Message` it tracks.

 Joinable by identity, not by a second lookup: an entry and its message share
 a key, so "fetch the body of the mail I was just told about" is one Message
 read with an id the client already holds.

 IT HOLDS NO BODY. `messaging.Message.text` is never copied here — that is the
 decision doc's rejected alternative ("Mailbox stores full message content"),
 and it stands. What IS carried is the inbox SUMMARY LINE the doc's own
 ListHeldMail spec enumerates (sender, subject, sent_at_ms): a mail client
 renders a list before anything is opened, and those three fields are the only
 way to serve that list without a second round trip per row. A summary line is
 not a second copy of the message, and the field that would make it one —
 `text` — is absent, as are `recipients` and `ticket_id`.

fields.name: delivery_id
fields.description:
delivery_id is the record key and messaging.Message.delivery_id verbatim.
 Bounded identically (512) — a shorter bound here would silently drop the
 deliveries whose recipient subject is long.

fields.name: message_id
fields.description:
message_id groups the N entries of one submission, the same way it groups
 the N Messages. EQ-filterable for the same reason it is there.

fields.name: recipient
fields.description:
recipient is whose mailbox this is, and the ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL — the
 same field, carrying the same annotation, as messaging.Message.recipient.
 The generated egress filter holds a caller's reads to their own rows, so
 ListHeldMail cannot return one person's mail to another even if this
 service's own predicate were wrong.

 spiffe_id below is the record's declared owner but is the PUBLISHER —
 mailbox's own service identity, stamped by eventbus — so it is the wrong
 field to filter a user's reads on, exactly as it is on Message.

enum_values.name: MAILBOX_ENTRY_STATUS_HELD
enum_values.description:
HELD: the delivery arrived on the topic and nobody has pulled it. Age alone
 does not change that, and no longer needs a marker to say so: an unpulled
 row may leave the store's MEMORY like any other and loses nothing by it —
 it stays complete and queryable on disk, and the next read reloads it.
 NOTHING removes a HELD row: the 90-day `held_since_ms` floor that used to
 was the kernel state root's bound, and the root went away with it on
 2026-09-27 — see Config.sweep_interval_seconds.

enum_values.name: MAILBOX_ENTRY_STATUS_RETRIEVED
enum_values.description:
RETRIEVED: the recipient acknowledged pulling it. Terminal in the normal
 path — `ListHeldMail` stops returning the row and `UpdateHeldMail` is a
 no-op on it — so this is the row's last write, and therefore where its
 residency idle clock starts running down.

fields.name: held_since_ms
fields.description:
held_since_ms is when this consumer group's copy landed. It is NOT a
 residency clock — residency runs on the row's last touch, which is
 store_epoch_ms and is the store's business, not a business field's. It is
 not an expiry clock either, as of 2026-09-27: the state-root sweep it used
 to drive is gone with the state root, and no record-side clock replaced it
 (see Config.sweep_interval_seconds). What survives is the question a user
 asks with it — "how long has this been sitting in my mailbox" — and the
 ordering `ListHeldMail` presents.

 RANGE-filterable because "what has been sitting in my mailbox since last
 week" is a question about this field.

types.name: MessageFilter
MessageWatchChange

message.name: Message
message.description:
Message is ONE DELIVERY: one message, to one recipient.

 It is NOT one row per submission. A submission naming three recipients
 becomes three `Message` rows sharing a `message_id`, differing in
 `delivery_id` and `recipient`, each independently consumable and
 independently ACKable. See the fan-out note at the top of this file for why
 EventBus cannot do that split itself.

 spec.record implies spec.event, so tacplus synthesizes the topic wrapper
 MessageBus with topic ref messaging.MessageBus.stream. Do NOT hand-write that
 wrapper.

fields.name: delivery_id
fields.description:
delivery_id is the record key: "<message_id>/<recipient>". One per
 (message, recipient) pair, which is what makes the N publishes of one
 submission N separately-keyed records rather than N copies of one.

 Derived rather than random ON PURPOSE: the value a caller would need to
 reconstruct to ACK a delivery is exactly (which message, for whom), so
 deriving it means an agent that knows both never has to have been told the
 id. It is also what makes the fan-out replay-safe — a retried submission
 regenerates the same delivery ids rather than a second set of rows.

fields.name: message_id
fields.description:
message_id groups the N deliveries of ONE submission. EQ-filterable,
 because "every delivery of the message I sent" is the question a sender
 asks, and it is the only way back from a delivery to its siblings.

fields.name: sender
fields.description:
sender is who sent it — the authenticated principal subject bound by the
 (spec.principal) field on SendMessageRequest below, never a caller-written
 string.

fields.name: recipient
fields.description:
recipient is THE recipient this delivery is for — one of `recipients`
 below, and the half of delivery_id that varies across the fan-out.

 It is also the ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL for the record query plane's c2s
 half. spiffe_id below is the record's declared owner but is the PUBLISHER —
 eventbus stamps messaging's own service identity onto it — so filtering a
 user's reads on that field would show every user nothing. `sender` is the
 other candidate and is the wrong one: a mailbox read is "messages addressed
 to me", so the field the generated egress filter holds a caller's reads to
 must be the addressee.

 The consequence is stated rather than hidden: a SENDER cannot read their own
 sent messages through this record's c2s plane, because only one field may
 carry (spec.store_principal) and this is it. Sent-items is a mailbox
 concern and the mailbox service is Phase 1 item 8, undesigned; inventing a
 second read path for it here would be inventing that service's shape.

 The EQ criterion is what carries the row filter into the plane's SIZE-ONLY
 RPCs: Get<T>Count returns a number over the handle's predicate and no rows,
 so no egress filter can narrow it. The generated c2s wrapper pins this
 criterion to the caller at Create<T>Query and every later call on the
 handle inherits it.

fields.name: recipients
fields.description:
recipients is the full To: line — every recipient of the submission, the
 SAME list on all N deliveries. `recipient` above says which one this row is
 for; this says who else got it.

 Carrying it is not redundancy. Without it a recipient cannot see who else
 was addressed, which is information the sender chose to disclose by
 addressing them together — the same reason a To: header exists and a Bcc:
 one does not. (This file models no Bcc; nothing has asked for one.)

 Bounded at 256 to match Config.max_recipients' ceiling above.

fields.name: subject
fields.description: subject is the message's subject line.

fields.name: text
fields.description: text is the message body. Free text, and nothing parses it — see ticket_id.

fields.name: ticket_id
fields.description:
ticket_id OPTIONALLY references the ticket this message pertains to.

 A dedicated field, never a value embedded in `text`. Routing and status
 display have to associate a message with its ticket to act, and the
 standing rule is that anything that must be parsed to be acted on should
 have been a field. Optional because most messages pertain to no ticket, and
 EQ-filterable because "every message about this ticket" is the question the
 field exists to answer.

 This is the ONLY ticket-shaped thing on Message, and it is an opaque id.
 Ticket's own churn — advice sealing, decision chains, amend/reconsider —
 stays entirely inside Ticket. That is what keeps this type stable.

fields.name: sent_at_ms
fields.description:
sent_at_ms is the business clock — when the sender submitted — and the
 RANGE criterion, because "my messages from last week" is the question a
 mailbox asks.

 Identical across all N deliveries of one submission: they were one act.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner. The name is LOAD-BEARING: eventbus's topic
 discovery matches the literal field name "spiffe_id" of string type when it
 decides which topics get publisher-identity stamping, so renaming this
 field silently turns the stamping off.

 It holds MESSAGING'S OWN service identity, not the sender's, because the
 publish is s2s from this service — that is the direct consequence of the
 SUPERSEDED ruling. `sender` above is where the human is.

fields.name: spiffe_actor
fields.description:
spiffe_actor is the ORIGIN signal: the delegate that made the call, stamped
 by EventBus from the publishing token's `act` claim at publish time.

   "a message is marked as originating from the user directly or from the
    user's Scotty acting on their behalf... A message sent by
    Scotty-for-Dennis carries `act` populated; one Dennis sends directly
    doesn't." — decisions/messaging-vs-ticketing-2026-08-31.md

 The service does not set it and must not: like spiffe_id above, a value
 written here would be a claim about identity that nothing verified.
 Provenance only — sys/spec.proto forbids wiring it into a principal.

 GAP, STATED NOT PAPERED OVER. That quote describes the pre-supersession
 model, where the user published to EventBus DIRECTLY and EventBus saw the
 user's own delegated token. Under the corrected model the publish is s2s
 from messaging, so the token EventBus stamps from is messaging's own
 service token and carries no `act` claim at all — this field will be empty
 in the ordinary case, including for a genuine Scotty-for-Dennis send. The
 annotation is declared anyway, and correctly: the seam is the right one and
 the field is where the value belongs the moment the delegated-publish path
 exists. Closing it needs an s2s publish that carries the caller's exchanged
 token, which the generated publisher does not offer today. Written up in
 workers/big8-p1-messaging-questions.md rather than hand-rolled around.

fields.name: request_id
fields.description:
request_id is the JOIN KEY to the accounting plane — the same value
 accountingrecord.AccountingRecord carries under the same name with the same
 EQ query_field, so "which accounting rows belong to the request that sent
 this message" is one predicate asked of two record types.

 Empty is legitimate: a call with no authenticated Caller has none to read.

fields.name: agent_received
fields.description:
agent_received is the delivery ACK, written by the consuming agent after it
 processes this delivery. Unset at publish — this service never writes it.

message.name: AgentReceivedReceipt
message.description:
AgentReceivedReceipt is the delivery ACK — the agent (scotty, the mailbox
 service) took the record off the topic and processed it. Written by the
 consumer, never by the sender or by this service.

 It is the ACK, not a copy of it: there is one event here, not a delivery ACK
 plus a receipt derived from it.

fields.name: received_at_ms
fields.description:
received_at_ms is when the consuming agent completed processing — the same
 instant it commits its consumer-group offset, since committing before
 processing is exactly the discipline the queue semantics forbid.

fields.name: received_by
fields.description: received_by is the SPIFFE identity of the consuming agent instance.

fields.name: human_viewed
fields.description:
human_viewed is the separately-typed human signal. Unset at publish, and
 unset for as long as the person has not looked, which is the normal state
 of a delivered message.

message.name: HumanViewedReceipt
message.description:
HumanViewedReceipt fires when the actual person looked at the message. A
 distinct signal from AgentReceivedReceipt above: an agent can have ACKed a
 message hours before a human sees it, and business-hours-deferred
 presentation makes that gap the normal case rather than the exception.

 Presentation is a passive pull label — the reader is told "viewed", never
 pushed a notification. That is the design already built for tickets
 (decisions/ticket-read-receipts-2026-08-30.md), relocated to where it
 belongs.

fields.name: viewed_at_ms
fields.description: viewed_at_ms is when the person actually looked.

fields.name: viewed_by
fields.description:
viewed_by is the principal subject of the person who looked. It is normally
 equal to Message.recipient — a delivery is viewed by its addressee — but it
 is stored rather than assumed, because a delegate viewing on someone's
 behalf is a real case and an inferred value could not tell the two apart.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT, by EXACT string equality against the
 caller's namespace claim (never the level-or-below containment the
 administrative namespace rule uses). It is the tenant half of the identity
 `recipient` carries the subject half of: that field's (spec.store_principal)
 answers "are these MY rows", this one answers "is this MY tenant".

 MANDATORY, not opt-in: tacplus (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations) fails
 generation for any (spec.record) declaring no such field, on the reasoning
 that the record nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 TWO DIFFERENT ENFORCEMENTS, and they are not the same failure:
   - WRITE (this record's publish path). eventbus's PublishHandler stamps
     this field from the publishing token's namespace claim and REFUSES the
     publish with PERMISSION_DENIED when the token carries none. Stamp-or-
     refuse, deliberately not stamp-if-empty: a row published with an empty
     namespace is a row no legitimate caller can ever read.
   - READ (stratum's record query plane, c2s half). The generated egress
     filter holds every row to the reader's own claim, and a row that fails
     the comparison HALTS THE JVM rather than failing the one call — the
     filter is the backstop behind the store's own query, so it firing means
     that query is broken.

 Bounded like every other string here. Not a (spec.query_field): the field
 exists to be the egress boundary, and making it a caller-supplied predicate
 is not what a boundary is.

     this field from the publishing token's namespace claim and REFUSES the
     publish with PERMISSION_DENIED when the token carries none. Stamp-or-
     refuse, deliberately not stamp-if-empty: a row published with an empty
     namespace is a row no legitimate caller can ever read.
   - READ (stratum's record query plane, c2s half). The generated egress
     filter holds every row to the reader's own claim, and a row that fails
     the comparison HALTS THE JVM rather than failing the one call — the
     filter is the backstop behind the store's own query, so it firing means
     that query is broken.

 Bounded like every other string here. Not a (spec.query_field): the field
 exists to be the egress boundary, and making it a caller-supplied predicate
 is not what a boundary is.

message.name: Observation
message.description:
One row per fetched observation. observation_id folds (station_id,
 observed_at_ms), so re-polling the same hour is idempotent and does not append
 a duplicate.

 Units: NWS returns SI with explicit unit codes. This file stores ONE unit per
 quantity and names it in the field, rather than carrying a unit string per
 reading — a consumer that has to branch on a unit code will eventually forget
 to, and the conversion belongs on the ingest side where it is written once.
 Display units (°F, inches) are the app's business. Choice G.

fields.name: place_id
fields.description:
place_id is an EQ (spec.query_field): ListObservations and WatchObservations
 both take it as a declared parameter, and it is the criterion that turns
 "every observation the fleet has ever stored" into "this job site's".

fields.name: observed_at_ms
fields.description:
observed_at_ms is NWS's timestamp for the reading. fetched_at_ms is when
 this service pulled it. They differ by minutes normally and by hours when a
 station backfills, and the difference is the reason both are kept.

 observed_at_ms is a RANGE (spec.query_field), which emits
 observed_at_ms_from / observed_at_ms_to on ObservationFilter. It is the
 window ListObservations already declares (observed_from_ms /
 observed_to_ms), and it is the OTHER half of making a rain-day read bounded:
 a place with hourly readings accumulates 8,760 rows a year, so place_id
 alone is not a bound on a service that is meant to outlive the dispute.
 fetched_at_ms is deliberately NOT a criterion — no rpc offers it as a filter
 and a read about WHEN WE PULLED IT is a diagnostic, not a product question.

fields.name: temperature_c_x10
fields.description:
Scaled integers, not doubles: these are read back and compared, and a float
 that does not round-trip through JSON is a bug waiting on a rain day. _x10
 means "tenths".

fields.name: precipitation_mm_x10
fields.description:
precipitation_mm_x10 over the period ending at observed_at_ms. This is the
 field the rainfall-ledger question (choice D) is about.

fields.name: text_description
fields.description:
text_description is NWS's own words ("Thunderstorm in Vicinity"). Prose,
 unparsed.

fields.name: source_url
fields.description:
source_url is the exact api.weather.gov URL this row came from, and raw_id
 is NWS's own identifier for the observation. Provenance: a row nobody can
 trace back to what the bureau actually served is a row nobody can defend in
 a dispute.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace: mandatory, `/system` on every row, no criterion. See message Place,
 including the WATCH-egress hazard note on its copy of this field.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description: spiffe_id: the publisher's identity, stamped by eventbus. See message Place.

enum_values.name: RULE_EFFECT_FILTER

 requesting user sees a different screen because of it. The first and so far
 only rule kind the product has designed end to end — see

 UI".

enum_values.name: RULE_EFFECT_BEHAVIOR
enum_values.description:

 anyone else sees: what he volunteers, how he phrases things, when he

enum_values.description:

 answering for them, forwarding, standing in. AFFECTS OTHERS, so it gets the
 bidirectional discussion before it is created or reordered, never
 silence-is-consent.

message.name: Place
message.description:
===========================================================================
 THE FOUR RECORDS HAVE NO TENANT, AND THIS IS THE ONE PLACE THAT IS WRITTEN
 DOWN. Place is the first of them, so the reasoning lives here and the other
 three point at it.

 Every record in this fleet before this file was one of three shapes:

   - rows with an OWNING PERSON (work.WorkActivity, scotty.ScottyActivity,
     scottypersonal.ChatSession): (spec.store_principal) on the field naming
     that person, and the c2s plane pins a caller to their own rows;
   - the same, plus (spec.record).private (profile.UserProfile) — "a user's
     data and nobody else's, ever";
   - rows with no owning person but an OWNING TENANT (work.Job, scotty.Ticket,
     scottypersonal.Chat): no principal, and `namespace` IS the boundary.

 THESE FOUR ARE THE FOURTH SHAPE: rows with NO owner of any kind. A place is a
 cell in NWS's grid. An observation is what the sky did there. Neither belongs
 to a person or to a company, both are DEDUPLICATED ACROSS THE FLEET by
 construction (choice A: place_id is DERIVED from the resolved cell, so two
 tenants 400m apart write the same key), and the whole reason this service is
 9a — one instance for the whole fleet — is that a per-tenant copy would be N
 copies of one fact and N callers hammering api.weather.gov.

 SO NO (spec.store_principal) ON ANY OF THE FOUR. There is no field that could
 truthfully carry one; `weather` has never had a (spec.principal) anywhere and
 the reads take no caller into account at all.

 NOT `private` EITHER, and here it is not even close. These are PUBLIC FACTS.
 ValidateRecordPrivateAnnotations additionally requires a private record to
 carry (spec.store_principal) — which there is nothing to put in — and refuses
 s2s_subscribe on one, which would leave these rows with no declared ingest
 path into stratum at all. Item 3's "private where the data is one person's"
 does not fire for this service in either direction.

 AND `namespace` IS DECLARED, EMPTY ON EVERY ROW, AND IS NOT A QUERY
 CRITERION. That is the sentence a reviewer should push back on, so here is the
 whole of it.

   (spec.store_namespace) is MANDATORY on a record —
   ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations fails generation without it, on the
   reasoning that "the record nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one
   that leaks". So the field exists here because the platform insists a record
   name its owning tenant, and this record HAS no owning tenant.

   THE VALUE IS `/system` ON EVERY ROW, FOREVER, and it is derived rather than
   invented. Kernel mints this service's subject as
   `/system/services/weather` (SpiffeIds.build with an empty namespace is "the
   shared /system root"; a tenant-owned instance would get
   `/tenants/<t>/services/<svc>` instead), and the platform's own
   `namespace_from_spiffe` reduces that subject to the namespace `/system`. So
   `/system` IS the namespace of the identity that owns these rows, computed by
   the platform's rule — which is the most truthful thing the field can hold for
   a 9a service, and reads as what it is: the platform owns this row, no tenant
   does. `spiffe_id` below carries the full identity; this carries its
   namespace, which is exactly the relationship the two annotations describe
   everywhere else.

   THE EMPTY STRING WAS THE OTHER CANDIDATE AND IS STRICTLY WORSE. It would say
   "no tenant" just as well, but it is indistinguishable from the field nobody
   filled in — the failure ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations exists to prevent
   — and, decisively, it would make the WATCH rpcs ABORT THIS SERVICE on every
   frame. See the hazard note on the field itself.

   AND IT CARRIES NO (spec.query_field), SO NO READ PINS IT. This is where this
   file departs from `work` and `scotty`, which both added an EQ criterion and
   pin it on every read. There, the pin IS the tenant boundary: the record
   plane's S2S half reads FLEET-WIDE by declared doctrine, so without a pinned
   criterion one tenant's handler would read another's rows. Here every row in
   the type carries the same value, so a criterion on it cannot narrow
   ANYTHING — and it is not free: the record store's by-key fast path
   (RecordMapImplGenerator.pointRead) fires only when the key criterion is the
   ONLY criterion set, so pinning an always-true namespace would turn every
   point read in this service — including the poller's write-once check, once
   per row per pass over up to ten million of them — into a predicate scan. A
   criterion that narrows nothing and costs the point read is not a boundary,
   it is overhead wearing a boundary's clothes.

   WHAT IS LOST IS NOTHING THAT EXISTED. The no-(spec.principal)/-(spec.namespace)
   note on the `Weather` service block already says it out loud: "`weather` has
   NO GENERATED TENANT BOUNDARY ON ANY SURFACE. That is correct for public rows.
   The day a tenant-specific field lands on one of these rows, nothing at build
   time or runtime will catch it." That was true when these were kernel
   collections and it is true now; the storage move neither added the exposure
   nor closed it. WHAT HAS CHANGED, and it is a real narrowing, is that a
   kernel collection was chrooted per tenant and a record store is one
   fleet-wide set of rows — which for these four types is not a loss, because
   fleet-wide is what a deduplicated public fact wants and what the old code
   already asked kernel for.

 THE PUSHDOWNS ARE REAL HERE, unlike in `work`. work's D4 declared no
 (spec.query_field) beyond the tenant, on the grounds that half a read in the
 store and half in the handler is no behaviour change over a tenant's rows.
 That argument does not survive the absence of a tenant: with nothing pinned,
 "every row of the type" is up to ten million observations, and a handler-side
 filter over them is a paged gRPC walk of the whole store on every ListObservations.
 So the criteria that are DECLARED PARAMETERS of a read rpc AND actually narrow
 are pushed down — place_id and the time window on Observation and Forecast, the
 time window on Alert — and nothing else is. What stays in the handler is named
 per record below.
 ===========================================================================

fields.name: latitude
fields.description:
The point as asked for. Kept because NWS /points snaps to a ~2.5km cell and
 "what did we ask about" is worth keeping alongside "what NWS gave us".

fields.name: grid_office
fields.description:
The NWS gridpoint: office id + x/y. Forecasts are per gridpoint.
 e.g. grid_office "HGX", grid_x 65, grid_y 97.

fields.name: station_id
fields.description:
station_id is the nearest NWS observation station (e.g. "KHOU").
 Observations are per STATION, not per gridpoint — a distinction NWS makes
 and this file keeps rather than flattening.

fields.name: forecast_zone_id
fields.description:
Zones are how ALERTS arrive. A point sits in a forecast zone and a county
 zone and the two are different ids issuing different products, so both are
 kept. e.g. "TXZ213" / "TXC201".

fields.name: nws_place_name
fields.description:
A person-readable label NWS returns for the point ("Houston, TX"). For
 display only; nothing parses it (scotty design record §5).

fields.name: resolved_at_ms
fields.description: resolved_at_ms is when /points was last asked.

fields.name: superseded_by_place_id
fields.description:
superseded_by_place_id: set on the OLD row when NWS re-cut the grid under
 this point. Empty on the current row. This is the ONE field a Place gains
 after creation, and there is deliberately no rpc that sets it: the service
 writes it through the generated state client (PutPlaces), which is the
 established mechanism for a service writing its own state and needs no verb
 registry exception, because the generated state service is Synthesized by
 construction. VERIFY 3 in the design doc, confirmed.

 The caveat that comes with it, worth carrying: PutPlaces REPLACES the whole
 row (there is no compare-and-swap). Fine for a single-writer poller; not
 once a second writer exists.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is MANDATORY on a record and is `/system` ON EVERY ROW OF THIS
 TYPE — the namespace of this service's own identity, not any tenant's. Read
 the block above this message for the whole argument; the short form is that a
 Place has no owning tenant by construction, `/system` is what the platform's
 own rule reduces `/system/services/weather` to, and the field deliberately
 carries no (spec.query_field) so that no read pins a criterion that could not
 narrow anything and would cost the store's by-key fast path.

 A HAZARD THIS FIELD NOW CARRIES, AND IT IS A TACPLUS GAP RATHER THAN A DESIGN
 CHOICE. Making these types records turns on the generated WATCH egress
 backstop, which compares EVERY snapshot frame and EVERY delta against the
 CALLER'S namespace claim and calls std::process::abort() on a mismatch. The
 unary and PAGE seams apply that filter only for a c2s service or the record
 plane's own s2s wrapper, and they carry a `__ns_pinned` escape so a /system
 peer keeps a fleet-wide read; the WATCH seam
 (rust/types/servicewrapper_gen.go:1511-1517 against :1882/:1947) has NEITHER
 gate. So today:

   - every caller on this service's auth_services list is a SHARED service
     whose own namespace claim is `/system`, so `/system` on the row MATCHES
     and the three WATCH rpcs work;
   - the day a TENANT-OWNED service watches this one — which is exactly what
     `reveille` is meant to be — its claim is `/tenants/<t>` , the guard
     mismatches, AND WEATHER'S PROCESS ABORTS. Not a refused call: an abort.

 There is no value of this field that avoids that, because a fleet-shared row
 read by callers in different namespaces cannot equal all of their claims.
 The fix is in tacplus, not here: the WATCH seam needs the same gate its unary
 and PAGE siblings have. Recorded in
 decisions/weather-record-shapes-2026-09-25.md as the one thing that must land
 before `reveille` exists.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record's declared `owner` and the PUBLISHER — eventbus
 stamps weather's own service identity onto it. The field NAME is load-bearing
 (eventbus's topic discovery matches the literal string "spiffe_id" of string
 type when it decides which topics get publisher-identity stamping), which is
 why it carries (spec.identity_spiffe_subject).

 ON THIS SERVICE IT IS THE ONLY OWNERSHIP STATEMENT THERE IS, and it is the
 true one: these rows belong to the platform's weather service, which is
 exactly what a 9a service's rows are. It is never a read filter — every row
 of every one of these four types carries the same value.

   AND IT CARRIES NO (spec.query_field), SO NO READ PINS IT. This is where this
   file departs from `work` and `scotty`, which both added an EQ criterion and
   pin it on every read. There, the pin IS the tenant boundary: the record
   plane's S2S half reads FLEET-WIDE by declared doctrine, so without a pinned
   criterion one tenant's handler would read another's rows. Here every row in
   the type carries the same value, so a criterion on it cannot narrow
   ANYTHING — and it is not free: the record store's by-key fast path
   (RecordMapImplGenerator.pointRead) fires only when the key criterion is the
   ONLY criterion set, so pinning an always-true namespace would turn every
   point read in this service — including the poller's write-once check, once
   per row per pass over up to ten million of them — into a predicate scan. A
   criterion that narrows nothing and costs the point read is not a boundary,
   it is overhead wearing a boundary's clothes.

   WHAT IS LOST IS NOTHING THAT EXISTED. The no-(spec.principal)/-(spec.namespace)
   note on the `Weather` service block already says it out loud: "`weather` has
   NO GENERATED TENANT BOUNDARY ON ANY SURFACE. That is correct for public rows.
   The day a tenant-specific field lands on one of these rows, nothing at build
   time or runtime will catch it." That was true when these were kernel
   collections and it is true now; the storage move neither added the exposure
   nor closed it. WHAT HAS CHANGED, and it is a real narrowing, is that a
   kernel collection was chrooted per tenant and a record store is one
   fleet-wide set of rows — which for these four types is not a loss, because
   fleet-wide is what a deduplicated public fact wants and what the old code
   already asked kernel for.

 THE PUSHDOWNS ARE REAL HERE, unlike in `work`. work's D4 declared no
 (spec.query_field) beyond the tenant, on the grounds that half a read in the
 store and half in the handler is no behaviour change over a tenant's rows.
 That argument does not survive the absence of a tenant: with nothing pinned,
 "every row of the type" is up to ten million observations, and a handler-side
 filter over them is a paged gRPC walk of the whole store on every ListObservations.
 So the criteria that are DECLARED PARAMETERS of a read rpc AND actually narrow
 are pushed down — place_id and the time window on Observation and Forecast, the
 time window on Alert — and nothing else is. What stays in the handler is named
 per record below.
 ===========================================================================

fields.name: latitude
fields.description:
The point as asked for. Kept because NWS /points snaps to a ~2.5km cell and
 "what did we ask about" is worth keeping alongside "what NWS gave us".

fields.name: grid_office
fields.description:
The NWS gridpoint: office id + x/y. Forecasts are per gridpoint.
 e.g. grid_office "HGX", grid_x 65, grid_y 97.

fields.name: station_id
fields.description:
station_id is the nearest NWS observation station (e.g. "KHOU").
 Observations are per STATION, not per gridpoint — a distinction NWS makes
 and this file keeps rather than flattening.

fields.name: forecast_zone_id
fields.description:
Zones are how ALERTS arrive. A point sits in a forecast zone and a county
 zone and the two are different ids issuing different products, so both are
 kept. e.g. "TXZ213" / "TXC201".

fields.name: nws_place_name
fields.description:
A person-readable label NWS returns for the point ("Houston, TX"). For
 display only; nothing parses it (scotty design record §5).

fields.name: resolved_at_ms
fields.description: resolved_at_ms is when /points was last asked.

fields.name: superseded_by_place_id
fields.description:
superseded_by_place_id: set on the OLD row when NWS re-cut the grid under
 this point. Empty on the current row. This is the ONE field a Place gains
 after creation, and there is deliberately no rpc that sets it: the service
 writes it through the generated state client (PutPlaces), which is the
 established mechanism for a service writing its own state and needs no verb
 registry exception, because the generated state service is Synthesized by
 construction. VERIFY 3 in the design doc, confirmed.

 The caveat that comes with it, worth carrying: PutPlaces REPLACES the whole
 row (there is no compare-and-swap). Fine for a single-writer poller; not
 once a second writer exists.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is MANDATORY on a record and is `/system` ON EVERY ROW OF THIS
 TYPE — the namespace of this service's own identity, not any tenant's. Read
 the block above this message for the whole argument; the short form is that a
 Place has no owning tenant by construction, `/system` is what the platform's
 own rule reduces `/system/services/weather` to, and the field deliberately
 carries no (spec.query_field) so that no read pins a criterion that could not
 narrow anything and would cost the store's by-key fast path.

 A HAZARD THIS FIELD NOW CARRIES, AND IT IS A TACPLUS GAP RATHER THAN A DESIGN
 CHOICE. Making these types records turns on the generated WATCH egress
 backstop, which compares EVERY snapshot frame and EVERY delta against the
 CALLER'S namespace claim and calls std::process::abort() on a mismatch. The
 unary and PAGE seams apply that filter only for a c2s service or the record
 plane's own s2s wrapper, and they carry a `__ns_pinned` escape so a /system
 peer keeps a fleet-wide read; the WATCH seam
 (rust/types/servicewrapper_gen.go:1511-1517 against :1882/:1947) has NEITHER
 gate. So today:

   - every caller on this service's auth_services list is a SHARED service
     whose own namespace claim is `/system`, so `/system` on the row MATCHES
     and the three WATCH rpcs work;
   - the day a TENANT-OWNED service watches this one — which is exactly what
     `reveille` is meant to be — its claim is `/tenants/<t>` , the guard
     mismatches, AND WEATHER'S PROCESS ABORTS. Not a refused call: an abort.

 There is no value of this field that avoids that, because a fleet-shared row
 read by callers in different namespaces cannot equal all of their claims.
 The fix is in tacplus, not here: the WATCH seam needs the same gate its unary
 and PAGE siblings have. Recorded in
 decisions/weather-record-shapes-2026-09-25.md as the one thing that must land
 before `reveille` exists.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record's declared `owner` and the PUBLISHER — eventbus
 stamps weather's own service identity onto it. The field NAME is load-bearing
 (eventbus's topic discovery matches the literal string "spiffe_id" of string
 type when it decides which topics get publisher-identity stamping), which is
 why it carries (spec.identity_spiffe_subject).

 ON THIS SERVICE IT IS THE ONLY OWNERSHIP STATEMENT THERE IS, and it is the
 true one: these rows belong to the platform's weather service, which is
 exactly what a 9a service's rows are. It is never a read filter — every row
 of every one of these four types carries the same value.

types.name: PolicyVersionFilter
PolicyVersionWatchChange

message.name: PolicyVersion
message.description:
PolicyVersion is ONE version of one written policy, and it is immutable.

 §2, and the word doing the work is "written": "A written policy has a
 document, an author and a date, so policy is quotable or it isn't policy —
 which converts 'Scotty invented a company policy' from a prompt problem into
 a structural one."

 So all four properties are fields, not conventions: body (the document),
 authored_by_human_id (the author), authored_at_ms (the date) and
 effective_from_ms + version (the "at the time" axis). There is no
 UpdatePolicyVersion RPC anywhere in this file. Amending a policy means
 creating version N+1; that is what makes "what did the policy say on the day
 Dennis acted" answerable at all.

 DELIBERATELY ABSENT: any scope/binding field ("who does this bind"). §2 is
 explicit that the answer is a query over (person, context), not a field, and
 that the hierarchy which would feed it is unsettled. Inventing a scope field
 here would silently settle it. See the schematic looper's
 decisions/written-policy-scope-omitted.md (pre-split snoopy history, not in
 this repo).

 A stratum record since 2026-09-25, tenant-owned and not `private` — the block
 above `message Human` is the reasoning for all six and is not repeated.

fields.name: policy_version_id
fields.description:
policy_version_id is the record key — one row per (policy_id, version).
 (spec.indexed) went with the state collection; see Human.human_id.

fields.name: policy_id
fields.description:
policy_id is stable ACROSS versions. It is what "policy P version 3
 effective D" (§4's definition of a finding as a citation) names.

fields.name: version
fields.description:
version starts at 1 and increments. Server-assigned, so two authors cannot
 both write version 4.

fields.name: body
fields.description:
body is the document itself — the thing that makes the policy quotable. It
 is prose by nature and must never be parsed to act on.

fields.name: authored_by_human_id
fields.description:
authored_by_human_id is the ATTRIBUTION. §2's known gap turns on this
 field: "Joe overrides a policy Alicia wrote; Dennis is notified, Alicia
 isn't... authorship and override-visibility come apart, and an author
 should know that going in." Recording the author is what makes that gap
 stateable rather than invisible.

 May be empty for POLICY_WEIGHT_STATUTORY, which "isn't authored by anyone
 in the org, so it isn't in the hierarchy at all". Who a statutory policy is
 attributed to is an open product question — see the schematic looper's
 decisions/statutory-policy-authorship-open.md (pre-split snoopy history,
 not in this repo).

fields.name: effective_from_ms
fields.description:
effective_from_ms is when this version began to bind. There is no
 effective_to: a version is superseded by the next version's
 effective_from_ms, which cannot drift out of agreement with itself the way
 a separately-written end date can.

fields.name: weight
fields.description:
weight is AUTHORED, never inferred — §2, stated as a rule. It is an enum so
 an undefined weight cannot be stored at all.

enum_values.name: POLICY_WEIGHT_SOFT
enum_values.description: Soft — push back once, capture the reason, comply, notify.

enum_values.name: POLICY_WEIGHT_HEAVY
enum_values.description:
Heavy — override requires SOMEONE ELSE's entitlement; the actor cannot
 self-clear.

enum_values.name: POLICY_WEIGHT_STATUTORY
enum_values.description:
Statutory — not overridable in-system by anyone. Ships with the product as
 trade knowledge: "Dennis shouldn't have to know to write the 811 policy."

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
The row's owning TENANT, new with the move to stratum for the reason
 Human.namespace gives. Its write half is (spec.namespace) on
 CreatePolicyVersionRequest.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description: The publisher, as on Human. Never a read filter; see Human.spiffe_id.

types.name: Predicate
PredicateGroup
PullAccountingRecordRequest
PullAccountingRecordResponse

message.name: AccountingRecord
message.description:
AccountingRecord is one completed RPC, stored in full by stratum.

 Every service in the fleet is a producer, so the s2s surface is open to all
 service identities. There is no c2s surface: accounting rows are written by
 the chassis, never by a browser client.

fields.name: accounting_id
fields.description: accounting_id is the record key: one row per accounting event.

fields.name: request_id
fields.description:
request_id is THE correlation key — the x-request-id the gateway generates
 and every hop forwards. The EQ query_field is what lets a caller ask "which
 accounting rows belong to the request that wrote this row", which is the
 whole reason this record exists rather than a log line.

fields.name: source_id
fields.description:
source_id identifies the emitting process ("{service_id}-{instance_id}"),
 copied verbatim from accounting.Event.source_id.

fields.name: timestamp_ms
fields.description: timestamp_ms is the RANGE criterion — "everything in this window".

fields.name: level
fields.description:
level is carried on the envelope so a consumer can filter without
 inspecting the payload; same reasoning applies to the stored row.

fields.name: method
fields.description: method is the RPC that was accounted for.

fields.name: code
fields.description: code is the gRPC status code the call completed with.

fields.name: duration_ms
fields.description: duration_ms is the measured call duration.

fields.name: principal_sub
fields.description:
principal_sub is the verified human principal behind the call — the claim
 the Authorizer actually checked, not a caller-written header. Caller-decided
 redaction, the same leg TaskActivity.created_by exercises: redacted by
 default, raw only for a caller holding a matching data grant.
 It is also the ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL for the record query plane's c2s half:
 (spec.store_principal) is what the generated wrapper filters a user's reads
 down to, and it must name the HUMAN, not spiffe_id below. spiffe_id is the
 emitting service, so filtering on it would narrow every user to the rows it
 emitted itself — which for a human is none. The two annotations disagree on
 purpose and this one wins, exactly as sys/spec.proto describes.

 The row filter runs BEFORE the redaction above, on the raw stored value, so
 a caller without the data grant is still matched against its own principal
 rather than against a redacted string.
 NOT a (spec.query_field), deliberately, and that is a real tension rather
 than an oversight. Making it an EQ criterion is what would carry the row
 filter into the plane's SIZE-ONLY RPCs — Get<T>Count returns a number over
 the handle's predicate and no rows, so no egress filter can narrow it — but
 ValidateDataEntitlementAnnotations refuses a field that is both
 (spec.redact) and (spec.query_field), because a filterable field defeats
 redaction. That refusal is right for the S2S half of the plane, where no
 per-caller pin applies and a peer could filter on this field freely.

 So accounting ROWS are filtered to the caller at egress and accounting
 COUNTS are not. Closing that needs a per-surface criterion (c2s-only,
 wrapper-pinned) which does not exist today; it is written up in the item 2
 report rather than bought by weakening the redaction rule.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner: the EMITTING SERVICE's identity, not the end
 user's (the human principal is principal_sub above). The field name is
 load-bearing — eventbus's topic discovery matches the LITERAL name
 "spiffe_id" of string type to decide which topics get publisher-identity
 stamping, so renaming it silently turns the stamping off.

fields.name: store_epoch_ms
fields.description:
store_epoch_ms is this row's LAST-WRITE clock, Unix milliseconds, owned and
 stamped by the generated wrapper — a producer that supplies one is refused
 (INVALID_ARGUMENT), so the value can never be caller-influenced.

 It is what makes memory/disk tiering possible: the residency clock is
 measured from this clock, and it is the predicate the memory and disk legs
 partition the query on.

 NOT timestamp_ms: that is the emitting service's business clock. Two
 different clocks; only this one is store-owned. On an append-only record
 they are written together and never diverge afterwards — which is a property
 of THIS record, not of the epoch.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT: the namespace claim of the caller
 whose RPC this row accounts for. (spec.store_namespace) is the tenant twin
 of principal_sub's (spec.store_principal) above — the same egress seam, a
 different boundary. That one answers "are these MY rows"; this one answers
 "is this MY tenant", by EXACT string equality against the caller's claim.

 MANDATORY, not opt-in: tacplus (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations) fails
 generation for any (spec.record) declaring no such field, on the reasoning
 that the record nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 The filter is generated on the READ side, which is not this record's own
 s2s publish surface above: stratum's record query plane (the (spec.trait) in
 the app proto's vservices/query.proto) exposes a c2s List/Sample/Watch over
 EVERY record in the fleet, and the namespace check is spliced into each of
 them for this type. A row reaching one of those with a namespace other than
 the caller's halts the JVM rather than failing the one call.

 Bounded like every other string field on this message. Not a
 (spec.query_field): the field exists to be the egress boundary, and making
 it a caller-supplied predicate is not what a boundary is.

fields.name: principal_sub_redacted

types.name: PullAgentCursorRequest
PullAgentCursorResponse

message.name: AgentCursor
message.description:
AgentCursor is one row per user: everything a cycle needs to know about what
 the previous cycle did.

 IT WAS KERNEL STATE UNTIL 2026-09-25 AND IS A STRATUM RECORD NOW. The
 departure was deliberate and written up (workers/big8-p1-scotty-agent-
 questions.md §1); the ruling in decisions/kernel-no-durability-user-data-to-
 stratum-2026-09-25.md reverses it, on the ground that kernel holds no durable
 user data. Item 3 of that ruling allows "a cursor may stay if it is
 rebuildable; the owning looper decides and says why". THIS CURSOR IS NOT
 ALLOWED TO STAY, and the field that decides it is last_fencing_token below: a
 stale-write reject that does not survive a restart is not a stale-write
 reject. decisions/scottyagent-record-shapes-2026-09-25.md D1.

 WHAT THE MOVE COSTS, said here and not only in the decision record, because
 the three reasons the row was kernel state were real and only one of them has
 gone away:

   - VISIBILITY. The design record requires a write to be "visible to the very
     next cycle even if it runs moments later on a different instance". A
     record reaches stratum through an EventBus publish and an ASYNCHRONOUS
     ingest, so it is not. The per-user kernel.FencedLock still serializes the
     read-modify-write; what it can no longer do is make the previous cycle's
     write readable. This is a real weakening and it is D3 of the decision
     record — read it before changing anything in `cycle_under_lock`.
   - THE READ PATH. GONE. `(spec.record_read)` at the top of this file plus
     the s2s_read grant below generate `sm.agent_cursor_record_reader()`; the
     shared `query` trait this comment used to describe is no longer how a
     service reads its own rows.
   - THE NAMESPACE STAMP. GONE, and the old comment was wrong about the
     mechanism rather than only out of date. eventbus's PublishHandler is
     ACCEPT-or-stamp-or-refuse: a row that arrives with (spec.store_namespace)
     ALREADY SET keeps that value, and only an unset one is stamped from the
     publisher (decisions/namespace-fix-corrected-2026-09-02.md). So this
     service writes the DELIVERY's tenant onto the row exactly as it did into
     kernel state, and the row lands in the user's namespace, not in
     `/system`. See the hazard note on `namespace` below.

 AgentCycle below is the other record and is unchanged: append-shaped, never
 read back by this service, and what the design record's user-facing "Bird's
 Eye View" reads through the generated c2s record query plane.

fields.name: user
fields.description:
user is the principal this cursor belongs to, the RECORD KEY, and the
 ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL.

 For a message-triggered cycle it is messaging.Message.recipient — the
 ADDRESSEE, not the sender: the loop that wakes is the recipient's agent.

 (spec.store_principal) is the same annotation AgentCycle.user carries and
 it does the same job here: the generated egress filter on ListMyAgentState
 drops any row whose `user` is not the caller's own subject, on top of the
 (spec.principal) stamp that already bound the request. Belt and braces by
 construction rather than by a hand-written check, and it is what stands in
 for `private` — see the record block above.

 NO (spec.query_field). It would be redundant with the key, which already
 produces the `user` criterion on AgentCursorFilter, and a second criterion
 is exactly what takes stratum's by-key point read away (pointRead fires
 only when the key criterion is the ONLY one set).

fields.name: cycles_completed
fields.description:
cycles_completed counts the loop cycles that have finished for this user.
 Monotonic, and the source of AgentCycle.cycle below.

fields.name: last_fencing_token
fields.description:
last_fencing_token is THE FENCE, and it is what makes the lock a fencing
 lock rather than a mutex.

 A fencing token is kernel's Raft log index of the granting Acquire:
 strictly increasing over every grant of every key, never reused. A resource
 owner stores the highest token it has seen and REJECTS a write carrying a
 lower one — that, not the lock, is what makes a paused or partitioned stale
 holder safe. This field is that stored highest-seen value, and this service
 is the resource owner doing the comparing (see service.rs `write_cursor`).

 Without it, a holder that stalled long enough for its lease to lapse could
 wake up and overwrite the cursor a newer holder had already advanced. The
 lock alone narrows that window; it does not close it.

fields.name: last_cycle_at_ms
fields.description: last_cycle_at_ms is when the last completed cycle finished.

fields.name: last_instance_id
fields.description:
last_instance_id is the instance that ran it. Recorded because consecutive
 cycles for one user legitimately run on different instances and "which pod
 was that" is otherwise unanswerable after the fact — NOT because anything
 routes on it. Nothing reads this field to make a decision.

fields.name: last_wake
fields.description: last_wake is the last event that woke a cycle for this user.

message.name: WakeEvent
message.description:
WakeEvent is ONE thing that woke the loop. A cycle carries every event it
 aggregated, not just the first, so "why did you wake" has a complete answer
 even when several arrived at once.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: reason is the trigger kind.

enum_values.name: WAKE_REASON_MESSAGE
enum_values.description:
A messaging.Message arrived on this user's EventBus queue and this
 instance's consumer group took it.

fields.name: source_id
fields.description:
source_id identifies the specific event. For WAKE_REASON_MESSAGE it is the
 messaging.Message's delivery_id — the record key of the one delivery this
 wake is for, not the message_id it shares with its siblings, because the
 delivery is what this consumer group consumed.

fields.name: observed_at_ms
fields.description: observed_at_ms is when this instance took the event off the queue.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT, by exact string equality against the
 reader's namespace claim.

 (spec.store_namespace) here generates the READ-side egress filter on every
 surface that returns this row — including the MCP dispatch, which resolves
 the caller's claim itself, holds each returned row to it, and ABORTS THE
 PROCESS on a row it would otherwise have to drop. That abort is the
 designed behaviour for a genuine tenant violation, not a bug.

 WHERE THE VALUE COMES FROM, stated because it is the weak link and hiding
 it would be worse. An event-driven cycle has NO CALLER: nothing
 authenticated this work, so there is no verified claim to stamp from. The
 only tenant signal available is the consumed messaging.Message's own
 `namespace`, and this service copies that. That value is itself stamped by
 eventbus from MESSAGING'S service token rather than from the sender's
 (workers/big8-p1-messaging-questions.md §1, a fleet-wide open gap), so it
 is the right FIELD carrying a value whose provenance is not yet what the
 design intends. Copying it is still correct: it is the only tenant fact the
 event carries, and the moment tacplus grows a delegated s2s publish the
 value becomes the sender's with no change here.

 Not a query field: the field exists to BE the egress boundary, a boundary a
 caller can predicate on is not one, and since 2026-09-25 there is a second
 reason — a criterion on it would cost this type its by-key point read. See
 the record block above and D2 of the decision record.

 WHAT THE MOVE TO A RECORD CHANGED, AND WHAT IT DID NOT. Nothing about where
 the value comes from: this service still copies the delivery's namespace
 onto the row. eventbus's PublishHandler is ACCEPT-or-stamp-or-refuse — a
 row arriving with this field already set KEEPS that value, and only an
 unset one is stamped from the publishing token
 (decisions/namespace-fix-corrected-2026-09-02.md) — so the row lands in the
 USER'S tenant and the caller's own read of it matches.

 THE HAZARD IF THAT EVER STOPS BEING TRUE, because it is a process abort and
 not a dropped row: this service's own namespace is `/system`, so a cursor
 that reached the topic with this field empty would come back stamped
 `/system`, and ListMyAgentState's generated backstop aborts on a row it
 would have to drop. A delivered messaging.Message always carries a
 non-empty namespace (eventbus refuses a publish without one), which is why
 there is no guard in service.rs against a case the platform cannot produce.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner, and the NAME IS LOAD-BEARING for the same
 reason it is on AgentCycle: eventbus's topic discovery matches the literal
 field name "spiffe_id" of string type when it decides which topics get
 publisher-identity stamping, so renaming this field silently turns the
 stamping off. It holds THIS SERVICE's identity, because the publish is s2s;
 `user` above is where the person is.

 Left empty by this service on publish. No (spec.query_field): nothing reads
 a cursor by publisher — every read of this type is by key.

types.name: PullAgentCycleRequest
PullAgentCycleResponse

message.name: AgentCycle
message.description:
AgentCycle is one completed loop cycle: what woke it, when, on which
 instance, under which fencing token.

 It is the durable history the design record calls the "Bird's Eye View" —
 "an ordinary generated read surface on that record — no new mechanism". This
 file therefore declares no read RPC for it: the c2s record query plane
 generated from (spec.store_principal) and the query fields below IS that
 surface, and hand-writing a second one would be the drift the typed-contract
 argument exists to prevent.

 Append-shaped by construction: the key carries the cycle number, so a cycle
 is a new row and no cycle ever rewrites another.

 spec.record implies spec.event, so tacplus synthesizes the topic wrapper
 AgentCycleBus with topic ref scottyagent.AgentCycleBus.stream. Do NOT
 hand-write that wrapper.

fields.name: cycle_id
fields.description: cycle_id is the record key: "<user>/<cycle>".

fields.name: user
fields.description:
user is whose agent ran, and the ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL.

 (spec.store_principal) is what holds a caller's reads of this record to
 their own rows on the c2s query plane, and it is the reason the Bird's Eye
 View needs no filtering code: "my cycles" is the only query the plane will
 answer. `spiffe_id` below is the record's declared owner but holds THIS
 SERVICE's identity (eventbus stamps the publisher), so filtering on that
 would show every user nothing.

 The EQ criterion is what carries the filter into the plane's size-only
 RPCs, which return a number over the handle's predicate and no rows for an
 egress filter to narrow.

fields.name: cycle
fields.description: cycle is this user's monotonic cycle number, the second half of cycle_id.

fields.name: fencing_token
fields.description:
fencing_token is the kernel.FencedLock token this cycle ran under. Carried
 onto the row so the history itself shows the fence: cycles for one user
 must appear in strictly increasing token order, and a row that does not is
 visible evidence of a stale holder that got through.

fields.name: woke_for
fields.description:
woke_for is EVERY event this cycle aggregated, in the order they were
 observed — not just the one that started it. That is the aggregation the
 design record asks for, made legible: "multiple events can land within one
 loop cycle; they are aggregated and processed together".

 Bounded at 256 to match Config.max_events_per_cycle's ceiling.

message.name: WakeEvent
message.description:
WakeEvent is ONE thing that woke the loop. A cycle carries every event it
 aggregated, not just the first, so "why did you wake" has a complete answer
 even when several arrived at once.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: reason is the trigger kind.

enum_values.name: WAKE_REASON_MESSAGE
enum_values.description:
A messaging.Message arrived on this user's EventBus queue and this
 instance's consumer group took it.

fields.name: source_id
fields.description:
source_id identifies the specific event. For WAKE_REASON_MESSAGE it is the
 messaging.Message's delivery_id — the record key of the one delivery this
 wake is for, not the message_id it shares with its siblings, because the
 delivery is what this consumer group consumed.

fields.name: observed_at_ms
fields.description: observed_at_ms is when this instance took the event off the queue.

fields.name: started_at_ms
fields.description:
started_at_ms is the business clock — when the cycle began, which is after
 the lock was granted. It is what retention measures age from, and the RANGE
 criterion because "what did my agent do last week" is the question the
 Bird's Eye View asks.

fields.name: finished_at_ms
fields.description: finished_at_ms is when it ended, before the release.

fields.name: instance_id
fields.description:
instance_id is the instance that ran the cycle. Provenance, not routing —
 see AgentCursor.last_instance_id.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner. The NAME IS LOAD-BEARING: eventbus's topic
 discovery matches the literal field name "spiffe_id" of string type when it
 decides which topics get publisher-identity stamping, so renaming this
 field silently turns the stamping off. It holds THIS SERVICE's identity,
 because the publish is s2s; `user` above is where the person is.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT. MANDATORY on a (spec.record):
 tacplus's ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations fails generation for any
 record declaring no such field, on the reasoning that the record nobody
 remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 Left EMPTY by this service on publish, on purpose. eventbus's
 PublishHandler stamps it from the publishing token's namespace claim and
 REFUSES the publish with PERMISSION_DENIED when the token carries none —
 stamp-or-refuse, deliberately not stamp-if-empty, because a row published
 with an empty namespace is a row no legitimate caller can ever read. A
 value written here would be this service asserting a tenant nothing
 verified. (That the stamp is the SERVICE's namespace rather than the user's
 is the gap AgentCursor.namespace describes.)

types.name: PullAgentEventRequest
PullAgentEventResponse

message.name: AgentEvent
message.description:
AgentEvent is the top-level event published to EventBus.
 Each event represents one hook firing in one coding-agent session.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
── Identity ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────
 spiffe_id is the acting principal's SUBJECT SPIFFE ID
 (spiffe://<root>/tenants/<tenant_id>/users/<sub>), the durable EventDB
 owner. Stamped by EventBus from the caller's verified token at publish
 time — not populated by clients. (Replaces the former email owner.)

fields.name: event_id
fields.description:
event_id is the globally unique identifier for this event.
 Generated server-side. Not populated by clients.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_SESSION_START
enum_values.description: Session lifecycle.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_TOOL_USE
enum_values.description: Tool use (any tool: Bash, Read, Write, Edit, Grep, Agent, etc.)

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_SUBAGENT_START
enum_values.description: Subagent lifecycle — agent spawned or finished.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_TASK_COMPLETED
enum_values.description: Task lifecycle.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_COMPACT
enum_values.description: Context management.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_PROMPT
enum_values.description: User prompt submitted.

enum_values.name: SENSOR_EVENT_TYPE_STOP
enum_values.description: Stop — agent finished responding.

fields.name: store_epoch_ms
fields.description:
store_epoch_ms is this row's LAST-WRITE clock, Unix milliseconds, owned and
 stamped by the generated wrapper — a producer that supplies one is refused
 (INVALID_ARGUMENT), so the value can never be caller-influenced.

 It is what makes AgentEvent REPLAYABLE in stratum's hot tier: each node's
 redo log is partial, so recovery is a union across nodes and the epoch is
 the only clock that resolves it. Without this field the type keeps its
 in-memory replication and its quorum gate but gets no redo log at all
 (stratum's HotStoreGenerator refuses one it could not safely merge).

 NOT timestamp_ms: that is the author's business clock. Two different
 clocks; only this one is store-owned.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT — the namespace claim of the principal
 whose session produced this event. It is the tenant half of the identity
 spiffe_id carries the subject half of: spiffe_id names WHO acted, this names
 WHICH TENANT the row belongs to, and the generated egress filter holds a c2s
 read to rows matching the caller's claim by EXACT equality (never the
 level-or-below containment the administrative namespace rule uses).

 MANDATORY, not opt-in: tacplus (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations) fails
 generation for any (spec.record) declaring no such field, on the reasoning
 that the record nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 The filter is generated on the READ side, which is not this record's own
 s2s publish surface above: stratum's record query plane (the (spec.trait) in
 the app proto's vservices/query.proto) exposes a c2s List/Sample/Watch over
 EVERY record in the fleet, and the namespace check is spliced into each of
 them for this type. A row reaching one of those with a namespace other than
 the caller's halts the JVM rather than failing the one call.

 Deliberately NOT projected into any transformation above: adding it there
 would widen four already-explicit column lists, which is a separate call.

message.name: SessionEvent
message.description: SessionEvent captures session start/end metadata.

message.name: ToolUseEvent
message.description: ToolUseEvent captures a single tool invocation.

message.name: FileEvent
message.description: FileEvent captures a file operation.

message.name: SubagentEvent
message.description: SubagentEvent captures subagent spawn/stop.

message.name: PromptEvent
message.description: PromptEvent captures a user prompt submission.

message.name: StopEvent
message.description: StopEvent captures why the agent stopped responding.

types.name: PullAgentSessionStateRequest
PullAgentSessionStateResponse

message.name: AgentSessionState
message.description:
AgentSessionState is the CURRENT state of one coding-agent session: one row
 per session, rewritten in place every time the session moves.

 It exists because the fleet had no mutable warm record and two properties of
 the warm tier are only observable on one. AgentEvent (hot) and AccountingRecord
 (warm, append-only) are both write-once by their own nature — an event and a
 completed RPC have no later state — so nothing exercised the store epoch
 REFRESHING, which is the whole reason the epoch is a last-write clock rather
 than a creation stamp.

 A session is the natural carrier for that: it is open for as long as the agent
 is working, its status and counters change while it is open, and once it has
 ended the row is a historical record that ages out of memory exactly like an
 accounting row. Both halves of the warm window apply to it, and unlike the two
 records above it moves while it is resident.

 There is no row-mutating RPC and there is not meant to be one: rows reach the
 store by EventBus publish, so an UPDATE is a republish of the same session_id.
 The generated wrapper restamps store_epoch_ms on that republish, which is what
 puts the row back inside the residency window.

fields.name: session_id
fields.description: session_id is the record key: one row per session, not one per transition.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner — the acting principal's SUBJECT SPIFFE ID,
 stamped by EventBus from the caller's verified token, exactly as on
 AgentEvent. The literal field name is load-bearing for that stamping.

fields.name: started_at_ms
fields.description:
started_at_ms is the session's business clock, fixed at the first publish and
 NOT rewritten afterwards.

 The contrast with store_epoch_ms below is the point of this record: on an
 append-only row the two clocks are written together and never diverge, so
 nothing could tell them apart. Here they diverge on every update.

fields.name: status
fields.description: status is the session's current state — the mutable field an update carries.

fields.name: tool_use_count
fields.description:
tool_use_count is how many tool invocations the session has made so far.
 Monotonic, but rewritten in place: the row holds the running total, not one
 row per increment.

fields.name: store_epoch_ms
fields.description:
store_epoch_ms is this row's LAST-WRITE clock, Unix milliseconds, owned and
 stamped by the generated wrapper — a producer that supplies one is refused
 (INVALID_ARGUMENT), so the value can never be caller-influenced.

 On this record it MOVES. Every republish of the same session_id restamps it,
 which resets the row's residency: a session that has aged out of the memory
 window and is then updated is inside the window again, because the window is
 measured from the last write and the row was just written. That is the
 property a mutable stored record without MUTABILITY_APPEND_ONLY exists to
 state, and it is why the residency clock cannot be started_at_ms.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT — the namespace claim of the principal
 whose session this row tracks, the same value AgentEvent carries for the
 events emitted inside that session. Held to EXACT equality against the
 caller's claim by the generated c2s egress filter.

 MANDATORY on every (spec.record): tacplus fails generation for one that
 declares none (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations).

 Unlike status and tool_use_count, this is NOT a field an update carries: a
 session does not change tenant. It is rewritten with the same value on every
 republish of the same session_id, which is what makes the row's tenant
 stable across the restamping described for store_epoch_ms above.

types.name: PullAlertRequest
PullAlertResponse

message.name: Alert
message.description:
NWS issues alerts against zones, and a zone covers many places. Storing an
 Alert per place would store the same hurricane watch once per job site in
 Harris County. So the row is keyed by NWS's own alert id and carries the zones
 it names; "alerts for this place" is a read that resolves the place's zones
 first (ListAlerts takes either form). Choice E.

 Write-once like the rest: an alert NWS UPDATEs or CANCELs arrives as a NEW
 alert row whose references name the one it supersedes. Nothing is edited in
 place, which is also why there is no "active" boolean — active is a function
 of (effective, expires, superseded) AT THE MOMENT YOU ASK, not a stored flag
 some poller has to remember to clear.

fields.name: zone_ids
fields.description:
zone_ids are the NWS zones this alert names — forecast zones, county zones,
 or both. Order is NWS's.

 A NOTE ON THE REPEATED-STRING BOUND, the same one work.Job carries:
 (spec.assert_max_size) does DOUBLE DUTY on a repeated string field — tacplus
 reads it as the element byte cap AND as the element count, and there is no
 second annotation that separates them. 256 here therefore means "at most 256
 zone ids, each at most 256 bytes". A zone id is 6 bytes; 256 zones is a wide
 hurricane watch but not an unheard-of one, and this is the number to revisit
 first if a real alert is ever truncated.

fields.name: event
fields.description:
event is NWS's event name, verbatim: "Hurricane Watch", "Flash Flood
 Warning", "Heat Advisory". NOT an enum: NWS's list is long, changes, and is
 authoritative elsewhere. A rule in Reveille matches on this string, and
 matching on the bureau's own word is more honest than matching on our lossy
 re-encoding of it. Choice F.

fields.name: severity
fields.description:
ALL FOUR CARRY (spec.assert_enum_defined), AND THAT ANNOTATION REFUSES THE
 *_UNSPECIFIED ZERO VALUE. It is worth saying at the point of use because the
 consequence is a long way from the declaration: a row stored with one of
 these left at zero is written happily by the state client and then fails
 RESPONSE validation inside the generated wrapper on every read of it,
 including every WATCH frame. That is why the ingest in services/weather/
 src/nws.rs falls back to a DECLARED value for each — UNKNOWN for the first
 three, and ALERT for message_type, which is also CAP's own default for the
 field — rather than leaving an absent value at zero.

fields.name: sent_at_ms
fields.description:
sent_at_ms is a RANGE (spec.query_field), emitting sent_at_ms_from /
 sent_at_ms_to — ListAlerts's declared window and this type's ONLY store-side
 criterion beyond the key. The other four stamps are not criteria: they are
 what `active_at_ms` is COMPUTED from, and that computation needs the
 supersession set over every alert, so narrowing on one of them in the store
 would change the answer rather than speed it up.

fields.name: sender_name
fields.description: sender_name is the issuing office ("NWS Houston/Galveston TX").

fields.name: references
fields.description:
references are the alert ids this one updates, corrects or cancels. The
 superseded rows STAY. Same rule as a renewed permit in `work` and a
 corrected document in the Doc Manager: the correction is a new row that
 points at the old one. Bounded at 256 for the same double-duty reason as
 zone_ids — an alert id is up to 256 bytes, so the count cannot be lower.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace: mandatory, `/system` on every row, no criterion. See message Place,
 including the WATCH-egress hazard note on its copy of this field.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description: spiffe_id: the publisher's identity, stamped by eventbus. See message Place.

types.name: PullBlobLinkRequest
PullBlobLinkResponse

message.name: BlobLink
message.description:
BlobLink is one shareable URL, keyed by the HASH of its token (R7).

 THE RAW TOKEN APPEARS NOWHERE PERSISTENT. It is returned once, by the call
 that minted it, and this row holds only `sha256(token)`; ListLinks returns no
 tokens, and the gateway redacts `/b/*` and `/upload/*` paths from its logs.
 So a reader of the record store — or of a log, or of a backup — cannot
 resolve any link.

 REVOCATION IS IMMEDIATE, which is v3's improvement over the v2 signed-URL
