 design: we serve the bytes, so `revoked_ms` is checked on every resolve
 rather than waiting for a cloud URL to expire. It is kept rather than deleted
 so an audit can still say a link existed.

fields.name: token_hash
fields.description:
token_hash is the record key: the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw token.
 A resolve hashes what arrived in the path and looks up THAT, so the lookup
 key is not a secret even though the path is.

fields.name: blob_id
fields.description: blob_id is the Blob this link resolves to.

fields.name: filename
fields.description:
filename is what `Content-Disposition` offers, and the ONLY source of it
 (R8) — never a client-supplied header, never a query parameter. Validated
 at mint: a basename, no CR/LF, quote, backslash, semicolon, control
 character or path separator.

enum_values.name: LINK_POLICY_BEARER
enum_values.description:
BEARER: whoever holds the token. The only policy today (R7); SAME_TENANT
 and FLEET_ONLY are additive later and need a caller identity on the `/b/`
 path, which BEARER deliberately does not have.

fields.name: expires_ms
fields.description:
expires_ms is 0 for a durable shared link and non-zero for the short-lived
 one the owner mints for its own use. Checked on resolve alongside
 revoked_ms; the two are indistinguishable to the caller, who gets a 404
 either way.

fields.name: revoked_ms
fields.description:
revoked_ms is when the owner revoked the link, 0 while live. The row is
 KEPT — see the type comment.

types.name: PullBlobLinkStatsRequest
PullBlobLinkStatsResponse

message.name: BlobLinkStats
message.description:
BlobLinkStats is the coarse rollup of one link's resolutions (R10).

 The counters live IN MEMORY on the pod that served the request and are
 flushed here at most once a minute per token. That is the whole design: a
 `/b/` resolve must not cost a record write, and nobody needs a resolution
 count to be exact.

 `bytes_served` is honest here in a way it could not be in the v2 cloud
 design: we serve the bytes ourselves, so we count them rather than inferring
 them from a signed URL that may or may not have been followed.

 TWO PODS, TWO COUNTERS. Each pod flushes what it served, and a flush is a
 read-modify-write of this row — so the row is the SUM only as of the last
 flush either pod made. Exactness was never on offer for an in-memory counter;
 what matters is that a flush never loses another pod's contribution, which is
 why it reads before it adds.

fields.name: token_hash
fields.description:
token_hash is the key, and the same key BlobLink carries — the two rows are
 one link's two halves, split because the stats half is rewritten on a
 minute cadence and the link half is written once.

types.name: PullBlobRequest
PullBlobResponse

message.name: Blob
message.description:
Blob is one promoted file: bytes that are fsynced and renamed into place on
 BOTH pods. A Blob row never points at bytes that are not on both pods (R9).

 IMMUTABLE AND CONTENT-ADDRESSED, PER TENANT (R5). Identity is
 `(group, namespace, content_hash)` and dedup is within a tenant and group
 only: two tenants holding the same bytes hold two files and each pays. A
 global key would have been a cross-tenant content oracle — ask whether a hash
 exists and learn that someone else has the document — and it contradicted
 DocHashIndex's own per-namespace rule.

 NO VERSIONING. A new version is a new blob and the consumer moves its own
 pointer. The filename is the consumer's and lives on BlobLink, not here.

fields.name: blob_id
fields.description:
blob_id is the record key and the file's path: `<group>/<ns>/<sha256-hex>`.
 Carried as one string rather than derived on read because it IS the key,
 and a key a reader has to assemble from three fields is a key two callers
 can assemble differently.

fields.name: group
fields.description:
group is the volume group this blob belongs to — the group whose rules
 admitted it. EQ-filterable because per-group quota accounting is a query
 over exactly this field plus `namespace`.

fields.name: content_hash
fields.description:
content_hash is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the bytes, computed by this
 service AS THE UPLOAD STREAMS — native and exact. It is checked against the
 client's declared hash at end of stream and the upload fails if they
 differ (R9 step 3).

fields.name: size_bytes
fields.description: size_bytes is the byte count as counted on the wire, not as declared.

fields.name: content_type
fields.description:
content_type is what `GET /b/` serves. It survived both the group's
 allow-list and the magic-byte sniff, so it describes the stored bytes
 rather than merely what the uploader said about them.

fields.name: created_ms
fields.description:
created_ms is when the blob was promoted. RANGE-filterable: "what landed
 this week" is a question about this field, and it is what a later GC over
 consumers' pointers (R12) would scan.

fields.name: owner_principal
fields.description:
owner_principal is the OWNING SERVICE identity — docmanager, not blobstore
 — and the row's owning principal (R6). Only this identity creates or
 revokes links or deletes the blob.

 `spiffe_id` below is the record's declared owner but is the PUBLISHER,
 which is always blobstore, so it is the wrong field to filter an owner's
 reads on — the same split mailbox.MailboxEntry makes between `recipient`
 and `spiffe_id`.

fields.name: deleted
fields.description:
deleted marks the blob logically gone. The BYTES are not deleted by the
 record: the owner's Delete is what unlinks them from both pods, and this
 flag is what stops a resolve and starts the purge clock.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record's owner in the store's sense — the publisher, which
 is blobstore's own workload identity. See owner_principal.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the OWNING TENANT (R6) and the second segment of blob_id. It
 is what makes dedup per-tenant: the same bytes under two namespaces are two
 rows and two files.

types.name: PullChatEventRequest
PullChatEventResponse

message.name: ChatEvent
message.description:
ChatEvent is the append-only record of what was said and what Scotty did. One
 row per OWNER copy, which is what makes history entitleable per person with
 no hand-written check: `owner` carries (spec.store_principal) and the
 generated filter does the rest.

 A stratum record since 2026-09-25, principal-owned and NOT `private` — see
 the (spec.record_read) block at the top of this file, whose second reason is
 about THIS type: one logical event is one row per member, and appending it
 reads every other member's high-water seq. A pin that admits only the
 caller's own rows cannot do that.

fields.name: event_key
fields.description:
event_key is the record key: "<event_id>/<owner>". event_id for a sent
 message is "<chat_id>/<sender>/<client_message_id>", which is what makes a
 retried send rewrite the same rows instead of appending duplicates.
 Service-originated events mint event_id timestamp-first.

 (spec.indexed) is gone with the state collection — see Chat.chat_id.

fields.name: chat_id
fields.description:
chat_id is the ONE predicate this file pushes down past the two pins, and
 it is the exception that proves work's rule (its D4: "there is no predicate
 pushdown here beyond the tenant"). Two things make it different. It is a
 DECLARED PARAMETER of both reads that use it — ListChatEvents(chat_id) and
 ListMyChatHistory(chat_id) — rather than a predicate the handler invents;
 and this collection is the largest in the file by two orders of magnitude
 (its state bound was 10,000,000 against Chat's 100,000), so "every event
 this person owns, then filter" is the one read here where the difference
 is a number rather than a preference. An empty chat_id is still the
 unified timeline: the criterion is simply not sent.

fields.name: owner
fields.description:
owner is whose COPY this is — the personal principal, as on ChatSession.
 EQ-queryable since 2026-09-25 — see ChatMembership.principal.

fields.name: seq
fields.description:
seq is monotonic PER OWNER across all their chats: it is the WATCH revision
 and the PAGE keyset in one.

 HOW IT IS ASSIGNED IS OPEN, and the split is what opened it. The 2026-09-07
 sketch assigns it under the owner's kernel.FencedLock, copying scottyagent
 — but that needs (spec.grpc_s2s_client) = {service: "kernel.FencedLock"},
 which is service-identity S2S reach and is exactly what DECISIONS.md item
 9c denies this class of service. A delegated user token cannot stand in: a
 per-owner sequence is the SERVICE's bookkeeping, not an action taken on the
 user's behalf, and it must hold across owners who are mid-turn in different
 tenants. Nothing here decides the answer — the field's meaning is unchanged
 whichever way it is assigned. Written up rather than improvised.

fields.name: author
fields.description:
author is the principal whose message or action this is; author_actor is
 the delegate that produced it (the author's Scotty), empty when the human
 did it directly. Same split as scotty.TicketDecision.decided_by /
 decided_by_actor and messaging.Message.spiffe_actor: "attribution must be
 tracked state, not inferred per-turn" (design record §9).

fields.name: text
fields.description: MESSAGE, and the message half of MOVED_OUT.

fields.name: ticket_id
fields.description:
TICKET_*: which ticket, and (TICKET_OPENED) the other side's chat if known.

 A TICKET ID HERE NAMES A ROW IN A TENANT'S `scotty`, NOT IN THIS SERVICE.
 That is the split working as intended and not a dangling reference: the
 artifact has exactly one home (login doc §4 rule 1) and this row is the
 personal-side KNOWLEDGE that it happened. There is deliberately no field
 recording which tenant, because the chat's own routing already fixed it and
 a second copy could disagree with the first.

fields.name: tool_name
fields.description:
TOOL_CALLED: which generated tool, and whether Config.max_turn_hops halted
 the turn.

fields.name: moved_to_chat_id
fields.description: MOVED_OUT: where Scotty filed it; on the target copy, where it came from.

fields.name: member_principal
fields.description: MEMBER_JOINED / MEMBER_LEFT.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace: see ChatSession.namespace. Same field, same open question, same
 reason for keeping it. EQ-queryable because c2s_read requires it.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record's declared `owner` and the PUBLISHER — this
 SERVICE, never the person. `owner` above is where the person is; filtering
 a person's reads on THIS field would show them every row in the fleet while
 looking like it showed them their own. See Chat.spiffe_id.

fields.name: thread_id
fields.description:
MESSAGE: the A29 thread the message belongs to, as sent on
 CreateChatMessageRequest.thread_id. The same value on every member's copy.

types.name: PullChatMembershipRequest
PullChatMembershipResponse

message.name: ChatMembership
message.description:
ChatMembership is what ONE person has decided about one chat: archived,
 muted, what they told their Scotty to do about it, how far they have read.
 None of it is anyone else's business and none of it is shared, which is why
 this row can carry the pin `Chat` cannot.

 It is also the chat list. Every read of "my chats" goes through here, so the
 generated per-principal filter is the list's authorization, not a check.

 A stratum record since 2026-09-25, principal-owned and NOT `private` — read
 the (spec.record_read) block at the top of this file for why `private` is the
 right description of this row and the wrong annotation for it today.

fields.name: membership_id
fields.description:
membership_id is the record key: "<chat_id>/<principal>". Derived rather
 than minted, exactly as ChatSession.session_id is and for the same reason:
 one row per (chat, person) by construction.

 (spec.indexed) is gone with the state collection — see Chat.chat_id.

fields.name: principal
fields.description:
principal is the OWNING principal — the personal principal, as on
 ChatSession. (spec.store_principal) generates the read-side filter that
 pins every surface returning this row to the caller's own subject, which is
 what makes archive and mute per person with no hand-written check.

 EQ-queryable since 2026-09-25, and that is half the annotation rather than
 decoration: the c2s record-read plane REFUSES C2S_SCOPE_PRINCIPAL when no
 principal criterion resolves (rather than degrading it to a tenant-wide
 read), and the handler pins this same field into the predicate before the
 store is asked, which is what keeps `total` this person's own count instead
 of the fleet's.

fields.name: archived
fields.description:
archived hides the chat from the live list. It is NOT terminal —
 UpdateChatMembership clears it. Purging a chat would be a Delete, and there
 is none: a chat is never gone.

fields.name: muted
fields.description:
muted: Scotty surfaces nothing from this chat unless notify_policy_text
 says otherwise.

fields.name: notify_policy_text
fields.description:
notify_policy_text is this person's standing instruction to THEIR OWN
 Scotty about this chat ("only tell me if there is something I should
 know"). Read by that runtime and nothing else; prose by nature, and no
 other member's runtime may read it — the principal pin above is what makes
 that true rather than promised.

fields.name: last_read_seq
fields.description:
last_read_seq is this owner's ChatEvent.seq high-water mark, which is what
 "unread" is computed from.

 IT INHERITS ChatEvent.seq's UNSOLVED ASSIGNMENT. Read that field's comment
 before treating this number as a reliable watermark: until per-owner seq
 assignment has an answer, so does unread.

fields.name: last_event_at_ms
fields.description:
last_event_at_ms orders the chat list. Maintained by the handler when it
 appends this owner's copy of an event.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace: see ChatSession.namespace. EQ-queryable because tacplus refuses
 (spec.record).c2s_read on a record whose (spec.store_namespace) field is
 not: the client-facing plane pins the field to the caller's verified claim
 before the store is asked, and a pin needs a criterion to be pinned into.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record's declared `owner` and the PUBLISHER — this
 SERVICE, never the person. `principal` above is where the person is. See
 Chat.spiffe_id for why the name is load-bearing and why it is never a read
 filter.

types.name: PullChatRequest
PullChatResponse

message.name: Chat
message.description:
Chat is who is in a conversation. It is the one row in this service that
 belongs to SEVERAL people at once, and that is the whole difficulty with it.

 NO (spec.store_principal), AND THAT IS NOT AN OMISSION. The annotation pins a
 row to exactly one subject — tacplus refuses a second field carrying it
 (`principal_validate.go`, recorded in decisions/work-service-2026-09-09.md
 VERIFY answer 4) — and a chat with four participants has no one owner to pin
 to. `created_by` would pin reads to the creator and hide the chat from
 everyone else in it. So this collection gets NO generated egress filter, and
 "only a member may read a chat" is a hand-written check in the handler,
 enforced against the caller's own ChatMembership row.

 That is the same unbuilt entitlement gap `scotty.Human` records (see
 schematic/looper/schematic/decisions/scotty-read-authorization-not-wired.md)
 and it is NOT solved here. What IS structural is the membership row: every
 list of chats goes through ChatMembership, which is principal-pinned, so the
 only way to learn a chat_id you are not in is to be told one.

 A stratum record since 2026-09-25, and the ONE of this file's four with no
 owning principal — which is exactly what decides its record shape. Read the
 (spec.record_read) block at the top of this file for why it gets no c2s half.

fields.name: chat_id
fields.description:
chat_id is DERIVED for the singletons and minted otherwise:
   DIRECT: "direct/<min(a,b)>/<max(a,b)>"  — 1:1, one per pair by
           construction, so CreateChat on an existing pair returns it
           instead of making a second one.
   SELF default: "self/<principal>/default" — the catch-all a message with
           no chat lands in.
   SELF other, GROUP, JOB: minted timestamp-first.

 (spec.indexed) WAS HERE AND IS GONE WITH THE STATE COLLECTION: it is the
 statedb field-index marker, and there is no state map left to index. The
 key is an EQ criterion on ChatFilter without any annotation, because
 declaring s2s_read above folds a record's key into its filter
 (record_map.go's keyFilterCriterion) — which is what the point read behind
 GetChat is.

enum_values.name: CHAT_KIND_SELF_CHAT
enum_values.description:
SELF: the user and their own Scotty. Goes nowhere. Many per user.

 NAMED _SELF_CHAT AND NOT _SELF, and that is a tacplus defect worked around
 rather than a shade of meaning. `CHAT_KIND_SELF` renders as the Rust variant
 `Self`, which is a reserved word: prost's own emitter sanitizes it to
 `Self_`, but tacplus's `toProstEnumVariant`
 (pkg/internal/rust/types/enums.go:229) PascalCases without consulting its
 own `rustKeywords` set, so the serde and helper files it generates alongside
 say `ChatKind::Self` and the model crate does not compile:
   error[E0433]: `Self` in paths can only be used in start position
     types/services/scottypersonal/helpers.rs:25  "chat-kind-self" => Ok(ChatKind::Self)
     types/services/scottypersonal/scottypersonal.serde.rs:2364  Self::Self => "CHAT_KIND_SELF"
 (verified 2026-09-11 against tacplus c33d7d56 by building services/work,
 the first Rust service generated since this enum landed). The upstream fix
 is for toProstEnumVariant to mirror prost's trailing-underscore rule; until
 it does, no proto in this fleet may end an enum value in _SELF. Rename this
 back the day that lands — nothing has ever been stored under either name.

enum_values.name: CHAT_KIND_DIRECT
enum_values.description: DIRECT: two people (and their Scottys). One per pair.

enum_values.name: CHAT_KIND_GROUP
enum_values.description: GROUP: people who join and leave.

enum_values.name: CHAT_KIND_JOB
enum_values.description:
JOB: a GROUP whose closure is company-wide. Reserved from the 2026-09-07
 sketch: the job type does not exist yet and nothing here invents it.

fields.name: participants
fields.description:
participants are HUMAN principals and AGENT identities. The caller's own
 Scotty is implicit in every chat and is not listed; a participant of kind
 AGENT is a NAMED one (a DocManager, a JobManager, a customer's agent).

 A PARTICIPANT IS A PERSONAL PRINCIPAL, not a per-tenant identity, for the
 same reason ChatSession.principal is: the chat spans every tenant its
 members belong to. A member of this chat is not thereby a member of any
 tenant — where work gets FILED is the routing map's business, and
 GetMyRoutingMap answers it separately for each person.

fields.name: principal
fields.description: principal is a token subject for HUMAN, an agent identity for AGENT.

fields.name: joined_at_ms
fields.description: joined_at_ms is stamped by the handler, never by the caller.

fields.name: title
fields.description:
title is set by the creator or by Scotty (through UpdateChat). Prose;
 nothing derives from it.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace: see ChatSession.namespace. Same field, same open question about
 what claim a personal principal carries, same reason for keeping it.

 EQ-queryable since 2026-09-25, because it is now the ONLY pin this record
 has: with no owning principal, the caller's verified namespace is the whole
 of what `require_chat` pins into the store predicate before it asks (the
 same value it compared in-process when these rows came from kernel).

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record's declared `owner` and the PUBLISHER — eventbus
 stamps this service's own identity onto it. The field NAME is load-bearing
 (eventbus's topic discovery matches the literal string "spiffe_id" of
 string type when it decides which topics get publisher-identity stamping),
 which is why it carries (spec.identity_spiffe_subject) exactly as
 work.WorkActivity.spiffe_id does.

 IT IS THE SERVICE, NOT A PERSON, and so it is never a read filter. Every
 row of this type in the fleet carries the same value; narrowing a read by
 it would show a reader every chat in the fleet while looking like it
 narrowed something.

types.name: PullChatSessionRequest
PullChatSessionResponse

message.name: ChatSession
message.description:
ChatSession is what one person's Scotty is currently holding in mind about
 one chat. It is knowledge, re-derivable from ChatEvent; it is not an
 artifact, which is why this service's state root carries no
 requires_artifact_on_write. What Scotty DOES from a chat leaves its artifact
 where the doing happens — a ticket in the tenant that owns it.

 A stratum record since 2026-09-25, principal-owned and NOT `private` — see
 the (spec.record_read) block at the top of this file. THIS is the one type in
 this file that `private` would fit on its own terms (it is never read across
 owners); it stays non-private with its siblings because the reader it would
 need does not exist, and because one private row among three ordinary ones
 buys a second plane client and no guarantee the store_principal pin does not
 already give.

fields.name: session_id
fields.description:
session_id is the record key: "<chat_id>/<principal>". Derived rather than
 minted, so one person has exactly one session per chat by construction and
 a second one cannot be created by racing.

 (spec.indexed) is gone with the state collection — see Chat.chat_id.

fields.name: principal
fields.description:
principal is the OWNING principal, and it is the whole egress mechanism for
 this collection: (spec.store_principal) generates the read-side filter that
 pins every surface returning this row to the caller's own subject.

 It is the PERSONAL principal (login doc §2b: the device's synced keychain
 key), never a per-tenant identity. That is the split: this row is one
 person's, across every tenant they belong to, and there is no tenant-scoped
 reader of it at all.

 EQ-queryable since 2026-09-25 — see ChatMembership.principal for why that
 is half the annotation and not decoration.

fields.name: state_text
fields.description:
state_text is the ONE generic text field Jody asked for: the LLM gets it,
 modifies it, puts it back whole. Nothing parses it, nothing derives
 authority from it, and NO FACT MAY LIVE ONLY HERE — see the 2026-09-07
 decision doc §2. In particular the routing map is not remembered here: it
 is read from kernel every time (login doc §4, and GetMyRoutingMap below).

fields.name: state_version
fields.description:
state_version increments on every replace and must be presented on the
 next replace. A stale replace is FAILED_PRECONDITION. Cheap insurance
 against a dormant session that woke twice.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning namespace, held to the reader's claim by
 exact equality by the generated egress filter.

 WHAT VALUE A PERSONAL PRINCIPAL'S ROWS CARRY IS NOT SETTLED, and this is
 the one place the service split reaches down to a field. Device principals
 do not exist yet (login doc §6 item 1) and nothing has decided what
 namespace claim one holds. What IS settled is that it must not be a
 TENANT's: a personal chat spans every tenant the person belongs to, so
 pinning the row to one tenant would contradict §3's "the personal runtime
 sees everything the user sees".

 The field is kept — with the marker — rather than dropped, because
 (spec.store_namespace) is only mandatory on a (spec.record) and a state row
 may legally omit it, which would mean silently generating NO egress
 backstop at all. Whoever settles the device-principal claim settles this
 field's value; the annotation is not the thing to remove if it turns out
 the claim is empty.

 MANDATORY NOW, not merely kept: tacplus's ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations
 fails generation for a (spec.record) declaring no such field, "on the
 reasoning that the record nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one
 that leaks". The paragraph above anticipated this ("(spec.store_namespace)
 is only mandatory on a (spec.record)") — the move to stratum is what made
 it so. EQ-queryable because c2s_read requires it.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record's declared `owner` and the PUBLISHER — this
 SERVICE, never the person. See Chat.spiffe_id.

types.name: PullCompanyStructureRequest
PullCompanyStructureResponse

message.name: CompanyStructure
message.description:
CompanyStructure — ONE row per tenant (A17), keyed by tenant id. Written
 only from the web console by the owner role (D6); for the first tenant,
 seeded once by the import service (Q27). Deterministic rules are structured
 fields here, checked by the service path, not by a model.

 NOT HERE, on purpose (Jody, 2026-09-29):
   - Quiet hours / holds. Whether a PERSON is interrupted is their own
     Scotty's call against their own rules; no company dog decides a hold.
     TODO(CP3): A17 listed quiet hours as a company rule; that entry is
     superseded by "holds are Scotty's" and no field is declared.
   - Language. A per-person user setting, not a company one.
   - Birthdays / anniversaries and muting a persona. Scotty rules on the
     person's profile, not company features.
   - Break-glass. Tenant two.

 RETENTION: OPERATIONAL.

fields.name: reports_to
fields.description:
reports_to orders the org chart; it also sets Scotty budget precedence
 among members (A11).

fields.name: room_ids
fields.description:
room_ids: for a guest role, the ONLY rooms they see and may @ a dog in
 (A21).

fields.name: time_zone
fields.description:
time_zone is IANA; the scheduler and the budget day are tenant-local and
 DST-safe (A18).

fields.name: muster_minute
fields.description: muster_minute: tenant-local minute of the daily muster (Sarge's routine).

fields.name: escalation_chain
fields.description:
escalation_chain: roles in order, first to last. The top is who decides
 when nobody else will (DQ35); the ack window before the next is tried is
 runtime Config (DQ14: 30 min in work hours).

fields.name: offboarding_role
fields.description: offboarding_role handles a member leaving.

fields.name: dog_budgets
fields.description:
Tenant policy (A16). One DogBudget per company dog; a dog with no entry
 gets the D18 defaults.

message.name: DogBudget
message.description:
DogBudget is one company dog's two daily buckets, in integer micro-USD
 (A11). Defaults (D18): $1 day job, $1 above-and-beyond; revisable after the
 pilot. Scotty's $0.50/person/day is SeaBeam's (A24) and not tenant policy,
 so it is not here.

fields.name: reserve_micro_usd
fields.description:
reserve_micro_usd is the tenant's daily priority lane for approvals and
 Barry's safety events (A11; D18 default $2).

fields.name: all_dogs_room_id
fields.description: all_dogs_room_id is the tenant's all-dogs channel (Q12: CHAT_KIND_CREW).

fields.name: office_room_id
fields.description:
office_room_id is where unroutable inbound mail lands for a person
 (crew-email decision: no match is never a guess).

types.name: PullCrewCursorRequest
PullCrewCursorResponse

message.name: CrewCursor
message.description:
CrewCursor is one row per logical instance: scottyagent.AgentCursor
 generalized. Queued = done_through_seq < seq < next_seq.
 RETENTION: follows CHAT (runtime bookkeeping).

fields.name: instance_key
fields.description:
instance_key is the KEY and the only criterion (scottyagent-record-shapes
 D2: a second criterion loses the point read).

fields.name: next_seq
fields.description: next_seq is the seq the next enqueued event will take.

fields.name: done_through_seq
fields.description:
done_through_seq is the highest seq acknowledged by `done`. It is written
 AFTER the step checkpoints, never with them (A1). Under A29 acks are per
 thread (ThreadMapEntry.done_through_seq) and this is their LOW-WATER MARK
 over live threads (lowest un-acked seq minus one), used only by restart
 recovery.

fields.name: parked_until_ms
fields.description:
parked_until_ms is set when the budget parks the queue (A11): events keep
 queueing, nothing is re-delivered, no run starts before this time
 (tenant-local midnight), and catch-up is one compacted run.

fields.name: fence_epoch
fields.description:
fence_epoch / fence_counter: the last run lease's token (A2). Stratum is
 the guard (high-water mark per lock name, ask S7); this copy is for
 recovery and inspection.

types.name: PullCrewEventRequest
PullCrewEventResponse

message.name: CrewEvent
message.description:
CrewEvent is ONE queued event for ONE logical dog instance. The runtime
 writes it before it acks the source, so an event is durable here or still
 on the source topic, never only in process memory (§2.3, A1). A redelivered
 source is recognised by source_key and not given a second seq.

 RETENTION: CHAT (90 days working set, archived 1 year) — it carries text.

fields.name: instance_key
fields.description:
instance_key is the logical instance: "<dog>" for a TENANT persona (the
 tenant is `namespace`), "<dog>/<person>" for Scotty.

fields.name: seq
fields.description:
seq is strictly increasing per instance_key, no gaps once assigned. The
 single writer is the dog's pod under its run lease (A2).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_ROOM_MESSAGE
enum_values.description:
A room message or DM addressed to this dog (a messaging delivery whose
 recipient is the dog's principal; Q8).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_RECORD_CHANGE
enum_values.description: A row of a subscribed record type was written.

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_SCHEDULE_TICK
enum_values.description: A Scheduler wake-up fired (§5; ask S1).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_CREW_COMMAND
enum_values.description: A CrewCommand from another dog, or the reply to one of this dog's (A4).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_PROPOSAL_DECISION
enum_values.description: A decision on a scotty.Ticket this dog filed (A10).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_EMAIL
enum_values.description:
Inbound mail routed to this dog by the tenant's mailbox (D4, D16;
 decisions/crew-email-2026-09-29.md).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_WAIT_DEADLINE
enum_values.description: A Wait's deadline passed with no match (A3).

enum_values.name: EVENT_SOURCE_PIGEON
enum_values.description:
A FROM_PIGEON / FROM_COOP message on coop.PigeonMessage for a run this
 instance started (A30).

fields.name: source_key
fields.description:
source_key identifies the source event: a delivery_id, "<record type>/
 <key>/<store_epoch>", a scheduler fire id, a decision id, a mail id.

fields.name: actor
fields.description: actor is the principal that caused the event. Empty for a schedule tick.

fields.name: actor_is_member
fields.description:
actor_is_member is resolved at enqueue against the tenant's memberships.
 A fact for the disclosure policy (A32); it does not gate the queue.

fields.name: refs
fields.description: refs are the job / room / record the event references.

fields.name: record_type
fields.description: record_type is the proto full name for REF_KIND_RECORD, e.g. "work.Permit".

fields.name: text
fields.description:
text is UNTRUSTED (A9).
 TODO(CP4): for a person<->Scotty conversation this stays EMPTY — those
 conversations are never logged (Jody, 2026-09-29); Scotty reads the text
 from the person's own private chat rows at run time.

fields.name: is_direct
fields.description: is_direct: a DM rather than a room message.

fields.name: addressed
fields.description:
addressed: the dog was @-mentioned or DM'd, so the message earns a reply.
 False = woken by a wake word: act silently and log (A5, A8).

message.name: RecordChange
message.description: RecordChange carries a written row as record_type + key + proto3 JSON (Q6).

fields.name: wakeup_id
fields.description: wakeup_id is the Scheduler's id for the registration that fired.

fields.name: tag
fields.description:
tag is the registration's name, keyed (dog, tenant, name) (A18): "muster",
 "wait:<wait_id>", "proposal-expiry:<ticket_id>", "permit-expiry:<id>".

message.name: ProposalDecided
message.description: ProposalDecided points at the scotty.Ticket and its decision (A10).

message.name: EmailMessage
message.description:
EmailMessage is one inbound mail the tenant's mailbox routed to this dog
 (decisions/crew-email-2026-09-29.md). UNTRUSTED (A9). The company has ONE
 address; the dog was chosen by the thread token, a plus-address hint or the
 classifier, never by a per-dog address.
 TODO(FD-8): per-dog email is open (the crew-email decision); nothing here
 names a dog's own address.

fields.name: mail_thread_token
fields.description:
mail_thread_token is the +t.<thread> token the reply came back on; empty
 for genuinely new mail.

fields.name: auto_submitted
fields.description:
auto_submitted: the mail declared itself automated (Auto-Submitted other
 than "no", Precedence bulk/junk/list, or our own agent header). The
 runtime never replies to such a mail (loop protection).

message.name: CrewCommand
message.description:
CrewCommand is a typed request from one dog to the dog that owns a record
 type (A4): "change your record this way". Sent in the open room; the owner
 fulfils or declines on its own record. No field-level rights machinery.

fields.name: record_type
fields.description: record_type + record_key: the target, e.g. "beagle.JobPermits" + job id.

fields.name: read_version
fields.description: read_version is the version the sender read (A4 optimistic versions).

fields.name: verb
fields.description: verb is one of the owning dog's command verbs ("add_permit").

fields.name: args_json
fields.description:
args_json: JSON because the verbs are per owner and a oneof over every
 dog's verbs would make this file import the crew (Q6's reasoning).

message.name: CrewCommandReply
message.description: CrewCommandReply is the owner's answer, in the same thread.

fields.name: new_version
fields.description: new_version of the owner's record after a fulfilment.

message.name: ConversationMove
message.description:
ConversationMove is the typed "moving this to …" (A6). Rendered as that
 line; the chat's CHAT_EVENT_KIND_MOVED_OUT event still records the move.

message.name: PigeonEvent
message.description:
PigeonEvent is one coop.PigeonMessage for a run this instance started
 (A30). The thread is CrewEvent.thread_id: the pigeon thread, an ordinary
 ThreadMapEntry. body is DATA (A9). A FROM_COOP PIGEON_GONE or ENDED closes
 any wait_for on the thread.

fields.name: body
fields.description: body is set for FROM_PIGEON.

message.name: FromPigeon
message.description: FromPigeon is the body of a FROM_PIGEON message (pigeon -> dog).

enum_values.name: RUN_MODE_MIXED
enum_values.description: MIXED: script with model takeover at one or more steps (§1.7 drift).

fields.name: note
fields.description: note is one line for the logbook ("county list loaded", "draft saved").

fields.name: question
fields.description: question: the pigeon needs a choice the request did not make.

message.name: Question
message.description:
Question: the page offers a choice the request does not decide (e.g. two
 county matches). The pigeon never guesses a field the request names. Script
 mode asks too (PG7).

fields.name: field
fields.description: field is the request field it concerns.

fields.name: prompt
fields.description: prompt is scrubbed (§1.5).

fields.name: snapshot
fields.description: snapshot is the page as the pigeon saw it.

message.name: EvidenceRef
message.description:
EvidenceRef points at one blob the pigeon captured (blobstore, tenant
 namespace). Declared here and imported by crew, beagle and tally.

fields.name: source_url
fields.description: source_url is scrubbed of query secrets (§1.5 S5).

fields.name: answer_by_ms
fields.description:
answer_by_ms: after this the run ends RESULT_STATUS_NEEDS_ANSWER (PG7:
 5 min after asking by default).

fields.name: result
fields.description: result is terminal; the pigeon then waits for discard or deadline.

enum_values.name: RUN_MODE_MIXED
enum_values.description: MIXED: script with model takeover at one or more steps (§1.7 drift).

enum_values.name: RESULT_STATUS_NEEDS_ANSWER
enum_values.description: NEEDS_ANSWER: a Question went unanswered by answer_by_ms.

fields.name: draft_id
fields.description:
draft_id is the portal's suspended-ticket id: the prepared ticket lives in
 Sonar's state account as a draft until a person submits it.

fields.name: entered
fields.description:
entered: field -> value as the portal shows it after entry (read back
 from the review page), for the §1.6 compare.

fields.name: review_page
fields.description: review_page: screenshot + HTML of the final review step.

fields.name: status
fields.description: status is the portal's word, verbatim.

fields.name: fields
fields.description: fields as filed, for the compare.

fields.name: evidence
fields.description:
evidence: every page/screenshot/download the result relies on (blobstore,
 tenant namespace). The dog copies refs onto its own record; never the bytes.

fields.name: failure
fields.description: failure is set iff status != OK.

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_UNRECOGNIZED_PAGE
enum_values.description: UNRECOGNIZED_PAGE: script mode, and model mode is not allowed for the kind.

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_LEASE_UNAVAILABLE
enum_values.description: LEASE_UNAVAILABLE: coop FAILED_PRECONDITION until the lease store exists.

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_DOMAIN_BLOCKED
enum_values.description: DOMAIN_BLOCKED: pigeonproxy refused a CONNECT.

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_PORTAL_REJECTED
enum_values.description: PORTAL_REJECTED: the portal's validation message, quoted in detail.

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_COMMIT_CONTROL_BLOCKED
enum_values.description: COMMIT_CONTROL_BLOCKED: the path required actuating a commit control.

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_READBACK_MISMATCH
enum_values.description: READBACK_MISMATCH: the §1.6 compare failed.

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_SCRUB_FAILED
enum_values.description: SCRUB_FAILED: a snapshot could not be scrubbed and was withheld (§1.5 S7).

enum_values.name: FAILURE_CODE_INVALID_TASK
enum_values.description: INVALID_TASK: the body failed the kind's schema.

fields.name: detail
fields.description: detail is scrubbed (§1.5).

fields.name: trace
fields.description: trace: scrubbed step snapshots.

fields.name: recorded_path
fields.description:
recorded_path: set when any step ran in model mode and the run succeeded
 (§1.7). A blob of RecordedStep rows; the promotion input.

fields.name: error_code
fields.description:
error_code / error_detail are set for FROM_COOP, e.g. "PIGEON_GONE" /
 "discarded".

fields.name: thread_id
fields.description: thread_id of the message this event carries or was caused by (A6).

fields.name: causation_id
fields.description:
causation_id + hop_count (A7): copied from the message that caused this
 one with the hop incremented; a human message starts a new chain at 0.
 The model is warned past the soft threshold and the chain is parked at the
 hard ceiling (runtime Config; Jody: soft 10, hard 50).

fields.name: wait_id
fields.description: wait_id is set when this event closes a Wait (A3).

fields.name: actor_name
fields.description:
The A32 envelope. 25 is the pigeon payload arm.
 actor_name is the actor's crew or person name, rendered "name@tenant".

fields.name: actor_tenant
fields.description: actor_tenant is from the actor's SPIFFE tenant, never the body.

fields.name: orgs_present
fields.description: orgs_present are the tenants in the room, plus the addressed org.

types.name: PullDocFileMetadataRequest
PullDocFileMetadataResponse

message.name: DocFileMetadata
message.description:
DocFileMetadata is the customer-facing view: owner, namespace, and the
 folder/path structure the customer sees — independent of how the bytes
 are actually stored. Fast lookup by owner/namespace/path.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
store_namespace: MANDATORY. Exact-match isolation — a caller only ever
 sees rows in their own namespace. Also (spec.query_field) = {op:
 QUERY_OP_EQ}: the s2s record_read plane (unlike c2s reads) does not
 auto-scope by namespace, so this is what lets a record_read caller
 actually filter by it — see
 decisions/record-read-mechanism-not-yet-built-2026-09-01.md point 1.
 Without this, DocFileMetadataFilter would carry only the record key
 (file_id), and a namespace-scoped list against the reader would have to
 filter every row in the fleet client-side instead of at the query.

fields.name: owner_principal
fields.description:
owner_principal: who owns this file. (spec.store_principal), NOT
 (spec.principal) — the latter is for a REQUEST field the wrapper stamps
 from the caller's subject on the way IN; this is a RECORD field naming
 the row's owning principal for egress filtering (every c2s read of this
 record type is filtered down to rows the caller owns). Found the
 distinction by hitting stratum's real generation error: "RecordQuery
 ...GetDocFileMetadataSample cannot be generated for a c2s surface
 because its response field 'items' carries (spec.record) rows declaring
 no owner the wrapper can filter on" — (spec.principal) doesn't count as
 that, only (spec.store_principal) does. CreateIngestRequest.owner_principal
 below is a genuine request field, so it correctly keeps (spec.principal).

fields.name: customer_path
fields.description:
customer_path is the folder/file path as the customer sees it (the
 Box Drive tree, once that milestone lands) — independent of
 content_hash, which only identifies the bytes.

fields.name: content_hash
fields.description:
content_hash joins to DocHashIndex.content_hash. Not declared as a
 foreign-key type here — tacplus's record plane has no cross-record FK
 annotation as of this writing; the join is application-level.

fields.name: stage
fields.description: Ingest pipeline stage this row has reached. See IngestStage below.

fields.name: blob_id
fields.description:
blob_id is the platform blob store's id for this document's bytes,
 `documents/<namespace>/<content_hash>` — the same value DocHashIndex.blob_id
 carries for this row's content_hash. It is what makes a document a CONSUMER
 POINTER at a blob rather than a thing that owns bytes (blob store v3 R5: "a
 consumer's record points at a hash and moves its own pointer"), and it is
 the one field CreateDocFileLink below needs in order to call
 blobstore.CreateLink.

 It comes STRAIGHT FROM blobstore's CreateUploadResponse.blob_id, copied onto
 this row by the same CreateIngest handler that writes the DocHashIndex row
 from the same response (services/docmanager/src/service.rs, write_ingest) —
 NOT read back off the DocHashIndex row at this content_hash. That
 distinction is not a style choice: DocHashIndex has no `s2s_read` grant, so
 tacplus generates no reader over it, and a file_id -> blob_id join through
 it is therefore not expressible today. Copying the value at ingest is the
 only path that exists, and it is safe to copy because a blob_id is derived
 entirely from (group, namespace, content_hash) and blobs are immutable, so
 the two copies cannot drift.

 DocHashIndex stays the per-tenant content_hash -> blob_id index for dedup
 lookups; this field is the per-document pointer. Same 1024 bound
 DocHashIndex.blob_id uses, for the same value.
 See decisions/documents-volume-group-2026-09-26.md.

types.name: PullDocHashIndexRequest
PullDocHashIndexResponse

message.name: DocHashIndex
message.description:
DocHashIndex is the content-addressing index: a hash resolves to where the
 actual bytes live in the external object store. Near-infrastructure — this
 is NOT the customer-facing view of a document, which is DocFileMetadata
 below. One row per distinct content hash: identical bytes uploaded twice
 produce one row, which is the dedup the design doc calls out.

fields.name: content_hash
namespace
fields.description:
store_namespace: MANDATORY per the namespace-isolation decision. A hash
 index row is still per-tenant — two tenants uploading byte-identical
 files must not collide across the isolation boundary, even though the
 content hash alone would be identical. Dedup therefore happens WITHIN a
 namespace, not globally across tenants.

fields.name: blob_id
fields.description:
blob_id is the platform blob store's id for these bytes:
 `documents/<namespace>/<content_hash>`, the `documents` volume group
 declared on the service below. It is NOT assembled here — blobstore
 returns it from CreateUpload (blobstore.proto's CreateUploadResponse.blob_id,
 known before a byte moves because the key IS the declared content hash),
 and DocManager stores what it was given.

 This field was `object_store_location`, an opaque caller-supplied
 placeholder, until 2026-09-26. Same field number: the placeholder was
 renamed to the real value it always stood for, which is why the record
 shape did not have to change when the store was wired in.
 See decisions/documents-volume-group-2026-09-26.md.

fields.name: indexed_at_ms
fields.description:
indexed_at_ms is when this hash was first indexed. It was the retention
 clock until retention was removed (see the record option above); nothing
 measures from it today.

fields.name: ref_count
fields.description:
ref_count is a hint for reclamation (delete the object once no
 DocFileMetadata row references this hash any more), maintained by
 DocManager's own write path, not derived by generation.

fields.name: owning_service
fields.description:
owning_service names DocManager's own service identity, NOT a customer.
 A hash-index row has no single natural owner — dedup means several
 customers' DocFileMetadata rows can reference the same content_hash
 within a namespace — so there is no per-user principal to declare
 honestly here. This record type still needs SOME (spec.store_principal)
 field: stratum hosts a generic RecordQuery/RecordMap c2s surface over
 EVERY (spec.record) in the fleet regardless of that record's own
 s2s/c2s declaration (confirmed by reading tacplus's
 recordprincipal_gen.go — javaRecordPrincipalUnenforceable fails
 generation for any (spec.record) with no resolvable owner, fleet-wide,
 not just for records that opt into the query trait themselves), so this
 field exists purely to satisfy that platform-wide constraint. Declaring
 the SERVICE as owner (same pattern spec.proto documents for
 service-emitted accounting rows) is also the semantically-honest answer
 AND fails closed: no human caller's token subject will ever equal a
 service identity, so DocHashIndex's (otherwise unused — see
 decisions/docmanageragent-read-path-open-2026-09-01.md, Reveille
 reads DocFileMetadata directly via its own stratum grant, not this
 trait) c2s query surface can never actually return rows to anyone.

types.name: PullEquipmentRequest
PullEquipmentResponse

message.name: Equipment
message.description:
ios-app-layout §13: "BLE beacons ... as soon as you sit on it Scotty can pop
 up and tell you stuff like 'the oil life is at 97%'" and "'Dennis said do not
 drive this off the office lot'" — a written policy attached to a piece of
 equipment. The policy lives in scotty.PolicyVersion; attaching it to a THING
 needs a subject ref on PolicyVersion that does not exist yet (choice E,
 flagged there, not invented here).
 A stratum record since 2026-09-25, tenant-owned and not `private` — the block
 above `message Job` is the reasoning for all six.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
name is what the crew calls it: "C88", "Truck 12". unit_number is what the
 paperwork calls it.

fields.name: beacon_id
fields.description:
beacon_id is the iBeacon identity (UUID/major/minor) on the machine. Empty
 when no beacon is fitted. Matching it is the phone's job.

fields.name: hours_x10
fields.description:
Latest readings, stamped by whoever reported them (a person, a telematics
 feed later). Knowledge, re-derivable from the maintenance record.

fields.name: job_id
fields.description: job_id it is assigned to today; empty in the yard.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description: The publisher, as on Job. Never a read filter; see Job.spiffe_id.

types.name: PullForecastRequest
PullForecastResponse

message.name: Forecast
message.description:
ONE ROW PER FETCH, carrying the whole set of periods that fetch returned. Not
 one row per period: the unit of "what the forecast said" is the ISSUANCE, and
 splitting it would make "the 4pm Tuesday forecast" a reassembly job.

 A revised forecast is a NEW Forecast row with a later issued_at_ms. Nothing
 marks the old one stale and nothing deletes it. "Current forecast for this
 place" is ListForecasts ordered by issued_at_ms, take the newest.

fields.name: place_id
fields.description: place_id is an EQ (spec.query_field), for Observation.place_id's reason.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: NOT a (spec.query_field) — see the note on the record block above.

enum_values.name: FORECAST_KIND_DAILY
enum_values.description:
DAILY is NWS's /forecast: twelve-hour named periods ("Tuesday",
 "Tuesday Night").

enum_values.name: FORECAST_KIND_HOURLY
enum_values.description: HOURLY is NWS's /forecast/hourly.

fields.name: issued_at_ms
fields.description:
issued_at_ms is NWS's "updated" stamp for this issuance — the fact a later
 argument turns on. fetched_at_ms is when we pulled it.

 issued_at_ms is a RANGE (spec.query_field), emitting issued_at_ms_from /
 issued_at_ms_to. It is ListForecasts's declared window, and it is the
 criterion "what did the forecast say Tuesday" is actually made of.

fields.name: periods
fields.description:
periods in NWS's own order, earliest first. Bounded at 160: NWS's hourly
 product runs 156.

fields.name: name
fields.description: name is NWS's label, empty on hourly periods.

fields.name: probability_of_precipitation_pct
fields.description:
probability_of_precipitation_pct is -1 when NWS gave none, because 0 means
 "no chance of rain" and the two are different statements.

fields.name: short_forecast
fields.description:
short_forecast ("Chance Showers And Thunderstorms") and detailed_forecast
 (the paragraph). NWS's words, unparsed — the same reasoning the scotty
 design record §5 gives for prose over premature enums.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace: mandatory, `/system` on every row, no criterion. See message Place,
 including the WATCH-egress hazard note on its copy of this field.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description: spiffe_id: the publisher's identity, stamped by eventbus. See message Place.

types.name: PullGrantRequest
PullGrantResponse

message.name: Grant
message.description:
Grant — a right delegated from one person to another through the
 delegator's Scotty (A15): time-boxed, in force automatically inside its
 window, revocable, and dead the moment the delegator no longer holds the
 right. Checked by the service path wherever the right is checked. Written
 only on the delegator's explicit instruction (DQ28).
 RETENTION: OPERATIONAL.

fields.name: scope
fields.description:
scope narrows the grant (e.g. one job); empty = wherever the delegator
 holds the right.

fields.name: record_type
fields.description: record_type is the proto full name for REF_KIND_RECORD, e.g. "work.Permit".

fields.name: revoked_at_ms
fields.description: revoked_at_ms: 0 = not revoked.

types.name: PullHumanRequest
PullHumanResponse

message.name: Human
message.description:
Human is the durable identity record.

 The load-bearing principle, from architecture-sketch.md §4 and reaffirmed by
 the design record: "the Human record is the durable source of truth;
 OAuth/SAML claims are ephemeral proof of 'this session is really this
 person', never themselves the store of who someone is or what they're
 allowed to do."

 DELIBERATELY ABSENT — every one of these appears in the architecture sketch's
 draft and is contradicted or unsettled by the later design record:
   - org_unit_id / reports_through: §2 "Hierarchy" says these as single
     strings "do not express this", because a chain can differ per job.
   - rule_auth_level: "rule" was retired in favour of "written policy", and
     the sketch derived this field FROM org_unit_id, which is the field above.
   - personal_scotty_id: agent-instance binding is not settled as a type.
 See the schematic looper's decisions/human-hierarchy-fields-omitted-not-invented.md
 (pre-split snoopy history, not in this repo).

 Human carries NO (spec.store_principal). On tasks.Task that option filters
 every read down to the creating caller — correct for a personal task list and
 wrong here, because a Human record exists precisely to be read by people
 other than whoever typed it in. Read authorization for Human is entitlement
 work and is not done; see the schematic looper's
 decisions/scotty-read-authorization-not-wired.md (pre-split snoopy history,
 not in this repo).

 A STRATUM RECORD SINCE 2026-09-25, AND TENANT-OWNED RATHER THAN `private`.
 Human is the first of the six, so the reasoning that applies to all of them
 lives here and the other five point at it.

 Item 3 of the ruling says "private where the data is one person's". NONE of
 these six is one person's, and Human is the clearest case: the file header
 above already says it carries no (spec.store_principal) precisely because
 "a Human record exists to be read by people other than whoever typed it in".
 A private record is additionally REQUIRED to carry (spec.store_principal)
 (ValidateRecordPrivateAnnotations) and is REFUSED an s2s_subscribe, which
 would leave these rows with no declared ingest path into stratum at all —
 the gap that has `profile` unable to read its own rows today
 (decisions/profile-private-record-read-gap-2026-09-23.md). So `private` is
 not merely wrong for the data, it is unbuildable for it.

 WHAT KEEPS TENANTS APART IS `namespace`, AND IT IS BOTH HALVES OF THAT JOB.
 (spec.store_namespace) is mandatory on a record (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations)
 and drives the generated wrapper's egress filter; the EQ (spec.query_field)
 beside it is what lets a criterion be PINNED into the predicate before the
 store is asked. The query_field is the half that is easy to forget: the store
 evaluates only the criteria a record annotates, so an unannotated namespace
 field yields a filter that is present, generated and inert, leaving the
 aborting egress backstop as the only boundary. It matters MORE than it did in
 kernel: kernel state was chrooted per tenant, while (spec.record).s2s_read's
 own doctrine is that "an authorized peer service reads FLEET-WIDE, across
 every tenant's rows". So the pin is not belt-and-braces here, it IS the
 tenant boundary, and services/scotty/src/service.rs applies it on every read
 path from the caller's verified claim.

 NO OTHER (spec.query_field) ON ANY OF THE SIX, deliberately — `work`'s D4
 rule, and it holds here for a reason of scotty's own. Every filter these rpcs
 offer (a policy_id, a chain_id, a routed_to_human_id, a ticket_id, the
 participant gate, the requester predicate) is applied by the handler over the
 tenant's rows, which is exactly what it did when they came from kernel's
 fetch_all. A ticket_id pushdown onto the three appended sides looks tempting
 and is the one that would HURT: `count_chain_hops` counts the advice and
 comments of every ticket sharing a chain_id, so pinning ticket_id would turn
 one scan into one read per ticket in the chain, on the write path of every
 create. When a collection gets big enough that the tenant scan is the
 problem, the pushdown is a measured change with a number behind it, not a
 guess made here.

fields.name: human_id
fields.description:
human_id is the record key: required, non-empty.

 (spec.indexed) WAS HERE AND IS GONE WITH THE STATE COLLECTION: it is the
 statedb field-index marker, and there is no state map left to index. The
 key is an EQ criterion on HumanFilter without any annotation, because
 declaring s2s_read above folds a record's key into its filter — which is
 what GetHuman's point read is.

fields.name: email
fields.description:
email and phone are AUTHORED facts in the §1 sense — "a phone number, a
 written policy, a stated deadline — are not distilled from anything" — so a
 write to either has to leave an artifact, which requires_artifact_on_write
 above enforces.

 Not (spec.assert_email): an empty string is a legitimate value here (an
 unskilled labourer who rolls up through someone else may have no address on
 file at all), and assert_email would reject it.

fields.name: skill
fields.description:
skill is the SETTLED axis. feature-ideas.md: "CONFIRMED by Dennis
 (2026-08-11): agreed skilled labor interfaces with the system directly,
 unskilled labor rolls up through someone else." It replaces the
 Director/Foreman/Worker hierarchy the earlier drafts used.

enum_values.name: SKILL_CLASSIFICATION_SKILLED
enum_values.description: SKILLED: interfaces with the system directly.

enum_values.name: SKILL_CLASSIFICATION_UNSKILLED
enum_values.description: UNSKILLED: rolls up through whoever they are working under.

fields.name: credentials
fields.description:
credentials is plural and typed because a single `license` field was
 explicitly rejected: "Credentialing needs to support multiple types (state
 license number, industry cert, company-asserted judgment), not one field."

message.name: Credential
message.description: Credential is one credential a Human holds.

fields.name: credential_type
fields.description:
credential_type carries the RELIABILITY CLASS of the claim, which
 feature-ideas.md calls out as the reason one field would not do: a state
 licence number and a company's own judgement are "different reliability
 classes of fact and worth treating that way".

enum_values.name: CREDENTIAL_TYPE_STATE_LICENSE
enum_values.description:
A state occupational licence (electrical, plumbing) — tied to permitting
 and code inspection.

enum_values.name: CREDENTIAL_TYPE_INDUSTRY_CERT
enum_values.description:
An industry certification (AWS, NCCER) — how welding and heavy equipment
 operation are actually governed.

enum_values.name: CREDENTIAL_TYPE_COMPANY_ASSERTED
enum_values.description:
The company's own judgement about autonomy/experience, with no papers
 behind it.

fields.name: trade
fields.description:
trade is the trade the credential is in (welder, electrician, operator).
 Prose for now, deliberately: §5 "prose earns fields once the pattern is
 known", and the trade taxonomy is not settled. It must never be parsed —
 "if anything has to parse it to act on it, it should have been a field".

fields.name: issuing_body
fields.description: issuing_body is empty for COMPANY_ASSERTED, which has no issuer.

fields.name: credential_number
fields.description:
credential_number is the licence/certificate number. Empty for
 COMPANY_ASSERTED for the same reason.

fields.name: expires_at_ms
fields.description:
expires_at_ms is 0 for a credential that does not expire. Credential
 expiry tracking is listed in §9 as its own typed capability ("a ticket that
 lapses") and is NOT built here — this field is the fact, not the mechanism.

fields.name: verified_by_human_id
fields.description:
verified_by_human_id is who stood behind the claim. For COMPANY_ASSERTED it
 is the whole of the credential's authority, which is why it is a Human id
 rather than a free-text name.

fields.name: identity_links
fields.description:
identity_links are the external subjects that map ONTO this record. The
 direction is the whole point: links point at the Human, never the reverse.

message.name: IdentityLink
message.description: IdentityLink binds one external auth identity to this Human.

fields.name: subject
fields.description:
subject is the provider's own subject claim. It is opaque and must never be
 parsed for meaning.

fields.name: business_hours
fields.description:
business_hours is INFERRED KNOWLEDGE, not configuration, and it is stamped
 by the server — CreateHumanRequest has no field for it and no RPC updates
 it. Jody, 2026-08-30: "business hours are really something we can figure
 out on our own... not a setting."

 It sits on Human rather than on an org type because there is no org type:
 §2 "Hierarchy" leaves org structure unsettled and this file does not invent
 it. Per-person is also the finer of the two grains the ruling allowed, so a
 later per-org layer is a source of the PRIOR, not a move of this field.

message.name: BusinessHours
message.description:
BusinessHours is when this person is taken to be working. It is KNOWLEDGE in
 §1's sense — "what was learned" — not a setting, and nothing in the API lets
 a caller author it.

 TWO LAYERS, and `source` says which one produced the values in this message:

   PRIOR    — an industry+geography default, which is what a brand-new record
              with zero history has. It is a guess, and it is marked as one.
   OBSERVED — refined from the person's own recorded activity once there is
              enough of it to say anything.

 Only the PRIOR layer is WRITTEN today. The observed layer is shape here and
 nothing else, deliberately: the naive refinement (widen the window to cover
 every hour a read was seen at) would defeat the thing the deferral exists to
 protect — one 11pm read would make 11pm business hours. That is a question
 about what evidence of "working" means, not an implementation detail, and it
 is written up rather than guessed. See
 loopers/schematic/decisions/business-hours-inferred-not-configured.md.

 SINGLE CONCEPT. This is the same "business hours" feature-ideas.md's loop
 cadence needs ("looped more frequently Mon-Fri during business hours"). Do
 not add a second notion of it.

enum_values.name: BUSINESS_HOURS_SOURCE_PRIOR
enum_values.description: PRIOR: an industry+geography default. No activity data went into it.

enum_values.name: BUSINESS_HOURS_SOURCE_OBSERVED
enum_values.description: OBSERVED: refined from this person's own recorded activity.

fields.name: start_of_day_minutes
fields.description:
Minutes past LOCAL midnight, start < end. Nothing validates these on the
 way in because nothing writes them but the service itself; a stored row
 that does not describe a usable window is ignored on the read path in
 favour of the prior, rather than being repaired in place.

fields.name: working_days
fields.description:
The days that are working days. Repeated rather than a mask so the value
 reads as itself in a dump. An empty set is not a usable window, and is
 treated the same way an inverted start/end is — see above.

fields.name: utc_offset_minutes
fields.description:
utc_offset_minutes is the GEOGRAPHY half of the prior, in the crudest form
 that is still correct for the thing it is used for: a fixed offset, no
 DST and no tz database. A Texas crew reading a thread at 23:03 local is
 23:03 whether or not the offset moved an hour in March, and the label the
 deferral produces is a date-and-time, not an instant anyone schedules
 against. A real tz identifier is future work, noted in the decision doc.

fields.name: observed_event_count
fields.description:
observed_event_count is how much activity the OBSERVED layer was refined
 from, and is 0 while source is PRIOR. It is on the message so that "how
 confident is this" is answerable from the row rather than from a guess
 about how old it is.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT, and it is NEW with the move to
 stratum — this type never carried one, because a kernel collection was
 chrooted per tenant and needed no field to say so. A record is not: it is
 one fleet-wide store, so the tenant has to be ON THE ROW. Mandatory
 (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations), and EQ-queryable so the handler's pin
 reaches the predicate — see the block above this message for both halves.

 Its WRITE half is (spec.namespace) on CreateHumanRequest, added with it:
 stamped from the caller's claim when empty, accepted when equal, refused
 with INVALID_ARGUMENT when different, UNAUTHENTICATED when the caller
 carries no claim at all.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record's declared `owner` and the PUBLISHER — eventbus
 stamps scotty's own service identity onto it. The field NAME is
 load-bearing (eventbus's topic discovery matches the literal string
 "spiffe_id" of string type when it decides which topics get
 publisher-identity stamping), which is why it carries
 (spec.identity_spiffe_subject) exactly as ScottyActivity.spiffe_id does.

 IT IS THE SERVICE, NOT A PERSON, and so it is never a read filter. Every
 row of this type in the fleet carries the same value; narrowing a read by
 it would show a reader every row in every tenant while looking like it
 narrowed something. The value the reads narrow by is `namespace` above.

types.name: PullJobBidRequest
PullJobBidResponse

message.name: JobBid
message.description:
JobBid — the job's bid piece (A4), keyed by job id: how the job remembers
 the bid it came from. It exists only for won bids: Tally writes it once
 Sarge's crew.CrewCommandReply names the new job (TA-6..8: the Job is created
 at WON). Tally is the only writer; another dog asks her with a
 crew.CrewCommand (record_type "tally.JobBid", record_key = job_id).
 Updatable with the version guard (A4); writes take the per-record lock
 job/<job_id>/bid (A2).
 RETENTION: OPERATIONAL (7 years after job close).

fields.name: job_id
fields.description: job_id is the key: work.Job.job_id.

fields.name: version
fields.description: version is optimistic (A4).

fields.name: rfp_id
fields.description: rfp_id is the work.Rfp that was won.

fields.name: brief_id
fields.description: brief_id is the latest non-superseded BidBrief.

fields.name: won_event_id
fields.description: won_event_id is the BidEvent{WON} with who decided and why.

fields.name: our_price_cents
fields.description: our_price_cents as a person stated it (TA-4); 0 = not stated.

fields.name: terms
fields.description: terms that bind the job, copied from the brief with their cites.

message.name: BidTerm
message.description: BidTerm is one piece of a bid's fine print.

fields.name: at_ms
fields.description: at_ms is 0 when the term is not a date.

fields.name: cite_document_id
fields.description: cite_document_id + cite_where: the docmanager document and page/section.

fields.name: evidence
fields.description:
evidence: what Tally's pigeons captured for the bid (the bid packet's
 documents from bidportal.fetch_packet, post-MVP), each resolving through
 the blob door.

message.name: EvidenceRef
message.description:
EvidenceRef points at one blob the pigeon captured (blobstore, tenant
 namespace). Declared here and imported by crew, beagle and tally.

fields.name: source_url
fields.description: source_url is scrubbed of query secrets (§1.5 S5).

types.name: PullJobEquipmentRequest
PullJobEquipmentResponse

message.name: JobEquipment
message.description:
JobEquipment — the job's equipment piece (A4), keyed by job id. Which
 machine goes on the job stays a person's decision that Sarge records as an
 assignment (otto-never-pulls-iron); this is Otto's side of it: the machines'
 condition and what falls due inside the job's window (OT-5). Otto is the
 only writer; another dog asks him with a crew.CrewCommand (record_type
 "otto.JobEquipment", record_key = job_id). Updatable with the version guard
 (A4); writes take the per-record lock job/<job_id>/equipment (A2).
 RETENTION: OPERATIONAL (follows the job: 7 years after job close).
