fields.description: surface_kind is "s2s", "c2s", "c2d", or "w2s".

fields.name: transport
fields.description: transport is "grpc", "grpc_over_rest", or "unix".

fields.name: auth_model
fields.description: auth_model is the auth model enforced on this surface.

fields.name: tenant_scope
fields.description:
tenant_scope for this one surface. Non-empty only on the "s2s" surface of
 the record query plane's peer-facing half; see RpcInfo.tenant_scope for the
 values and for why the field exists at all.

types.name: ServiceInfo
types.description: ServiceInfo describes a gRPC service as a first-class object.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Service name, e.g. "PolicyService".

fields.name: description
fields.description: Human-readable description from proto comments.

fields.name: package
fields.description: Proto package this service belongs to.

fields.name: grpc_service
fields.description: Full gRPC service path, e.g. "policy.PolicyService".

fields.name: rpcs
fields.description: RPCs defined on this service.

message.name: RpcInfo
message.description: RpcInfo describes a protobuf RPC in the generated registry.

fields.name: service
fields.description:
Owning service as the project-specific ServiceName enum — a placeholder
 populated downstream (SERVICE_NAME_UNSPECIFIED in the base registry); use
 service_name (field 2) for the name tacplus emits.

fields.name: grpc_path
fields.description: Full gRPC method path, e.g. "/policy.PolicyService/GetApiCatalog".

fields.name: http_path
fields.description:
HTTP REST convention path, e.g. "/identity/IdentityService/ListProviders".
 Always present for gateway-exposed RPCs: /{package}/{Service}/{MethodName}.
 The service segment mirrors the gRPC + entitlement-grant identity so routes
 stay collision-free when a package hosts multiple services sharing a method.

fields.name: http_methods
fields.description:
HTTP methods for REST access. POST is always present for convention routes.
 Additional methods come from spec.rest_method (e.g. ["POST", "GET"]).

fields.name: http_alias_path
fields.description:
HTTP alias path from spec.rest_path, at the origin root.
 When present, creates an additional route (e.g. "/.well-known/openid-configuration").
 Same http_methods apply to the alias.

fields.name: auth_disabled
fields.description: Auth policy — inherited from service-level annotation.

fields.name: auth_actors
fields.description:
auth_actors: the (spec.rpc).auth_actors patterns this rpc declares — the
 delegate identities allowed to call it on another principal's behalf,
 matched against the token's `act` claim. Empty means no delegated call is
 admitted at all (see spec.proto's RpcAnnotation.auth_actors).

fields.name: auth_model
fields.description:
auth_model: "s2s" (service-to-service), "c2s" (client-to-service),
 or "c2d" (client-to-daemon local IPC).

fields.name: collection_mode
fields.description:
method_collection (collection-returning read) — see docs/API.md.
 collection_mode is "SNAPSHOT" | "WATCH" | "PAGE"; empty when the RPC is not
 a collection read. The remaining fields are the declared bounds.

fields.name: collection_default_page_size
fields.description:
PAGE keyset default page size when the request omits a limit (0 on
 SNAPSHOT/WATCH). The wrapper bounds an explicit limit to collection_max_items.

fields.name: rpc_verb
fields.description:
Governed RPC classification derived from the method name and streaming /
 collection shape. Empty when the method does not yet classify cleanly.

fields.name: target_namespace_field
fields.description:
Namespace authorization metadata. These fields expose the same level-or-below
 decision inputs that generated authorizers enforce at runtime.

fields.name: verb_status
fields.description: verb_status is "classified", "unclassified", or "exempt".

fields.name: folded_to_verb
fields.description: folded_to_verb is the canonical verb for a rejected leading synonym, when known.

fields.name: surfaces
fields.description:
surfaces lists every generated transport/auth surface for this RPC. This
 includes derived W2S gRPC-over-REST exposure when a C2S RPC has REST route
 metadata.

message.name: RpcSurfaceInfo
message.description: RpcSurfaceInfo describes one transport/auth surface for an RPC.

fields.name: surface_kind
fields.description: surface_kind is "s2s", "c2s", "c2d", or "w2s".

fields.name: transport
fields.description: transport is "grpc", "grpc_over_rest", or "unix".

fields.name: auth_model
fields.description: auth_model is the auth model enforced on this surface.

fields.name: tenant_scope
fields.description:
tenant_scope for this one surface. Non-empty only on the "s2s" surface of
 the record query plane's peer-facing half; see RpcInfo.tenant_scope for the
 values and for why the field exists at all.

fields.name: mcp
fields.description:
mcp is true when the rpc declares principal RPC_PRINCIPAL_MCP: it is an MCP
 tool, not a gRPC call. The tool's description is the `description` field
 (field 8) — the rpc's own doc comment — so there is no second description
 here to drift from it.

fields.name: mcp_tool_name
fields.description:
mcp_tool_name is the tool name this rpc is published under: the RPC name in
 snake_case, or the spec.rpc mcp_tool_name override when one is declared.
 Empty unless mcp is true.

fields.name: mcp_session_carrier
fields.description:
mcp_session_carrier is true for the one rpc per MCP-hosting service that
 tacplus generates rather than the author declaring: the bidirectional
 session over which MCP JSON-RPC frames reach that service's tools. Its
 exposure is the owning ServiceInfo.mcp_exposure. Mutually exclusive with
 `mcp` — the carrier is the transport, not a tool.

fields.name: tenant_scope
fields.description:
tenant_scope says whether an authorized caller of this rpc reads every
 tenant's rows or only its own. It is emitted ONLY on the S2S record query
 plane — the synthesized RecordMap service, whose rpcs carry
 (spec.record).s2s_read.auth_services. It is empty everywhere else and says
 nothing about those rpcs.

 It exists because subject_namespace_source is misleading on this one
 surface. "token.namespace" reads as "the caller's namespace is consulted
 uniformly", which here is true only conditionally:

   "caller_pinned" — consulted, as a RUNTIME branch on the CALLER's own
                     token namespace claim: a /system caller stays
                     fleet-wide, a /tenants/<t> caller reads only <t>'s
                     rows.

 "caller_pinned" is a property of WHO CALLS, not of the record, and not of
 the host. It does NOT depend on the record plane's host declaring
 option (spec.service).tenant_owned: a tenant caller reading through a
 shared host is pinned just the same, which is the entire point of keying
 the boundary on the token rather than on deployment shape. So every rpc on
 this plane carries this one value; there is no second value, because there
 is no longer an S2S record plane generated without the runtime branch.

 No record declares its own tenant scope and no request field selects one —
 a scope a caller could name would not be a tenant boundary. Two callers of
 the same rpc over the same record get different row sets under this value;
 that is what it is reporting.

fields.name: boundaries
fields.description: Boundary names owned by this service's state root.

fields.name: event_label
fields.description: event_label is the routing label for gateway-exposed event services.

fields.name: smb
fields.description:
smb marks a Service Mesh Blackbox service: its own instances talk over a
 black-box peer protocol within a single cluster (SPIFFE
 plan D7). Consumers read this from the registry, not proto text, to drive
 the per-SMB CA + member-cert wiring.

fields.name: smb_authority
fields.description:
smb_authority marks the consumer service designated to issue per-SMB CAs +
 member certs for smb services (SPIFFE plan D7). Read from the registry so an
 SMB service / its tooling can resolve which service to obtain its CA + cert
 from. tacplus does not implement the authority.

fields.name: smb_root
fields.description:
smb_root is present when smb is true and records the trust profile selected
 by spec.smb. SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED is the default; SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER requests a
 per-SMB intermediate rooted in the cluster CA.

enum_values.name: SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED
enum_values.description: SMB_ROOT_ISOLATED uses a self-signed per-SMB CA, scoped only to this SMB.

enum_values.name: SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER
enum_values.description: SMB_ROOT_CLUSTER signs the per-SMB intermediate under the cluster CA.

fields.name: host_label
fields.description: host_label is the service_s2s label for hosted vservice RPC surfaces.

fields.name: mcp
fields.description:
mcp is true when at least one of this service's rpcs declares principal
 RPC_PRINCIPAL_MCP. That fact alone is what decides whether the service gets
 the generated session-carrying MCP transport; it is never declared.

fields.name: mcp_exposure
fields.description:
mcp_exposure is the derived exposure of that generated carrier: the
 most-permissive (union) exposure of this service's MCP rpcs, so one EXTERNAL
 tool makes the carrier reachable from outside to serve it. Meaningless
 unless mcp is true.

enum_values.name: RPC_EXPOSURE_INTERNAL
enum_values.description: RPC_EXPOSURE_INTERNAL: reachable only from inside the cluster boundary.

enum_values.name: RPC_EXPOSURE_EXTERNAL
enum_values.description: RPC_EXPOSURE_EXTERNAL: reachable from outside the cluster boundary.

fields.name: tenant_owned
fields.description:
tenant_owned mirrors (spec.service).tenant_owned: true when the operator
 runs one instance of this service per tenant, identity
 spiffe://<td>/tenants/<tenant>/services/<name>. Read by the operator, the
 gateway, and the record-plane store wrapper. Default false.

fields.name: pinned_tenant
fields.description:
pinned_tenant mirrors (spec.service).pinned_tenant: non-empty when the
 operator runs exactly ONE instance of this tenant-owned service, in that
 tenant, instead of one per configured tenant. Meaningful only when
 tenant_owned is true. Read by the operator. Default empty.

fields.name: volume_groups
fields.description:
volume_groups mirrors this service's (spec.volume_group) declarations: the
 blob-store volume groups it owns. Read by the operator to render the blob
 store's group config. Group names are unique fleet-wide.

message.name: VolumeGroupInfo
message.description: VolumeGroupInfo describes one declared blob-store volume group.

fields.name: name
fields.description: Volume group identifier, unique across the fleet.

fields.name: max_blob_bytes
fields.description: Largest single blob this group accepts.

fields.name: content_types
fields.description: Allow-list of MIME types this group accepts, e.g. "application/pdf".

fields.name: tenant_quota_bytes
fields.description: Per-tenant storage quota within this group.

fields.name: source_package

fields.name: source_state_root

fields.name: source_field

fields.name: source_type_fqn

types.name: TransformationInfo
types.description:
TransformationInfo describes a derived row type produced by a pure typed
 conversion of a source message. Store-neutral: dedup and cardinality_hint are
 semantic intent, not backend DDL. It carries no lifetime: a pure typed
 conversion has none.

message.name: TransformationFieldInfo
message.description: TransformationFieldInfo describes a single field in a transformation.

DedupPolicyInfo is the registry mirror of spec.DedupPolicy — the store-neutral

fields.name: projection_source

projection source path from (spec.projection_source), e.g. "agent_id" or "tool_use.tool_name".
 Maps a projection field to a field path on the source event message.

fields.name: timeseries_order_key
fields.description:
Position in the store-neutral sort-key role from (spec.timeseries_column).order_key
 (1-indexed, 0 = not a sort key).

fields.name: timeseries_partition_key
fields.description:
True when this column is part of the store-neutral partition role from
 (spec.timeseries_column).partition_key.

fields.name: oneof
fields.description: True when this field is a member of a protobuf oneof group.

fields.name: oneof_name
fields.description: Name of the protobuf oneof group when oneof is true.

fields.name: store_key
fields.description: True when this field is the key field for a service_store message.

fields.name: quorum_write
fields.description: True when writes involving this field require quorum acknowledgement.

fields.name: constraint_infos
fields.description: Machine-readable constraints derived from proto annotations and defaults.

message.name: FieldConstraintInfo
message.description: FieldConstraintInfo describes one machine-readable validation constraint.

fields.name: rule
fields.description: rule is the source annotation or derived rule name, e.g. assert_max_size.

fields.name: target
fields.description: target identifies what the rule constrains: field, element, key, or value.

fields.name: value_kind
fields.description: value_kind is bool, int, float, string, enum, int_list, or float_list.

fields.name: operator
fields.description:
operator carries comparisons such as gt, ge, lt, le, eq, ne, in, not_in,
 or multiple_of for compound numeric annotations.

fields.name: defaulted
fields.description: defaulted is true for compiler-provided default bounds.

fields.name: unit
fields.description: unit is bytes, elements, entries, or another rule-specific unit.

fields.name: source
fields.description: source is annotation or default_bound.

fields.name: timeseries_cardinality_hint
fields.description:
Store-neutral distinct-value hint from (spec.timeseries_column).cardinality_hint.
 (Field 25, the spec's suggested number, is already taken by `oneof`.)

fields.name: data_entitlement_mode
fields.description:
data-entitlement mode for this field, from (spec.redact) or inherited from the
 message-level (spec.data_entitlement) default: DROP / PSEUDONYMIZE /
 MAY_REDACT / MAY_ANONYMIZE. UNSPECIFIED = not annotated (never transformed).
 This field's wire number is the field id reported in the sanitize
 redacted-id set and checked by the data-entitlement drift guard.

fields.name: filter_mode
fields.description:
filter_mode is the field's RecordMap filterability, from (spec.query_field).op:
 EQ  -> the generated <T>Filter carries `optional <type> <name>`;
 RANGE -> it carries `optional <type> <name>_from` + `optional <type> <name>_to`.
 UNSPECIFIED = the field carries no (spec.query_field) and is NOT filterable — a
 record type whose fields are all UNSPECIFIED gets no <T>Filter message at all.

fields.name: store_principal
fields.description:
Store-boundary role markers, so a registry consumer names a field by its
 ANNOTATION rather than by matching the field's spelling. A service whose
 principal field is not literally "recipient" is invisible to a name-matching
 heuristic, and a boundary that depends on spelling is not a boundary.
 True when this field carries (spec.store_principal).

fields.name: store_namespace
fields.description: True when this field carries (spec.store_namespace).

fields.name: record_key
fields.description: True when this field is the one named by the message's (spec.record).key.

fields.name: transformations

TransformationInfo describes a derived row type produced by a pure typed

 semantic intent, not backend DDL. It carries no lifetime: a pure typed
 conversion has none.

message.name: DedupPolicyInfo

DedupPolicyInfo is the registry mirror of spec.DedupPolicy — the store-neutral

 onto an engine's merge/dedup mechanism.

lifetime of its own. Retired 2026-08-25.

 its .dedup. Unset = append-only (no dedup) — the standalone-table default.

fields.name: data_entitlement_default
fields.description:
Message-level data-entitlement default from (spec.data_entitlement): the
 default transform applied to this message's eligible fields, overridden per
 field by (spec.redact). UNSPECIFIED = no message-level default.

 accepted value.

fields.name: match_expressions

rpcs.description:
ManageCert: bidi cert lifecycle. Any authenticated service may open a
 stream — the SecurityInterceptor validates the bearer token before
 the handler runs, and the handler matches the token's location-agnostic
 service path (token.service_path(), derived from sub_type/sub — never a
 raw SPIFFE URI claim) to the requested service_name in the first Init
 message.

services.name: TlsCertService
services.description:
TlsCertService provides automatic TLS certificate lifecycle management.
 The certificate authority service implements the server side. Services with
 auto_tls: true open a bidi stream via the generated ServiceManager.

 Flow:
   1. Service sends Init (identifies itself) + Csr (public key)
   2. Certificate authority signs cert under service's intermediate CA, returns CertDelivery
   3. At half-life, certificate authority sends Renew
   4. Service generates new keypair, sends Csr
   5. Certificate authority signs, returns CertDelivery
   6. Repeat from 3

values.description:

types.name: MintDelegateOfflineTokenRequest
types.description:
MintDelegateOfflineTokenRequest is the input for runtime delegation (C2S).
 The user's own identity is the caller's bearer token; only the delegate to
 bind the Offline Token to, and an optional narrowing scope, are carried here.

fields.name: delegate_name
fields.description:
delegate_name is the Delegate.name of the agent this OT is minted for. It
 becomes the token's act claim. Paired with delegate_namespace: the name
 alone does not identify a delegate.

fields.name: delegate_namespace
fields.description:
delegate_namespace is the Delegate.tenant_namespace completing the
 (name, namespace) key. Empty means the /system delegate of that name.

fields.name: scope
fields.description:
scope narrows the delegation below the platform default. Unset means the
 platform default; every later mint intersects fresh OPA output with this,
 so it can only ever narrow, never widen.

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: principal_scope
fields.description:
principal_scope is how wide the caller's authority over PRINCIPALS is, as a
 spec.PrincipalScope enum VALUE NAME (e.g. "PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_ANY"). It is the
 claim the generated (spec.owner_default) guard reads to tell an owner acting
 on its own row from a principal whose authority is wider than itself.
 Absent, empty, PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED and PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_SELF_ONLY all
 mean self-scoped: the guard fails closed, so a policy that stamps nothing
 leaves every caller exactly as narrow as it is today.
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity
 property, never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

MintDelegateOfflineTokenResponse returns ONLY the one-time code. The Offline
 Token itself is withheld and never transits the user's client; the delegate
 obtains it via RedeemDelegateOfflineToken.

fields.name: code
fields.description:
code is the short-lived, single-use redemption code the user hands to the
 delegate. Opaque; kernel holds the minted OT against it.

fields.name: expires_at_ms
fields.description: expires_at_ms is when the code stops being redeemable, epoch milliseconds.

types.name: MintExternalServiceTokenRequest
types.description:
MintExternalServiceTokenRequest is the input for minting a service's OWN
 identity token for an off-cluster audience (e.g. a workload identity
 federation jwt-bearer assertion). The token minter answers with
 TokenMintResponse.access_token: sub = the caller's SPIFFE ID, aud = aud,
 iss = the fleet issuer, signed ES256, a fresh jti on every call, and an exp
 no more than 600 seconds out. Callers must not cache or reuse the result.

fields.name: input_token
fields.description:
input_token is the caller's kernel-signed service token (the
 self-authenticating credential, as on MintServiceToken's exchange path).

fields.name: aud
fields.description: aud is the external audience, e.g. "https://api.anthropic.com".

fields.name: exp
fields.description:
exp is the requested expiry (Unix seconds); the minter rejects a value
 more than 600 seconds out.

types.name: MintServiceTokenRequest
types.description:
MintServiceTokenRequest is the input for service-token minting.

 Credential proof: exactly one of input_token, cloud_proof, kubernetes_token,
 or external_oidc_token authenticates the caller. The kernel groups these into a
 oneof (credential_proof) and routes on the discriminator; clients may set a
 single flat field — proto3 oneof membership is a property of the parsing
 descriptor, so a flat field at the same tag/wire type is decoded into the
 matching oneof case and remains wire-compatible.

message.name: CloudIdentityProof
message.description:
CloudIdentityProof carries a cloud-native identity assertion.
 Exactly one of presigned_request or identity_token must be set,
 determined by the cloud vendor.

fields.name: vendor
fields.description: vendor identifies the cloud provider that issued this proof.

fields.name: presigned_request
fields.description:
presigned_request is used for AWS: a signed STS GetCallerIdentity
 request that the server executes to verify the caller's IAM identity.
 The request has a short TTL to prevent replay.

message.name: PresignedHttpRequest
message.description:
PresignedHttpRequest carries a pre-signed HTTP request that the server
 executes on behalf of the caller. For AWS, this is a SigV4-signed
 STS GetCallerIdentity request.

fields.name: method
fields.description: method is the HTTP method (e.g. "POST").

fields.name: url
fields.description: url is the full request URL including query parameters.

 Keys are header names, values are header values.

fields.name: body

fields.name: identity_token
fields.description:
identity_token is used for GCP and Azure: a signed JWT or OAuth2
 token obtained from the cloud metadata service. The server validates
 it against the provider's public JWKS/OIDC endpoint.

enum_values.name: TOKEN_PURPOSE_REFRESH
enum_values.description: Refresh token — long-lived, used to obtain new access tokens.

enum_values.name: TOKEN_PURPOSE_ACCESS
enum_values.description: Access token — short-lived, carries entitlements for a specific service.

enum_values.name: TOKEN_PURPOSE_SERVICE
enum_values.description: Service token — access token scoped to a specific target service (aud).

enum_values.name: TOKEN_PURPOSE_BOOTSTRAP
enum_values.description:
Bootstrap token — very short-lived, used to bootstrap a child workload.
 Parent mints this via WorkloadMint and passes it to the child process.
 Child exchanges it with the token authority for a real access + refresh pair.

enum_values.name: TOKEN_PURPOSE_LOCALITY
enum_values.description:
Locality token — rotated by parent, shared with all children.
 Children present this on refresh to prove they can still reach their parent.

fields.name: kubernetes_token
fields.description:
kubernetes_token is a projected Kubernetes service-account JWT carrying the
 configured kernel workload audience ("kernel"; it must NOT
 be the "kmaker" audience). The kernel maps the verified
 (namespace, service account) to a Delegate. Tag 8 matches the kernel's
 credential_proof oneof so a flat field here is wire-compatible.

fields.name: external_oidc_token
fields.description:
external_oidc_token is an OIDC ID token minted natively by tenant-owned CI
 (e.g. a GitHub Actions OIDC token or a GitLab CI ID token), presented so
 that CI may act as a tenant-scoped service. The kernel verifies the token
 against the tenant's enrolled-issuer list (KernelTenantConfig) and maps the
 verified issuer plus claims to an enrolled config via a Delegate matcher.
 Tag 9 matches the kernel's credential_proof oneof so a flat field here is
 wire-compatible.

types.name: MintUserTokenRequest
types.description: MintUserTokenRequest is the input for user-token minting.

fields.name: broker_kind
fields.description:
broker_kind is the class of proof this call presents. Kernel refuses if
 the resolved Delegate's auth_broker_kinds does not contain it.

enum_values.name: AUTH_BROKER_KIND_IDP
enum_values.description:
An IdP assertion the broker has already validated (oauth). Kernel
 trusts the broker's attestation — today's behaviour, unchanged.

enum_values.name: AUTH_BROKER_KIND_DEVICE
enum_values.description:
Possession of a personal principal's device key. Kernel verifies the
 proof itself; may mint only a /people/<pid> personal token.

enum_values.name: AUTH_BROKER_KIND_EMAIL_LINK
enum_values.description: Control of an email address a tenant authorized.

enum_values.name: AUTH_BROKER_KIND_PERSONAL_LINK
enum_values.description: An admin-issued link accepted on the member's own device.

fields.name: proof_token
fields.description:
proof_token is the principal-held proof (a device- or link-signed JWT)
 that kernel verifies ITSELF. Required for every kind except IDP.

types.name: RedeemDelegateOfflineTokenRequest

 one-time code (S2S). The delegate's own identity is verified from its S2S
 bearer token, not carried here — kernel requires it to equal the withheld
 token's act claim.

message.name: X509CertRequest
message.description:
X509CertRequest represents a certificate signing request (CSR) for generating X.509 certificates.

 and issuer information needed to create a signed certificate.

message.name: PublicKey

PublicKey represents a public cryptographic key.
 The key is stored as a base64-encoded PEM block in PKIX format.
 Use NewProtoPublicKey() in Go or similar constructors in other languages to create.

fields.name: id
fields.description: Id is a unique identifier for the key (corresponds to kid in JWK)

fields.name: base64

fields.description:
Created is the Unix epoch timestamp (seconds) when the key was created
 Valid range: 1735689600 (2025-01-01) to 8045740800 (2225-01-01)

fields.name: exp
fields.description: Exp is the expiration timestamp (Unix time) for the certificate

fields.name: metadata

types.name: TraceEvent

fields.name: round
fields.description:
round is unset on the first event of a SubscribeTrace stream, which
 carries only the server-generated trace_id (see eventbus's
 WatchTraceHandler); it is set on every subsequent per-hop event.

message.name: TraceRound
message.description: TraceRound identifies a single service hop in a traced request.

fields.name: rpc
fields.description:
rpc identifies the specific service and method being traced using the
 generated AccountingMethod enum type. Exactly one field is set to the
 corresponding RPC enum value; all others default to 0.

message.name: AccountingMethod
message.description:
AccountingMethod identifies which RPC an event relates to.
 Only one field will be set — the rest default to 0 (UNSPECIFIED)
 and are not encoded by proto3, so there is no overhead.

fields.name: kind
fields.description: kind classifies where in the request lifecycle this event was emitted.

fields.name: error
fields.description:
error is set on response events when the request failed (auth rejection,
 backend unavailable, handler error, etc.). Empty on success.

types.name: TraceRequest
types.description:
TraceRequest replaces google.protobuf.Empty on the gRPC wire for RPCs with
 empty input types. This ensures every RPC can be traced, even read-only
 endpoints that take no parameters. The handler interface stays arg-free —
 TraceRequest has no user-meaningful fields.

types.name: TraceRound
types.description: TraceRound identifies a single service hop in a traced request.

enums.name: TraceEventKind
enums.description:
TraceEvent is published per-hop to the trace topic when a traced message
 passes through a service. EventBus matches these to active WatchTrace streams
 by trace_id. Ordering is determined by timestamp_ms in TraceRound.
 TraceEventKind classifies the trace event within the request lifecycle.
 External events are emitted by the gateway (edge); internal events are
 emitted by backend services.

types.name: AccountingRecord
types.description:
AccountingRecord is one completed RPC, stored in full by stratum.

 Every service in the fleet is a producer, so the s2s surface is open to all
 service identities. There is no c2s surface: accounting rows are written by
 the chassis, never by a browser client.

fields.name: accounting_id
fields.description: accounting_id is the record key: one row per accounting event.

fields.name: request_id
fields.description:
request_id is THE correlation key — the x-request-id the gateway generates
 and every hop forwards. The EQ query_field is what lets a caller ask "which
 accounting rows belong to the request that wrote this row", which is the
 whole reason this record exists rather than a log line.

fields.name: source_id
fields.description:
source_id identifies the emitting process ("{service_id}-{instance_id}"),
 copied verbatim from accounting.Event.source_id.

fields.name: timestamp_ms
fields.description: timestamp_ms is the RANGE criterion — "everything in this window".

fields.name: level
fields.description:
level is carried on the envelope so a consumer can filter without
 inspecting the payload; same reasoning applies to the stored row.

fields.name: method
fields.description: method is the RPC that was accounted for.

fields.name: code
fields.description: code is the gRPC status code the call completed with.

fields.name: duration_ms
fields.description: duration_ms is the measured call duration.

fields.name: principal_sub
fields.description:
principal_sub is the verified human principal behind the call — the claim
 the Authorizer actually checked, not a caller-written header. Caller-decided
 redaction, the same leg TaskActivity.created_by exercises: redacted by
 default, raw only for a caller holding a matching data grant.
 It is also the ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL for the record query plane's c2s half:
 (spec.store_principal) is what the generated wrapper filters a user's reads
 down to, and it must name the HUMAN, not spiffe_id below. spiffe_id is the
 emitting service, so filtering on it would narrow every user to the rows it
 emitted itself — which for a human is none. The two annotations disagree on
 purpose and this one wins, exactly as sys/spec.proto describes.

 The row filter runs BEFORE the redaction above, on the raw stored value, so
 a caller without the data grant is still matched against its own principal
 rather than against a redacted string.
 NOT a (spec.query_field), deliberately, and that is a real tension rather
 than an oversight. Making it an EQ criterion is what would carry the row
 filter into the plane's SIZE-ONLY RPCs — Get<T>Count returns a number over
 the handle's predicate and no rows, so no egress filter can narrow it — but
 ValidateDataEntitlementAnnotations refuses a field that is both
 (spec.redact) and (spec.query_field), because a filterable field defeats
 redaction. That refusal is right for the S2S half of the plane, where no
 per-caller pin applies and a peer could filter on this field freely.

 So accounting ROWS are filtered to the caller at egress and accounting
 COUNTS are not. Closing that needs a per-surface criterion (c2s-only,
 wrapper-pinned) which does not exist today; it is written up in the item 2
 report rather than bought by weakening the redaction rule.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner: the EMITTING SERVICE's identity, not the end
 user's (the human principal is principal_sub above). The field name is
 load-bearing — eventbus's topic discovery matches the LITERAL name
 "spiffe_id" of string type to decide which topics get publisher-identity
 stamping, so renaming it silently turns the stamping off.

fields.name: store_epoch_ms
fields.description:
store_epoch_ms is this row's LAST-WRITE clock, Unix milliseconds, owned and
 stamped by the generated wrapper — a producer that supplies one is refused
 (INVALID_ARGUMENT), so the value can never be caller-influenced.

 It is what makes memory/disk tiering possible: the residency clock is
 measured from this clock, and it is the predicate the memory and disk legs
 partition the query on.

 NOT timestamp_ms: that is the emitting service's business clock. Two
 different clocks; only this one is store-owned. On an append-only record
 they are written together and never diverge afterwards — which is a property
 of THIS record, not of the epoch.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT: the namespace claim of the caller
 whose RPC this row accounts for. (spec.store_namespace) is the tenant twin
 of principal_sub's (spec.store_principal) above — the same egress seam, a
 different boundary. That one answers "are these MY rows"; this one answers
 "is this MY tenant", by EXACT string equality against the caller's claim.

 MANDATORY, not opt-in: tacplus (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations) fails
 generation for any (spec.record) declaring no such field, on the reasoning
 that the record nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 The filter is generated on the READ side, which is not this record's own
 s2s publish surface above: stratum's record query plane (the (spec.trait) in
 the app proto's vservices/query.proto) exposes a c2s List/Sample/Watch over
 EVERY record in the fleet, and the namespace check is spliced into each of
 them for this type. A row reaching one of those with a namespace other than
 the caller's halts the JVM rather than failing the one call.

 Bounded like every other string field on this message. Not a
 (spec.query_field): the field exists to be the egress boundary, and making
 it a caller-supplied predicate is not what a boundary is.

fields.name: principal_sub_redacted

message.name: AccountingRecord
message.description:
AccountingRecord is one completed RPC, stored in full by stratum.

fields.name: request_id
fields.description:
request_id is THE correlation key — the x-request-id the gateway generates
 and every hop forwards. The EQ query_field is what lets a caller ask "which

 whole reason this record exists rather than a log line.

fields.name: source_id
fields.description:
source_id identifies the emitting process ("{service_id}-{instance_id}"),
 copied verbatim from accounting.Event.source_id.

fields.name: timestamp_ms
fields.description: timestamp_ms is the RANGE criterion — "everything in this window".

fields.name: level
fields.description:
level is carried on the envelope so a consumer can filter without

fields.name: method
fields.description: method is the RPC that was accounted for.

fields.name: code
fields.description: code is the gRPC status code the call completed with.

fields.name: duration_ms
fields.description: duration_ms is the measured call duration.

fields.name: principal_sub
fields.description:
principal_sub is the verified human principal behind the call — the claim

types.name: AgentSessionState
types.description:
AgentSessionState is the CURRENT state of one coding-agent session: one row
 per session, rewritten in place every time the session moves.

 It exists because the fleet had no mutable warm record and two properties of
 the warm tier are only observable on one. AgentEvent (hot) and AccountingRecord
 (warm, append-only) are both write-once by their own nature — an event and a
 completed RPC have no later state — so nothing exercised the store epoch
 REFRESHING, which is the whole reason the epoch is a last-write clock rather
 than a creation stamp.

 A session is the natural carrier for that: it is open for as long as the agent
 is working, its status and counters change while it is open, and once it has
 ended the row is a historical record that ages out of memory exactly like an
 accounting row. Both halves of the warm window apply to it, and unlike the two
 records above it moves while it is resident.

 There is no row-mutating RPC and there is not meant to be one: rows reach the
 store by EventBus publish, so an UPDATE is a republish of the same session_id.
 The generated wrapper restamps store_epoch_ms on that republish, which is what
 puts the row back inside the residency window.

fields.name: session_id
fields.description: session_id is the record key: one row per session, not one per transition.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner — the acting principal's SUBJECT SPIFFE ID,
 stamped by EventBus from the caller's verified token, exactly as on
 AgentEvent. The literal field name is load-bearing for that stamping.

fields.name: started_at_ms
fields.description:
started_at_ms is the session's business clock, fixed at the first publish and
 NOT rewritten afterwards.

 The contrast with store_epoch_ms below is the point of this record: on an
 append-only row the two clocks are written together and never diverge, so
 nothing could tell them apart. Here they diverge on every update.

fields.name: status
fields.description: status is the session's current state — the mutable field an update carries.

fields.name: tool_use_count
fields.description:
tool_use_count is how many tool invocations the session has made so far.
 Monotonic, but rewritten in place: the row holds the running total, not one
 row per increment.

fields.name: store_epoch_ms
fields.description:
store_epoch_ms is this row's LAST-WRITE clock, Unix milliseconds, owned and
 stamped by the generated wrapper — a producer that supplies one is refused
 (INVALID_ARGUMENT), so the value can never be caller-influenced.

 On this record it MOVES. Every republish of the same session_id restamps it,
 which resets the row's residency: a session that has aged out of the memory
 window and is then updated is inside the window again, because the window is
 measured from the last write and the row was just written. That is the
 property a mutable stored record without MUTABILITY_APPEND_ONLY exists to
 state, and it is why the residency clock cannot be started_at_ms.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT — the namespace claim of the principal
 whose session this row tracks, the same value AgentEvent carries for the
 events emitted inside that session. Held to EXACT equality against the
 caller's claim by the generated c2s egress filter.

 MANDATORY on every (spec.record): tacplus fails generation for one that
 declares none (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations).

 Unlike status and tool_use_count, this is NOT a field an update carries: a
 session does not change tenant. It is rewritten with the same value on every
 republish of the same session_id, which is what makes the row's tenant
 stable across the restamping described for store_epoch_ms above.

 The contrast with store_epoch_ms below is the point of this record: on an
 append-only row the two clocks are written together and never diverge, so
 nothing could tell them apart. Here they diverge on every update.

fields.name: status
fields.description: status is the session's current state — the mutable field an update carries.

fields.name: tool_use_count
fields.description:
tool_use_count is how many tool invocations the session has made so far.
 Monotonic, but rewritten in place: the row holds the running total, not one
 row per increment.

fields.name: store_epoch_ms
fields.description:
store_epoch_ms is this row's LAST-WRITE clock, Unix milliseconds, owned and
 stamped by the generated wrapper — a producer that supplies one is refused
 (INVALID_ARGUMENT), so the value can never be caller-influenced.

 On this record it MOVES. Every republish of the same session_id restamps it,
 which resets the row's residency: a session that has aged out of the memory
 window and is then updated is inside the window again, because the window is
 measured from the last write and the row was just written. That is the
 property a mutable stored record without MUTABILITY_APPEND_ONLY exists to
 state, and it is why the residency clock cannot be started_at_ms.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT — the namespace claim of the principal
 whose session this row tracks, the same value AgentEvent carries for the
 events emitted inside that session. Held to EXACT equality against the
 caller's claim by the generated c2s egress filter.

 MANDATORY on every (spec.record): tacplus fails generation for one that
 declares none (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations).

 Unlike status and tool_use_count, this is NOT a field an update carries: a
 session does not change tenant. It is rewritten with the same value on every
 republish of the same session_id, which is what makes the row's tenant
 stable across the restamping described for store_epoch_ms above.

types.name: EntitlementEvalInput
types.description:
EntitlementEvalInput is the input to the entitlements OPA policy.
 tacplus generates a typed EvalEntitlement RPC on opa from this message.

fields.name: claims
fields.description:
claims are the IDP-provided identity claims (e.g. email, groups, roles).
 Uses google.protobuf.Struct to preserve native JSON types (arrays, objects, booleans).

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the caller's project namespace (e.g. "/tenants/drpepper").
 OPA dispatches on it to run that project's policy. Empty = cluster-root policy.

types.name: EntitlementEvalResult
types.description:
EntitlementEvalResult is the output of the entitlements OPA policy.
 The policy returns a TokenEntitlements directly — kernel embeds it in the
 JWT service_entitlements claim without any further expansion.

fields.name: token_entitlements
fields.description: token_entitlements holds the per-service RPC grants returned by OPA.

message.name: TokenEntitlements
message.description:
TokenEntitlements holds compressed C2S entitlements embedded in user tokens.
 OPA returns this structure directly; the token authority embeds it in the JWT service_entitlements claim.
 grants may contain exact or wildcard grant tokens; generated helpers normalize them before authorization.

fields.name: grants
fields.description: grants is a flat list of generated grant tokens, e.g. PACKAGE_SERVICE_RPC.

fields.name: data_grants
fields.description:
data_grants is a flat list of generated data-entitlement grant tokens, e.g.
 PACKAGE_RECORD_FIELD. A data grant names what the caller may SEE RAW: a MAY_*
 redact field with a matching grant egresses raw; absent a grant the field gets
 its most-protective default (MAY_REDACT -> REDACT, MAY_ANONYMIZE -> ANONYMIZE).
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity property,
 never a request parameter.

fields.name: principal_scope
fields.description:
principal_scope is how wide the caller's authority over PRINCIPALS is, as a
 spec.PrincipalScope enum VALUE NAME (e.g. "PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_ANY"). It is the
 claim the generated (spec.owner_default) guard reads to tell an owner acting
 on its own row from a principal whose authority is wider than itself.
 Absent, empty, PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_UNSPECIFIED and PRINCIPAL_SCOPE_SELF_ONLY all
 mean self-scoped: the guard fails closed, so a policy that stamps nothing
 leaves every caller exactly as narrow as it is today.
 Stamped by OPA at token-exchange time alongside grants — an identity
 property, never a request parameter.

fields.name: azp
fields.description:
azp restricts these entitlements to tokens with a matching authorized party.
 Empty = entitlements apply regardless of azp.

fields.name: all_entitlements
fields.description:
all_entitlements grants unrestricted access to all services and RPCs.
 When true, kernel sets service_entitlements={"all":true} in the JWT,
 and gateway bypasses per-service entitlement checks entirely.
 Intended for admin users only.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the tenant namespace the policy assigns to this caller, as a
 leading-slash absolute path (e.g. "/tenants/acme"). IDP+OPA live at the
 tenant level, so this is the tenant subtree the caller's issuer/claims map
 to. When empty, kernel falls back to the cluster-root namespace.

fields.name: authorized_projects
fields.description:
authorized_projects are the project leaf names within the tenant that this
 caller may obtain an access token for (e.g. ["prod", "staging"]). The
 minted AT is always scoped to exactly one of these; a project switch
 re-mints against this list without requiring re-login. Leaf segments,
 relative to `namespace`.

fields.name: default_project
fields.description:
default_project is the project the caller is scoped to immediately after
 login, when no explicit project is requested. Must be one of
 authorized_projects. Leaf segment, relative to `namespace`.

Generated by tacplus from spec.opa_eval annotations.

rpcs.description: entry_point: data.entitlements.eval

types.name: ProxyPolicyEvalInput
types.description:
ProxyPolicyEvalInput is the input to the proxy policy OPA evaluation.
 tacplus generates a typed EvalProxyPolicy RPC on opa from this message.
 Kernel calls this before minting an external token — the caller's JWT payload
 and opaque routing metadata are the inputs the policy uses to decide.

fields.name: claims
fields.description:
claims are the caller's JWT payload claims (e.g. sub, email, groups,
 service_entitlements). Uses google.protobuf.Struct to preserve native
 JSON types (arrays, objects, booleans).

fields.name: metadata
fields.description:
metadata is the opaque string from the schematicctl listener config,
 forwarded verbatim by the proxy. The policy uses it to determine which
 upstream is being targeted (e.g. by mapping to a known URL or label)
 and whether the caller is permitted to reach it.

types.name: ProxyPolicyEvalResult
types.description:
ProxyPolicyEvalResult is the output of the proxy policy OPA evaluation.
 Kernel reads this result and either rejects the request (allow = false) or
 mints an external token incorporating the specified mutations.

fields.name: allow
fields.description:
allow indicates whether the request is permitted.
 When false, kernel rejects the ExternalTokenMint call with PERMISSION_DENIED.

fields.name: url
fields.description:
url, if non-empty, is the resolved destination URL for the upstream request.
 Kernel returns this to the proxy in ExternalTokenMintResponse so the proxy
 forwards to the correct destination. Empty means the proxy uses its own
 DEFAULT_API_ENDPOINT for the service.
constraints: must be a valid URL (scheme: URL_SCHEME_HTTP_OR_HTTPS)

fields.name: reason
fields.description:
reason explains the denial. Returned to the proxy in the denial status.
 Empty when allow = true.

fields.name: append_aud
fields.description:
append_aud contains zero or more audience values to append to the minted
 external token's aud claim. The caller's original aud is always preserved —
 OPA may only add audiences, never replace or remove the original.
 Most policies leave this empty. Set it when the upstream requires a specific
 audience value (e.g. an OIDC client ID) in addition to
 the caller's existing aud.

fields.name: extra_claims
fields.description:
extra_claims contains additional JWT claims to inject into the minted token.
 Kernel merges these into the token payload alongside the standard claims.
 Existing claims on the caller's token are never removed — only additions
 are permitted to prevent privilege escalation via claim stripping.

fields.name: auth_type
fields.description:
auth_type determines the credential format kernel returns to the proxy.
 TOKEN_TYPE_JWT (default): kernel returns a signed JWT in the response.
 Unset is treated as TOKEN_TYPE_JWT.

enum_values.name: TOKEN_TYPE_JWT
enum_values.description: TokenTypeJwt represents a JWT token

enum_values.name: TOKEN_TYPE_SSH
enum_values.description: TokenTypeSsh represents an SSH token

fields.name: token_use
fields.description:
token_use sets the token_use claim on the minted external token.
 Must be TOKEN_USE_EXTERNAL or TOKEN_USE_UNSPECIFIED (both result in
 TOKEN_USE_EXTERNAL being stamped). Kernel rejects any other value to
 ensure external tokens can never be replayed against internal services.
 Policies should set this explicitly to TOKEN_USE_EXTERNAL to document intent.

enum_values.name: TOKEN_USE_EXTERNAL
enum_values.description:
TOKEN_USE_EXTERNAL marks a token minted by the token authority for use with an external upstream service.
 Internal service auth middleware rejects any token carrying this token_use value,
 preventing a compromised proxy from replaying an externally-minted credential
 against platform-internal services.

enum_values.name: TOKEN_USE_OFFLINE
enum_values.description:
TOKEN_USE_OFFLINE is the long-lived, identity-only Offline Token (OT) held
 by the client daemon on disk. Carries no entitlements (its long TTL would
 make an embedded entitlement snapshot lie). Used as input to mint AT, and to
 self-renew via TokenMint(input=OT, no aud).

types.name: AccountingRecordFilter
AccountingRecordWatchChange

message.name: AccountingRecord
message.description:
AccountingRecord is one completed RPC, stored in full by stratum.

 Every service in the fleet is a producer, so the s2s surface is open to all
 service identities. There is no c2s surface: accounting rows are written by
 the chassis, never by a browser client.

fields.name: accounting_id
fields.description: accounting_id is the record key: one row per accounting event.

fields.name: request_id
fields.description:
request_id is THE correlation key — the x-request-id the gateway generates
 and every hop forwards. The EQ query_field is what lets a caller ask "which
 accounting rows belong to the request that wrote this row", which is the
 whole reason this record exists rather than a log line.

fields.name: source_id
fields.description:
source_id identifies the emitting process ("{service_id}-{instance_id}"),
 copied verbatim from accounting.Event.source_id.

fields.name: timestamp_ms
fields.description: timestamp_ms is the RANGE criterion — "everything in this window".

fields.name: level
fields.description:
level is carried on the envelope so a consumer can filter without
 inspecting the payload; same reasoning applies to the stored row.

fields.name: method
fields.description: method is the RPC that was accounted for.

fields.name: code
fields.description: code is the gRPC status code the call completed with.

fields.name: duration_ms
fields.description: duration_ms is the measured call duration.

fields.name: principal_sub
fields.description:
principal_sub is the verified human principal behind the call — the claim
 the Authorizer actually checked, not a caller-written header. Caller-decided
 redaction, the same leg TaskActivity.created_by exercises: redacted by
 default, raw only for a caller holding a matching data grant.
 It is also the ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL for the record query plane's c2s half:
 (spec.store_principal) is what the generated wrapper filters a user's reads
 down to, and it must name the HUMAN, not spiffe_id below. spiffe_id is the
 emitting service, so filtering on it would narrow every user to the rows it
 emitted itself — which for a human is none. The two annotations disagree on
 purpose and this one wins, exactly as sys/spec.proto describes.

 The row filter runs BEFORE the redaction above, on the raw stored value, so
 a caller without the data grant is still matched against its own principal
 rather than against a redacted string.
 NOT a (spec.query_field), deliberately, and that is a real tension rather
 than an oversight. Making it an EQ criterion is what would carry the row
 filter into the plane's SIZE-ONLY RPCs — Get<T>Count returns a number over
 the handle's predicate and no rows, so no egress filter can narrow it — but
 ValidateDataEntitlementAnnotations refuses a field that is both
 (spec.redact) and (spec.query_field), because a filterable field defeats
 redaction. That refusal is right for the S2S half of the plane, where no
 per-caller pin applies and a peer could filter on this field freely.

 So accounting ROWS are filtered to the caller at egress and accounting
 COUNTS are not. Closing that needs a per-surface criterion (c2s-only,
 wrapper-pinned) which does not exist today; it is written up in the item 2
 report rather than bought by weakening the redaction rule.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner: the EMITTING SERVICE's identity, not the end
 user's (the human principal is principal_sub above). The field name is
 load-bearing — eventbus's topic discovery matches the LITERAL name
 "spiffe_id" of string type to decide which topics get publisher-identity
 stamping, so renaming it silently turns the stamping off.

fields.name: store_epoch_ms
fields.description:
store_epoch_ms is this row's LAST-WRITE clock, Unix milliseconds, owned and
 stamped by the generated wrapper — a producer that supplies one is refused
 (INVALID_ARGUMENT), so the value can never be caller-influenced.

 It is what makes memory/disk tiering possible: the residency clock is
 measured from this clock, and it is the predicate the memory and disk legs
 partition the query on.

 NOT timestamp_ms: that is the emitting service's business clock. Two
 different clocks; only this one is store-owned. On an append-only record
 they are written together and never diverge afterwards — which is a property
 of THIS record, not of the epoch.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT: the namespace claim of the caller
 whose RPC this row accounts for. (spec.store_namespace) is the tenant twin
 of principal_sub's (spec.store_principal) above — the same egress seam, a
 different boundary. That one answers "are these MY rows"; this one answers
 "is this MY tenant", by EXACT string equality against the caller's claim.

 MANDATORY, not opt-in: tacplus (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations) fails
 generation for any (spec.record) declaring no such field, on the reasoning
 that the record nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 The filter is generated on the READ side, which is not this record's own
 s2s publish surface above: stratum's record query plane (the (spec.trait) in
 the app proto's vservices/query.proto) exposes a c2s List/Sample/Watch over
 EVERY record in the fleet, and the namespace check is spliced into each of
 them for this type. A row reaching one of those with a namespace other than
 the caller's halts the JVM rather than failing the one call.

 Bounded like every other string field on this message. Not a
 (spec.query_field): the field exists to be the egress boundary, and making
 it a caller-supplied predicate is not what a boundary is.

fields.name: principal_sub_redacted

message.name: AgentCursor
message.description:
AgentCursor is one row per user: everything a cycle needs to know about what
 the previous cycle did.

 departure was deliberate and written up (workers/big8-p1-scotty-agent-
 questions.md §1); the ruling in decisions/kernel-no-durability-user-data-to-
 stratum-2026-09-25.md reverses it, on the ground that kernel holds no durable
 user data. Item 3 of that ruling allows "a cursor may stay if it is
 rebuildable; the owning looper decides and says why". THIS CURSOR IS NOT
 ALLOWED TO STAY, and the field that decides it is last_fencing_token below: a
 stale-write reject that does not survive a restart is not a stale-write
 reject. decisions/scottyagent-record-shapes-2026-09-25.md D1.

 WHAT THE MOVE COSTS, said here and not only in the decision record, because
 the three reasons the row was kernel state were real and only one of them has
 gone away:

   - VISIBILITY. The design record requires a write to be "visible to the very
     next cycle even if it runs moments later on a different instance". A
     record reaches stratum through an EventBus publish and an ASYNCHRONOUS
     ingest, so it is not. The per-user kernel.FencedLock still serializes the
     read-modify-write; what it can no longer do is make the previous cycle's
     write readable. This is a real weakening and it is D3 of the decision
     record — read it before changing anything in `cycle_under_lock`.
   - THE READ PATH. GONE. `(spec.record_read)` at the top of this file plus
     the s2s_read grant below generate `sm.agent_cursor_record_reader()`; the
     shared `query` trait this comment used to describe is no longer how a
     service reads its own rows.
   - THE NAMESPACE STAMP. GONE, and the old comment was wrong about the
     mechanism rather than only out of date. eventbus's PublishHandler is
     ACCEPT-or-stamp-or-refuse: a row that arrives with (spec.store_namespace)
     ALREADY SET keeps that value, and only an unset one is stamped from the
     publisher (decisions/namespace-fix-corrected-2026-09-02.md). So this
     service writes the DELIVERY's tenant onto the row exactly as it did into
     kernel state, and the row lands in the user's namespace, not in
     `/system`. See the hazard note on `namespace` below.

 AgentCycle below is the other record and is unchanged: append-shaped, never
 read back by this service, and what the design record's user-facing "Bird's
 Eye View" reads through the generated c2s record query plane.

fields.name: user
fields.description:
user is the principal this cursor belongs to, the RECORD KEY, and the
 ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL.

 For a message-triggered cycle it is messaging.Message.recipient — the
 ADDRESSEE, not the sender: the loop that wakes is the recipient's agent.

 (spec.store_principal) is the same annotation AgentCycle.user carries and
 it does the same job here: the generated egress filter on ListMyAgentState
 drops any row whose `user` is not the caller's own subject, on top of the
 (spec.principal) stamp that already bound the request. Belt and braces by
 construction rather than by a hand-written check, and it is what stands in
 for `private` — see the record block above.

 NO (spec.query_field). It would be redundant with the key, which already
 produces the `user` criterion on AgentCursorFilter, and a second criterion
 is exactly what takes stratum's by-key point read away (pointRead fires
 only when the key criterion is the ONLY one set).

fields.name: cycles_completed
fields.description:
cycles_completed counts the loop cycles that have finished for this user.
 Monotonic, and the source of AgentCycle.cycle below.

fields.name: last_fencing_token
fields.description:
last_fencing_token is THE FENCE, and it is what makes the lock a fencing
 lock rather than a mutex.

 strictly increasing over every grant of every key, never reused. A resource
 owner stores the highest token it has seen and REJECTS a write carrying a
 lower one — that, not the lock, is what makes a paused or partitioned stale
 holder safe. This field is that stored highest-seen value, and this service
 is the resource owner doing the comparing (see service.rs `write_cursor`).

 wake up and overwrite the cursor a newer holder had already advanced. The
 lock alone narrows that window; it does not close it.

fields.name: last_cycle_at_ms
fields.description: last_cycle_at_ms is when the last completed cycle finished.

fields.name: last_instance_id
fields.description:

 cycles for one user legitimately run on different instances and "which pod
 was that" is otherwise unanswerable after the fact — NOT because anything
 routes on it. Nothing reads this field to make a decision.

fields.name: last_wake
fields.description: last_wake is the last event that woke a cycle for this user.

message.name: WakeEvent
message.description:

 aggregated, not just the first, so "why did you wake" has a complete answer
 even when several arrived at once.

fields.name: reason
fields.description: reason is the trigger kind.

 instance's consumer group took it.

 messaging.Message's delivery_id — the record key of the one delivery this

message.name: AgentCycle
message.description:
AgentCycle is one completed loop cycle: what woke it, when, on which
 instance, under which fencing token.

 argument exists to prevent.

 is a new row and no cycle ever rewrites another.

 AgentCycleBus with topic ref scottyagent.AgentCycleBus.stream. Do NOT
 hand-write that wrapper.

fields.name: cycle_id
fields.description: cycle_id is the record key: "<user>/<cycle>".

fields.name: user
fields.description:
user is whose agent ran, and the ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL.

 (spec.store_principal) is what holds a caller's reads of this record to

 RPCs, which return a number over the handle's predicate and no rows for an
 egress filter to narrow.

fields.name: cycle
fields.description: cycle is this user's monotonic cycle number, the second half of cycle_id.

fields.name: fencing_token
fields.description:
fencing_token is the kernel.FencedLock token this cycle ran under. Carried
 onto the row so the history itself shows the fence: cycles for one user
 must appear in strictly increasing token order, and a row that does not is
 visible evidence of a stale holder that got through.

fields.name: woke_for
fields.description:
woke_for is EVERY event this cycle aggregated, in the order they were
 observed — not just the one that started it. That is the aggregation the
 design record asks for, made legible: "multiple events can land within one
 loop cycle; they are aggregated and processed together".

 Bounded at 256 to match Config.max_events_per_cycle's ceiling.

 Bird's Eye View asks.

fields.description: finished_at_ms is when it ended, before the release.

fields.name: started_at_ms
fields.description:

 the lock was granted. It is what retention measures age from, and the RANGE

fields.name: finished_at_ms

fields.name: instance_id

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT. MANDATORY on a (spec.record):

 record declaring no such field, on the reasoning that the record nobody
 remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

fields.name: store_epoch_ms
fields.description:
store_epoch_ms is this row's LAST-WRITE clock, Unix milliseconds, owned and

types.name: AgentSessionStateFilter
AgentSessionStateWatchChange

message.name: AgentSessionState
message.description:
AgentSessionState is the CURRENT state of one coding-agent session: one row
 per session, rewritten in place every time the session moves.

 It exists because the fleet had no mutable warm record and two properties of
 the warm tier are only observable on one. AgentEvent (hot) and AccountingRecord
 (warm, append-only) are both write-once by their own nature — an event and a
 completed RPC have no later state — so nothing exercised the store epoch
 REFRESHING, which is the whole reason the epoch is a last-write clock rather
 than a creation stamp.

 A session is the natural carrier for that: it is open for as long as the agent
 is working, its status and counters change while it is open, and once it has
 ended the row is a historical record that ages out of memory exactly like an
 accounting row. Both halves of the warm window apply to it, and unlike the two
 records above it moves while it is resident.

 There is no row-mutating RPC and there is not meant to be one: rows reach the
 store by EventBus publish, so an UPDATE is a republish of the same session_id.
 The generated wrapper restamps store_epoch_ms on that republish, which is what
 puts the row back inside the residency window.

fields.name: session_id
fields.description: session_id is the record key: one row per session, not one per transition.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner — the acting principal's SUBJECT SPIFFE ID,
 stamped by EventBus from the caller's verified token, exactly as on
 AgentEvent. The literal field name is load-bearing for that stamping.

fields.name: started_at_ms
fields.description:
started_at_ms is the session's business clock, fixed at the first publish and
 NOT rewritten afterwards.

 The contrast with store_epoch_ms below is the point of this record: on an
 append-only row the two clocks are written together and never diverge, so
 nothing could tell them apart. Here they diverge on every update.

fields.name: status
fields.description: status is the session's current state — the mutable field an update carries.

fields.name: tool_use_count
fields.description:
tool_use_count is how many tool invocations the session has made so far.
 Monotonic, but rewritten in place: the row holds the running total, not one
 row per increment.

fields.name: store_epoch_ms
fields.description:
store_epoch_ms is this row's LAST-WRITE clock, Unix milliseconds, owned and
 stamped by the generated wrapper — a producer that supplies one is refused
 (INVALID_ARGUMENT), so the value can never be caller-influenced.

 On this record it MOVES. Every republish of the same session_id restamps it,
 which resets the row's residency: a session that has aged out of the memory
 window and is then updated is inside the window again, because the window is
 measured from the last write and the row was just written. That is the
 property a mutable stored record without MUTABILITY_APPEND_ONLY exists to
 state, and it is why the residency clock cannot be started_at_ms.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT — the namespace claim of the principal
 whose session this row tracks, the same value AgentEvent carries for the
 events emitted inside that session. Held to EXACT equality against the
 caller's claim by the generated c2s egress filter.

 MANDATORY on every (spec.record): tacplus fails generation for one that
 declares none (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations).

 Unlike status and tool_use_count, this is NOT a field an update carries: a
 session does not change tenant. It is rewritten with the same value on every
 republish of the same session_id, which is what makes the row's tenant
 stable across the restamping described for store_epoch_ms above.

types.name: AlertFilter
AlertWatchChange

message.name: Alert
message.description:
NWS issues alerts against zones, and a zone covers many places. Storing an
 Alert per place would store the same hurricane watch once per job site in
 Harris County. So the row is keyed by NWS's own alert id and carries the zones
 it names; "alerts for this place" is a read that resolves the place's zones
 first (ListAlerts takes either form). Choice E.

 Write-once like the rest: an alert NWS UPDATEs or CANCELs arrives as a NEW
 alert row whose references name the one it supersedes. Nothing is edited in
 place, which is also why there is no "active" boolean — active is a function
 of (effective, expires, superseded) AT THE MOMENT YOU ASK, not a stored flag
 some poller has to remember to clear.

fields.name: zone_ids
fields.description:
zone_ids are the NWS zones this alert names — forecast zones, county zones,
 or both. Order is NWS's.

 A NOTE ON THE REPEATED-STRING BOUND, the same one work.Job carries:
 (spec.assert_max_size) does DOUBLE DUTY on a repeated string field — tacplus
 reads it as the element byte cap AND as the element count, and there is no
 second annotation that separates them. 256 here therefore means "at most 256
 zone ids, each at most 256 bytes". A zone id is 6 bytes; 256 zones is a wide
 hurricane watch but not an unheard-of one, and this is the number to revisit
 first if a real alert is ever truncated.

fields.name: event
fields.description:
event is NWS's event name, verbatim: "Hurricane Watch", "Flash Flood
 Warning", "Heat Advisory". NOT an enum: NWS's list is long, changes, and is
 authoritative elsewhere. A rule in Reveille matches on this string, and
 matching on the bureau's own word is more honest than matching on our lossy
 re-encoding of it. Choice F.

fields.name: severity
fields.description:
ALL FOUR CARRY (spec.assert_enum_defined), AND THAT ANNOTATION REFUSES THE
 *_UNSPECIFIED ZERO VALUE. It is worth saying at the point of use because the
 consequence is a long way from the declaration: a row stored with one of
 these left at zero is written happily by the state client and then fails
 RESPONSE validation inside the generated wrapper on every read of it,
 including every WATCH frame. That is why the ingest in services/weather/
 src/nws.rs falls back to a DECLARED value for each — UNKNOWN for the first
 three, and ALERT for message_type, which is also CAP's own default for the
 field — rather than leaving an absent value at zero.

fields.name: sent_at_ms
fields.description:
sent_at_ms is a RANGE (spec.query_field), emitting sent_at_ms_from /
 sent_at_ms_to — ListAlerts's declared window and this type's ONLY store-side
 criterion beyond the key. The other four stamps are not criteria: they are
 what `active_at_ms` is COMPUTED from, and that computation needs the
 supersession set over every alert, so narrowing on one of them in the store
 would change the answer rather than speed it up.

fields.name: sender_name
fields.description: sender_name is the issuing office ("NWS Houston/Galveston TX").

fields.name: references
fields.description:
references are the alert ids this one updates, corrects or cancels. The
 superseded rows STAY. Same rule as a renewed permit in `work` and a
 corrected document in the Doc Manager: the correction is a new row that
 points at the old one. Bounded at 256 for the same double-duty reason as
 zone_ids — an alert id is up to 256 bytes, so the count cannot be lower.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace: mandatory, `/system` on every row, no criterion. See message Place,
 including the WATCH-egress hazard note on its copy of this field.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description: spiffe_id: the publisher's identity, stamped by eventbus. See message Place.

types.name: BlobFilter
BlobLinkFilter
BlobLinkStatsFilter
BlobLinkStatsWatchChange

message.name: BlobLinkStats
message.description:
BlobLinkStats is the coarse rollup of one link's resolutions (R10).

 The counters live IN MEMORY on the pod that served the request and are
 flushed here at most once a minute per token. That is the whole design: a
 `/b/` resolve must not cost a record write, and nobody needs a resolution
 count to be exact.

 `bytes_served` is honest here in a way it could not be in the v2 cloud
 design: we serve the bytes ourselves, so we count them rather than inferring
 them from a signed URL that may or may not have been followed.

 TWO PODS, TWO COUNTERS. Each pod flushes what it served, and a flush is a
 read-modify-write of this row — so the row is the SUM only as of the last
 flush either pod made. Exactness was never on offer for an in-memory counter;
 what matters is that a flush never loses another pod's contribution, which is
 why it reads before it adds.

fields.name: token_hash
fields.description:
token_hash is the key, and the same key BlobLink carries — the two rows are
 one link's two halves, split because the stats half is rewritten on a
 minute cadence and the link half is written once.

types.name: BlobLinkWatchChange

message.name: BlobLink
message.description:
BlobLink is one shareable URL, keyed by the HASH of its token (R7).

 THE RAW TOKEN APPEARS NOWHERE PERSISTENT. It is returned once, by the call
 that minted it, and this row holds only `sha256(token)`; ListLinks returns no
 tokens, and the gateway redacts `/b/*` and `/upload/*` paths from its logs.
 So a reader of the record store — or of a log, or of a backup — cannot
 resolve any link.

 REVOCATION IS IMMEDIATE, which is v3's improvement over the v2 signed-URL
 design: we serve the bytes, so `revoked_ms` is checked on every resolve
 rather than waiting for a cloud URL to expire. It is kept rather than deleted
 so an audit can still say a link existed.

fields.name: token_hash
fields.description:
token_hash is the record key: the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw token.
 A resolve hashes what arrived in the path and looks up THAT, so the lookup
 key is not a secret even though the path is.

fields.name: blob_id
fields.description: blob_id is the Blob this link resolves to.

fields.name: filename
fields.description:
filename is what `Content-Disposition` offers, and the ONLY source of it
 (R8) — never a client-supplied header, never a query parameter. Validated
 at mint: a basename, no CR/LF, quote, backslash, semicolon, control
 character or path separator.

enum_values.name: LINK_POLICY_BEARER
enum_values.description:
BEARER: whoever holds the token. The only policy today (R7); SAME_TENANT
 and FLEET_ONLY are additive later and need a caller identity on the `/b/`
 path, which BEARER deliberately does not have.

fields.name: expires_ms
fields.description:
expires_ms is 0 for a durable shared link and non-zero for the short-lived
 one the owner mints for its own use. Checked on resolve alongside
 revoked_ms; the two are indistinguishable to the caller, who gets a 404
 either way.

fields.name: revoked_ms
fields.description:
revoked_ms is when the owner revoked the link, 0 while live. The row is

types.name: BlobLinkWatchEvent

message.name: BlobLink
message.description:
BlobLink is one shareable URL, keyed by the HASH of its token (R7).

 THE RAW TOKEN APPEARS NOWHERE PERSISTENT. It is returned once, by the call
 that minted it, and this row holds only `sha256(token)`; ListLinks returns no
 tokens, and the gateway redacts `/b/*` and `/upload/*` paths from its logs.
 So a reader of the record store — or of a log, or of a backup — cannot
 resolve any link.

 REVOCATION IS IMMEDIATE, which is v3's improvement over the v2 signed-URL
 design: we serve the bytes, so `revoked_ms` is checked on every resolve
 rather than waiting for a cloud URL to expire. It is kept rather than deleted
 so an audit can still say a link existed.

fields.name: token_hash
fields.description:
token_hash is the record key: the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw token.
 A resolve hashes what arrived in the path and looks up THAT, so the lookup
 key is not a secret even though the path is.

fields.name: blob_id
fields.description: blob_id is the Blob this link resolves to.

fields.name: filename
fields.description:
filename is what `Content-Disposition` offers, and the ONLY source of it
 (R8) — never a client-supplied header, never a query parameter. Validated
 at mint: a basename, no CR/LF, quote, backslash, semicolon, control
 character or path separator.

enum_values.name: LINK_POLICY_BEARER
enum_values.description:
BEARER: whoever holds the token. The only policy today (R7); SAME_TENANT
 and FLEET_ONLY are additive later and need a caller identity on the `/b/`
 path, which BEARER deliberately does not have.

fields.name: expires_ms
fields.description:
expires_ms is 0 for a durable shared link and non-zero for the short-lived
 one the owner mints for its own use. Checked on resolve alongside
 revoked_ms; the two are indistinguishable to the caller, who gets a 404
 either way.

fields.name: revoked_ms
fields.description:
revoked_ms is when the owner revoked the link, 0 while live. The row is
 KEPT — see the type comment.

types.name: BlobWatchChange

message.name: Blob
message.description:
Blob is one promoted file: bytes that are fsynced and renamed into place on
 BOTH pods. A Blob row never points at bytes that are not on both pods (R9).

 IMMUTABLE AND CONTENT-ADDRESSED, PER TENANT (R5). Identity is
 `(group, namespace, content_hash)` and dedup is within a tenant and group
 only: two tenants holding the same bytes hold two files and each pays. A
 global key would have been a cross-tenant content oracle — ask whether a hash
 exists and learn that someone else has the document — and it contradicted
 DocHashIndex's own per-namespace rule.

 NO VERSIONING. A new version is a new blob and the consumer moves its own
 pointer. The filename is the consumer's and lives on BlobLink, not here.

fields.name: blob_id
fields.description:
blob_id is the record key and the file's path: `<group>/<ns>/<sha256-hex>`.
 Carried as one string rather than derived on read because it IS the key,
 and a key a reader has to assemble from three fields is a key two callers
 can assemble differently.

fields.name: group
fields.description:
group is the volume group this blob belongs to — the group whose rules
 admitted it. EQ-filterable because per-group quota accounting is a query
 over exactly this field plus `namespace`.

fields.name: content_hash
fields.description:
content_hash is the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the bytes, computed by this
 service AS THE UPLOAD STREAMS — native and exact. It is checked against the
 client's declared hash at end of stream and the upload fails if they
 differ (R9 step 3).

fields.name: size_bytes
fields.description: size_bytes is the byte count as counted on the wire, not as declared.

fields.name: content_type
fields.description:
content_type is what `GET /b/` serves. It survived both the group's
 allow-list and the magic-byte sniff, so it describes the stored bytes
 rather than merely what the uploader said about them.

fields.name: created_ms
fields.description:
created_ms is when the blob was promoted. RANGE-filterable: "what landed
 this week" is a question about this field, and it is what a later GC over
 consumers' pointers (R12) would scan.

fields.name: owner_principal
fields.description:
owner_principal is the OWNING SERVICE identity — docmanager, not blobstore
 — and the row's owning principal (R6). Only this identity creates or
 revokes links or deletes the blob.

 `spiffe_id` below is the record's declared owner but is the PUBLISHER,
 which is always blobstore, so it is the wrong field to filter an owner's
 reads on — the same split mailbox.MailboxEntry makes between `recipient`
 and `spiffe_id`.

fields.name: deleted
fields.description:
deleted marks the blob logically gone. The BYTES are not deleted by the
 record: the owner's Delete is what unlinks them from both pods, and this
 flag is what stops a resolve and starts the purge clock.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record's owner in the store's sense — the publisher, which
 is blobstore's own workload identity. See owner_principal.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the OWNING TENANT (R6) and the second segment of blob_id. It
 is what makes dedup per-tenant: the same bytes under two namespaces are two
 rows and two files.
