Choice C: a Permit is OWNED BY THE JOB (job_id required). A right-of-way
 permit that covers two jobs is two permits with the same number, because that
 is how the issuer sees it (each job's inspection cites its own). Equipment
 registrations and operator certifications are NOT permits: they hang off
 Equipment and scotty.Human.Credential respectively.
 A stratum record since 2026-09-25, tenant-owned and not `private` — the block
 above `message Job` is the reasoning for all six.

fields.name: expires_at_ms
fields.description: expires_at_ms 0 means "does not lapse".

fields.name: document_id
fields.description: document_id of the permit paper in the Doc Manager, when there is one.

fields.name: renews_permit_id
fields.description:
renews_permit_id: this permit is the renewal of that one. The old one is
 not edited; it stays with status LAPSED or CLOSED. Same rule as documents.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description: The publisher, as on Job. Never a read filter; see Job.spiffe_id.

types.name: SamplePlaceRequest
SamplePlaceResponse

message.name: Place
message.description:
===========================================================================
 THE FOUR RECORDS HAVE NO TENANT, AND THIS IS THE ONE PLACE THAT IS WRITTEN
 DOWN. Place is the first of them, so the reasoning lives here and the other
 three point at it.

 Every record in this fleet before this file was one of three shapes:

   - rows with an OWNING PERSON (work.WorkActivity, scotty.ScottyActivity,
     scottypersonal.ChatSession): (spec.store_principal) on the field naming
     that person, and the c2s plane pins a caller to their own rows;
   - the same, plus (spec.record).private (profile.UserProfile) — "a user's
     data and nobody else's, ever";
   - rows with no owning person but an OWNING TENANT (work.Job, scotty.Ticket,
     scottypersonal.Chat): no principal, and `namespace` IS the boundary.

 THESE FOUR ARE THE FOURTH SHAPE: rows with NO owner of any kind. A place is a
 cell in NWS's grid. An observation is what the sky did there. Neither belongs
 to a person or to a company, both are DEDUPLICATED ACROSS THE FLEET by
 construction (choice A: place_id is DERIVED from the resolved cell, so two
 tenants 400m apart write the same key), and the whole reason this service is
 9a — one instance for the whole fleet — is that a per-tenant copy would be N
 copies of one fact and N callers hammering api.weather.gov.

 SO NO (spec.store_principal) ON ANY OF THE FOUR. There is no field that could
 truthfully carry one; `weather` has never had a (spec.principal) anywhere and
 the reads take no caller into account at all.

 NOT `private` EITHER, and here it is not even close. These are PUBLIC FACTS.
 ValidateRecordPrivateAnnotations additionally requires a private record to
 carry (spec.store_principal) — which there is nothing to put in — and refuses
 s2s_subscribe on one, which would leave these rows with no declared ingest
 path into stratum at all. Item 3's "private where the data is one person's"
 does not fire for this service in either direction.

 AND `namespace` IS DECLARED, EMPTY ON EVERY ROW, AND IS NOT A QUERY
 CRITERION. That is the sentence a reviewer should push back on, so here is the
 whole of it.

   (spec.store_namespace) is MANDATORY on a record —
   ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations fails generation without it, on the
   reasoning that "the record nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one
   that leaks". So the field exists here because the platform insists a record
   name its owning tenant, and this record HAS no owning tenant.

   THE VALUE IS `/system` ON EVERY ROW, FOREVER, and it is derived rather than
   invented. Kernel mints this service's subject as
   `/system/services/weather` (SpiffeIds.build with an empty namespace is "the
   shared /system root"; a tenant-owned instance would get
   `/tenants/<t>/services/<svc>` instead), and the platform's own
   `namespace_from_spiffe` reduces that subject to the namespace `/system`. So
   `/system` IS the namespace of the identity that owns these rows, computed by
   the platform's rule — which is the most truthful thing the field can hold for
   a 9a service, and reads as what it is: the platform owns this row, no tenant
   does. `spiffe_id` below carries the full identity; this carries its
   namespace, which is exactly the relationship the two annotations describe
   everywhere else.

   THE EMPTY STRING WAS THE OTHER CANDIDATE AND IS STRICTLY WORSE. It would say
   "no tenant" just as well, but it is indistinguishable from the field nobody
   filled in — the failure ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations exists to prevent
   — and, decisively, it would make the WATCH rpcs ABORT THIS SERVICE on every
   frame. See the hazard note on the field itself.

   AND IT CARRIES NO (spec.query_field), SO NO READ PINS IT. This is where this
   file departs from `work` and `scotty`, which both added an EQ criterion and
   pin it on every read. There, the pin IS the tenant boundary: the record
   plane's S2S half reads FLEET-WIDE by declared doctrine, so without a pinned
   criterion one tenant's handler would read another's rows. Here every row in
   the type carries the same value, so a criterion on it cannot narrow
   ANYTHING — and it is not free: the record store's by-key fast path
   (RecordMapImplGenerator.pointRead) fires only when the key criterion is the
   ONLY criterion set, so pinning an always-true namespace would turn every
   point read in this service — including the poller's write-once check, once
   per row per pass over up to ten million of them — into a predicate scan. A
   criterion that narrows nothing and costs the point read is not a boundary,
   it is overhead wearing a boundary's clothes.

   WHAT IS LOST IS NOTHING THAT EXISTED. The no-(spec.principal)/-(spec.namespace)
   note on the `Weather` service block already says it out loud: "`weather` has
   NO GENERATED TENANT BOUNDARY ON ANY SURFACE. That is correct for public rows.
   The day a tenant-specific field lands on one of these rows, nothing at build
   time or runtime will catch it." That was true when these were kernel
   collections and it is true now; the storage move neither added the exposure
   nor closed it. WHAT HAS CHANGED, and it is a real narrowing, is that a
   kernel collection was chrooted per tenant and a record store is one
   fleet-wide set of rows — which for these four types is not a loss, because
   fleet-wide is what a deduplicated public fact wants and what the old code
   already asked kernel for.

 THE PUSHDOWNS ARE REAL HERE, unlike in `work`. work's D4 declared no
 (spec.query_field) beyond the tenant, on the grounds that half a read in the
 store and half in the handler is no behaviour change over a tenant's rows.
 That argument does not survive the absence of a tenant: with nothing pinned,
 "every row of the type" is up to ten million observations, and a handler-side
 filter over them is a paged gRPC walk of the whole store on every ListObservations.
 So the criteria that are DECLARED PARAMETERS of a read rpc AND actually narrow
 are pushed down — place_id and the time window on Observation and Forecast, the
 time window on Alert — and nothing else is. What stays in the handler is named
 per record below.
 ===========================================================================

fields.name: latitude
fields.description:
The point as asked for. Kept because NWS /points snaps to a ~2.5km cell and
 "what did we ask about" is worth keeping alongside "what NWS gave us".

fields.name: grid_office
fields.description:
The NWS gridpoint: office id + x/y. Forecasts are per gridpoint.
 e.g. grid_office "HGX", grid_x 65, grid_y 97.

fields.name: station_id
fields.description:
station_id is the nearest NWS observation station (e.g. "KHOU").
 Observations are per STATION, not per gridpoint — a distinction NWS makes
 and this file keeps rather than flattening.

fields.name: forecast_zone_id
fields.description:
Zones are how ALERTS arrive. A point sits in a forecast zone and a county
 zone and the two are different ids issuing different products, so both are
 kept. e.g. "TXZ213" / "TXC201".

fields.name: nws_place_name
fields.description:
A person-readable label NWS returns for the point ("Houston, TX"). For
 display only; nothing parses it (scotty design record §5).

fields.name: resolved_at_ms
fields.description: resolved_at_ms is when /points was last asked.

fields.name: superseded_by_place_id
fields.description:
superseded_by_place_id: set on the OLD row when NWS re-cut the grid under
 this point. Empty on the current row. This is the ONE field a Place gains
 after creation, and there is deliberately no rpc that sets it: the service
 writes it through the generated state client (PutPlaces), which is the
 established mechanism for a service writing its own state and needs no verb
 registry exception, because the generated state service is Synthesized by
 construction. VERIFY 3 in the design doc, confirmed.

 The caveat that comes with it, worth carrying: PutPlaces REPLACES the whole
 row (there is no compare-and-swap). Fine for a single-writer poller; not
 once a second writer exists.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is MANDATORY on a record and is `/system` ON EVERY ROW OF THIS
 TYPE — the namespace of this service's own identity, not any tenant's. Read
 the block above this message for the whole argument; the short form is that a
 Place has no owning tenant by construction, `/system` is what the platform's
 own rule reduces `/system/services/weather` to, and the field deliberately
 carries no (spec.query_field) so that no read pins a criterion that could not
 narrow anything and would cost the store's by-key fast path.

 A HAZARD THIS FIELD NOW CARRIES, AND IT IS A TACPLUS GAP RATHER THAN A DESIGN
 CHOICE. Making these types records turns on the generated WATCH egress
 backstop, which compares EVERY snapshot frame and EVERY delta against the
 CALLER'S namespace claim and calls std::process::abort() on a mismatch. The
 unary and PAGE seams apply that filter only for a c2s service or the record
 plane's own s2s wrapper, and they carry a `__ns_pinned` escape so a /system
 peer keeps a fleet-wide read; the WATCH seam
 (rust/types/servicewrapper_gen.go:1511-1517 against :1882/:1947) has NEITHER
 gate. So today:

   - every caller on this service's auth_services list is a SHARED service
     whose own namespace claim is `/system`, so `/system` on the row MATCHES
     and the three WATCH rpcs work;
   - the day a TENANT-OWNED service watches this one — which is exactly what
     `reveille` is meant to be — its claim is `/tenants/<t>` , the guard
     mismatches, AND WEATHER'S PROCESS ABORTS. Not a refused call: an abort.

 There is no value of this field that avoids that, because a fleet-shared row
 read by callers in different namespaces cannot equal all of their claims.
 The fix is in tacplus, not here: the WATCH seam needs the same gate its unary
 and PAGE siblings have. Recorded in
 decisions/weather-record-shapes-2026-09-25.md as the one thing that must land
 before `reveille` exists.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record's declared `owner` and the PUBLISHER — eventbus
 stamps weather's own service identity onto it. The field NAME is load-bearing
 (eventbus's topic discovery matches the literal string "spiffe_id" of string
 type when it decides which topics get publisher-identity stamping), which is
 why it carries (spec.identity_spiffe_subject).

 ON THIS SERVICE IT IS THE ONLY OWNERSHIP STATEMENT THERE IS, and it is the
 true one: these rows belong to the platform's weather service, which is
 exactly what a 9a service's rows are. It is never a read filter — every row
 of every one of these four types carries the same value.

types.name: SamplePolicyVersionRequest
SamplePolicyVersionResponse

message.name: PolicyVersion
message.description:
PolicyVersion is ONE version of one written policy, and it is immutable.

 §2, and the word doing the work is "written": "A written policy has a
 document, an author and a date, so policy is quotable or it isn't policy —
 which converts 'Scotty invented a company policy' from a prompt problem into
 a structural one."

 So all four properties are fields, not conventions: body (the document),
 authored_by_human_id (the author), authored_at_ms (the date) and
 effective_from_ms + version (the "at the time" axis). There is no
 UpdatePolicyVersion RPC anywhere in this file. Amending a policy means
 creating version N+1; that is what makes "what did the policy say on the day
 Dennis acted" answerable at all.

 DELIBERATELY ABSENT: any scope/binding field ("who does this bind"). §2 is
 explicit that the answer is a query over (person, context), not a field, and
 that the hierarchy which would feed it is unsettled. Inventing a scope field
 here would silently settle it. See the schematic looper's
 decisions/written-policy-scope-omitted.md (pre-split snoopy history, not in
 this repo).

 A stratum record since 2026-09-25, tenant-owned and not `private` — the block
 above `message Human` is the reasoning for all six and is not repeated.

fields.name: policy_version_id
fields.description:
policy_version_id is the record key — one row per (policy_id, version).
 (spec.indexed) went with the state collection; see Human.human_id.

fields.name: policy_id
fields.description:
policy_id is stable ACROSS versions. It is what "policy P version 3
 effective D" (§4's definition of a finding as a citation) names.

fields.name: version
fields.description:
version starts at 1 and increments. Server-assigned, so two authors cannot
 both write version 4.

fields.name: body
fields.description:
body is the document itself — the thing that makes the policy quotable. It
 is prose by nature and must never be parsed to act on.

fields.name: authored_by_human_id
fields.description:
authored_by_human_id is the ATTRIBUTION. §2's known gap turns on this
 field: "Joe overrides a policy Alicia wrote; Dennis is notified, Alicia
 isn't... authorship and override-visibility come apart, and an author
 should know that going in." Recording the author is what makes that gap
 stateable rather than invisible.

 May be empty for POLICY_WEIGHT_STATUTORY, which "isn't authored by anyone
 in the org, so it isn't in the hierarchy at all". Who a statutory policy is
 attributed to is an open product question — see the schematic looper's
 decisions/statutory-policy-authorship-open.md (pre-split snoopy history,
 not in this repo).

fields.name: effective_from_ms
fields.description:
effective_from_ms is when this version began to bind. There is no
 effective_to: a version is superseded by the next version's
 effective_from_ms, which cannot drift out of agreement with itself the way
 a separately-written end date can.

fields.name: weight
fields.description:
weight is AUTHORED, never inferred — §2, stated as a rule. It is an enum so
 an undefined weight cannot be stored at all.

enum_values.name: POLICY_WEIGHT_SOFT
enum_values.description: Soft — push back once, capture the reason, comply, notify.

enum_values.name: POLICY_WEIGHT_HEAVY
enum_values.description:
Heavy — override requires SOMEONE ELSE's entitlement; the actor cannot
 self-clear.

enum_values.name: POLICY_WEIGHT_STATUTORY
enum_values.description:
Statutory — not overridable in-system by anyone. Ships with the product as
 trade knowledge: "Dennis shouldn't have to know to write the 811 policy."

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
The row's owning TENANT, new with the move to stratum for the reason
 Human.namespace gives. Its write half is (spec.namespace) on
 CreatePolicyVersionRequest.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description: The publisher, as on Human. Never a read filter; see Human.spiffe_id.

types.name: SampleReportRequest
SampleReportResponse

message.name: Report
message.description:
Report — the dogs' formal, auditable channel to SeaBeam, and the ONLY one
 (A27). Lands on the company record; SeaBeam answers on the same record.
 TODO(Q23): SeaBeam reads a stripped projection with no message text through
 one fleet-level ops service; neither the projection nor that service exists.
 TODO(DQ31): a report from a personal (Scotty) run lands in the person's
 private record instead; that private type is not declared here.
 RETENTION: LOG (2 years).

fields.name: words
fields.description: words is the dog's own account.

fields.name: answer
fields.description: answer is SeaBeam's reply, written back on the same record.

types.name: SampleRfpRequest
SampleRfpResponse

message.name: Rfp
message.description:
A stratum record since 2026-09-25, tenant-owned and not `private` — the block
 above `message Job` is the reasoning for all six.

fields.name: job_id
fields.description: job_id once won and opened as a job.

fields.name: document_ids
fields.description: Same double-duty bound as Job.document_ids; see the note there.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description: The publisher, as on Job. Never a read filter; see Job.spiffe_id.

types.name: SampleRuleNodeRequest
SampleRuleNodeResponse
types.schema_json:
{
  "name": "SampleRuleNodeResponse",
  "package": "query",
  "fields": [
    {
      "name": "items",
      "type": "message",
      "repeated": true,
      "constraints": [
        "maximum size: 1024 elements (default)"
      ],
      "constraint_infos": [
        {
          "rule": "default_max_size",
          "target": "field",
          "value_kind": "int",

message.name: RuleNode
message.description:
RuleNode is ONE node of one person's rule tree: a group, or a rule.

 ONE UNIFIED TYPE, per the ruling, rather than a Group record and a Rule
 record. A group and a rule are ordered against each other in the same list
 and precedence runs depth-first across both, so two types would mean two
 position spaces the runtime has to interleave, and interleaving them is
 exactly the ambiguity `position` exists to remove.

 ORDER IS PRECEDENCE. "Rules are ordered inside their group; groups are
 ordered among their siblings. Earlier wins on conflict, depth-first." That is
 the deterministic tie-break the runtime needs and the lever the user already
 understands. Reordering is therefore a BEHAVIORAL CHANGE and gets the same
 treatment as a new rule — announced, silence-is-consent for self-affecting
 effects, bidirectional confirmation for DELEGATION.

 REWRITTEN IN PLACE. A record has no update RPC and is not getting one: rows
 reach the store by publish, so an UPDATE IS A REPUBLISH OF THE SAME node_id.
 (spec.record).mutability is left unset = MUTABILITY_CRUD, which is what every
 record in this repo does. MUTABILITY_APPEND_ONLY would be exactly wrong — it
 makes the generator refuse to emit any row-mutating path at all.

 NEVER HARD-DELETED. decisions/scotty-rules-and-filters-2026-09-19.md: "a
 citation always resolves to the exact rule text that was in force, even after
 the user 'deleted' it." `deleted` below is the whole mechanism.

 spec.record implies spec.event, so tacplus synthesizes the topic wrapper
 RuleNodeBus with topic ref profile.RuleNodeBus.stream. Do NOT hand-write it.

fields.name: node_id
fields.description:
node_id is the record key AND the citation token. Minted, not derived: a
 derived key would have to be derived from something that says what the rule
 IS, and a corrected rule, a superseded rule and its replacement all have to
 coexist. Short enough to say out loud in an announcement, which is what
 decisions/scotty-rules-and-filters-2026-09-19.md asks of it.

fields.name: owner_principal
fields.description:
owner_principal is whose rule this is, and the ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL. See
 Profile.owner for why this and not spiffe_id.

fields.name: kind
fields.description:
kind selects which of the fields below mean anything. EQ-filterable so the
 runtime can read rules without groups when it is evaluating rather than
 rendering.

enum_values.name: RULE_NODE_KIND_GROUP
enum_values.description:
GROUP holds other nodes and says nothing itself. It has `text` (the name
 the user gave the group) and no `effect` and no `match`.

enum_values.name: RULE_NODE_KIND_RULE
enum_values.description: RULE is one standing instruction.

fields.name: parent_id
fields.description:
parent_id is the containing GROUP's node_id. EMPTY MEANS ROOT. Groups nest,
 so a group's parent_id may name another group.

 EQ-filterable because "this group's children" is how the tree is walked,
 and because it is the first component of the order the tree is read in.

fields.name: position
fields.description:
position is a SORTABLE STRING KEY, fractional/lexicographic — not an int.
 The ruling: "a drag-to-reorder is a single-row write with no renumbering of
 siblings." Siblings sort by byte order of this value; a node dropped
 between two neighbours gets a key that sorts between theirs.

 The generation scheme is the runtime's business and not fixed here, beyond
 the one property the ordering depends on: keys must compare correctly as
 BYTES, so no scheme may produce a key that is a prefix-extension of an
 adjacent one in a way that reorders. Ties are broken by node_id wherever
 this field is ordered on, so equal positions are survivable rather than
 silently non-deterministic.

fields.name: text
fields.description:
text IS THE SOURCE OF TRUTH — "the sentence the user said or accepted". It
 is what the user sees, what Scotty cites, and what the model reads at
 decision time. On a GROUP it is the group's name.

 Everything else on this row is derived from it or is metadata about it.
 When a correction changes this sentence the handler writes a NEW node and
 sets `supersedes`, rather than overwriting, so an old citation still
 resolves to the words that were actually in force. See UpdateRule.

fields.name: match_summary
fields.description:
match_summary is the derived pre-filter summary. Absent on a GROUP and
 legitimately absent on a RULE Scotty could not summarize. See RuleMatch for
 the contract — in particular that it never decides.

 THE RULING CALLS THIS FIELD `match` AND IT CANNOT BE NAMED THAT. tacplus
 refuses the name outright — "field \"match\" ... is a blocked name (keyword
 in Rust) — rename the field and use json_name to preserve wire format"
 (verified 2026-09-20, `tacplus validate`). json_name keeps the JSON and MCP
 spelling at `match`, so the ruling's name survives everywhere a human or a
 model sees it and only the Rust/proto identifier differs.

message.name: RuleMatch
message.description:
RuleMatch is Scotty's own DERIVED structured summary of what a rule is about.
 The ruling: "match // Scotty-derived structured summary: labels, senders,
 rooms, time window", and, decisively, "`match` is Scotty's own derived
 summary, used only for cheap pre-filtering and for the 'what is being
 filtered' tap-through; it never decides."

 THE CONTRACT, stated here because every field below is meaningless without
 it and the design doc argues it at length:

   1. IT IS A NECESSARY CONDITION, NEVER A SUFFICIENT ONE. A node whose match
      fails may be skipped without reading it. A node whose match passes is
      handed to the model WITH ITS `text`, and the text decides. There is no
      path on which a rule fires because its match matched.
   2. IT MAY OVER-SELECT AND MUST NEVER UNDER-SELECT. A match wider than the
      sentence costs a few tokens. A match narrower than the sentence silently
      breaks the rule, and the user has no way to see why — they can only read
      the sentence, which still says what they think it says. Derivation is
      conservative or it is wrong.
   3. EMPTY MEANS "NO PRE-FILTER AVAILABLE", so the node is always a
      candidate. That is the correct value whenever Scotty cannot summarize a
      sentence, and it is the value a hand-written rule starts with.
   4. WITHIN a field the values OR; ACROSS fields they AND. That is the whole
      composition grammar and it is not going to grow one. No negation, no
      wildcards, no nesting, no operators — each of those is the first step
      into an expression language, and an expression language here would be a
      second, weaker statement of the rule that can disagree with the
      sentence. If a rule needs something this cannot say, the answer is an
      empty match, not a richer schema.
   5. IT IS DERIVED AND DISPOSABLE. Scotty recomputes it on any write and the
      user never edits it. Nothing validates it against `text`, because
      nothing could.

 NO (spec.query_field) ON ANYTHING IN HERE, and that is not an oversight: the
 runtime loads one user's rules — a bounded handful of rows, pinned by
 store_principal — and evaluates the match in process. Pushing these into
 store criteria would make the summary look like a query language, which is
 precisely what item 4 refuses.

fields.name: labels
fields.description:
labels the rule is about, as the tag projection spells them
 (roadmap/PLAN.md's "Tags, not hierarchy"). "just show me the urgent jobs"
 summarizes to labels ["urgent"].

fields.name: senders
fields.description:
senders are principals the rule is about — "anything from Dennis".
 Bounded like every other principal in the fleet.

fields.name: rooms
fields.description:
rooms are chat ids the rule is about — "in the Muleshoe job room". Named
 and bounded to match scottypersonal.Chat.chat_id exactly (600), because it
 holds that value and two spellings of one id is drift.

fields.name: time_window
fields.description:
time_window is when the rule is about — "after six", "on weekends". Absent
 means the rule is not time-scoped, which is not the same as a window
 covering the whole day, so this is a message with presence rather than two
 ints inlined here.

message.name: RuleTimeWindow
message.description:
RuleTimeWindow is the time half of a match summary.

 Minutes since local midnight in Preferences.timezone, the same convention and
 the same wrap rule as QuietHours: end BEFORE start wraps midnight. No zone of
 its own — one person, one timezone, on their profile.

fields.name: weekdays
fields.description:
weekdays narrows the window to particular days. EMPTY MEANS EVERY DAY, not
 "no days" — a match block that matched nothing would be a rule that can
 never fire, which is not a thing a summary should be able to say.

fields.name: effect
fields.description:
effect is what this rule does. See RuleEffect, including why it carries no
 (spec.assert_enum_defined): a GROUP has none, and the annotation cannot say
 "required on one kind only".

enum_values.name: RULE_EFFECT_FILTER
enum_values.description:
FILTER narrows what the user is shown. Self-affecting: nobody but the
 requesting user sees a different screen because of it. The first and so far
 only rule kind the product has designed end to end — see
 decisions/scotty-rules-and-filters-2026-09-19.md, "Filters are rules, not
 UI".

enum_values.name: RULE_EFFECT_BEHAVIOR
enum_values.description:
BEHAVIOR changes how Scotty acts for this user without changing what
 anyone else sees: what he volunteers, how he phrases things, when he
 interrupts. Self-affecting.

enum_values.name: RULE_EFFECT_DELEGATION
enum_values.description:
DELEGATION lets Scotty act on the user's behalf toward someone else —
 answering for them, forwarding, standing in. AFFECTS OTHERS, so it gets the
 bidirectional discussion before it is created or reordered, never
 silence-is-consent.

fields.name: created_by
fields.description: created_by is USER or SCOTTY_INFERRED. See RuleAuthor.

fields.name: expires_at_ms
fields.description:
expires_at_ms is the lifetime. 0 MEANS PERMANENT, not "expired at the
 epoch" — the two lifetimes the filters doc names are "time-expiring or
 permanent", and a permanent rule has no expiry to state. An inferred filter
 is written with now + 24h per that doc's announced default; "keep it" is a
 correction that republishes the same node with 0 here.

 EXPIRY IS DATA, NOT AN EVENT. Nothing wakes at this timestamp and nothing
 rewrites the row when it passes — "Expiry is silent". The runtime compares
 it to now at evaluation time, and so does the app's read, which is also why
 it is RANGE-filterable.

fields.name: supersedes
fields.description:
supersedes is the node_id this node replaced, if any — the chain a citation
 walks backwards. Empty on an original.

 It is what lets a text correction be a new node instead of an overwrite:
 the citation "rule n-8f2c" keeps resolving to the sentence that was
 actually in force, and the replacement says which one it grew out of.

fields.name: deleted
fields.description:
deleted is the soft-delete flag and the whole deletion mechanism. A deleted
 node is inert for evaluation, still visible in the history view, and still
 resolvable by a citation until it is purged.

 (spec.deleted_flag) — the 2026-09-20 stratum-record-lifecycle record's
 marker, which the pin now carries. It makes the generated query plane
 exclude these rows from List / Watch / Count / Sample by default, and it is
 what residency.deleted_max_age_seconds above measures the year from. Get by
 node_id still returns the row, deleted or not, until it is purged — which
 is the citation guarantee.

fields.name: created_ms
fields.description:
created_ms never moves again — not on a correction, not on a move, not on a
 delete. updated_ms is the business clock of the last write and is the
 retention timestamp_field. Both RANGE-filterable: "what rules did I set
 last spring" is the question a months-long history exists to answer.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id, store_epoch_ms, namespace: the platform triple. See the
 identically-annotated fields on UserProfile for what each one is and why it
 is spelled this way — including, for `namespace`, why it is NOT a tenant's
 and why tenant_scope below is the field that answers "which company".

fields.name: tenant_scope
fields.description:
tenant_scope is WHERE THIS RULE APPLIES, and it is the whole per-company
 half of Jody's 2026-09-20 amendment (see the service-class note at the top
 of this file). It sits down here, after the platform triple rather than
 beside `effect` where it belongs by meaning, only so the tags stay in
 order: it was added after this message already had 17 of them.

   EMPTY = EVERYWHERE. The rule is the person's own and follows them into
   every tenant they belong to. This is the default and the common case:
   "never interrupt me before 7am" is not a company's business.

   A TENANT NAMESPACE = ONLY THERE. "File anything from Dennis under the
   Muleshoe job" is a rule about one company, and it must not follow the
   person out of that company — which is precisely what would happen if a
   personal profile held it unscoped.

 It is a string and not a repeated one: a rule that genuinely applies in two
 named tenants and not a third is two rules, and the person can say so. A
 list here would be a second scoping grammar beside `text` of the kind
 RuleMatch item 4 refuses.

 NOT THE SAME FIELD AS `namespace` ABOVE, and the distinction is
 load-bearing: `namespace` is the store's egress backstop, which says who
 may READ the row; this says where the rule has EFFECT once read. A reader
 in tenant B legitimately sees a rule scoped to tenant A — it is their own
 rule, it is in their own list, and it simply does not fire.

 NO (spec.query_field), for the same reason nothing inside RuleMatch has
 one. The evaluating runtime wants "scoped to here OR scoped nowhere", which
 is a two-value OR that an EQ criterion cannot express; it loads the user's
 bounded rule set and decides in process, as it already does for `match`.

fields.name: trace_id
fields.description:
TAGS 19-99 ARE FREE FOR ENVELOPE FIELDS (18 is tenant_scope, added
 2026-09-20). An `oneof effect_params` starts at 100 the day one is
 needed — see RuleEffect's growth path. Without the gap
 the next envelope field and the first effect payload would compete for
 adjacent numbers and a reader could no longer tell the two halves apart.

types.name: SampleRunCheckpointRequest
SampleRunCheckpointResponse

message.name: RunCheckpoint
message.description:
RunCheckpoint records one completed step, written after stratum acked the
 step's publish (A1, design §13.1). Its key IS the idempotency key
 (dog, tenant, event_seq, step): "<instance_key>/<event_seq>/<step>" in the
 row's namespace. A replay serves a matching call (same tool, same
 request_sha256) from here instead of calling again (Q20).
 RETENTION: follows CHAT.

types.name: SampleScottyActivityRequest
SampleScottyActivityResponse

message.name: ScottyActivity
message.description:
ScottyActivity is the ARTIFACT left by every write into knowledge.

 §1: "Nothing reaches knowledge without leaving an artifact. Authored facts —
 a phone number, a written policy, a stated deadline — are not distilled from
 anything, so if current state could change with no immutable record, the
 authored half is unrecoverable." ScottyState's requires_artifact_on_write
 enforces that this type exists; this is that type.

 §4 is the reason it is a generated RECORD rather than something the service
 writes for itself: "Scotty must not be the writer of the accounting. If it
 were, 'doesn't rat Dennis out' becomes 'can omit'... Accounting is a
 byproduct of the call path, stamped at the generated seam." The neutral
 auditor reads THIS, and this carries what was DONE — entity kind, entity id,
 principal, request id — never what was said.

 spec.record implies spec.event, so tacplus synthesizes the topic wrapper
 ScottyActivityBus with topic ref scotty.ScottyActivityBus.stream. Do NOT
 hand-write that wrapper.

fields.name: activity_id
fields.description: activity_id is the record key: one row per WRITE, not one per entity.

fields.name: entity_kind
fields.description:
entity_kind and entity_id name what was written. EQ-filterable, because
 "every artifact for this ticket" is the question provenance has to answer.

enum_values.name: SCOTTY_ENTITY_KIND_TICKET_CHAIN
enum_values.description:
A TICKET_CHAIN artifact is left ONCE per chain, on the hop that reaches
 Config.max_chain_hops — the moment Scotty stops mediating. entity_id is the
 chain_id. It records that AI mediation hit its limit, which is a thing that
 was DONE and therefore belongs in the auditor's store; no ticket is decided
 by it.

fields.name: occurred_at_ms
fields.description:
occurred_at_ms is the RANGE criterion — "what happened between D1 and D2"
 is the auditor's own question.

fields.name: acted_by
fields.description:
acted_by is the principal on whose behalf the write happened. NOT redacted:
 §4 says a finding is a citation naming "action A by principal X at T", and
 a citation whose principal egress clears is not a citation.
 It is also the ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL for the record query plane's c2s
 half. spiffe_id below is the record's declared owner but is the PUBLISHER
 — eventbus stamps scotty's own service identity onto it — so filtering a
 user's reads on that field would show every user nothing. acted_by is the
 authenticated human the write happened for, taken from the verified token
 (service.rs `principal()`) or from the written row's own (spec.principal)
 field, never from anything the caller writes. That is the value the
 generated wrapper's row filter must compare against.
 The EQ criterion is what carries the row filter into the plane's SIZE-ONLY
 RPCs: Get<T>Count returns a number over the handle's predicate and no rows,
 so no egress filter can narrow it. The generated c2s wrapper pins this
 criterion to the caller at Create<T>Query, and every later call on the
 handle inherits it.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner. The name is LOAD-BEARING: eventbus's topic
 discovery matches the literal field name "spiffe_id" of string type when it
 decides which topics get publisher-identity stamping, so renaming this
 field silently turns the stamping off.

fields.name: request_id
fields.description:
request_id is the JOIN KEY to the accounting plane — the same value
 accountingrecord.AccountingRecord carries under the same name with the same
 EQ query_field, so "which accounting rows belong to the request that wrote
 this row" and "which row did that request write" are one predicate asked of
 two record types. Without it provenance stops at the accounting plane's
 edge, which is precisely where §4's auditor starts.

 Empty is legitimate, not an error: an unauthenticated path has no Caller to
 read one from, so a required-and-absent field would fail the publish rather
 than record the gap.

fields.name: spiffe_actor
fields.description:
spiffe_actor is the DELEGATE that made the call, stamped by EventBus from
 the token's `act` claim at publish time — the agent acting for the person
 in acted_by, unset in the ordinary non-delegated case. Provenance only: it
 is never the principal, and sys/spec.proto forbids wiring it into one.

 The service does not set it and must not: like spiffe_id above, a value
 written here would be a claim about identity that nothing verified.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT: the namespace claim of the caller
 whose write this artifact records. It is the tenant half of the identity
 acted_by carries the subject half of — that field's (spec.store_principal)
 answers "are these MY rows", this one answers "is this MY tenant", by EXACT
 string equality against the caller's claim (never the level-or-below
 containment the administrative namespace rule uses).

 MANDATORY, not opt-in: tacplus (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations) fails
 generation for any (spec.record) declaring no such field, on the reasoning
 that the record nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 The filter is generated on the READ side, which is not this record's own
 s2s publish surface above: stratum's record query plane (the (spec.trait) in
 vservices/query.proto) exposes a c2s List/Sample/Watch over EVERY record in
 the fleet, and the namespace check is spliced into each of them for this
 type. A row reaching one of those with a namespace other than the caller's
 halts the JVM rather than failing the one call.

 Bounded like acted_by.

 AN EQ (spec.query_field), and it did not used to be. The reasoning that kept
 it off was that a boundary is not a caller-supplied predicate — which is
 right about the CALLER and wrong about the SERVER. The client-facing read
 plane pins this field to the caller's verified namespace claim BEFORE the
 store is asked, and a pin needs a criterion to be pinned into; the record
 store evaluates only the criteria a record annotates, so without this line
 the pin is generated and silently ignored, leaving the aborting egress
 filter as the only tenant boundary. tacplus refuses (spec.record).c2s_read
 on a record whose namespace field is not EQ-queryable, for exactly that
 reason.

 It stays uncallable by clients, which is the part the old comment cared
 about: the emitted GetScottyActivityRequest and ListScottyActivityRequest
 carry no namespace field, and ScottyActivityReadFilter — the only filter a
 c2s caller supplies — is generated without one.

types.name: SampleTaskRequest
SampleTaskResponse

message.name: Task
message.description:
A Task is SHARED between whoever raised it and whoever it is for ("approve
 Tara's timesheet" is Tara's ask and your task). That is why it lives here and
 not in Scotty's private plane. Scotty CURATES the list — decides what to
 raise, in what words, with what due — and writes it through the MCP tool
 below; the person completes it.
 A stratum record since 2026-09-25, tenant-owned and not `private`. The block
 above `message Job` is the reasoning for all six and is not repeated; the one
 thing that is specific to Task is that its no-(spec.store_principal) has TWO
 reasons rather than one — the company owns the row, AND a task has two
 parties, which is the older argument already written on `assigned_to` below.

fields.name: detail
fields.description: detail is prose for the person. Nothing parses it.

fields.name: assigned_to
fields.description:
assigned_to is the principal the task is FOR.

 NO (spec.store_principal) HERE, and that is choice B's answer rather than
 its abandonment. A task is read by TWO people — the one it is for and the
 one who raised it — and tacplus pins to exactly one: principal_validate.go
 refuses a second (spec.store_principal)/(spec.principal) field on one
 message, and (spec.record_read).c2s.scope has no "principal in one of these
 fields" value. Pinning to assigned_to alone would make the person who
 RAISED the task unable to see it, which is the wrong half to keep.

 So the two-principal gate is where scotty.Ticket already puts the identical
 problem: in the handler. scotty's `is_participant` admits the requester who
 opened a ticket or the decider it is routed to; work's task reads admit
 assigned_to or raised_by, by the same construction and for the same reason.
 Anything WIDER than those two — a superintendent's view of the crew's tasks
 — is the unbuilt entitlement work `scotty.Human` is already waiting on
 (schematic looper's decisions/scotty-read-authorization-not-wired.md,
 pre-split snoopy history, not in this repo) and is not invented here.

fields.name: raised_by
fields.description:
raised_by is who asked. A person, or the caller's Scotty acting for them
 (then the delegated token's subject — the person — with actor = Scotty,
 recorded on the artifact, not here).

fields.name: done
fields.description:
done is the ONLY mutable fact on a task. Ticking it is UpdateTask; the
 artifact records who and when. There is no delete: a task that was wrong is
 done with a comment on the artifact, not erased. Choice F.

fields.name: job_id
fields.description:
origin: what this task came from, so the app can open it. At most one of
 these is set; all may be empty (a bare reminder).

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description: The publisher, as on Job. Never a read filter; see Job.spiffe_id.

types.name: SampleThreadMapEntryRequest
SampleThreadMapEntryResponse

message.name: ThreadMapEntry
message.description:
ThreadMapEntry is one thread of one logical instance (A29; backlog-scotty-
 slices §2.2). The dispatcher routes each CrewEvent by thread_id to that
 thread's session worker; this row is what survives the worker. A pigeon's
 private thread is an ordinary entry (room_ref = the pigeon thread, A30).
 Queued for thread T = events with thread_id T and seq > T.done_through_seq.
 RETENTION: OPERATIONAL (BQ10).

fields.name: instance_key
fields.description: instance_key as on CrewCursor.

fields.name: thread_id
fields.description: thread_id in the A29 format t_<created_ms base36>_<16 hex> (§2.3, BQ8).

fields.name: parent_thread_id
fields.description: parent_thread_id: set when this thread revived an aged-out one.

fields.name: successor_thread_id
fields.description:
successor_thread_id: set on the aged-out entry at revival, so a late reply
 to the old id is routed to the new one.

fields.name: room_ref
fields.description:
room_ref is the room the thread lives in (REF_KIND_ROOM), or the pigeon
 thread. move_conversation updates it (A6).

fields.name: record_type
fields.description: record_type is the proto full name for REF_KIND_RECORD, e.g. "work.Permit".

fields.name: last_used_ms
fields.description: last_used_ms drives age-out.

fields.name: use_counter
fields.description: use_counter is A29's "last-used counter": turns taken.

fields.name: done_through_seq
fields.description:
done_through_seq is the PER-THREAD ack (A29): the highest instance seq in
 this thread acked by `done`.

enum_values.name: THREAD_STATE_AGED_OUT
enum_values.description:
AGED_OUT: the session worker dropped its context (idle past the runtime's
 thread_idle_ms, or evicted LRU past max_live_threads). A message to it
 revives it as a new thread with parent_thread_id = this one (§2.4).

fields.name: version
fields.description: version: republish-in-place (A4 arbitration).

types.name: SampleTicketAdviceRequest
SampleTicketAdviceResponse

message.name: TicketAdvice
message.description:
TicketAdvice is Scotty's advice, SEALED.

 §3: "The advice is sealed when given, not composed at decision time.
 Otherwise a Scotty built to serve Dennis softens a warning it knows he's
 about to override — nobody would have to instruct it to." And: "Immutable to
 Dennis_Scotty too, not only to Dennis."

 Sealing here is STRUCTURAL, not a flag. There is no UpdateTicketAdvice RPC in
 the Scotty service, so no caller — human or agent — has a mutation path to
 reach. A `sealed: bool` would be decoration; an absent RPC is not.

 Advice may be given more than once on a ticket ("Ruiz is back Friday"). Each
 giving is a new sealed row, and the LAST one is the final advice. The design
 record says the ticket carries "the final advice PLUS the asserted facts that
 moved it, not the deliberation" — the append chain is that, with the
 intermediate rows retained rather than discarded. See
 decisions/ticket-advice-append-vs-single-row.md.

 A stratum record since 2026-09-25, tenant-owned and not `private` — the block
 above `message Human` is the reasoning for all six. THE VISIBILITY SPLIT IS
 WHY THIS IS ITS OWN RECORD RATHER THAN A VARIANT INSIDE Ticket's: §3's "Joe
 sees the decision and Dennis's comment. Not the advice" needs the restricted
 rows to be reachable by a DIFFERENT read from the unrestricted ones, and the
 (spec.record_read) block at the top of this file is careful to give none of
 the three a generated client-facing plane that would bypass that.

fields.name: advice_id
fields.description: (spec.indexed) went with the state collection; see Human.human_id.

fields.name: advice_text
fields.description:
advice_text is what Scotty advised. Prose, and untrusted at the context
 seam exactly as request_text is — §5 puts "policy text authored by Alicia,
 an override reason from Joe, and a summary distilled by Scotty" in the same
 shape with very different standing, and the standing lives in the
 attribution, not the string.

fields.name: asserted_facts
fields.description:
asserted_facts are the CLAIMS that moved the advice. §3: "Dennis can move
 his Scotty with claims, which land on the record and can be wrong, never
 with vibes." Their landing on the record is the entire mechanism — a claim
 that is not recorded cannot later be found to have been false.

message.name: AssertedFact
message.description: AssertedFact is one claim offered to move advice.

fields.name: claim_text
fields.description:
claim_text is the claim as stated ("Ruiz is back Friday"). Prose, and it
 can be wrong — that is the point of recording it.

fields.name: asserted_by_human_id
fields.description: asserted_by_human_id is who is on the hook for it.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT — the same isolation pair Ticket
 carries, on this row for the same reason: the generated egress filter is
 per-record-type, so an appended row left unstamped would be a hole in the
 boundary the ticket it hangs off has. Stamped from CreateTicketAdviceRequest's
 (spec.namespace) field, matched at egress by EXACT equality, and a row that
 has to be dropped aborts the process. EQ-queryable since the move to
 stratum, for the reason Ticket.namespace now gives.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description: The publisher, as on Human. Never a read filter; see Human.spiffe_id.

types.name: SampleTicketCommentRequest
SampleTicketCommentResponse

message.name: TicketComment
message.description:
TicketComment is a decider's own comment, appended. §3: "Dennis can add his
 own comments... Dennis's comment APPENDS as a separate record, same primitive
 as a field-log correction."

 It is visible to the requester where advice is not — "Joe sees the decision
 and Dennis's comment. Not the advice."

 A stratum record since 2026-09-25, tenant-owned and not `private` — the block
 above `message Human` is the reasoning for all six.

fields.name: comment_id
fields.description: (spec.indexed) went with the state collection; see Human.human_id.

fields.name: authored_by
fields.description: authored_by is the authenticated principal, stamped from the token.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT — the same isolation pair Ticket
 carries, on this row for the same reason: the generated egress filter is
 per-record-type, so an appended row left unstamped would be a hole in the
 boundary the ticket it hangs off has. Stamped from CreateTicketCommentRequest's
 (spec.namespace) field, matched at egress by EXACT equality, and a row that
 has to be dropped aborts the process. EQ-queryable since the move to
 stratum, for the reason Ticket.namespace now gives.

types.name: SampleTicketDecisionRequest
SampleTicketDecisionResponse

message.name: TicketDecision
message.description:
TicketDecision is the authorise/decline. §3: "when Dennis authorizes or
 declines the request the ticket shows what Scottys advice is and its
 immutable to Dennis."

 Append-only for the same structural reason advice is: no Update RPC. A
 reversal is a new decision row, which keeps "what was decided, and when" from
 being overwritten by "what is decided now".

 A stratum record since 2026-09-25, tenant-owned and not `private` — the block
 above `message Human` is the reasoning for all six.

fields.name: decision_id
fields.description: (spec.indexed) went with the state collection; see Human.human_id.

fields.name: outcome
fields.description:
outcome is authorise, decline or amend-requested. All three are TERMINAL
 for the ticket they are recorded against — an amend request does not
 reopen this ticket, it invites a NEW one carrying the same chain_id. The
 absence of a decision row still means the ask is unresolved, which §3 calls
 "the highest-value finding".

enum_values.name: TICKET_DECISION_OUTCOME_AMEND_REQUESTED
enum_values.description:
AMEND_REQUESTED: this ask, as written, is not being granted, and the
 decider is inviting a revised one. The requester answers it by opening a
 new ticket with amends_ticket_id set to this one, which carries the chain
 forward. Tag 3 is NEW — 1 and 2 keep their wire values.

fields.name: decided_by
fields.description:
decided_by is the authenticated principal that decided, stamped from the
 token by the generated wrapper. It is ALWAYS the human — Scotty never
 decides as itself.

fields.name: decided_by_actor
fields.description:
decided_by_actor is the token's `act` claim: the delegate that actually
 made the call, when the human's Scotty made it under a standing policy
 rather than the human making it directly. EMPTY is the ordinary case and
 means the human decided in person; it is not an error or an unknown.

 The distinction is only worth recording if the REQUESTER can see it, which
 is why it is on this row and therefore on GetTicketResponse.decisions,
 rather than only on the artifact envelope. "Dennis authorized this" and
 "Dennis's Scotty authorized this under a policy Dennis wrote" are different
 answers to the question the requester is actually asking.

 NOT (spec.principal) and NOT (spec.store_principal) — the principal is
 decided_by above and stays that way. sys/spec.proto says the same of its
 event-envelope counterpart (spec.identity_spiffe_actor): actor is
 provenance, never the owning principal. There is no store-side annotation
 for it on a state row, so the service stamps it from the generated token
 accessor; see the decision doc for that generator gap.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT — the same isolation pair Ticket
 carries, on this row for the same reason: the generated egress filter is
 per-record-type, so an appended row left unstamped would be a hole in the
 boundary the ticket it hangs off has. Stamped from CreateTicketDecisionRequest's
 (spec.namespace) field, matched at egress by EXACT equality, and a row that
 has to be dropped aborts the process. EQ-queryable since the move to
 stratum, for the reason Ticket.namespace now gives.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description: The publisher, as on Human. Never a read filter; see Human.spiffe_id.

types.name: SampleTicketRequest
SampleTicketResponse

message.name: Ticket
message.description:
Ticket is the IMMUTABLE CORE of a request. §3: "The ticket is a general
 primitive, not a time-off feature — request, routed, advised, decided,
 commented, immutable, appendable, accounted. It covers overrides, permits and
 approvals generally, and it exercises the entire stack."

 NO STATUS FIELD, and that is not an omission. "Immutable" and "a lifecycle
 enum this row keeps up to date" are contradictory, and the lifecycle is
 already fully derivable: a ticket is decided iff a TicketDecision exists for
 it, advised iff a TicketAdvice does. Storing it twice creates a state that
 can disagree with the records it summarises. See the schematic looper's
 decisions/ticket-status-derived-not-stored.md (pre-split snoopy history,
 not in this repo).

 NO KIND/CATEGORY FIELD either. §5: "Prose earns fields once the pattern is
 known; a field never degrades to prose because it got inconvenient."
 Time-off, override and permit tickets have not yet shown a common structure,
 so classifying them now would be inventing the taxonomy. request_text carries
 it as attributed prose until the pattern is known. See the schematic
 looper's decisions/ticket-kind-field-deliberately-absent.md (pre-split
 snoopy history, not in this repo).

 NO (spec.store_principal), unlike tasks.Task. That option filters reads to
 the row's creating caller, which would make a routed ticket unreadable BY THE
 PERSON IT IS ROUTED TO — the one read the primitive exists to serve.

 A stratum record since 2026-09-25, tenant-owned and not `private` — the block
 above `message Human` is the reasoning for all six. The one thing specific to
 Ticket is that its no-(spec.store_principal) has TWO reasons rather than one:
 the company owns the row, AND a ticket has two parties, which is the older
 argument already written just above.

fields.name: ticket_id
fields.description: (spec.indexed) went with the state collection; see Human.human_id.

fields.name: requested_by
fields.description:
requested_by is the authenticated PRINCIPAL that opened the ticket, stamped
 from the token by the generated wrapper (see CreateTicketRequest). It is
 the token subject, not a Human id, because it has to be the thing the
 platform can actually vouch for.

fields.name: subject_human_id
fields.description:
subject_human_id is the Human the request is ABOUT. Usually the requester
 ("can I take off early Friday"), but not necessarily — a foreman opens a
 ticket about a crew member who has no direct access at all, which is
 exactly the unskilled-rolls-up-through-someone case.

 Its relationship to requested_by is the open half: the design settles that
 the Human record is the source of truth and the token is ephemeral proof,
 but not how a principal is resolved to a Human id at the seam. See
 decisions/principal-to-human-id-resolution-open.md.

fields.name: routed_to_human_id
fields.description:
routed_to_human_id is whose decision is being sought — the "routes to
 Dennis_Scotty" half of §3. One recipient, not a list: §2's propagation rule
 is "escalation is exceptional, and ONE LEVEL ONLY. You do not ask your
 boss's boss", and a repeated field would quietly permit the thing that rule
 forbids.

fields.name: request_text
fields.description:
request_text is the ask, in the requester's own words. It is UNTRUSTED
 INPUT by construction — §5: "Ticket routing puts one person's text into
 another person's agent's context by design; that is a prompt-injection
 channel created by the feature." The two defences are structural and both
 apply here: authority never derives from this string (every authorisation
 in this file is an entitlement or a typed field), and it is attributed at
 the context seam — "Joe wrote:", never a directive.

fields.name: chain_id
fields.description:
chain_id groups every ticket of ONE negotiation. Jody, 2026-08-30:
 "the requestor should be able to ask for reconsideration by amending
 request... you want the entire chain."

 A resubmission after TICKET_DECISION_OUTCOME_AMEND_REQUESTED is a NEW
 ticket row, never a mutation of the old one — this row is immutable and the
 rest of the design is append-only for the reasons
 decisions/ticket-advice-append-vs-single-row.md gives. chain_id is what
 makes the several rows one conversation.

 SERVER-ASSIGNED, and the caller cannot supply it: CreateTicketRequest
 carries amends_ticket_id only, and the server copies the predecessor's
 chain_id. Only the FIRST ticket of a chain has chain_id == ticket_id.

 Not (spec.indexed): that option marks the COLLECTION KEY, which is
 ticket_id. "The entire chain" is ListTickets filtered by this field, the
 same shape routed_to_human_id already has, and it is a service-side filter
 over the collection read — see
 decisions/ticket-decision-chain-2026-08-30.md for the cost.

fields.name: amends_ticket_id
fields.description:
amends_ticket_id names the IMMEDIATE PREDECESSOR, and is empty for the
 first ticket in a chain. It is kept alongside chain_id rather than instead
 of it because the two answer different questions: this one is "what did
 this ticket revise", chain_id is "what conversation is this", and reading
 the whole chain off chain_id is one filtered read instead of a walk.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT, and the read half of the isolation
 pair this retrofit adds. Its twin is (spec.namespace) on the Create request
 above: that one binds the field to the caller's namespace claim on the way
 IN (stamp when empty, accept when equal, INVALID_ARGUMENT when different);
 this one is what the generated wrapper filters egress rows against on the
 way OUT, by EXACT string equality — never the level-or-below containment
 the administrative namespace rule uses, because "users and data always has
 to land in a leaf".

 A row that has to be dropped by that filter ABORTS THE PROCESS rather than
 failing the one call. Reaching it means kernel handed this service another
 tenant's row, which is a leak the filter exists to make impossible, and the
 decision record settles that a crash is the cheaper failure against it.

 Bounded like ScottyActivity.namespace.

 AN EQ (spec.query_field) SINCE 2026-09-25, AND IT DID NOT USED TO BE. The
 reasoning that kept it off was that a boundary is not a caller-supplied
 predicate — right about the CALLER, wrong about the SERVER, and the same
 correction ScottyActivity.namespace already carries. Now that this row
 lives in stratum rather than in a per-tenant kernel collection, the handler
 has to pin the caller's verified claim into the predicate BEFORE the store
 is asked, and a pin needs a criterion to be pinned into; without this line
 the pin is generated and silently ignored. It stays uncallable by clients —
 the c2s surface of a ticket is GetTicket/ListTickets, whose request
 messages carry no namespace field.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description: The publisher, as on Human. Never a read filter; see Human.spiffe_id.

types.name: SampleToolCallOutcomeRequest
SampleToolCallOutcomeResponse

message.name: ToolCallOutcome
message.description:
ToolCallOutcome — one per tool call, written by the runtime (A26). It
 carries no arguments and no text, only classes and ids, so it can never hold
 a person<->Scotty conversation (never logged, Jody 2026-09-29). Weekly
 rollup per dog x tool x class; a recurring failure becomes an eval case.
 RETENTION: LOG (2 years).

fields.name: persona_version
fields.description: persona_version is PersonaDefinition.version_hash at the time.

fields.name: error_path
fields.description:
error_path is the JSON path tacplus reports for a parse/validation error
 (ask T8).

types.name: SampleUploadSessionRequest
SampleUploadSessionResponse

message.name: UploadSession
message.description:
UploadSession is one upload's durable reservation and audit trail (R9).

 IT IS THE AUTHORIZATION FOR THE PUT. The upload token carries nothing: it is
 raw randomness, and this row — keyed by its sha256 — is where the upload's
 terms live. A pod receiving a PUT hashes the token, reads this row, and takes
 the group, namespace, declared hash, size and content type from it. Exactly
 the shape BlobLink gives a `/b/` token (R3, R7); there is no signing key and
 nothing to rotate.

 THE COST, STATED: a record reaches stratum on an eventbus publish, which is
 enqueue-and-retry, so a PUT arriving milliseconds after CreateUpload returned
 can find this row missing and be refused. BlobLink has had exactly that race
 since it was written and it is accepted there for the same reason — a caller
 that just asked for the token retries.

 This row is ALSO the quota reservation, the expiry sweep that releases it, the
 single-use ledger (state leaves PENDING once), and the answer to "what was
 uploaded, by whom, when".

fields.name: upload_id
fields.description:
upload_id is the record key: the lowercase hex SHA-256 of the raw upload
 token, exactly as BlobLink.token_hash is for a `/b/` token. A PUT hashes
 what arrived in the path and looks up THAT, so the key is not a secret even
 though the path is. It is derived from the token and not from the content
 hash: two tenants uploading the same bytes at the same time are two
 sessions.

fields.name: group
fields.description:
group, content_hash, size_bytes and content_type are what the upload
 DECLARED. The Blob row carries what actually arrived; the two are compared
 at end of stream and a mismatch fails the upload (R9 step 3).

fields.name: reserved_bytes
fields.description:
reserved_bytes is what this session holds against the tenant's group quota
 while it is PENDING. It is the DECLARED size — the only number available
 before the bytes arrive — which is why `max_blob_bytes` is also enforced on
 the wire: the reservation is a promise the stream still has to keep.

fields.name: state
fields.description: state is the session's terminal answer. See UploadState.

enum_values.name: UPLOAD_STATE_PENDING
enum_values.description:
PENDING: quota is reserved and the token is live. No bytes have been
 promoted.

enum_values.name: UPLOAD_STATE_COMMITTED
enum_values.description:
COMMITTED: the bytes are fsynced and renamed on both pods and the Blob row
 is published. The reservation became real usage.

enum_values.name: UPLOAD_STATE_ABORTED
enum_values.description:
ABORTED: CancelUpload, an expiry sweep, or a failed PUT. Temps are gone
 from both pods and the reservation is released.

fields.name: created_ms
fields.description:
created_ms and expires_ms bound the token. expires_ms is checked when the
 PUT ARRIVES, not while it streams: a 50 MiB upload on a slow link must not
 fail at minute 16 having transferred everything.

fields.name: owner_principal
fields.description:
owner_principal and namespace are the owning service and owning tenant, as
 on Blob. The reservation is against exactly this pair's group quota.

types.name: SampleUserProfileRequest
SampleUserProfileResponse

message.name: UserProfile
message.description:
UserProfile is ONE PERSON, ACROSS EVERY TENANT THEY BELONG TO: their
 preferences and their activity counter. One row per owning principal, and
 exactly one — a person has one timezone and one language.

 spec.record implies spec.event, so tacplus synthesizes the topic wrapper
 ProfileBus with topic ref profile.UserProfileBus.stream. Do NOT hand-write it.

fields.name: profile_id
fields.description:
profile_id is the record key: the owner principal verbatim — see the
 option block. It duplicates `owner` below because the key field and the
 (spec.store_principal) field are two different annotations on this
 platform and tacplus refuses to fold them into one.

fields.name: owner
fields.description:
owner is whose profile this is, and the ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL. It is the
 PERSON: /tenants/people/users/<u>, where <u> is derived from the IdP
 provider and its stable subject
 (decisions/identity-people-tenant-devices-private-2026-09-21.md §1). Never
 a per-company identity — a user in drpepper reaches their own row through
 the `linked` claim (§2), not by owning a second one. This row is one
 person's, across every tenant they belong to.

 IT IS ALSO WHAT `private` ABOVE PINS TO. The value is stamped from the
 caller's `sub` at write time and is never caller-supplied: every write
 request below carries it as a (spec.principal) field, which the generated
 wrapper fills and refuses to let a caller set.

 (spec.store_principal) is what holds a caller's reads to their own rows on
 the query plane. spiffe_id below is the record's declared owner but holds
 THIS SERVICE's identity (eventbus stamps the publisher), so filtering on
 that would show every user nothing. The EQ criterion carries the filter
 into the plane's size-only RPCs, which return a number over the handle's
 predicate and no rows for an egress filter to narrow.

message.name: Preferences
message.description:
Preferences is how the user wants to be spoken to. One message on the profile
 row, with exactly the fields the ruling lists and nothing else: "Expanded
 later; nothing else earns its way in now."

fields.name: display_name
fields.description:
display_name is what Scotty calls this person and what other people see.
 Prose; nothing derives from it.

fields.name: language
fields.description:
language is a BCP-47 tag ("en", "es", "es-MX"). The per-person language of
 the metric-twin/Spanish work (roadmap/PLAN.md item 2's §35-§36 note):
 messages are stored in the author's language and translated on tap, so this
 says which language to PRODUCE for this person, never which to store.

fields.name: timezone
fields.description:
timezone is an IANA zone name ("America/Chicago"). Every local time this
 service holds — QuietHours above, RuleTimeWindow below — is resolved
 against it, which is why neither of those carries a zone of its own.

message.name: QuietHours
message.description:
QuietHours is the daily window in which Scotty does not interrupt.

 A PREFERENCE, NOT A RULE. It is here rather than as a RuleNode because the
 user sets it directly in the app and nothing about it is a sentence Scotty
 inferred, cites, or reorders. A rule that happens to mention a time window
 carries its own RuleTimeWindow in `match` and is a different object.

fields.name: start_minute_of_day
fields.description:
Minutes since local midnight, in Preferences.timezone. 0..1439.

 end BEFORE start WRAPS MIDNIGHT — 22:00 to 06:00 is start 1320, end 360 —
 which is the common case and the reason these are two ints rather than a
 start plus a duration. start == end means no quiet hours at all; a
 twenty-four-hour quiet day is "mute", which is not this field.

fields.name: show_metric_units
fields.description:
show_metric_units and show_customary_units are INDEPENDENT BOOLS, not a
 two-valued enum, and that is the metric-twin decision rather than a
 hedge: the same person legitimately wants both shown at once (a nominal
 size beside its measurement), and a single "unit system" field cannot say
 that. Both false is a display with no units, which is a real thing to ask
 for and not an error state to validate against.

fields.name: hit_count
fields.description:
hit_count and last_hit_ms are ACTIVITY, owned and written only by this
 service. The ruling: "Never bumped as a side effect of a query, never on
 rule rows. This is the AgentSessionState.tool_use_count pattern."

 THERE IS NO RPC FOR THIS AND THERE IS NOT MEANT TO BE ONE (Jody,
 2026-09-20). The first pass of this file declared an S2S `RecordHit` /
 `UpdateProfileActivity` rpc for the bump, which made the service's own
 bookkeeping into a contract somebody else had to call — and its only
 plausible caller, the user's own Scotty, is a class 9c service with no S2S
 identity to call it with. Instead this service bumps these two fields ON
 ITS OWN ROW, in process, from inside its own user-RPC handlers below,
 coalesced to at most one republish per user per
 Config.activity_coalesce_seconds (one hour by default) and dropped silently
 inside the window rather than queued. That is what "owned and written only
 by the profile service" already said; the rpc was the part that did not
 follow from it.

 COALESCING IS THE HANDLER'S, AND CANNOT BE ANYBODY ELSE'S. A caller that
 had to remember when it last bumped would get it wrong across restarts and
 across pods, and the counter would then measure caller behaviour rather
 than user activity.

 They are product data, not a residency signal. Residency of this row is
 stratum's idle clock's business and these two fields must never be read as
 one — that conflation is exactly what the 2026-09-20 lifecycle record
 separates when it takes the residency clock out of store_epoch.

fields.name: created_ms
fields.description:
created_ms and updated_ms are the AUTHOR's clocks: when this profile first
 existed, and when it was last written. Distinct from store_epoch_ms below,
 which the store owns. updated_ms is the retention timestamp_field.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner. The NAME IS LOAD-BEARING: eventbus's topic
 discovery matches the literal field name "spiffe_id" of string type when it
 decides which topics get publisher-identity stamping, so renaming this
 field silently turns the stamping off. It holds THIS SERVICE's identity
 because the publish is s2s; `owner` above is where the person is.

fields.name: store_epoch_ms
fields.description:
store_epoch_ms is the row's LAST-WRITE clock, stamped by the generated
 subscription dispatch over whatever arrived, so it cannot be producer-
 influenced. Declared because this row is rewritten in place and therefore
 diverges from the business clocks above on every write.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning namespace, held to the reader's claim by
 EXACT string equality. MANDATORY on a (spec.record): tacplus's
 ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations fails generation for any record
 declaring no such field, on the reasoning that the record nobody remembered
 to annotate is exactly the one that leaks. Left EMPTY by the producer on
 purpose — eventbus's PublishHandler stamps it from the publishing token's
 namespace claim and REFUSES a publish whose token carries none.

 IT IS THE `people` TENANT'S, AND IT IS NO LONGER THE MECHANISM. The
 publisher is this service's own identity and this service now lives in
 `people` (see the SERVICE CLASS note at the top), so the stamped claim is
 the `people` namespace — the same value on every row, for every person,
 which is exactly why it cannot be what keeps people apart. `private` above
 is what does that. The 2026-09-20 wording this replaces reasoned about a
 /system claim and about deriving a namespace per tenant; both are gone with
 the service class that produced them, and there is no namespace derivation
 anywhere in this file or in the handlers.

 The annotation is kept because it is MANDATORY and because it is a genuine
 backstop — a reader standing outside `people` is refused before `private`
 is even consulted, and decisions/identity-people-tenant-devices-private-2026-09-21.md
 §2 is what lets a caller standing in drpepper past it: the generated
 backstop accepts a row matching either the `namespace` claim or a `linked`
 claim. Per-company scoping of a RULE is still RuleNode.tenant_scope, which
 is a different axis from either.

 EQ-queryable because tacplus refuses (spec.record).c2s_read on a record
 whose namespace field is not: the client-facing plane pins this field to
 the caller's verified claim before the store is asked, and a pin needs a
 criterion to be pinned into. It stays uncallable by clients — the emitted
 request messages carry no namespace field.

fields.name: deleted
fields.description:
deleted is this row's soft-delete state, and it is what gives
 residency.deleted_max_age_seconds above something to measure: a record
 declaring no (spec.deleted_flag) field is never purged at all. A flagged
 profile stays fetchable by profile_id for its year and is dropped from the
 generated List / Watch / Count / Sample plane meanwhile.

 No RPC sets it today. The write surface is a republish, like every other
 field on this record and like RuleNode.deleted.

types.name: SampleWaitRequest
SampleWaitResponse

message.name: Wait
message.description:
Wait is a pending expectation. wait_for writes it and the run EXITS; the
 matching event (enqueued with wait_id) or the deadline (a Scheduler
 registration "wait:<wait_id>", EVENT_SOURCE_WAIT_DEADLINE) wakes the dog

     be pinned into.

message.name: ScottyActivity
message.description:
ScottyActivity is the ARTIFACT left by every write into knowledge.

 §1: "Nothing reaches knowledge without leaving an artifact. Authored facts —
 a phone number, a written policy, a stated deadline — are not distilled from
 anything, so if current state could change with no immutable record, the
 authored half is unrecoverable." ScottyState's requires_artifact_on_write
 enforces that this type exists; this is that type.

 §4 is the reason it is a generated RECORD rather than something the service
 writes for itself: "Scotty must not be the writer of the accounting. If it
 were, 'doesn't rat Dennis out' becomes 'can omit'... Accounting is a
 byproduct of the call path, stamped at the generated seam." The neutral
 auditor reads THIS, and this carries what was DONE — entity kind, entity id,
 principal, request id — never what was said.

 spec.record implies spec.event, so tacplus synthesizes the topic wrapper
 ScottyActivityBus with topic ref scotty.ScottyActivityBus.stream. Do NOT
 hand-write that wrapper.

fields.name: activity_id
fields.description: activity_id is the record key: one row per WRITE, not one per entity.

fields.name: entity_kind
fields.description:

enum_values.name: SCOTTY_ENTITY_KIND_TICKET_CHAIN
enum_values.description:

 by it.

fields.name: occurred_at_ms
fields.description:
occurred_at_ms is the RANGE criterion — "what happened between D1 and D2"
 is the auditor's own question.

fields.name: acted_by
fields.description:
acted_by is the principal on whose behalf the write happened. NOT redacted:
 §4 says a finding is a citation naming "action A by principal X at T", and
 a citation whose principal egress clears is not a citation.
 It is also the ROW'S OWNING PRINCIPAL for the record query plane's c2s
 half. spiffe_id below is the record's declared owner but is the PUBLISHER
 — eventbus stamps scotty's own service identity onto it — so filtering a
 user's reads on that field would show every user nothing. acted_by is the
 authenticated human the write happened for, taken from the verified token
 (service.rs `principal()`) or from the written row's own (spec.principal)
 field, never from anything the caller writes. That is the value the
 generated wrapper's row filter must compare against.
 The EQ criterion is what carries the row filter into the plane's SIZE-ONLY
 RPCs: Get<T>Count returns a number over the handle's predicate and no rows,
 so no egress filter can narrow it. The generated c2s wrapper pins this
 criterion to the caller at Create<T>Query, and every later call on the
 handle inherits it.

fields.name: spiffe_id
fields.description:
spiffe_id is the record owner. The name is LOAD-BEARING: eventbus's topic
 discovery matches the literal field name "spiffe_id" of string type when it
 decides which topics get publisher-identity stamping, so renaming this
 field silently turns the stamping off.

fields.name: request_id
fields.description:
request_id is the JOIN KEY to the accounting plane — the same value
 accountingrecord.AccountingRecord carries under the same name with the same
 EQ query_field, so "which accounting rows belong to the request that wrote
 this row" and "which row did that request write" are one predicate asked of
 two record types. Without it provenance stops at the accounting plane's
 edge, which is precisely where §4's auditor starts.

 Empty is legitimate, not an error: an unauthenticated path has no Caller to
 read one from, so a required-and-absent field would fail the publish rather
 than record the gap.

fields.name: spiffe_actor
fields.description:
spiffe_actor is the DELEGATE that made the call, stamped by EventBus from
 the token's `act` claim at publish time — the agent acting for the person
 in acted_by, unset in the ordinary non-delegated case. Provenance only: it
 is never the principal, and sys/spec.proto forbids wiring it into one.

 The service does not set it and must not: like spiffe_id above, a value
 written here would be a claim about identity that nothing verified.

fields.name: namespace
fields.description:
namespace is the row's owning TENANT: the namespace claim of the caller
 whose write this artifact records. It is the tenant half of the identity
 acted_by carries the subject half of — that field's (spec.store_principal)
 answers "are these MY rows", this one answers "is this MY tenant", by EXACT
 string equality against the caller's claim (never the level-or-below
 containment the administrative namespace rule uses).

 MANDATORY, not opt-in: tacplus (ValidateRecordNamespaceAnnotations) fails
 generation for any (spec.record) declaring no such field, on the reasoning
 that the record nobody remembered to annotate is exactly the one that leaks.

 The filter is generated on the READ side, which is not this record's own
 s2s publish surface above: stratum's record query plane (the (spec.trait) in
 vservices/query.proto) exposes a c2s List/Sample/Watch over EVERY record in
 the fleet, and the namespace check is spliced into each of them for this
 type. A row reaching one of those with a namespace other than the caller's
 halts the JVM rather than failing the one call.

 Bounded like acted_by.

 AN EQ (spec.query_field), and it did not used to be. The reasoning that kept
 it off was that a boundary is not a caller-supplied predicate — which is
 right about the CALLER and wrong about the SERVER. The client-facing read
 plane pins this field to the caller's verified namespace claim BEFORE the
 store is asked, and a pin needs a criterion to be pinned into; the record
 store evaluates only the criteria a record annotates, so without this line
 the pin is generated and silently ignored, leaving the aborting egress
 filter as the only tenant boundary. tacplus refuses (spec.record).c2s_read
 on a record whose namespace field is not EQ-queryable, for exactly that
 reason.

 It stays uncallable by clients, which is the part the old comment cared
 about: the emitted GetScottyActivityRequest and ListScottyActivityRequest
 carry no namespace field, and ScottyActivityReadFilter — the only filter a
 c2s caller supplies — is generated without one.
